documents.title: Misconduct
documents.tagline: Ambition can be deadly
documents.overview: An ambitious lawyer finds himself caught in a power struggle between a corrupt pharmaceutical executive and his firm’s senior partner. When the case takes a deadly turn, he must race to uncover the truth before he loses everything.
documents.plot:
Arthur Denning is the owner of a major pharmaceutical firm. He is very controlling of his girlfriend Emily Hynes, and she is physically intimidated by his security guards. She is abducted, and Denning is sent photos of her bruised face. He is ordered to go to an art gallery with the ransom. When a man approaches him, Denning attacks him, but learns that he was the gallery owner.
Before her abduction, Hynes reaches out to her ex-boyfriend Ben Cahill. She hints at Denning's abuse and shares some dirt that she has on him. At her apartment, she shows Cahill some files that she has stolen from Denning's laptop that reveal his criminal behavior during drug trials. She soon convinces a stranger to beat her up for the photo that she sends to Denning.
Cahill uses the information from Hynes to pitch a class-action lawsuit to his boss Charles Abrams that he files against Denning. That evening, Cahill is stunned to find Hynes dead in her apartment. With a bottle of pills in her hand and a lethal cocktail of drugs in her system, her death is suspicious but possibly just a suicide. Cahill decides to leave the scene without reporting it to the police and tries to cover his tracks, secretly telling only his wife about it.
At a preliminary deposition to the lawsuit, Denning suddenly settles the suit for $400 million, provided that the stolen documents are returned to him. Before long, Hynes's body is found in Cahill's home. Convinced that he is being framed, he confronts Denning, who is amused at Cahill's passion, but assures him that he had nothing to do with it.
A hitman kidnaps Cahill and his wife Charlotte (Eve), but Cahill overpowers and kills him. When he inspects the hitman's files, he realizes that the villain is actually his boss. Abrams has been colluding with Denning for years, deliberately losing all of the cases that his clients brought against the pharmaceutical magnate. The settlement was all just an elaborate way of protecting Denning from criminal liability.
Cahill submits the hitman's files to the police, who arrest Abrams. Before he can be taken into custody, however, Abrams grabs an officer's gun and kills himself.
As Cahill packs for a move to a new house, he notices that some of his wife's clothing smells like Hynes's perfume. He asks her what happened between the two of them. Charlotte confesses that she confronted Hynes about her involvement with her husband. They had an argument in which Charlotte hit Hynes, causing her to fall and hit her head. Although Charlotte is a nurse, she did not help her and stages the scene for the police.

documents.title: Taylor Swift: The 1989 World Tour - Live
documents.original_title: Taylor Swift: The 1989 World Tour - Live
documents.tagline: She lost him, but she found herself. And somehow that was everything.
documents.overview: Filmed in front of 76,000 fans at the ANZ Stadium in Sydney, Australia, "The 1989 World Tour Live" captures Taylor Swift's entire performance while also mixing in behind-the-scene, rehearsal, and special guest footage from her 1989 Tour.
documents.plot:
The 1989 World Tour Live is a 2015 American concert film by the singer-songwriter Taylor Swift, documenting her fourth concert tour, the 1989 World Tour, staged in support of her fifth studio album, 1989 (2014), her first record marketed as pop rather than country. Directed by Jonas Åkerlund and produced in partnership with Apple Music, the film was shot at the show of 28 November 2015 at ANZ Stadium in Sydney, Australia, and also includes behind-the-scenes footage and appearances by special guests from shows in North America and Europe. Its release marked Swift's first collaboration with Apple, coming months after she pulled her catalog from Spotify over its payment model and after Apple agreed to pay artists during the free trial period of its streaming service.

The concert opens with black-and-white projections of street scenes as Swift rises from beneath the stage to sing "Welcome to New York," followed by "New Romantics" and "Blank Space," and an industrial rock version of "I Knew You Were Trouble." The set moves through "I Wish You Would," a Singin' in the Rain-inspired staging of "How You Get the Girl" with dancers twirling neon umbrellas, and "I Know Places," in which masked dancers chase her through moving doors. Swift introduces "Clean" by sharing lessons from her personal life and performs a synth-driven "Love Story" on an elevated platform that sweeps around the stadium. Later highlights include "Style," "This Love," "Bad Blood" in a black leather suit, a rock rendition of "We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together" on electric guitar, a piano mashup of "Enchanted" and "Wildest Dreams," and "Out of the Woods" beneath giant paper planes, before the show closes with "Shake It Off" on a platform above the crowd amid fireworks and confetti.

The tour began in Tokyo on 5 May 2015 and ended in Melbourne on 12 December, spanning 85 shows. It was the highest-grossing tour of 2015, selling more than 2.27 million tickets and grossing over 250 million dollars, and critics praised Swift's stage presence and connection with her audience, while her parade of celebrity guests drew wide comment. Announced on 13 December 2015, the film premiered exclusively on Apple Music on 20 December 2015 and remained on the service until 22 May 2020; footage from it was also used in the music video for "New Romantics."

documents.title: Snatched
documents.tagline: Mess with me, mess with my mother.
documents.overview: When her boyfriend dumps Emily, a spontaneous woman in her 30s, she persuades her ultra-cautious mom to accompany her on a vacation to Ecuador. When these two very different women are trapped on this wild journey, their bond as mother and daughter is tested and strengthened while they attempt to navigate the jungle and escape.
documents.plot:
Recently fired from her job and dumped by her rock musician boyfriend, Emily Middleton is determined to enjoy a previously planned non-refundable trip to Ecuador. Learning of her relationship status from social media, her mother, Linda, tells her to come home in order to move on, where she reunites with her agoraphobic brother, Jeffrey. Initially refusing, Linda agrees to go on the trip with her daughter.
In Ecuador, after they check into the upscale hotel, Emily meets a handsome man named James at the hotel bar, and they begin a relationship. After one night of drinking and dancing with James, Emily and her mother take a sightseeing day trip with him. During their ride, a white van rams James' Jeep and the masked men abduct Emily and Linda. James escapes, but Linda suspects he was in on the kidnapping plot from the start. Emily awakens inside a cell and begins to panic, while Linda tries to calm herself by reading men's magazines. The leader, Hector Morgado, contacts Jeffrey and demands $100,000 in ransom money. Morgado then has his nephew take both women away from the kidnappers' hideout to another location. They manage to escape from their captors' car and stow away into a passing truck. As it drives away, Emily kills the leader's nephew who is chasing them by pounding his head with a shovel. The truck's driver then stops his truck and leaves them both in the middle of the jungle.
They find a phone at a nearby bar, where they call the U.S. State Department officer Morgan Russell, saying that they are in peril, and Morgan advises them to go to the US Embassy in Bogotá, Colombia. They meet a rugged-looking American named Roger Simmons. He agrees to help them find the consulate. After the three share a meal, Morgado and his men track them down. Morgado is about to kill them both as revenge for his only nephew's death, but Linda distracts him while Emily retrieves a nearby spear gun with which to threaten him. As she retrieves it, she accidentally fires it, killing Morgado's only son. They manage to escape with Simmons onto a boat. Soon, however, they are forced off the boat when the captain detects another boat nearby that is looking for the two women.
Meanwhile, Jeffrey, learning that his mother and sister have been kidnapped, calls Morgan at the State Department, saying he will join forces with the agents in order to find his mother and sister. Morgan reluctantly agrees. In Colombia, Emily, Linda, and Simmons hike through the jungle until Simmons falls to his death from a cliff. Later, Emily passes out from the effects of a tapeworm infestation. After a local village doctor removes the tapeworm from her body, Morgado and his men track them down again. They spot a zip line and decide to use it to escape. Unfortunately, the zip line is good for only one person. Linda forces Emily to leave her behind and is recaptured.
Emily safely arrives at the US Consulate.

documents.title: Episode of Sabo: The Three Brothers' Bond - The Miraculous Reunion
documents.original_title: ワンピース エピソード オブ サボ～3兄弟の絆 奇跡の再会と受け継がれる意志～
documents.tagline: The Three Brothers' Bond, The Miraculous Reunion
documents.overview: Sabo visits a grave-site where he reflects back on his childhood with his brothers Luffy and Ace. After a flashback of his past Sabo travels to the Kingdom of Dressrosa and meets up with a fellow member of the Revolutionary Army to discuss their next mission. Unbeknownst to Sabo, Luffy and his crew are also on the island searching to destroy an artificial Devil Fruit factory.
documents.plot: From a brotherhood bound by three cups of sake, one brother’s story has yet to be told! Visiting Dressrosa under orders of the Revolutionary Army, Sabo’s top-secret mission derails when Doflamingo announces the grand prize for battling in the Colosseum. The tragedy at Marineford still weighing on his mind, Sabo reunites with his little brother to protect the promises they made with Ace. Now, they’ll fight in disguise for the Colosseum’s ultimate prize: Ace’s Flame-Flame Fruit.

documents.title: One Piece: Adventure of Nebulandia
documents.original_title: ONE PIECE 〜アドベンチャー オブ ネブランディア〜
documents.tagline: It’s a Devil Fruit user’s nightmare come true.
documents.overview: Kōmei devises a plan where Zoro and Sanji take part in an eating contest, and the two eat a strange "good-for-nothing-only" mushroom that turns them into good-for-nothing men. The two are then locked in a jail cell. When the rest of the Straw Hat Pirates chase after their imprisoned crew, they land on the island of Nebulandia, which features a mysterious fog made from sea water, and it has the same effects as seastone. The Straw Hat Pirates' arrival on Nebulandia is also a part of Kōmei's plan.
documents.plot:
One Piece: Adventure of Nebulandia is a 2015 Japanese animated television special based on the One Piece manga and anime and produced by Toei Animation. Directed by Konosuke Uda, the original series director of the One Piece anime, from a screenplay by Atsuhiro Tomioka, it was broadcast on 19 December 2015 in the Saturday Premium slot as the sixth One Piece special in that slot, following Episode of Sabo earlier that year. Unlike specials that retell manga arcs, it is an original story, and it brings back the Foxy Pirates, the crew the Straw Hats defeated in the anime's Davy Back Fight arc, with new members. It was released on Blu-ray and DVD in March 2016.

Sailing in the New World, Monkey D. Luffy and the Straw Hat Pirates are challenged by Captain Foxy to a Davy Back Fight rematch. The contest is a trap devised by Kōmei, a brilliant strategist who has recently joined Foxy's crew. During an eating contest, Zoro and Sanji consume a strange mushroom that saps their strength and turns them into good-for-nothings, and the pair are captured and carried away. Chasing their friends, the Straw Hats reach Nebulandia, an island shrouded in a mist formed from sea water that, like seastone, neutralises the powers of Devil Fruit users. Their arrival is exactly what Kōmei planned.

Kōmei is in fact a vice admiral of the Navy and a special operations strategist who infiltrated the Foxy Pirates by deliberately losing to them. Having lost his home town to pirates as a child, he despises them and dreams of proving that ordinary people without powers can defeat Devil Fruit users through cunning, thereby changing the Navy itself. Luffy is forced into an uneasy alliance with his old Davy Back rival Foxy for the rescue. Using the island's terrain and a series of traps, especially the pitfalls he favours, Kōmei captures Robin, Franky and Usopp, but Brook and Chopper, searching for an antidote to the mushroom, foil his attempt to seize Luffy. In the final battle, Kōmei floods his base with sea water to weaken Luffy, but Foxy's Slow-Slow Beam and a pitfall turn the tables, and Luffy defeats him with a decisive blow.

The regular voice cast returns, led by Mayumi Tanaka as Luffy, Kazuya Nakai as Zoro and Hiroaki Hirata as Sanji, with Toshio Shimada as Foxy. Ichikawa Ennosuke voices Kōmei, a role he modelled on the Three Kingdoms strategist Zhuge Liang, while Hoka Kinoshita plays another new crew member who is secretly a Navy officer.

documents.title: The Love Witch
documents.tagline: She loved men... to death
documents.overview: A modern-day witch uses spells and magic to get men to fall in love with her, with deadly consequences.
documents.plot:
The Love Witch is a 2016 American campy horror comedy film written and directed by Anna Biller. The film is a loving homage to 1960s Technicolor films, particularly those of Roger Corman and Russ Meyer.

At its core, The Love Witch explores the theme of toxic masculinity and the objectification of women in society. The main character, Elaine, is a modern-day witch who uses magic to seduce men, only to ultimately destroy them with her charms. However, as the film progresses, it becomes clear that Elaine's actions are motivated by a deep-seated desire for validation and acceptance from men.

The film also critiques the societal norms of the 1960s, particularly those related to beauty standards and femininity. The characters in the film embody the idealized feminine roles of the time, with Elaine being the ultimate femme fatale. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that these roles are suffocating and limiting for women.

Furthermore, The Love Witch is a commentary on the commodification of sex and the ways in which women's bodies are objectified and exploited for male pleasure. Elaine's magic is a metaphor for the ways in which women are forced to use their bodies as objects of desire in order to survive.

Throughout the film, Biller uses vibrant colors, lush costumes, and over-the-top performances to create a sense of nostalgia and campiness. However, beneath its playful surface, The Love Witch is a biting critique of patriarchal society and the ways in which women are forced to navigate a world that is hostile to their desires and agency.

Ultimately, The Love Witch is a film about female empowerment and the importance of self-love and acceptance. Elaine's journey is one of self-discovery and growth, as she learns to reject the toxic norms of society and forge her own path.

documents.title: One Piece Film: GOLD
documents.original_title: ワンピース　フィルム GOLD
documents.tagline: It's a life-or-death gamble!
documents.overview: The glittering Gran Tesoro, a city of entertainment beyond the laws of the government, is a sanctuary for the world’s most infamous pirates, Marines, and filthy rich millionaires. Drawn by dreams of hitting the jackpot, Captain Luffy and his crew sail straight for the gold. But behind the gilded curtains lies a powerful king whose deep pockets and deeper ambitions spell disaster for the Straw Hats and the New World alike.
documents.plot:
One Piece Film: Gold is a Japanese animated adventure film based on the popular manga and anime series "One Piece" created by Eiichiro Oda. The film was produced by Toei Animation and directed by Kiyoshi Matsuda.

The story takes place after the events of the Dressrosa Arc in the One Piece manga and anime series. Monkey D. Luffy, the main protagonist, is on a quest to find the legendary treasure known as "One Piece" that will grant him the title of Pirate King. Luffy's crew, the Straw Hat Pirates, are also searching for the treasure.

The film begins with Luffy and his crew arriving in the city of Gold Town, where they meet a young boy named Trafalgar Law, who is on a mission to find the legendary "Gold" that will grant him immense power. Law is revealed to be the son of Shanks, one of the Seven Warlords of the Sea, and has inherited his father's powers.

As Luffy and his crew search for the treasure, they become entangled in a conflict between Law and the World Government, who seek to capture Law and use his powers for their own gain. The Straw Hats soon discover that the "Gold" is actually a powerful artifact known as the "Will of D." which has the power to grant immense strength and abilities.

Throughout the film, Luffy and his crew face numerous challenges and battles against the World Government's agents, including the ruthless Admiral Kizaru. Along the way, they also meet new allies, such as Trafalgar Law's sister, Boa Hancock, who becomes a valuable member of the Straw Hats.

As the story unfolds, it is revealed that the "Gold" is actually a powerful artifact created by the ancient civilization known as the "Poneglyphs." The Poneglyphs were said to hold the secrets of the world and the location of the One Piece treasure. However, the World Government seeks to use the "Will of D." for their own gain, leading to a climactic battle between Luffy and Law.

In the end, Luffy and his crew successfully defeat the World Government's agents and claim the "Gold," which is revealed to be a powerful artifact that holds the secrets of the world. The film concludes with Luffy and his crew setting sail once again, determined to find the One Piece treasure and become the Pirate King.

Overall, One Piece Film: Gold is an action-packed adventure film that explores themes of power, friendship, and the pursuit of one's dreams. With its stunning animation and engaging storyline, it is a must-see for fans of the One Piece series.

documents.title: Planetarium
documents.tagline: You never know what's about to change...
documents.overview: In 1930s France, two sisters who are thought to be able to communicate with ghosts meet a visionary producer while performing in Paris.
documents.plot:
In the late 1930s, two American sisters, Laura and Kate Barlow, travel to France where they perform séances at cabarets with Laura hosting the session and Kate channeling the spirits. A public performance of theirs is seen by French film producer Andre Korben. Impressed by their act, he books them for a private session and is moved by the spirit that visits him.
Feeling stifled by the lack of innovation in the French film industry, Korben convinces investors and his team to film a séance as it happens. Unfortunately for Korben, the reels look ridiculous. But the director is drawn to Laura, who, despite not being a spiritualist, has a face that photographs well. The film team conceives of a conventional script in which Laura plays a medium who channels the spirit of a widower's wife and the three become locked in a love triangle with the widower unsure if he is falling in love with his former wife or the medium.
Laura and Kate move in with Korben, who is generous and kind to them. However, he continues to hold private séances with Kate, much to Laura's displeasure. (She fears, rightly, that Korben's interest in the spirit world is sexual.) Eventually, Laura is forced to leave for the coast to continue filming. Korben takes Kate to a metaphysical scientist and films their sessions together.
On the coast, Laura realizes that the rise of anti-semitism means the tides are turning against Korben. Rumours that he once performed in porn abound; and someone writes that she is a Jew's whore on her mirror. When Korben and Kate arrive to reunite with Laura, Korben shows his producers and investors the film of him and Kate which shows nothing. The director walks off the film and blames the money Korben has wasted chasing ghosts as an excuse. Meanwhile, Kate falls ill and reveals that she hasn't been faking but really can see ghosts. She believes this is because she is dying. Kate has leukemia, which is a death sentence at the time.
Korben is jailed for his wasted investments and the trial strips him of his French citizenship.
Years later, Kate is dead; and Korben has been sent to a death camp in "the East". Laura runs into Eva, an actress she once knew, who helps her get a part in a film working with her former director. No longer involved with spiritualism or Korben, Laura's film career in Nazi era France is assured.

documents.title: I, Daniel Blake
documents.tagline: My name is Daniel Blake. I am a man, not a dog.
documents.overview: A middle aged carpenter, who requires state welfare after injuring himself, is joined by a single mother in a similar scenario.
documents.plot:
Daniel Blake, a widowed 59-year-old joiner from Newcastle, has had a heart attack. Though his doctor has not allowed him to return to work, he is deemed fit to do so after a Work Capability Assessment and is denied Employment and Support Allowance. Daniel is frustrated to learn that his doctor was not contacted about this decision and thus applies for an appeal, a process Daniel finds difficult because he must complete forms online and is not computer literate.
Daniel befriends Katie Morgan, a single mother, after she is sanctioned for arriving late to her Jobcentre appointment. Katie and her children have just moved to Newcastle from a homeless shelter in London, as there is no affordable accommodation. Daniel helps the family by repairing objects, teaching them how to heat rooms without electricity, and crafting wooden toys for the children.
During a food bank visit, Katie breaks down crying, having become overwhelmed by hunger due to feeding her children instead of herself. After she is caught shoplifting at a supermarket, a security guard secretly offers Katie work as a prostitute. Daniel surprises her at the brothel where she goes to work and begs her to give up the job, but Katie tearfully insists she has no other way to feed her children.
As a condition for receiving Jobseeker's Allowance, Daniel must keep looking for work. He refuses a job at a garden centre because his doctor will not allow him to work yet. When his work coach tells him he must work harder to find a job or be sanctioned, Daniel spray paints "I, Daniel Blake, demand my appeal date before I starve" on the side of the building. Daniel earns the support of bystanders, including other people claiming benefits, but is arrested and cautioned by the police.
Daniel sells most of his belongings and becomes a recluse but is pulled out of his depression by Katie's daughter, Daisy, who brings him a homemade meal to repay Daniel for his kindness. On the day of Daniel's appeal, Katie accompanies him to the tribunal, where a welfare adviser tells Daniel that his case looks promising. Upon seeing the judge and doctor who will decide his fate, Daniel becomes anxious and excuses himself to use the toilet, where he suffers another heart attack and dies.
Later, Katie reads a eulogy at his public health funeral, including a speech he had intended to read at his appeal. The speech describes his feelings about how the welfare system failed him, and states, "I am not a blip on a computer screen or a national insurance number, I am a man."

documents.title: Toni Erdmann
documents.tagline: Life is just passing by...
documents.overview: Without warning a father comes to visit his daughter abroad. He believes that she lost her humor and therefore surprises her with a rampage of jokes.
documents.plot:
Winfried Conradi is a divorced music teacher from Aachen with a passion for bizarre pranks involving several fake personas. Following the death of his beloved dog, he decides to reconnect with his daughter, Ines, who is pursuing a career in business consulting. Ines is working in Bucharest, Romania, on an outsourcing project in the oil industry. Consumed by her work, she seems to have little time for her family.
Winfried spontaneously travels to Bucharest and waits for Ines in the lobby of an office complex. After several hours, she finally appears, accompanied by several of her client's board members and on the way to a meeting. Winfried puts on sunglasses and fake teeth as a playful disguise, and approaches the group from the side while hiding behind a newspaper. Ines ignores him, but meets with him briefly after work and invites him to a business reception at the US Embassy.
In the evening, Winfried and Ines attend the reception, where they meet Henneberg, a German oil company CEO with whom Ines wishes to secure a consulting contract. Ines tries to gain Henneberg's attention, but Henneberg seems more interested in her father. Winfried tells Henneberg that he has hired a replacement daughter because Ines is always busy. To Ines's surprise, Henneberg invites Winfried and Ines for drinks, along with his entourage. At the bar, Henneberg once again brushes Ines aside and makes fun of Winfried.
After several days, Ines and Winfried are struggling to get along. Stressed out from work, Ines oversleeps, missing a planned rendezvous with clients, and blames her father for not waking her up. Feeling alienated and unwanted, he leaves in a taxi for the airport. Ines continues with her work as normal, and several days later arranges to meet two female friends at a bar. While Ines and her friends are chatting, a man approaches and introduces himself as "Toni Erdmann". The man is clearly Winfried in a wig and false teeth, but Ines does not let on. Her two friends politely engage "Erdmann" in conversation; he explains that he is a "life coach" and consultant visiting Bucharest to attend the funeral of his friend's turtle.
Ines is increasingly frustrated and unfulfilled in her work and personal life, but continues to encounter "Erdmann" sporadically at parties or outside her office. At first Ines is angry with her father, and accuses him of trying to "ruin" her, but as time goes on she comes to see the value of her father's interventions in her life, and plays along with the ruse. "Erdmann" accompanies her on a night out with her work friends, and eventually even accompanies her to a business meeting. In turn, "Erdmann" takes Ines to a Romanian family's Easter party, where he forces her into a reluctant performance of Whitney Houston's "Greatest Love of All". After singing, Ines promptly rushes off.
Back at her flat, Ines is preparing to host a business team-building brunch to celebrate her birthday.

documents.title: After the Storm
documents.overview: Ryota is an unpopular writer although he won a literary award 15 years ago. Now, Ryota works as a private detective. He is divorced from his ex-wife Kyoko and he has an 11-year-old son Shingo. His mother Yoshiko lives alone at her apartment. One day, Ryota, his ex-wife Kyoko, and son Shingo gather at Yoshiko's apartment. A typhoon passes and the family must stay there all night long.
documents.plot:
After the Storm (Japanese: 海よりもまだ深く, Umi yori mo Mada Fukaku, "Even Deeper than the Sea") is a 2016 Japanese family drama film written, directed and edited by Hirokazu Kore-eda. Hiroshi Abe stars as a failed novelist, with Kirin Kiki as his mother, Yoko Maki as his former wife and Taiyo Yoshizawa as his son. It premiered in the Un Certain Regard section of the 2016 Cannes Film Festival and was released in Japan on May 21, 2016.

Ryota once won a minor literary prize for his only novel, and still clings to the idea that he is a serious writer. In reality, he works at a small private detective agency, where he sometimes supplements his income by blackmailing the people he is hired to investigate, and squanders his money on gambling, leaving him unable to pay child support. He turns down an offer to write for a manga series, considering it beneath him, while telling people he is researching his next book.

Since the recent death of Ryota's father, a gambler like his son, his widowed mother, Yoshiko, lives alone and seems to be moving on, taking up hobbies with other elderly women. Ryota visits her frequently. His sister, Chinatsu, suspects his motives, and he in turn suspects that she is sponging off their mother. When Ryota goes to an old hiding place where his mother used to conceal money from his father, he finds only cardboard and a teasing note from his sister.

Meanwhile, Ryota's former wife, Kyoko, has lost patience with his excuses, and threatens to stop his monthly visits with their young son, Shingo, unless he pays what he owes. Ryota, jealous of Kyoko's new boyfriend, fears that her remarriage would cost him his relationship with his son. During one of his visits with Shingo, a typhoon strikes, and Ryota, Kyoko and the boy are forced to spend the night at his mother's apartment. As the storm rages, Kyoko tells Ryota that their marriage is truly over, explaining that adults cannot live on love alone and that he never acted like a family man when it mattered. Accepting this, Ryota takes Shingo out into the storm to shelter in a playground structure, as he once did with his own father, and the two share a rare moment of connection. In the morning, the storm has passed, and they go their separate ways.

After the Storm received critical acclaim, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 96% approval and a consensus praising its timeless observations on parental responsibility, personal bonds and forgiveness.

documents.title: Dunkirk
documents.tagline: Survival is Victory
documents.overview: The story of the miraculous evacuation of Allied soldiers from Belgium, Britain, Canada and France, who were cut off and surrounded by the German army from the beaches and harbour of Dunkirk between May 26th and June 4th 1940 during World War II.
documents.plot:
Dunkirk is a 2017 war drama film directed by Christopher Nolan, produced by Warner Bros. Pictures, and distributed by Warner Bros. The film is set during World War II and tells the story of the Dunkirk evacuation, also known as the Miracle of Dunkirk.

The film begins on May 26, 1940, with a dramatic sequence showing the German army's invasion of France. The British Expeditionary Force (BEF), led by General Lord Gort, is trapped in Dunkirk, a coastal town in northern France. As the Germans close in, the BEF is surrounded and outnumbered.

The story then shifts to three main plot threads: the evacuation of Allied soldiers from Dunkirk, the rescue efforts by the Royal Air Force (RAF), and the experiences of a young British soldier named Tommy (Fionn Whitehead). The film's narrative is presented in a non-linear fashion, with each thread intersecting and overlapping at various points.

The evacuation of Allied soldiers from Dunkirk is depicted as a chaotic and desperate effort. Thousands of soldiers are stranded on the beaches of Dunkirk, with no clear way to escape. The British Navy, led by Admiral Bertram Ramsay (Kenneth Branagh), launches a massive rescue operation, with ships and boats converging on the beach to evacuate the soldiers.

Meanwhile, the RAF is engaged in a fierce dogfight with German aircraft, trying to protect the evacuation fleet from enemy attack. The film's aerial sequences are intense and suspenseful, showcasing the bravery and skill of the RAF pilots.

Tommy, who has been separated from his family during the evacuation, finds himself on the beach, struggling to survive amidst the chaos. He joins a group of other soldiers, including Mr. Dawson (Mark Rylance), a civilian who is helping to evacuate the soldiers. As they try to escape, Tommy and Mr. Dawson face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, enemy fire, and personal losses.

As the evacuation continues, the film's narrative builds towards a dramatic climax. The British Navy launches a final push to clear the beach of German forces, while the RAF provides cover with its aircraft. The soldiers are finally able to escape, but not before many have lost their lives or been separated from their loved ones.

The film ends with Tommy, who has survived the evacuation, watching as the last of the ships depart from Dunkirk. He is reunited with his family, who had been searching for him throughout the ordeal. The final shot is of a small boat, which is revealed to be carrying Mr. Dawson's body, symbolizing the sacrifice and bravery of those who helped evacuate the soldiers.

Throughout the film, Nolan uses innovative cinematography and editing techniques to create a sense of tension and urgency. The film's score, composed by Hans Zimmer, adds to the emotional impact of the story. Overall, Dunkirk is a powerful and moving tribute to the bravery and sacrifice of those who fought in World War II.

documents.title: Detective Conan: The Darkest Nightmare
documents.original_title: 名探偵コナン 純黒の悪夢（ナイトメア）
documents.tagline: Can you forget your past... no matter how dark it is?
documents.overview: On a dark night, the Japanese police is raided by a spy. Different countries' intelligence agencies - such as England's MI6, Germany's BDN, and America's CIA - as well as the FBI's secret files are going to be taken, but public safety officers lead by Tooru Amuro arrive just in time. The spy steals a car and escapes. The spy and Amuro are then locked in a dead heat on the highway, and just as it is about to cause an accident with multiple cars, the spy's car is hit by FBI agent Shuichi Akai's rifle bullet and falls of the roadway. The next day, Conan and his friends go to a newly-remodeled aquarium in Tokyo. Under the main attraction, a Ferris wheel, Conan finds an attractive woman alone and injured. Her left and right eyes are different colors.
documents.plot:
A Black Organization spy, codenamed Curaçao, infiltrates the NPA Security Bureau Office, stealing the NOC list of MI6, BND, CSIS, FBI and CIA agents working undercover in the Black Organization. Yuya Kazami, an officer of the Public Security Bureau, catches her red handed and Curaçao is forced to run away. Rei Furuya, also known as Bourbon, attempts to stop her from escaping and later engages in a car chase on the Rainbow Bridge, with Akai Shuichi joining later. The car chase ends up causing a havoc, and Akai decides to shoot the tire of Curaçao's vehicle, causing the car to crash and fall off the bridge. Curaçao escapes from the car as it is falling and lands in the water. She later surfaces at Tohto Aquarium near the crash site.
The next day, the Detective Boys discover Curaçao at Tohto Aquarium. She is suffering from amnesia and her phone is broken as a result of the car crash the day prior. Conan retrieves the broken phone and takes photos of Curaçao, sends the photos to Ran, who, in turn, sends them to the Tokyo Metropolitan Police, then hands the phone to Dr. Agasa so he can recover the data on it. The Detective Boys then decide to stay with Curaçao to help her regain her memory. After noticing Curaçao's perfect aiming skills while playing darts and her swift act of saving Genta from falling from high a place, Haibara and Conan notice that Curaçao is not an ordinary woman, and Haibara herself gets a sense that Curaçao is likely to be another Black Organization agent. Meanwhile, Dr. Agasa attempts to recover the message from Curaçao's broken cell phone, and finds out that Curaçao attempted to send the names of known NOC agents (Stout, Aquavit, Riesling, Bourbon/Rei, and Kir/Hidemi Hondo) to the organization. Stout, Aquavit, Riesling are later killed by members of the Black Organization in London, Toronto and Berlin respectively, and Rei and Hidemi are held hostage in Tokyo. Curaçao also screams out the names of those NOC agent in front of the Detective Boys when the ferris wheel they were riding in reaches the top and the various colors she sees triggers a reaction.
The Tokyo Metropolitan Police later come and take Curaçao into custody, transferring her to the Police Hospital, but they are forced to surrender her to the PSB as the Bureau believes Curaçao was the spy infiltrating the Bureau Office the day before. The Bureau becomes aware that Curaçao appears to react to certain events in the Tohto Aquarium, and decides to take her back to the Aquarium. The same night, the Black Organization, who arrived by the Bell Boeing V-22 Osprey, knocks out the electricity for the entire aquarium and plan to intercept Curaçao when the Ferris wheel reaches the top. After Curaçao regains her memory by looking at the specific color patterns of the projected lights like she did earlier before, Yuya Kazami, who boarded the Ferris wheel with her, is knocked unconscious by her and she escapes.

documents.title: Under the Shadow
documents.tagline: Fear will find you.
documents.overview: After Shideh's building is hit by a missile during the Iran-Iraq War, a superstitious neighbor suggests that the missile was cursed and might be carrying malevolent Middle-Eastern spirits. She becomes convinced a supernatural force within the building is attempting to possess her daughter Dorsa, and she has no choice but to confront these forces if she is to save her daughter and herself.
documents.plot: After Shideh's building is hit by a missile during the Iran-Iraq War, a superstitious neighbor suggests that the missile was cursed and might be carrying malevolent Middle-Eastern spirits. She becomes convinced a supernatural force within the building is attempting to possess her daughter Dorsa, and she has no choice but to confront these forces if she is to save her daughter and herself.

documents.title: Duck Duck Goose
documents.tagline: Family can be a wild ride
documents.overview: After he’s grounded by an injury, a high-flying bachelor is saddled with two wide-eyed orphans as they come face-to-face with the dangers and beauty of the outside world.
documents.plot:
Duck Duck Goose (Chinese: 妈妈咪鸭) is a 2018 animated adventure comedy film directed by Chris Jenkins, who wrote the original story and co-wrote the screenplay with Rob Muir, Scott Atkinson and Tegan West. An international co-production between the United States, China and the United Kingdom, it features the voices of Jim Gaffigan as Peng, a self-absorbed swan goose, Zendaya and Lance Lim as the Mandarin duckling siblings Chi and Chao, Greg Proops as the villainous Pallas's cat Banzou, Reggie Watts as the flying squirrel Carl, and Carl Reiner as Larry, a softshell turtle, with Natasha Leggero, Stephen Fry, Craig Ferguson and Diedrich Bader.

Peng is a carefree goose whose reckless attitude irritates Bing, the leader of his flock, which departs on its migration across China while he sleeps. One of his careless stunts separates two ducklings, Chi and Chao, from their own flock as it travels to a fabled place called Pleasant Valley. Seeing Peng drive off the predatory Banzou, the ducklings shelter beside him for the night. Startled to find them, Peng flies off carelessly, crashes into a gong and breaks his wing. Unable to fly and afraid of predators, he decides to use the ducklings as cover while he makes his way back to his flock, and they reluctantly join him.

Through a string of misadventures Peng grows fond of the ducklings, but when they encounter his flock, Chi and Chao discover his selfish motives and the two parties go their separate ways. Peng is knocked out of the sky by Carl, who fits him with a makeshift wing, and he sets off to find the ducklings. They meanwhile reunite with their flock and learn that Pleasant Valley is really a restaurant that cooks ducklings. Peng rescues them, but they are separated again in the escape, and Banzou takes the ducklings hostage. Peng is badly hurt fighting him, and Chi and Chao finish off the cat by launching him into the sky on a rocket. Carrying the weakened Peng through a snowstorm toward the geese's spring, the ducklings use a honk he taught them to summon Jingjing, Peng's love interest, who rescues him. Bing welcomes the ducklings into the flock, along with a newly responsible Peng.

The film opened in China on March 9, 2018. A North American theatrical release planned by Open Road Films for April 2018 was canceled when the company closed, and Netflix released it in North America on July 20, 2018. It grossed about $15.3 million worldwide in its initial run and received negative reviews from critics.

documents.title: The Favourite
documents.tagline: A bawdy, brilliant triumph.
documents.overview: England, early 18th century. The close relationship between Queen Anne and Sarah Churchill is threatened by the arrival of Sarah's cousin, Abigail Hill, resulting in a bitter rivalry between the two cousins to be the Queen's favourite.
documents.plot:
The Favourite is a 2018 period drama film directed by Yorgos Lanthimos, starring Olivia Colman, Emma Stone, and Rachel Weisz. The movie takes place in the early 18th century, during the reign of Queen Anne (Olivia Colman), who rules England with an iron fist.

The story begins with Queen Anne's close relationship with her adviser, Sarah Churchill (Rachel Weisz). However, as time passes, a new servant named Abigail Hill (Emma Stone) arrives at court. Abigail is a clever and ambitious young woman from a lower social class, determined to rise through the ranks of society.

Abigail quickly catches the eye of the Queen, who becomes infatuated with her charming personality and wit. As Abigail's influence grows, she begins to manipulate the Queen into making decisions that benefit herself and her family. Meanwhile, Sarah Churchill's power and influence begin to wane as a result of Abigail's rise.

As tensions between the three women escalate, the palace becomes a battleground for power and loyalty. The Queen is torn between her affection for Abigail and her duty to her adviser, Sarah. Abigail, on the other hand, uses her charm and cunning to turn the Queen against Sarah, ultimately leading to her downfall.

Throughout the film, Lanthimos employs his signature deadpan humor and absurdity, often using long takes and unsettling silences to create a sense of unease. The performances by Colman, Stone, and Weisz are outstanding, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

One of the most striking aspects of The Favourite is its exploration of themes such as power, ambition, and female relationships. The film raises questions about the nature of femininity and how women are perceived in society, particularly during this time period.

Ultimately, Abigail's machinations lead to a tragic confrontation between the three women. In the end, only one woman emerges victorious, but at what cost? The Favourite is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that offers a fresh perspective on a pivotal moment in history.

The film received widespread critical acclaim, with many praising its performances, direction, and screenplay. It won numerous awards, including several Academy Awards, and cemented the status of Yorgos Lanthimos as one of the most innovative filmmakers working today.

documents.title: The Salesman
documents.overview: Forced out of their apartment due to dangerous works on a neighboring building, Emad and Rana move into a new flat in the center of Tehran. An incident linked to the previous tenant will dramatically change the young couple’s life.
documents.plot:
Emad and Rana are a married couple who both work in the theatre, currently starring in a production of Death of a Salesman by Arthur Miller, with Emad portraying Willy Loman and Rana playing Linda. Emad is also a popular instructor at a local school, where the youth joke about him being a "salesman." One night, their apartment begins to collapse and they flee the building with the other residents. Knowing they need another place to live, their fellow actor Babak secures another apartment for them, where a woman has recently moved out, although she left in a hurry abandoning numerous belongings. The couple moves into the apartment and places the previous owner's belongings outside. One night, Rana is home alone and begins bathing. When Emad returns, he finds she is missing and the bathroom is covered with blood. He rushes to the hospital, where he is informed by his neighbours about his wife's condition and is told to change the apartment's locks. It becomes apparent that Rana has not had an accident, but has been assaulted by an intruder, to whom she opened the door using the intercom, thinking it was Emad returning home. Emad also learns from neighbours that the previous tenant was a prostitute who had conflicts with her clients.

Rana returns home, but suffers from trauma and is reluctant to go to the police. She does not bathe, fearing to go into the bathroom again, and in the middle of a performance, breaks down in tears and leaves the stage. Although she does not remember the face of her attacker, Emad finds the culprit left his car keys, which he matches to a pick-up parked outside. The attacker also left behind a mobile phone and some money which Rana purchased groceries with, thinking Emad had left it for her. Emad increasingly blames Babak for hiding the truth about the former tenant. After he hears a loving message from Babak on the previous tenant's answering machine, he calls Babak's character Charley a degenerate in the midst of a performance, although this is not in Miller's script.
Finally, Emad turns to one of his students, whose father used to work for the police. He is able to trace the truck to a man named Majid. He pretends to need a mover to lure Majid to their now empty old apartment, but Majid's prospective father-in-law arrives instead. Gradually, it becomes apparent the older man was himself the intruder, though he denies attacking Rana, implying he simply startled her. Emad calls the old man's family to the apartment, and locks him in a small room to wait, intending to reveal his true character to them all. When he opens the room the old man appears to be having heart trouble and Emad calls Rana in a panic. When Rana learns what Emad intends, she says it will be over between them if he pursues his revenge.
When the family arrives they believe they have been called to a medical emergency, thanking Emad for saving his life.

documents.title: Don't Hang Up
documents.tagline: Be Careful Who You Prank
documents.overview: An evening of drunken prank calls becomes a nightmare for a pair of teenagers when a mysterious stranger turns their own game against them.
documents.plot: An evening of drunken prank calls becomes a nightmare for a pair of teenagers when a mysterious stranger turns their own game against them.

documents.title: The Girl with All the Gifts
documents.original_title: The Girl with All the Gifts
documents.tagline: Our greatest threat is our only hope.
documents.overview: In the future, a strange fungus has changed nearly everyone into a thoughtless, flesh-eating monster. When a scientist and a teacher find a girl who seems to be immune to the fungus, they all begin a journey to save humanity.
documents.plot:
In the near future, humanity has been ravaged by a disease caused by a parasitic fungus transmitted by bodily fluids. Over the prior decade, most of humanity that was infected turned into fast mindless zombies called "hungries". The only remaining hope is a cure that could be obtained from research on a small group of carrier, but apparently normal, children.
The children are imprisoned by a group of soldiers (led by Sergeant Eddie Parks), and go to school at an army base in the Home Counties, where they are experimented on by Dr. Caroline Caldwell. Helen Justineau is responsible for educating and studying the children. Among them is an exceptional girl named Melanie, whom Justineau grows particularly close to, thus forming a special bond.
When Melanie is about to be dissected, the base is overrun by hungries and the operating lab is breached. Melanie escapes and wanders outside, where soldiers are being violently attacked. Melanie and Justineau board an escaping truck with an injured Caldwell, Sergeant Parks, and two surviving soldiers, Gallagher and Dillon. Melanie is restrained and muzzled to prevent her from biting the others. Dillon is killed when hungries attack as the group stops for water, and the truck is disabled when a fuel line is broken.
The group reaches London by foot and makes their way through a swarm of dormant hungries using a "blocker" gel that masks their scent, rendering them largely invisible. They take shelter in an abandoned hospital for the night. Caldwell reveals to Melanie that second-generation hungries, or neonates, were discovered after babies killed their infected mothers by eating organs to get out of the womb, and while they crave living flesh, they still think and learn, as the fungus has a symbiotic relationship with those born infected.
In the morning, the group realises they have been surrounded by hungries. Melanie, as a second-generation hungry, is ignored by them and therefore goes to explore abandoned houses, eating a stray cat during her time out. She helps the group by leading the hungries away with a stray dog so the group can escape.
As they progress through London, they come across piles of infected bodies encircling the BT Tower, which has been overgrown by a massive fungal growth. Caldwell explains that the growth contains pods which, upon maturity, could release airborne spores that would end humankind. They take shelter in an abandoned mobile laboratory that was sent into the city earlier by the military authorities.
Caldwell, injured and dying of sepsis, reasons that she can save the human race by sacrificing Melanie to complete her vaccine research in the lab. As the group runs out of food, Gallagher ventures into the city on a supply run, but is killed by a tribe of feral hungry children who have learned to trick uninfected people with a trail of food cans. When Parks and Justineau are surrounded by the feral children, Melanie fights and handcuffs the leader and kills him with a bat.

documents.title: Robin Hood
documents.tagline: The legend you know. The story you don't.
documents.overview: A war-hardened Crusader and his Moorish commander mount an audacious revolt against the corrupt English crown.
documents.plot:
Robin Hood is a 2018 American action-adventure film directed by Otto Bathurst and written by Ben Chandler and David James Kelly from Chandler's story, a modern retelling of the outlaw legend that centers on Robin's training by John. First announced in February 2015 with a Joby Harold script and Leonardo DiCaprio's Appian Way producing, the project was acquired by Lionsgate and cast Taron Egerton as Robin later that year. Eve Hewson, Jamie Foxx and Ben Mendelsohn followed, and filming ran from February to May 2017. The film was released by Lionsgate's Summit Entertainment on November 21, 2018.

Robin of Loxley, an aristocrat and skilled longbowman, lives in Nottingham with Marian until the corrupt Sheriff drafts him into the Third Crusade. Four years later, after he fails to stop his commander, Guy of Gisbourne, from executing unarmed prisoners, including a teenage boy, he is sent home accused of treason. He returns to learn from Friar Tuck that the Sheriff declared him dead and seized his estate to fund the war at the urging of Cardinal Franklin, while the townspeople have been driven into a mining settlement. Marian is now with Will Tillman, a would-be leader of the commoners. The father of the boy Robin tried to save, Yahya, who says his name translates as John, proposes that they end the war by stealing back the people's money.

After hard training in his ruined manor, Robin robs the Sheriff's coffers as a hooded thief nicknamed the Hood while posing as a frivolous lord loyal to the regime. He and Marian, who recognizes him by his voice, discover that the Church is secretly funding the Saracen army in order to topple the king and seize power. John is captured and tortured but reveals nothing. Robin reveals himself to the commoners, who embrace him, and seizes a caravan carrying the Sheriff's fortune to the Saracens while Will stages a riot. After Will, scarred during the fighting, sees Marian kiss Robin, he turns against them. Robin surrenders to end the bloodshed, but John, disguised as a guard, kills the Sheriff, and the rebels retreat as outlaws to Sherwood Forest. The Cardinal then installs a vengeful Will as sheriff, and Robin dares him to come after them.

Egerton stars with Foxx as John, Mendelsohn as the Sheriff, Hewson as Marian, Tim Minchin as Tuck and Jamie Dornan as Will. Critics panned it, with 14% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and comparisons to King Arthur: Legend of the Sword. It grossed about $85 million against a $100 million budget.

documents.title: Then Came You
documents.tagline: Living in the moment is hard to do alone.
documents.overview: An American hypochondriac who is working as a baggage handler is forced to confront his fears when a British teenager with a terminal illness enlists him to help her carry out her eccentric bucket list.
documents.plot:
Then Came You, also known as Departures, is an American romantic comedy-drama of 2018 directed by Peter Hutchings and written by Fergal Rock. Asa Butterfield plays Calvin Lewis, a young hypochondriac, and Maisie Williams plays Skye Aitken, a teenager with terminal cancer, with Nina Dobrev as the flight attendant Izzy, Tyler Hoechlin as Calvin's brother Frank, David Koechner as their father and Margot Bingham as Frank's wife Lucy.

Skye has been told that her cancer is in its final stages and that she has little time left. Calvin, an airport baggage handler, has a crush on Izzy and lives in constant fear of dying. His doctor sends him to a cancer support group for perspective. There he meets Skye, who takes an instant interest in him, and although he tries to explain that he does not actually have cancer, the two become friends and he agrees to help her complete her list of things to do before she dies. At first irritated by her bluntness and unpredictability, Calvin comes to treasure her company, and as they spend more time together his fear of death begins to fade.

Skye arranges a date between Calvin and Izzy, telling Izzy that he has cancer too, and the pair start dating. Skye admits she always knew Calvin was healthy, but he hesitates to tell Izzy, fearing she only likes him for his illness. From Lucy, Skye learns that Calvin's mother withdrew from life after his twin sister was killed at the age of eight in a car crash while their mother was driving. When Calvin finally confesses the truth, Izzy, hurt by the lie, breaks up with him, and he sinks into depression until his father persuades him to return to work. Skye, meanwhile, loses her virginity to Will, a boy she has a crush on, and finds the experience a letdown.

When Skye collapses and is taken to the hospital, Lucy goes into labor at the same time, and Frank and Lucy ask Calvin and Skye to be their baby's godparents. Calvin panics, but Frank reminds him that Skye still needs him. With help from Izzy and Skye's parents, he helps her finish her list, and he tells her that he stopped celebrating his birthday for his mother's sake after his sister's death. After Skye dies, birthday cards from her arrive in the mail to make up for the ones he missed. Overcoming his fear of heights, Calvin takes a flight, exchanging hopeful glances with Izzy.

 The film premiered at the Woodstock Film Festival in October 2018 and was released by Shout! Factory on 1 February 2019, to mixed reviews.

documents.title: No Manches Frida
documents.tagline: The students are bad, the teachers are worse.
documents.overview: After his release from prison, bank robber Zequi sets off to recover the stolen money that was buried by his dizzy accomplice. He's horrified to learn that a high school gymnasium is now standing over the site where the loot is stashed. Needing to infiltrate the building, Zequi lands a job as a substitute teacher for a group of wild and unruly students. As the ex-con tries to lay down the law, he starts to realize that life in jail may have been easier than trying to deal with rebellious teens.
documents.plot:
No Manches Frida is a 2016 Spanish comedy film directed by Pablo Lombardo and written by Pablo Lombardo and Javier Gullón. The movie stars Karra Elejalde, Blanca Suárez, and Luis Zahera.

The story revolves around Carlos (played by Karra Elejalde), a former professional soccer player who has lost his passion for the game after a serious injury. He is now working as a coach at a local soccer school in Madrid, where he tries to teach young players the basics of the sport. However, his unorthodox coaching methods and lack of patience with his students make him unpopular among both the kids and their parents.

One day, Carlos receives an offer from a wealthy businessman named Juan (played by Luis Zahera) to coach his daughter, Frida (played by Blanca Suárez), in a series of high-stakes soccer matches. The catch is that Frida has never played soccer before, but she's determined to become the best player in Spain.

As Carlos begins working with Frida, he realizes that she's not just any ordinary student - she's a talented and feisty young woman who refuses to be told what to do. Despite their initial disagreements, Carlos starts to see potential in Frida and decides to help her develop her skills.

Throughout the movie, Carlos and Frida face numerous challenges as they prepare for the big matches. They encounter rival coaches, tough opponents, and even some personal struggles that threaten to derail their partnership. However, with each passing match, Carlos and Frida grow closer, both on and off the field.

As the stakes get higher, Carlos starts to realize that his feelings for Frida go beyond mere coaching. He begins to develop romantic feelings for her, but he's hesitant to express them, fearing it might compromise their professional relationship.

In the end, Carlos and Frida face off against their toughest opponents yet - a team of ruthless and experienced players who will stop at nothing to win. With Carlos' unorthodox tactics and Frida's determination, they manage to pull off an incredible comeback victory.

As the dust settles, Carlos finally confesses his feelings to Frida, and she reveals that she feels the same way. The movie ends with a heartwarming moment of tenderness between the two leads, as they share a kiss on the field.

Overall, No Manches Frida is a fun and entertaining film that explores themes of love, friendship, and perseverance. With its lighthearted tone and engaging storyline, it's a great choice for anyone looking for a feel-good movie experience.

documents.title: Bad Sister
documents.tagline: How long has it been since your last confession?
documents.overview: As a top student at St. Adeline's Catholic Boarding School, Zoe senses that something is not quite right about the school's new nun-- a sense proven to be true when it is revealed the "good' nun is an imposter with a fatal attraction to Zoe's brother.
documents.plot:
Bad Sister is a 2015 American-Canadian thriller television film written and directed by Doug Campbell for Lifetime, produced with Johnson Production Group and Golden Oak Entertainment. It stars Alyshia Ochse as a woman posing as a nun, with Devon Werkheiser, Ryan Whitney Newman, Helen Eigenberg, Robert Leeshock, Lise Simms, Sloane Avery and James Handy. Although dated 2015, it premiered on Lifetime on 3 January 2016.

Jason Brady (Werkheiser), a teenager who posts videos of his songs online, is sent by his parents to a Catholic boarding school after wrecking his father's car; they disapprove of his musical ambitions. His studious sister Zoe (Newman) attends the same school. The new teacher, Sister Sophia (Ochse), is welcomed by the headmistress, Sister Rebecca (Eigenberg), but Zoe soon notices that she skips the morning prayer and knows little about the faith. In truth she is Laura, a disturbed woman who became obsessed with Jason through his videos, murdered the real Sister Sophia and took her identity. Under her habit she wears lingerie and makeup; she moves Jason's girlfriend Sara (Avery) away from him in class, threatens her, and lets the boy glimpse her undressing. She plants a joint that gets Sara suspended and hides whiskey in Jason's room so that he must stay at school over a weekend, seduces him and secretly films them together, then frames Zoe for cheating when the girl grows suspicious. After Sara returns, Laura kills her in the shower and stages it as an accident. At a family dinner, Zoe catches the "nun" in lie after lie, and Jason confesses the affair and the sex tape she is using against him. The siblings search her computer, discover her real name and seek out Sister Rebecca, only to find her knocked unconscious. Laura confronts them in the chapel, but Sister Rebecca intervenes and Jason stabs the impostor with a screwdriver.

Reviewers who cover Lifetime films responded warmly to its excesses. Lisa Marie Bowman of Through the Shattered Lens called it an over-the-top masterpiece of the network's style, praising Campbell for playing up the sordid melodrama without taking it too seriously and singling out Ochse's switches between the cheerful nun and the irritated Laura. Lifetime Uncorked gave it a rating of three knives, though it found the casting of a genuinely teenage-looking actor as Jason somewhat creepy.

documents.title: The Discovery
documents.overview: In the near future, due to a breakthrough scientific discovery by Dr. Thomas Harbor, there is now definitive proof of an afterlife. While countless people have chosen suicide to reset their existence, others try to decide what it all means. Among them is Dr. Harbor's son Will, who has arrived at his father's isolated compound with a mysterious young woman named Isla. There, they discover the strange acolytes who help Dr. Harbor with his experiments.

documents.title: Miss Sloane
documents.tagline: Make sure you surprise them.
documents.overview: An ambitious lobbyist faces off against the powerful gun lobby in an attempt to pass gun control legislation.
documents.plot:
Elizabeth Sloane is a workaholic cutthroat lobbyist who has been called before a congressional hearing led by Senator Ronald Sperling to answer questions about possible violations of Senate ethics rules during her tenure at Washington D.C. lobbying firm Cole Kravitz & Waterman.
Three months and one week earlier, Sloane's firm is approached by gun manufacturing representative Bill Sanford to lead the opposition to the proposed Heaton-Harris bill that would expand background checks on gun purchases, specifically by targeting female voters. Sloane ridicules Sanford's idea and is later approached by Rodolfo Schmidt, the head of rival lobbying firm Peterson Wyatt, to instead lead the effort in support of the bill. Sloane agrees and takes most of her staff along with her, though her closest associate Jane Molloy refuses to leave.
At Peterson Wyatt, Sloane selects Esme Manucharian to conduct the majority of the firm's media appearances, and they begin to make significant progress in garnering votes for the bill. Sloane confronts Esme with knowledge of her background as having survived a school shooting. Even though Esme does not want to disclose the information, Sloane reveals Esme's secret during a live television debate. Later, Esme is held up at gunpoint while leaving her office, but her attacker is shot dead by another civilian who is legally carrying a gun. Gun rights supporters capitalize on this event, which causes the Heaton-Harris bill to lose support in the Senate. This is compounded by the news of the Senate inquiry into Sloane's lobbying practices.
Returning to the congressional hearing, Senator Sperling produces a form requesting approval of overseas travel for a Senator. It was filed by a non-profit organization but completed in Sloane's handwriting, indicating she violated Senate ethics rules with her involvement, as a lobbyist, in arranging the travel. In answer to other questions, Sloane swears under oath that she has never practiced illegal wiretapping.
In her final statement at the hearing, Sloane admits she anticipated the opposition might attack her personally if Peterson Wyatt made too much progress with the Heaton-Harris bill. She reveals that she had someone (Molloy, her former assistant) secretly working for her, and that she did use a wiretap – which recorded Senator Sperling accepting bribes from her former boss George Dupont.
Ten months later, Sloane is visited by her lawyer in prison. The bill passed, Dupont and Sperling are under investigation, and he has petitioned for her early release. He asks if it was worth career suicide, she answers: better than suicide by career.

documents.tagline: Silence can be killer
documents.overview: A deaf woman is stalked by a psychotic killer in her secluded home.
documents.plot: A deaf woman is stalked by a psychotic killer in her secluded home.

documents.title: Amateur Night
documents.tagline: Every job has pros and cons
documents.overview: Guy Carter, an insecure expectant father unable to find work in his field, accepts a job driving hookers around Los Angeles. One long and crazy evening proves to our hero that he is, in fact, up to the task of fatherhood.
documents.plot:
Amateur Night is a 2016 American crime sex comedy written and directed by Lisa Addario and Joe Syracuse, who drew on their own early experiences in Hollywood for the story. Jason Biggs stars alongside Jenny Mollen, Janet Montgomery, Ashley Tisdale and Bria Murphy. The film premiered in Los Angeles on July 25, 2016, and was released in American cinemas by Cinedigm in early August.

Guy Carter is an unemployed architect with a pregnant wife, Anne, and a growing pile of bills. Anne finds a Craigslist advertisement for a driver and sends him, against his wishes, to apply. Expecting to deliver pizzas, Guy discovers that he has been hired to chauffeur Nikki, a sex worker, around Los Angeles for the night. Their first stop is a regular client, a kinky doctor in Bel Air. When Nikki fails to return for hours, Guy breaks into the house, finds her tied up in what he assumes is a torture session and "rescues" her by spraying the doctor with air freshener; the man falls and hits his head, and the pair flee.

Calmed down by Nikki, Guy learns that he will receive a share of the night's takings and warms to the job. They pick up two of her colleagues, Jaxi and Fallon, and Guy is made to clean a bag of well-used sex toys before driving the women to a bachelor party at a luxury Beverly Hills hotel. There the women put Guy in charge of keeping a crowd of rowdy former fraternity brothers in line, and the evening descends into a series of increasingly explicit and humiliating episodes for him. When Anne goes into false labour, Guy steps out, only to be taken hostage by the vengeful doctor, armed with a syringe of paralysing drug, until Nikki turns the needle on him.

The party resumes until the women discover they have been robbed and hold the guests at gunpoint to retrieve their money. One of the men turns out to be an undercover police officer who tries to arrest Nikki, and Guy leads the police on a chase before crashing his car, and the group escapes by bus. As dawn breaks, Nikki hires Guy to design a house for her. Expecting police at his door, Guy finds instead that his car was repossessed before the police could trace it. The end credits play over re-enactments of incidents the filmmakers say really happened.

Critics panned the film; Rotten Tomatoes recorded no positive reviews from six critics, and it grossed only about $63,000.

documents.title: Bad Moms
documents.tagline: Party like a mother.
documents.overview: When three overworked and under-appreciated moms are pushed beyond their limits, they ditch their conventional responsibilities for a jolt of long overdue freedom, fun, and comedic self-indulgence.
documents.plot: When three overworked and under-appreciated moms are pushed beyond their limits, they ditch their conventional responsibilities for a jolt of long overdue freedom, fun, and comedic self-indulgence.

documents.title: The Edge of Seventeen
documents.tagline: You're only young once… is it over yet?
documents.overview: Two high school girls are best friends until one dates the other's older brother, who is totally his sister's nemesis.
documents.plot:
The Edge of Seventeen is a coming-of-age comedy-drama film released in 2016, directed by Kelly Fremon Craig and produced by Lianne Halfon, Molly Smith, and Jennifer Ventimilia. The movie follows the life of Nadine Byrd (played by Hailee Steinfeld), a high school junior navigating her senior year while dealing with her complicated relationships and family dynamics.

The story begins with Nadine's mother, Mary (played by Kyra Sedgwick), who is recently divorced from her husband, Jim (played by Woody Harrelson). The tension between the two parents is palpable, and Nadine struggles to cope with the changes in her life. Her father has moved out, and she feels abandoned.

Nadine's best friend, Krista (played by Haley Lu Richardson), tries to be supportive, but their friendship is put to the test as they face various challenges together. The two girls try to navigate high school cliques, relationships, and social pressures while dealing with Nadine's emotional turmoil.

As the story unfolds, Nadine develops feelings for her classmate, Eric (played by Blake Jenner), who seems perfect on the surface but turns out to be shallow and unfaithful. Meanwhile, she also starts to develop a crush on her English teacher, Mr. Bruner (played by Tom Holland).

Throughout the film, Nadine's relationships with her family members are explored in depth. Her mother is portrayed as a complex character struggling to balance her own emotions and needs with those of her daughter. The tension between them is evident, but they also share moments of tenderness and understanding.

As the school year progresses, Nadine faces various setbacks, including a failed relationship and a disappointing college acceptance letter. However, she eventually finds solace in her friendship with Krista and begins to develop a stronger sense of self.

The film's climax revolves around Nadine's confrontation with Eric, who has been unfaithful to her. The scene is intense and emotional, showcasing Nadine's growth and resilience. In the end, Nadine comes to terms with her feelings and learns to move on from her past heartbreak.

The Edge of Seventeen received widespread critical acclaim for its authentic portrayal of teenage life, nuanced character development, and outstanding performances from the cast. The film's exploration of complex themes such as family dynamics, relationships, and identity resonated with audiences worldwide.

documents.title: High Life
documents.tagline: Oblivion Awaits.
documents.overview: A father and his daughter struggle to survive in deep space where they live in isolation.
documents.plot: Monte and his daughter are the last survivors of a damned and dangerous mission to deep space. The crew—death-row inmates led by a doctor with sinister motives—has vanished. As the mystery of what happened onboard the ship is unraveled, father and daughter must rely on each other to survive as they hurtle toward the oblivion of a black hole.

documents.title: Jackie
documents.tagline: I want them to see what they have done to Jack.
documents.overview: An account of the days of First Lady, Jacqueline Kennedy, in the immediate aftermath of John F. Kennedy's assassination in 1963.
documents.plot:
In 1963, a week after the assassination of United States President John F. Kennedy, a journalist visits his widow Jacqueline "Jackie" Kennedy for an interview at her home in Hyannis Port, Massachusetts regarding her husband's legacy. After Jackie reflects upon her 1962 televised tour of the White House, the journalist turns to inquiries about John F. Kennedy's assassination and its aftermath for Jackie and her family. She talks about events shortly prior to the assassination before describing her shock and horror in reaction.
Members of the White House close to the newly sworn-in president Lyndon B. Johnson and his wife Lady Bird are seen comforting Jackie in the aftermath aboard Air Force One. United States Attorney General and Jackie's brother-in-law, Robert F. Kennedy soon appears and shares her grief, escorting her back to Washington, D.C. Jackie expresses her deep concern for the well-being of her children in adjusting to the loss of their father.
Robert continues to support Jackie while dealing with his sadness and helps her in planning the funeral and looking after the family. She is seen struggling to sleep and becoming reliant on medications and alcohol. She is also seen regularly seeking spiritual counsel from a priest. Robert, along with President Johnson, Lady Bird, and members of the White House, witness the murder of Lee Harvey Oswald, the president's suspected killer, by Jack Ruby on live television.
Robert insists that Jackie not be informed of this by anyone but himself; he will tell her when he feels the time is right. However, she finds out about it almost immediately and condemns him for withholding it from her. After John F. Kennedy Jr.'s third birthday, Robert voices his fears to Jackie that her husband's short time as president will not be noted by future generations.
After the state funeral of John F. Kennedy, Jackie tells the priest she contemplated suicide following the assassination. She then admits to remembering what happened during the assassination and feels unbearable pain and guilt that she did not act in some way to protect her husband.
As the interview ends, Jackie makes it clear that she maintains the right to control which parts of the interview may come to press and which parts are to be withheld.
The film concludes with Jackie having her miscarried and stillborn children's coffins being re-interred next to her husband's grave at Arlington National Cemetery in Virginia.

documents.title: Frantz
documents.overview: In the aftermath of WWI, a young German who grieves the death of her fiancé in France meets a mysterious French man who visits the fiance’s grave to lay flowers.
documents.plot: In the aftermath of WWI, a young German who grieves the death of her fiancé in France meets a mysterious French man who visits the fiance’s grave to lay flowers.

documents.title: Morgan
documents.tagline: Don't let it out
documents.overview: A corporate risk-management consultant must determine whether or not to terminate an artificial being's life that was made in a laboratory environment.
documents.plot:
Lee Weathers is a "risk-management specialist" for genetic-engineering company SynSect. She arrives at a rural site hosting its L-9 project, an artificial being with nanotechnology-infused synthetic DNA named Morgan. The "hybrid biological organism with the capacity for autonomous decision making and sophisticated emotional responses" is smarter than humans and has matured quickly, walking and talking within a month and already physically equivalent to a young teenage girl despite being born only five years before.
The cold and precise Weathers, who insists on calling Morgan "it", is at the site to assess the project while a psychologist evaluates Morgan, who has used a pen to stab Dr. Kathy Grieff in the eye. Over dinner with the team of eight scientists, Weathers and project leaders Dr. Lui Cheng and Dr. Simon Ziegler discuss an incident in Helsinki involving Cheng in which 21 SynSect researchers were killed in an hour by "crude prototypes".
Lee learns that Morgan attacked Grieff when she was prohibited from leaving her room, a glass cell, after killing a deer impaled on a tree branch, out of compassion for its suffering, while exploring outside. The scientists have reared Morgan from birth following two failed attempts, and most consider her to be their child; Grieff defends Morgan to Weathers despite her injury, and Dr. Amy Menser wants to resume taking her on outings. Menser promises to take Morgan to a nearby lake that she describes as wonderful; the behavioral therapist understands that Morgan is, despite her intellect and physical appearance and abilities, emotionally strange. Although Morgan considers Cheng to be her "mother", the scientist is pessimistic about the project; she admits to Weathers that she ended the outings as it is cruel to expose Morgan to a world she cannot be allowed to enter.
Psychologist and artificial intelligence expert Dr. Alan Shapiro arrives to assess Morgan and quickly defies the scientists' requests to stay outside Morgan's room for the assessment. When Shapiro aggressively taunts Morgan as part of his evaluation, she looks at her hand, becomes angry and spontaneously kills him. Weathers tranquilizes Morgan after a brief escape, and decides that she is too unpredictable and must be terminated. The scientists refuse to kill Morgan; before Weathers can do so, they shoot her with a tranquilizer dart and imprison her in the cell in which Morgan was held. The scientists plan to escape with Morgan, but after waking, Morgan, believing they have betrayed her starts a killing spree. She kills Darren with a lethal injection, shoots Ted in the chest and the head, and beats Brenda to death with a pistol. Ziegler, unaware of the murders, commits suicide after realizing his life's work turned into a failure.
In the scientists' house, Cheng records an apology for the failure of the project.

documents.title: Railroad Tigers
documents.tagline: Roaring soon
documents.overview: A railroad worker in China in 1941 leads a team of freedom fighters against the Japanese in order to get food for the poor.
