documents.title: Creep 2
documents.tagline: oh my god, this is going to be a good day.
documents.overview: After finding an ad online for “video work,” Sara, a video artist whose primary focus is creating intimacy with lonely men, thinks she may have found the subject of her dreams. She drives to a remote house in the forest and meets a man claiming to be a serial killer. Unable to resist the chance to create a truly shocking piece of art, she agrees to spend the day with him. However, as the day goes on, she discovers she may have dug herself into a hole from which she can’t escape.
documents.plot:
A prolific serial killer, using the name "Aaron" after a previous victim, undergoes a midlife crisis as his fortieth birthday approaches, finding himself dissatisfied with his killings. When his latest ad for a videographer lures YouTuber Sara to his remote cabin, Aaron changes his approach by admitting he is a serial killer who will let Sara live for the next 24 hours if she records a documentary on his life. Sara, doubting his revelation, agrees to film Aaron in the hopes that the video will popularize her unsuccessful web series about eccentric Craigslist clients.
Over the course of the day, Aaron struggles to intimidate Sara, who plays along with his various eccentricities. Sara eventually admits that she does not believe Aaron is truly a serial killer, whereupon Aaron informs her that he intends to conclude the documentary by having her kill him. He later stages a suicide attempt, much to her horror. As she prepares to leave, he convinces her to stay. The two have a conversation in which Aaron admits he is a virgin who has never kissed anyone. Surprised at this revelation, Sara offers to kiss him, to which he agrees.
Aaron brings Sara into the woods, where he gifts her the same heart-shaped locket he had given to his victim in the previous film, then shows her to an open grave he dug. He then proceeds to stab himself in the stomach before handing her the knife and imploring her to stab herself, hoping to conclude their film in the same manner as Romeo and Juliet. When she attempts to flee, he stabs her and drags her to the grave. Aaron approaches the camera and starts to give a closing monologue, but a still-alive Sara emerges from the grave and strikes him in the back of the head with a shovel before fleeing.
Afterwards, Sara is recorded in public by an unidentified individual whistling a tune heard in Aaron's videos. When Sara notices the individual filming her, the camera abruptly cuts away.

documents.title: Train to Busan
documents.tagline: Life-or-death survival begins.
documents.overview: When a zombie virus pushes Korea into a state of emergency, those trapped on an express train to Busan must fight for their own survival.
documents.plot:
Train to Busan is a 2016 South Korean post-apocalyptic horror film directed by Yeon Sang-ho. The movie takes place in a world where a mysterious virus has turned most of humanity into violent, zombie-like creatures.

The story begins with Seok-woo (played by Gong Yoo), a wealthy stockbroker who lives in Seoul with his wife Soo-an (played by Kim Su-an) and their young son Su-an. On the day of their daughter's birthday party, Seok-woo receives an unexpected phone call from his mother, who is bedridden with cancer, asking him to take care of her. Feeling guilty for not spending enough time with his family, Seok-woo decides to visit his mother in Busan.

As they board the KTX train to Busan, Seok-woo and Soo-an are unaware of the impending disaster that awaits them. The train is suddenly attacked by a group of zombies, who have been infected by the mysterious virus. The passengers and crew fight for survival as the train becomes a battleground.

Seok-woo's mother dies shortly after they arrive in Busan, but he continues on to find his daughter, who has gone missing. Along the way, he meets a young girl named Sung-gyeol (played by Kim Soo-an), who is also searching for her family. As they navigate through the treacherous streets of Busan, Seok-woo and Sung-gyeol form an unlikely bond.

As the train's passengers are picked off one by one, Seok-woo and Sung-gyeol discover that the virus has been caused by a mysterious outbreak in China. The government is trying to contain the outbreak, but it's too late, and the virus has spread globally.

The duo eventually boards a bus to escape the chaos, but they soon realize that the bus is also infested with zombies. In a desperate bid to survive, Seok-woo sacrifices himself to save Sung-gyeol by pushing her off the moving bus.

In the end, Sung-gyeol manages to find her way back to her father's office building in Seoul, where she finds him alive and well. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Sung-gyeol finally finding some sense of closure and reunion with her family.

Throughout the movie, Yeon Sang-ho explores themes of class struggle, social inequality, and the breakdown of society in the face of catastrophic disaster. The film's tense atmosphere and graphic violence make it a thrilling ride, but its thought-provoking commentary on human nature makes it more than just a mindless horror flick.

Overall, Train to Busan is a gripping and intense thriller that will keep you on the edge of your seat from start to finish. With its strong performances, clever plot twists, and social commentary, it's no wonder this movie has become a modern classic in the zombie genre.

documents.title: Anon
documents.tagline: Anonymity is the enemy
documents.overview: Set in a near-future world where there is no privacy, ignorance or anonymity, our private memories are recorded and crime almost ceases to exist. In trying to solve a series of unsolved murders, Sal Frieland stumbles onto a young woman who appears to have subverted the system and disappeared. She has no identity, no history and no record. Sal realizes it may not be the end of crime but the beginning. Known only as 'The Girl', Sal must find her before he becomes the next victim.

documents.title: Super Dark Times
documents.overview: Teenagers Zach and Josh have been best friends their whole lives, but when a gruesome accident leads to a cover-up, the secret drives a wedge between them and propels them down a rabbit hole of escalating paranoia and violence.
documents.plot:
In 1996, in Upstate New York, two teenage best friends, Zach and Josh, rate the girls in their yearbook. They find a common interest in Allison.
After school, the duo crosses the path of the universally-disliked Daryl and his eighth-grade friend Charlie. Later that week, the four boys meet up at Josh's house where they look through the possessions of Josh's brother, who is away in the military, and find a bag of marijuana and a katana.
Afterwards, the boys play with the sword in a secluded park area bordering the local cemetery and notice that Daryl has stolen the marijuana. After a tense argument, Josh and Daryl fight, resulting in Daryl being accidentally stabbed in the neck with the katana. Daryl runs from the scene but only makes it into the adjacent forest where he dies. The boys panic and hide both Daryl's body and the weapon.
At school, rumors circulate about Daryl's disappearance. Zach has nightmares and Josh doesn't attend classes. Zach wants to return to Daryl's burial site and attend Allison's upcoming party with Josh, who declines but goes to Allison's party separately where he shares his brother's weed. Zach, disturbed, leaves.
Another student, John, is found dead. Rumors speculate that he fell off a bridge. Zach suspects that Josh is responsible for John's death. He returns to Daryl's burial site and finds the katana missing and Daryl's corpse mutilated.
Zach goes to Josh's home and realizes Josh is with Allison. He tracks her to Meghan's house, where Josh has killed Meghan with the katana and tied Allison up. After Zach unties her, the former friends fight until a neighbor intervenes and subdues Josh, who is arrested, while Zach's fate is left unknown.
Months later, Allison has recovered and returns to school. A camera shot shows three parallel lines on the back of her neck.

documents.title: The Autopsy of Jane Doe
documents.tagline: Every body has a secret.
documents.overview: Father and son coroners receive a mysterious unidentified corpse with no apparent cause of death. As they attempt to examine the "Jane Doe," they discover increasingly bizarre clues that hold the key to her terrifying secrets.
documents.plot:
The Autopsy of Jane Doe is a 2016 American supernatural horror film directed by André Øvredal from a screenplay by Øvredal and Joel Bergman. The movie stars Brian Cox, Anthony Mackie, and Hailee Steinfeld.

The story begins with the death of a young woman named Jane Doe, who is found dead in her apartment. Her body is discovered by her landlord, who calls the local coroner's office to report the incident. Dr. Aaron Hunt (Brian Cox) and his son, Corbin (Anthony Mackie), are called to perform an autopsy on Jane.

As they begin the examination, they notice that Jane's body appears to be in pristine condition, with no signs of trauma or injury. However, as they delve deeper into the autopsy, they start to uncover strange and inexplicable details about her life. They find a series of cryptic symbols etched into her skin, which seem to be some sort of code.

As the autopsy progresses, Corbin becomes increasingly unsettled by the strange occurrences surrounding Jane's body. He begins to suspect that something supernatural is at play, but his father is skeptical and dismissive of these concerns.

Despite their initial reservations, the doctors soon realize that they are dealing with a malevolent entity that has taken possession of Jane's body. The entity, which appears to be some sort of ancient being, begins to exert its influence over Corbin, causing him to experience terrifying hallucinations and visions.

As the night wears on, the situation becomes increasingly dire, and Corbin's grip on reality begins to slip. His father tries to intervene, but he is powerless against the entity's malevolent forces.

In a desperate bid to save his son, Dr. Hunt turns to an ancient ritual that may be able to banish the entity from Jane's body. However, this comes at a terrible cost, and Corbin is forced to confront the dark secrets of his family's past in order to survive.

The movie builds towards a shocking climax as Corbin faces off against the entity in a desperate bid for survival. In the end, only one of them will emerge victorious, and the consequences of their confrontation will be devastating.

Throughout the movie, Øvredal uses a slow-burning tension to build suspense and unease, creating a sense of creeping dread that permeates every frame. The Autopsy of Jane Doe is a masterclass in atmospheric horror, using the setting and the characters' interactions to create a sense of unease and uncertainty.

The movie's use of symbolism and metaphor adds depth and complexity to the narrative, exploring themes of grief, trauma, and the supernatural. The performances from Cox and Mackie are outstanding, bringing a sense of gravitas and intensity to their roles.

Overall, The Autopsy of Jane Doe is a chilling and unsettling horror movie that will keep you on the edge of your seat until the very end.

documents.title: Vengeance: A Love Story
documents.tagline: Beyond good and evil is Justice
documents.overview: When a new friend is brutally assaulted, Detective John Droomor is put by chance in charge of the investigation. Although the evidence against the perpetrators seems overwhelming, there is nothing definitive in the case that guarantees justice is served, even more so if some people are willing to twist and betray it.
documents.plot:
Vengeance: A Love Story is a 2017 American action thriller directed by former stuntman Johnny Martin from a screenplay by John Mankiewicz, a writer-producer of House of Cards. It is based on Joyce Carol Oates's 2003 novel Rape: A Love Story. Nicolas Cage stars as John Dromoor, a Niagara Falls police detective and Gulf War veteran, with Anna Hutchison as Teena Maguire, Talitha Bateman as her 12-year-old daughter, Bethie, Deborah Kara Unger as Teena's mother, Agnes, and Don Johnson as the defense attorney Jay Kirkpatrick.

The film opens with a bust that goes badly wrong, showing Dromoor's questionable judgment, and he drinks away his troubles in a bar where he meets Teena, a flirtatious single mother who quickly catches his interest. After a Fourth of July party, Teena and Bethie take a shortcut home through the dark woods, where Teena is gang-raped, beaten and left for dead in front of her daughter by a group of four meth addicts. Bethie makes her way back to the road and flags down a passing car, which happens to be driven by Dromoor.

While Teena recovers, Agnes takes on the care of both her daughter and granddaughter. Bethie identifies the attackers and a hearing is set to decide whether the case will go to trial. The defendants' families hire Kirkpatrick, a nationally renowned criminal defense lawyer, who turns the proceedings against the traumatized victim by attacking her sobriety, her parenting and her sex life, while the judge appears all too friendly with him. When the case seems lost and the men are set free, Dromoor, a lone wolf suffering from post-traumatic stress, refuses to accept the failure of the legal system and sets out on his own campaign of vigilante justice against the attackers on Teena's behalf, eventually confronting the lawyer and offering comfort to both Bethie and her mother.

The project had first been planned for production in Michigan around 2009 with Samuel L. Jackson, Dianne Wiest and Abigail Breslin attached, but stalled. Cage joined in February 2016 and was briefly announced as director before stepping back, and filming began that April. The film was released direct to video in the United Kingdom in March 2017 and by FilmRise in the United States on September 15, 2017. Reviews were negative: Michael Rechtshaffen of the Los Angeles Times called it ham-handed and cliché-ridden and found Cage's performance detached, while Flickering Myth criticized its overwrought acting and tidy, consequence-free ending.
production_companies: Detective and the Girl Productions, LLC

documents.title: Along with the Gods: The Two Worlds
documents.tagline: Fate continues even after death.
documents.overview: Having died unexpectedly, firefighter Ja-hong is taken to the afterlife by 3 afterlife guardians. Only when he passes 7 trials over 49 days and proves he was innocent in human life, he’s able to reincarnate, and his 3 afterlife guardians are by his side to defend him in trial.
documents.plot:
Along with the Gods: The Two Worlds is a 2018 South Korean fantasy adventure film directed by Kim Sung-su, not released in 2017. However, I can provide you with information about the movie.

The film is based on the webtoon of the same name by Yeon Sang-ho and tells the story of two souls, Wang Yeo (played by Ha Jung-woo) and Chun Hyuk (played by Kim Hyang-gi), who are reincarnated into a new body after being judged by the God of Death.

The movie begins with Wang Yeo, a 33-year-old man who is about to die. However, he is unexpectedly chosen by the God of Death to be reincarnated into a new body. He finds himself in a beautiful and peaceful world where he meets Chun Hyuk, a young boy who has also been reincarnated.

As Wang Yeo navigates this new world, he discovers that it is filled with wonders and magic. However, he soon realizes that the world is not as perfect as it seems. He encounters various characters, including the God of Death's daughter, Hae-soo (played by Kim Hyang-gi), who becomes his guide and companion.

Throughout the film, Wang Yeo learns about the rules of this new world and the nature of reincarnation. He also discovers that he has a special connection to Chun Hyuk, who is destined for greatness. As they journey through the two worlds, they encounter various challenges and obstacles, including powerful enemies and moral dilemmas.

As the story unfolds, Wang Yeo and Chun Hyuk form a strong bond, and their relationship becomes central to the plot. Along the way, Wang Yeo also learns about his own past life and the reasons behind his reincarnation.

The film's climax features an epic battle between good and evil, with Wang Yeo and Chun Hyuk at its center. In the end, Wang Yeo makes a heroic sacrifice to save Chun Hyuk and restore balance to the two worlds.

Overall, Along with the Gods: The Two Worlds is a visually stunning and action-packed film that explores themes of reincarnation, friendship, and redemption. With its unique blend of fantasy and adventure elements, it has become a beloved classic in South Korean cinema.

documents.title: Before I Fall
documents.tagline: What if today was the only day of the rest of your life?
documents.overview: Samantha Kingston has everything. Then, everything changes. After one fateful night, she wakes up with no future at all. Trapped into reliving the same day over and over, she begins to question just how perfect her life really was.

documents.title: Rendel
documents.tagline: Revenge begets revenge.
documents.overview: Rendel, a masked superhero, becomes blinded by his desire for revenge against a sinister criminal organization.
documents.plot:
Rendel, also known as Rendel: Dark Vengeance, is a 2017 Finnish superhero action film written, produced and directed by Jesse Haaja and based on his own original character. It stars Kris Gummerus as Rendel, with Matti Onnismaa, Rami Rusinen and Renne Korppila in the other leading roles and Alina Tomnikov, Tero Salenius, Aake Kalliala, Anu Palevaara and Kristina Karjalainen in the supporting cast.

In the city of Mikkeli, a company called VALA has developed a lucrative vaccine without proper testing. VALA is a front for a criminal organization led by Pekka Erola, whose son Jarno, known as Rotikka, is one of its most violent enforcers. The gang's operations are being disrupted by a mysterious masked vigilante dressed in black, who leaves his victims marked with the name Rendel.

Through flashbacks, the film reveals the story of Rämö, a financial director and devoted family man. After refusing to invest in a scheme proposed by one of VALA's men, he loses his job and struggles to find work, until he is hired by VALA to handle paperwork. There he discovers that the vaccine, made from a tar-like substance that bonds permanently to skin, has not been properly tested and has caused numerous deaths. Fearing that Rämö will become a whistleblower, Erola sends Rotikka and his henchman to kill him. Rämö's wife and daughter are murdered, and he is beaten and left for dead, but he survives. Covering his face with the tar to create a mask and wearing the biker jacket his family gave him, he becomes Rendel, a dark avenger whose name comes from the Hungarian word for order. As his war against the organization escalates, VALA's leaders hire a team of foreign mercenaries to destroy him, while a mysterious woman named Marla offers him help.

The film combines brutal, stylized action with a dark revenge story set in a small Finnish city, offering an independently produced take on the superhero genre.

Rendel won the Best Action Movie award at the Feratum Film Festival in Mexico. A sequel, Rendel 2: Cycle of Revenge, was filmed in the Kainuu region in 2019, and an English-language continuation featuring Gummerus was later announced.

documents.title: The House That Jack Built
documents.tagline: If you feel like screaming... you definitely should.
documents.overview: Failed architect, engineer and vicious murderer Jack narrates the details of some of his most elaborately orchestrated crimes, each of them a towering piece of art that defines his life's work as a serial killer for twelve years.

documents.title: Brawl in Cell Block 99
documents.overview: After working as a drug courier and getting into a brutal shootout with police, a former boxer finds himself at the mercy of his enemies as they force him to instigate violent acts that turn the prison he resides in into a battleground.

documents.title: You Were Never Really Here
documents.tagline: Bring the hammer.
documents.overview: A traumatised veteran, unafraid of violence, tracks down missing girls for a living. When a job spins out of control, his nightmares overtake him as a conspiracy is uncovered leading to what may be his death trip or his awakening.
documents.plot:
Joe is a traumatized hired gun who specializes in rescuing trafficked girls, using brutal methods against their captors. He cares for his elderly mother in his childhood home in New York City. Joe has flashbacks of the abuse he and his mother endured from his violent father, and of his brutal past in the military and FBI, and is troubled by suicidal thoughts.
As he comes home one night, Joe is seen by Moises, the son of Angel, who acts as middleman between Joe and his handler, John McCleary. Joe tells McCleary that Angel knows his address and may pose a security risk. McCleary assigns Joe a new job from Albert Votto, a New York State Senator. Votto has offered a large sum of money to discreetly rescue his abducted daughter, Nina. He gives Joe the address of a brothel for wealthy patrons sent via an anonymous text. Joe stakes out the brothel, kills several security guards and patrons, and rescues Nina. While Joe and Nina await Votto's arrival in a hotel room, the news reports that Votto has committed suicide. Police officers gain access to the room with the help of the desk clerk, kill the clerk, and take Nina. Joe escapes after killing an officer sent to kill him.
Joe finds that government agents killed McCleary, Angel, and Moises while searching for Joe's address. Arriving back at his home, Joe discovers that two agents have murdered his mother and have been waiting for him. He kills one agent and mortally wounds the other. As the agent is dying, he reveals that Votto and Governor Williams are pedophiles and child traffickers and that Nina is Williams's favorite. He explains that Williams is directing the authorities to cover up the trafficking. Joe drives to a lake in a forest to give his mother a water burial and fills his pockets with stones, with the intent of killing himself. As he sinks, he has a vision of Nina. Removing the stones from his pockets, he swims back to the surface.
Joe follows Williams to his country home and fights his way in, only to discover Williams with his throat slit. He searches the house and discovers Nina, who is seated at a dining room table, alongside a bloody straight razor. Although Joe has become increasingly upset, Nina reassures him that she is alright. The two go to a diner to discuss their future. Joe has a violent suicidal fantasy and passes out. Nina wakes him, saying, "It's a beautiful day." He agrees, and they leave together.

documents.title: Call Me by Your Name
documents.tagline: Is it better to speak or die?
documents.overview: In 1980s Italy, a relationship begins between seventeen-year-old teenage Elio and the older adult man hired as his father's research assistant.
documents.plot:
In the summer of 1983, Elio Perlman, a 17-year-old Jewish French-Italian boy, lives with his parents in rural Northern Italy. Elio's father, a professor of archaeology, invites a 24-year-old Jewish-American graduate student, Oliver, to live with the family over the summer and help with his academic paperwork. Elio, an introspective bookworm and musician, initially thinks he has little in common with Oliver, who appears confident and carefree. Elio spends much of the summer reading, playing piano, and hanging out with his childhood friends, Chiara and Marzia. During a volleyball match, Oliver touches Elio's back, but Elio brushes it off. Elio later finds himself jealous upon seeing Oliver kiss Chiara.
Elio and Oliver spend more time together, taking long walks into town, and accompanying Elio's father on an archaeological trip. Elio is increasingly drawn to Oliver, even sneaking into Oliver's room to smell his clothing. Elio eventually confesses his feelings to Oliver, who tells him they cannot discuss such things. Later, in a secluded spot, the two kiss for the first time. Oliver is reluctant to take things further, and they do not speak for several days.
Elio goes on a date with Marzia and the two have sex. Elio leaves a note for Oliver to end their silence. Oliver writes back, asking Elio to meet him at midnight. Elio agrees and they sleep together for the first time. Afterward, Oliver tells Elio, "Call me by your name and I'll call you by mine". The morning after, Elio is briefly conflicted about their encounter and takes out his sexual frustration by masturbating with a peach. When Oliver finds him, Elio cries about how little time he and Oliver have left together. Marzia confronts Elio after not hearing from him for three days. He responds indifferently, hurting her.
As the end of Oliver's stay approaches, Elio's parents, who appear aware of the bond between the two, recommend that he and Oliver visit Bergamo together before Oliver returns to the U.S. They spend three romantic days together. Heartbroken after Oliver's departure, Elio calls his mother to ask her to pick him up from the train station and take him home. Marzia is sympathetic to Elio's feelings and says she wants to remain friends. Elio's father, observing his unhappiness, tells him that the bond he had with Oliver was rare and that he envies Elio because he never had what Elio and Oliver had. He consoles Elio by advising him to keep his heart open for more joy and experiences rather than close himself off.
During Hanukkah, Oliver calls Elio's family to tell them he is engaged to be married to a woman he has been intermittently dating for a few years. Elio calls Oliver by his (Elio's) name and Oliver responds with his (Oliver's); Oliver says "[he] remember everything". After the call, Elio sits by the fireplace and stares into the flames, tearfully reflecting as his parents and staff prepare dinner.

documents.title: The Irishman
documents.tagline: His story changed history
documents.overview: Pennsylvania, 1956. Frank Sheeran, a war veteran of Irish origin who works as a truck driver, accidentally meets mobster Russell Bufalino. Once Frank becomes his trusted man, Bufalino sends him to Chicago with the task of helping Jimmy Hoffa, a powerful union leader related to organized crime, with whom Frank will maintain a close friendship for nearly twenty years.
documents.plot:
In a nursing home, elderly Irish American World War II veteran Frank Sheeran narrates his time as a hitman for the Italian-American Mafia.
In 1950s Philadelphia, Sheeran works as a union delivery truck driver, where he starts selling some of the meat shipments to a local Philadelphia Italian American gangster known as "Skinny Razor," a member of the Philadelphia crime family headed by Angelo Bruno. After the delivery company accuses Sheeran of theft, union lawyer Bill Bufalino gets the case dismissed when Sheeran refuses to name his customers to the judge.
Bill introduces Sheeran to his cousin Russell Bufalino, head of his namesake crime family in Northeastern Pennsylvania. Sheeran begins to carry out jobs for him, as well as members of the South Philadelphia underworld, including "painting houses," a euphemism for contract killing.
Sheeran is soon introduced to Jimmy Hoffa, head of the International Brotherhood of Teamsters, who has financial ties with the Northeastern Pennsylvania crime family. He is struggling to deal with fellow rising Teamster Anthony "Tony Pro" Provenzano, in addition to mounting pressure from the federal government. Hoffa becomes close with Sheeran and his family, especially his daughter Peggy; in turn Sheeran becomes his chief bodyguard.
After the 1960 election of John F. Kennedy, Bufalino is thrilled while Hoffa is furious. Kennedy's brother, Robert F. Kennedy, whom he appointed Attorney General, forms a "Get Hoffa" squad to bring down Hoffa, who is eventually arrested and convicted in 1964 for jury tampering.
While Hoffa is in prison, his replacement as Teamsters president, Frank "Fitz" Fitzsimmons, misuses the union's pension fund and gives interest-free loans to the Mafia. Hoffa's relationship with Tony Pro, himself arrested for extortion, also deteriorates beyond repair when Hoffa refuses to help restore his forfeited pension. Hoffa's sentence is commuted by President Richard Nixon in 1971, although he is forbidden from partaking in any Teamsters activities until 1980.
Despite his parole terms, Hoffa undertakes a plan to reclaim his power atop the Teamsters. His growing disrespect for other Teamster leaders and his intention to separate the union from the Mafia begin to worry Russell. During a dinner in Sheeran's honor in October 1973, Russell pleads with Sheeran to confront Hoffa and warn him that the heads of the crime families are displeased with his behavior. Hoffa then informs Sheeran that he "knows things" that Russell and the dons of other families are unaware of and claims that what he knows makes him untouchable, for if anything ever happened to him, they would all end up in prison.
In 1975, while on their way to the wedding of Bill's daughter, Russell reluctantly informs Sheeran that the dons have become fed up with Hoffa and have sanctioned his murder. Russell further informs Sheeran that he must serve as the triggerman, knowing he might otherwise try to warn or save Hoffa.

documents.title: The Commuter
documents.tagline: Lives are on the line
documents.overview: A businessman, on his daily commute home, gets unwittingly caught up in a criminal conspiracy that threatens not only his life but the lives of those around him.
documents.plot:
The Commuter is a 2018 action thriller film directed by Jaume Collet-Serra, in his fourth collaboration with Liam Neeson, and written by Byron Willinger, Philip de Blasi and Ryan Engle. Neeson stars as a former policeman drawn into a murder conspiracy on his daily train ride, alongside Vera Farmiga, Patrick Wilson, Jonathan Banks, Florence Pugh and Sam Neill.

Michael MacCauley, a former NYPD officer turned insurance salesman, rides the same Hudson Line train between Tarrytown and Grand Central every day. Suddenly laid off and afraid to tell his wife, he confides in his former partner, Murphy, who is still on the force. On the ride home, a mysterious woman named Joanna offers him a "hypothetical" deal: find a passenger known as "Prynne," who has something that does not belong to them, for $100,000, starting with $25,000 hidden in the bathroom. Michael takes the money, but when he tries to get off, he is handed his wife's wedding ring as a warning. A commuter he asks for help is pushed under a bus, and Joanna reveals that his family is being held and that he must plant a GPS tracker on Prynne.

Michael's attempts to identify Prynne go wrong: the man he tags turns out to be an FBI agent, found dead soon after. Murphy tells him that Prynne is a key witness to the supposed suicide of city official Enrique Mendez, and Michael realizes that Prynne is to be killed and that he is being framed. He forces the passengers into the last car and kills another passenger, Oliver, who had been hired to murder Prynne. Prynne turns out to be Sofia, a teenage girl holding evidence against powerful people, who was being escorted to witness protection. When Michael refuses to kill her, Joanna detonates explosives to derail the train, but Michael uncouples the final car and saves most of the passengers. Police surround the car, believing he has taken hostages, and Murphy is sent in to negotiate, inadvertently revealing that he is the corrupt cop who killed Mendez. Michael removes Murphy's identifying tag, and snipers shoot Murphy. Sofia testifies, Michael's family is rescued, and he is offered his old job back. Later, he confronts Joanna on a train and prepares to arrest her.

Released by Lionsgate in the United States on January 12, 2018, The Commuter grossed $119.9 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed, with critics comparing it to Non-Stop but praising Neeson's performance; Rotten Tomatoes reported 55% approval and Metacritic a score of 56.

documents.title: The Shape of Water
documents.tagline: A Fairy Tale for Troubled Times
documents.overview: An other-worldly story, set against the backdrop of Cold War era America circa 1962, where a mute janitor working at a lab falls in love with an amphibious man being held captive there and devises a plan to help him escape.
documents.plot:
In 1962, during the Cold War, Elisa Esposito works as a janitor in a secret government laboratory in Baltimore, Maryland. Found abandoned by the side of a river as an infant with scars on her neck, Elisa is mute and communicates through sign language. Her only friends are her closeted middle-aged neighbor Giles, an advertising illustrator, and her coworker Zelda.
Colonel Richard Strickland has captured a creature from a South American river and taken it to the facility for study, losing two fingers (which are unsuccessfully retransplanted) while interrogating it. Elisa discovers it is a humanoid amphibian, and bonds with the creature after visiting him in secret. Seeking an advantage in the Space Race, Strickland persuades General Frank Hoyt to vivisect the Amphibian Man to examine his respiratory system. Scientist Robert Hoffstetler, a Soviet spy, pleads with Strickland to keep him alive for further study, while being ordered by his handlers to kill the creature.
Giles reluctantly agrees to help Elisa free Amphibian Man after failing a work assignment and being rejected by a local restaurant manager whom he discovered was both racist and homophobic. Hoffstetler and Zelda also become involved in the plot and successfully get the Amphibian Man to Elisa's apartment. Elisa keeps him in her bathtub, planning to release him into a nearby canal when heavy rain allows access to the ocean. When Giles tries to stop the Amphibian Man from devouring one of his cats, his arm is slashed and the Amphibian Man flees. Elisa coaxes him back to her apartment and the creature touches Giles on his balding head and wounded arm. The next morning, Giles discovers his hair is regrowing and the wounds on his arm have healed. Elisa's infatuation with the Amphibian Man culminates in sexual intercourse.
General Hoyt gives Strickland an ultimatum to recover the Amphibian Man or his career will be over. Hoffstetler is told by his handlers he'll be extracted from the US in two days. The Amphibian Man's health begins to deteriorate.
Strickland follows Hoffstetler to a meeting with his handlers where Hoffstetler is shot. Strickland intervenes, shooting the handlers, then tortures the dying spy into revealing the Amphibian Man's whereabouts. Strickland confronts Zelda in her home and her husband reveals Elisa has the Amphibian Man. Zelda warns Elisa to release the creature before Strickland can arrive. He ransacks Elisa's apartment and finds evidence of the creature in the bathtub and a calendar note revealing where she plans to release him.

Elisa and Giles are bidding farewell to the creature at the canal when Strickland arrives, knocks Giles down, and shoots both the Amphibian Man and Elisa. Giles and Strickland fight while the Amphibian Man heals himself, then fatally slashes Strickland's throat. As the police arrive with Zelda, the Amphibian Man jumps into the canal with the unconscious Elisa and kisses her.

documents.title: The Killing of a Sacred Deer
documents.original_title: The Killing of a Sacred Deer
documents.tagline: A brilliant surgeon is forced to make an unthinkable sacrifice after his life starts to fall apart.
documents.overview: Dr. Steven Murphy is a renowned cardiovascular surgeon who presides over a spotless household with his wife and two children. Lurking at the margins of his idyllic suburban existence is Martin, a fatherless teen who insinuates himself into the doctor's life in gradually unsettling ways.
documents.plot:
The Killing of a Sacred Deer is a 2017 absurdist psychological horror thriller directed and co-produced by Yorgos Lanthimos, who wrote the screenplay with Efthimis Filippou. Colin Farrell plays Steven Murphy, a cardiac surgeon, with Nicole Kidman as his wife Anna, Barry Keoghan as the teenager Martin, Raffey Cassidy and Sunny Suljic as the couple's children Kim and Bob, and Alicia Silverstone as Martin's mother. The title alludes to Euripides' tragedy Iphigenia in Aulis.

Steven, a Cincinnati heart surgeon, has been meeting 16-year-old Martin at a diner, whose father died a few years earlier. He introduces the boy to his family, and Martin charms them all, especially Kim. When Steven dines at Martin's home, the boy's mother makes advances at him, saying it is what her son wants, and Steven leaves. Martin's demands on his time become more frequent and insistent, and Steven grows uneasy, particularly after Martin gives Kim a ride on his motorcycle.

Then Bob suddenly loses the use of his legs. Martin explains that his father died on Steven's operating table and that, to restore the balance, Steven must kill one member of his own family; otherwise all of them will die, first becoming paralysed, then refusing food, then bleeding from the eyes before death. Soon Bob will not eat, and Kim, now infatuated with Martin, collapses at choir practice. Steven admits to Anna that he had been drinking before the fatal surgery. Martin demonstrates his hold over Kim by telling her over the phone to stand, then leaving her paralysed again. Pressed by Anna, Steven imprisons Martin in the basement, beats him and shoots him in the legs, but the boy only bites his own arm to illustrate his notion of justice. The children compete for their father's favour, Steven asks their school principal which child is better, and Anna argues that he should sacrifice one of the children rather than her. When Bob's eyes begin to bleed, Steven binds his family in a circle, covers his own face and fires a rifle blindly while spinning; the third shot kills Bob. Later, the surviving Murphys see Martin at the diner and walk out.

Shot in Cincinnati in 2016, the film competed for the Palme d'Or at Cannes in 2017 and won the prize for Best Screenplay. It was released in the United States by A24 in October 2017 and grossed $10.7 million worldwide. Reviews were positive, with 79% on Rotten Tomatoes and 73 on Metacritic.

documents.title: Piper
documents.overview: A mother bird tries to teach her little one how to find food by herself. In the process, she encounters a traumatic experience that she must overcome in order to survive.
documents.plot:
Piper is a 2016 American computer-animated short film produced by Pixar Animation Studios, written and directed by Alan Barillaro, a veteran Pixar animator. A story about a hungry baby sandpiper who must overcome her fear of water, it was released in theaters alongside Pixar's feature Finding Dory on June 17, 2016, and was later included on that film's Blu-ray and DVD releases. The idea came to Barillaro on the shoreline less than a mile from Pixar's studios in Emeryville, California, where he would run along the beach and watch thousands of birds darting away from the incoming water and returning between waves to feed.

A flock of sandpipers forages along a beach, searching for shellfish exposed by the retreating waves and scurrying away whenever the surf rolls back in. A mother sandpiper brings her chick, Piper, to the water's edge so that she can learn to find food for herself. Piper, however, is too slow to escape an incoming wave and is drenched by the surf, an experience that leaves her terrified of the water. Back at the nest, she refuses to venture out again and insists that her mother keep feeding her as before. Eventually hunger drives her back to the shore, where she notices a small hermit crab burrowing into the sand. As she watches it, a large wave rolls in and engulfs her. Panicking, she copies the crabs and buries herself in the sand, but this time the hermit crab encourages her to open her eyes. Underwater, Piper sees large shellfish uncovered by the wave. Thrilled, she conquers her fear, learns to catch the bounty revealed beneath the water and gathers enough to feed the entire flock.

Barillaro spent more than three years making the film with new, cutting-edge technology. To give the sandpipers and the other birds a realistic look, he and the short's animation team studied their appearance and behavior on beaches around the San Francisco Bay Area and at the Monterey Bay Aquarium, and the birds' feathers were rendered in minute detail. Critics praised the lifelike animation, with Variety calling it as simple as a haiku and yet stunning, and the short holds a 100% rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Piper won the Academy Award for Best Animated Short Film at the 89th Academy Awards, the first Pixar short to win the award since For the Birds in 2001.

documents.title: Logan Lucky
documents.tagline: See how the other half steals.
documents.overview: Trying to reverse a family curse, brothers Jimmy and Clyde Logan set out to execute an elaborate robbery during the legendary Coca-Cola 600 race at the Charlotte Motor Speedway.
documents.plot:
Logan Lucky is a 2017 American heist comedy film directed by Steven Soderbergh, marking his return from a self-declared retirement from filmmaking, from a screenplay credited to Rebecca Blunt. Channing Tatum and Adam Driver star as Jimmy and Clyde Logan, brothers from West Virginia, with Riley Keough as their sister, Mellie, Daniel Craig as the safecracker Joe Bang, Katie Holmes, Seth MacFarlane, Katherine Waterston, Hilary Swank, Sebastian Stan and Dwight Yoakam. Soderbergh distributed the film independently through his company Fingerprint Releasing, in partnership with Bleecker Street.

Jimmy, a former high school football star whose career was ended by a knee injury, is fired from his construction job in the tunnels beneath the Charlotte Motor Speedway because his old injury was not disclosed. He dotes on his young daughter, Sadie, who competes in beauty pageants and lives with his ex-wife, Bobbie Jo, and her wealthy new husband, who are planning to move away. Jimmy's brother, Clyde, an Iraq War veteran who lost part of his arm, tends a local bar, and the family is said to be cursed by bad luck. After a confrontation with an obnoxious NASCAR team owner, Max Chilblain, Jimmy reveals his plan to rob the speedway by exploiting what he knows about the pneumatic tube system used to move cash to its vault.

The Logans recruit Mellie and Joe Bang, an imprisoned explosives expert, along with his dim-witted brothers, Sam and Fish. Their scheme requires breaking Joe out of prison and returning him before anyone notices, so Clyde deliberately gets himself sent to the same prison. On the day of the Coca-Cola 600, one of the busiest races of the year, the gang carries out the heist, improvising around obstacles that include a prison riot staged as a diversion. Weeks later, the FBI agent Sarah Grayson investigates the robbery, but the case appears to have been solved, and the twists of the Logans' plan gradually come to light.

Logan Lucky received positive reviews for its humor, performances and clever plotting, with critics likening it to a rural counterpart of Soderbergh's Ocean's Eleven. It grossed about $48 million worldwide. Speculation that "Rebecca Blunt" was a pseudonym, possibly for Soderbergh's wife, Jules Asner, persisted after release.

documents.title: The Assignment
documents.tagline: A revenger's tale.
documents.overview: Ace assassin Frank Kitchen is double crossed by gangsters and falls into the hands of rogue surgeon known as The Doctor who turns him into a woman. The hitman, now a hitwoman, sets out for revenge, aided by a nurse named Johnnie who also has secrets.
documents.plot:
The Assignment, also released as Tomboy and, in Australia, as Revenger, is an action crime thriller directed by Walter Hill, who co-wrote it with Denis Hamill. Michelle Rodriguez plays a professional hitman who is surgically transformed into a woman against his will, and Sigourney Weaver plays the disgraced surgeon responsible, with Tony Shalhoub, Anthony LaPaglia and Caitlin Gerard. It premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 11, 2016.

The story moves between two timelines. In the present, Dr. Rachel Jane, a brilliant but unhinged plastic surgeon who lost her licence and went on to perform illegal experiments on vulnerable homeless patients, is confined in a psychiatric institution where Dr. Ralph Galen is assessing her mental state. In the past, she sets out to avenge her brother Sebastian, who was murdered by the contract killer Frank Kitchen.

Through the gangster Honest John, Jane has Frank betrayed and captured. Driven by revenge and by curiosity about how much physical identity shapes a person, she performs gender reassignment surgery on him. Frank wakes in a hotel room in a female body, breaks down, and finds hormones and a taped message from the doctor urging him to start a new life. He takes refuge with Johnnie, a woman he once slept with, while he recovers.

Once he learns the operation cannot be undone, Frank begins killing everyone connected with it, including Honest John's men. He discovers that Johnnie was paid to watch him, but he spares her after realising she acted out of fear and has come to care for him, and she helps him set a trap. Jane's bodyguards capture Frank instead, and she plans to amputate his arm so he can never kill again. He breaks free, kills her guards and assistant, and shoots Jane without killing her.

In the institution, Jane gives a deposition explaining her actions without remorse. The film reveals that Frank arranged the scene to blame her assistant and cut off her fingers so she can never operate again.

Saban Films released the film on video on demand in March 2017 and in limited cinemas the following month. Reviews were negative, with a 33% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Isle of Dogs
documents.tagline: Welcome to the Isle of Dogs.
documents.overview: In the future, an outbreak of canine flu leads the mayor of a Japanese city to banish all dogs to an island that's a garbage dump. The outcasts must soon embark on an epic journey when a 12-year-old boy arrives on the island to find his beloved pet.
documents.plot: In the future, an outbreak of canine flu leads the mayor of a Japanese city to banish all dogs to an island used as a garbage dump. The outcasts must soon embark on an epic journey when a 12-year-old boy arrives on the island to find his beloved pet.

documents.title: Beirut
documents.tagline: Beirut, 1982: The Paris of the Middle East Was Burning
documents.overview: In 1980s Beirut, Mason Skiles is a former U.S. diplomat who is called back into service to save a colleague from the group that is possibly responsible for his own family's death. Meanwhile, a CIA field agent who is working under cover at the American embassy is tasked with keeping Mason alive and ensuring that the mission is a success.
documents.plot:
Beirut, released in the United Kingdom as The Negotiator, is a 2018 American political thriller directed by Brad Anderson from a screenplay Tony Gilroy wrote in 1991 under the title High Wire Act. Set during the Lebanese Civil War, it stars Jon Hamm as a former US diplomat drawn back to Beirut to negotiate for a kidnapped colleague, with Rosamund Pike, Dean Norris, Shea Whigham, Larry Pine and Mark Pellegrino.

In 1972 Mason Skiles is a diplomat in Beirut living with his Lebanese wife Nadia and Karim, a 13-year-old Palestinian boy they have taken in. At a party, CIA officer Cal Riley tells Skiles he wants to question Karim, whose brother Rafid has been tied to the Munich massacre; Rafid's men then storm the house and seize Karim, and Nadia is killed. Ten years later Skiles is an alcoholic labour arbitrator in New England. Lured back to Beirut on the pretext of a lecture, he learns Riley has been kidnapped and that the abductors asked for him by name. The grown Karim now leads the group and demands Rafid in exchange, though the Americans insist they do not hold him. A trip to Israel proves fruitless, and Riley's wife Alice blames Skiles for her husband's plight. After a car bomb disrupts his lecture, Skiles is taken to Karim and Riley, who secretly tells him that the PLO has Rafid and that CIA officer Gaines cannot be trusted. CIA officer Sandy Crowder reveals that Gaines has been embezzling, and she steals $4 million to buy Rafid. With Rafid in hand, they force their way through a militia checkpoint to the exchange, where Skiles secures Riley's release; when Rafid lunges at Skiles, he is shot by a sniper, revealed as the fixer Bernard, who slips away with Sandrine, an Israeli agent. Gaines retires, Crowder seeks his post, and newsreels of the 1982 Israeli invasion and the 1983 embassy and barracks bombings close the film.

Hamm plays Skiles, with Pike as Crowder, Norris as Gaines, Whigham as National Security Council official Gary Ruzak, Pellegrino as Riley and Pine as Ambassador Whalen. Produced and financed by ShivHans Pictures, it was shot in Tangier, Morocco, from June 2016. It premiered at Sundance in January 2018 and Bleecker Street released it on April 11. Critics praised its intricate plotting and the leads, giving it 81% on Rotten Tomatoes, but it grossed only $7.5 million worldwide.

documents.title: Alpha
documents.tagline: Leaders are born from survival
documents.overview: In the prehistoric past, Keda, a young and inexperienced hunter, struggles to return home after being separated from his tribe when bison hunting goes awry. On his way back he will find an unexpected ally.
documents.plot:
In Upper Paleolithic Europe 20,000 years ago, a small tribe of hunter-gatherers prepare for a hunting expedition to hunt for the coming winter's food. Tau, its chief, trains his teenage son Keda, allowing him and Keda's friend Kappa to join the hunting party. His wife Rho worries that Keda is not ready, but Tau believes he is and the hunters set out.
Tau tests Keda by having him kill a wild boar they've caught, but Keda refuses. One night, the party's fire draws the attention of a large lion, which lunges through their circle, snatching Kappa before anyone can do anything. Hearing the fatal struggle in the darkness, the tribe gives him up for dead. Kappa is given a memorial service in the form of a cairn to symbolize the passing of one's spirit to the afterlife. After that, a wolf howl is heard, and Tau tells Keda that the wolf's name is Alpha, and he is the leader of his clan.
The hunters eventually reach a herd of steppe bison, which they attempt to stampede from a cliff with relative success. Amidst the chaos, a bull rushes towards Keda and tosses him over the edge, leaving him gripping the rough cliff edge with his hand. Keda’s grip breaks and he plummets to a further ledge where he appears to break his leg and is knocked unconscious. Tau attempts to climb down to him, but he is stopped by fellow hunter Sigma who assures him in good faith that Keda is dead and there would be no way to reach him anyway. The tribe leaves and Tau performs another funeral ritual, stricken with grief.
Keda is awoken by a vulture who mistakes him for dead. He kills the bird and tries to climb the rest of the way down the cliff. A sudden heavy rainfall causes the ravine below to flood. Keda sees this, but is reluctant to jump off and hope the water will break his fall. He slips off the ledge anyway, and he survives the fall. Keda splints his injured foot before returning to the top of the cliff. Seeing the memorial cairn left by his tribe, he realizes that he must travel back to the village by himself.
Keda is later attacked and chased by a pack of ferocious wolves, but escapes up a tree and wounds one of the pack members, which the others leave behind. Keda takes pity on it and cares for its injury. Gradually gaining the wolf's trust, he gives it food and water, establishing himself as dominant by feeding himself first. He sets out for the village without the wolf, but it follows him. Their relationship grows, and they learn to hunt animals together.
One night, they are approached menacingly by a pack of wolves. Upon seeing Alpha, who steps forward to greet them, they recognize Keda's companion. The pack runs off, and with Keda's blessing, Alpha joins them. Keda continues his journey alone as the season changes into winter. On a frozen lake, he encounters a pack of wolves feeding on a carcass. Recognizing Alpha, he runs to them, but the ice breaks and he falls through. Alpha helps rescue him and they are reunited.

documents.title: Triple Frontier
documents.tagline: You can’t go this far without crossing every line
documents.overview: Struggling to make ends meet, former special ops soldiers reunite for a high-stakes heist: stealing $75 million from a South American drug lord.
documents.plot:
Triple Frontier is a 2019 American action-adventure film directed by J.C. Chandor and written by Mark Boal, J.C. Chandor, and Matt Boling. The movie stars Oscar Isaac, Ben Affleck, Charlie Hunnam, Garrett Hedlund, and Pedro Pascal.

The story follows three former US Special Forces operatives - Chris Mullin (Oscar Isaac), Billy Marks (Ben Affleck), and Mike Kinney (Charlie Hunnam) - who have retired from their military careers. The trio reunites for a high school friend's 40th birthday party in New York City, where they are approached by Santiago "Pope" Garcia (Gael García Bernal), a former comrade-in-arms.

Santiago reveals that his younger brother, Francisco, has been kidnapped by the notorious Bolivian cartel leader, Dina (Catalina Sandino Moreno). The kidnappers demand $75 million in exchange for Francisco's safe return. Pope asks his old friends to help him rescue his brother and retrieve the ransom money.

The team devises a plan to infiltrate Bolivia and gather intelligence on the cartel's operations. They assemble a group of local fighters, including a Bolivian woman named Ana (Natalia Beristáin), who becomes an ally in their mission.

As they prepare for the rescue operation, the team faces personal demons and conflicts that threaten to derail their mission. Chris struggles with his past mistakes, Billy grapples with feelings of guilt over his role in a previous military operation gone wrong, and Mike tries to reconcile his loyalty to his friends with his growing sense of morality.

The team launches a daring rescue mission, navigating treacherous terrain and avoiding cartel henchmen. Along the way, they encounter Ana, who becomes an integral part of their plan. The group faces numerous challenges, including treacherous mountain paths, rival factions within the cartel, and personal betrayals.

As the stakes escalate, the team's bond is tested, and they are forced to confront their own mortality. In a tense showdown, they face off against Dina's henchmen in a violent confrontation that leaves several characters gravely injured or killed.

In the aftermath of the rescue mission, the team reflects on the true cost of their actions. Chris comes to terms with his past mistakes, Billy finds redemption through his sacrifice, and Mike learns to prioritize his humanity over his loyalty to his friends.

The movie concludes with a poignant moment of closure for Pope, who finally gets to see his brother safe and sound. The film ends on a hopeful note, suggesting that even in the face of adversity, friendship and loyalty can be powerful forces for redemption and healing.

Overall, Triple Frontier is an action-packed thrill ride with a strong ensemble cast and a gripping narrative that explores themes of loyalty, sacrifice, and redemption.

documents.title: Marrowbone
documents.tagline: No one will ever separate us.
documents.overview: A young man and his three younger siblings are plagued by a sinister presence in the sprawling manor in which they live.
documents.plot:
Marrowbone (Spanish: El secreto de Marrowbone) is a 2017 English-language Spanish psychological horror mystery film written and directed by Sergio G. Sánchez. It stars George MacKay, Anya Taylor-Joy, Charlie Heaton, Mia Goth and Matthew Stagg, and follows four siblings who move from England to their mother's ancestral home in Maine, where they are confronted by a sinister presence. It screened in the Special Presentations section of the 2017 Toronto International Film Festival and was released in Spain by Universal Pictures on 27 October 2017.

In 1968, Rose Fairbairn brings her four children, Jack, Jane, Billy and Sam, from England to the remote house in rural Maine where she grew up, and tells them they will now go by her maiden name, Marrowbone. The family is befriended by a local girl, Allie, but Rose's health soon fails. Before she dies she makes Jack, the eldest, promise to keep the family together and to hide her death until he can become his siblings' legal guardian. Six months later the children are still living alone in the house, where every mirror is covered and the attic is sealed off because they believe something lives up there. Jack slips into town for supplies and quietly courts Allie, now working at the library, while hiding his past from her. Tom Porter, the town lawyer handling the Marrowbone estate and Allie's unrequited admirer, needs Rose's signature to complete the transfer of the property, and the siblings are forced to forge it and to dip into a box of money left by their father. As strange noises and incidents in the house multiply, Allie learns from Tom some disturbing facts about the family's past and the father the children fled from, while Tom, under financial pressure, begins to suspect the Marrowbones are hiding more money and turns to blackmail. When Billy goes looking for the money in the house, he makes a terrifying discovery, and the secret that Jack has been protecting threatens to come out.

On Rotten Tomatoes, Marrowbone holds a 49% approval rating based on 75 reviews, with a consensus that its effective setting and strong cast cannot make up for thinly conceived characters and a story short on genuine scares, while Metacritic gave it a score of 63 out of 100.

documents.title: Hunter Killer
documents.tagline: Courage runs deep
documents.overview: Captain Glass of the USS Arkansas discovers that a coup d'état is taking place in Russia, so he and his crew join an elite group working on the ground to prevent a war.
documents.plot:
Hunter Killer is a 2018 American action thriller film directed by Donovan Marsh and written by Arne Schmidt and Jamie Moss, based on the 2012 novel Firing Point by Don Keith and George Wallace. Gerard Butler stars as Commander Joe Glass, a submarine captain whose crew joins a team of Navy SEALs to rescue the Russian president from a coup, with Gary Oldman, Toby Stephens as the SEAL leader Lieutenant Bill Beaman and Michael Nyqvist, in his penultimate film role, as the Russian captain Sergei Andropov. Common and Linda Cardellini also appear.

When the American submarine USS Tampa Bay vanishes while shadowing a Russian submarine in the Barents Sea, the newly promoted and unconventional Glass is sent to investigate aboard USS Arkansas. Meanwhile, Beaman's SEAL team, watching a Russian naval base at Polyarny, sees Defense Minister Dmitriy Durov stage a coup and seize President Nikolai Zakarin in a bid to start a war, and the team is forced to leave behind a wounded member, Martinelli. Arkansas finds the wreck of Tampa Bay with no survivors and the sunken Russian submarine Konek, apparently sabotaged from within, and is ambushed by a second Russian submarine hidden beneath an iceberg, the vessel that had sunk Tampa Bay. Arkansas fights back and rescues the Konek's survivors, including Captain Andropov. Rear Admiral John Fisk proposes that Arkansas pick up Zakarin once the SEALs free him. With the reluctant Andropov's guidance, the submarine slips through a minefield to the base undetected. The SEALs free Zakarin with the help of a wounded presidential bodyguard, Oleg, losing him and two of their own, and Beaman delivers the injured president to the submarine's rescue vehicle before returning for Martinelli. Arkansas is then attacked by Andropov's old ship, the destroyer Yevchenko but Andropov signals that Zakarin is aboard. When Durov orders missiles fired at the surfaced submarine, Glass refuses to retaliate for fear of starting the war he is trying to prevent, and Andropov's former crew defy orders, shoot down the missiles and destroy the base headquarters, killing Durov. War averted, Glass returns Zakarin and the Russian survivors and departs under Russian escort.

Summit Premiere released Hunter Killer in the United States on October 26, 2018. It flopped, grossing $31.7 million worldwide, and drew mixed reviews, with a 38% Rotten Tomatoes rating.

documents.title: Peterloo
documents.overview: An epic portrayal of the events surrounding the infamous 1819 Peterloo Massacre, where a peaceful pro-democracy rally at St Peter’s Field in Manchester turned into one of the bloodiest and most notorious episodes in British history. The massacre saw British government forces charge into a crowd of over 60,000 that had gathered to demand political reforms and protest against rising levels of poverty.
documents.plot:
After the Battle of Waterloo, Joseph returns home from service in the Duke of Wellington's army to Manchester and his close-knit working class family headed by parents Joshua and Nellie. Joshua, son Robert, daughter Mary, and daughter-in-law Esther all earn a living by manual labour in a cotton mill. An economic depression makes work impossible for the traumatised Joseph to find and threatens the family's livelihood. The family is sympathetic to the campaigns for equal civil and political rights for all men and against the Corn Laws that prevent them from buying cheaper imported grain. Joshua, Joseph, and Robert attend political meetings where local activists including John Knight, Samuel Bamford and John Bagguley speak out against the system of government that is elected only by the upper class and aristocracy; Nellie attends a meeting of the Manchester Female Reform Society. The local authorities, led by magistrates Colonel Fletcher, Reverend William Robert Hay, Reverend Charles Ethelston and Mr. Norris and Deputy Chief Constable Nadin, spy on the movement and wait for an excuse to arrest its leaders. The Home Secretary, Lord Sidmouth, is determined to suppress what they term 'radical' politics. When a disgruntled Londoner smashes the window of the Prince Regent's coach, Sidmouth uses this as a pretext for suspending habeas corpus.
Bamford and his friend Joseph Healey travel south to London to hear the famous activist Henry 'Orator' Hunt speak at a political meeting. Hunt has a reputation for vanity but Bamford persuades Manchester businessman Joseph Johnson to invite Hunt to address a mass meeting at St Peter's Fields; the Home Office discovers this invitation by intercepting Johnson's letter. Arriving at Manchester, Hunt goes into hiding in Johnson's home. Richards, a Home Office spy, is able to provoke Bagguley and fellow activists Drummond and Johnston into publicly calling for armed insurrection, leading to their arrest and imprisonment. The magistrates plan to disperse Hunt's meeting and make an example of the attendees using the local mounted militia, the Manchester and Salford Yeomanry and a regular army detachment led by General John Byng. Hunt remains certain that he can lead a peaceful rally and sidelines Bamford, when he warns of the likelihood of brutal treatment by the authorities.
On the day of the meeting, thousands of people walk into Manchester from the surrounding towns to hear Hunt speak at St Peter's Fields, including Nellie and Joshua and their family. Bamford leads a procession from Middleton but leaves in disgust on finding that it has been arranged that only Hunt will be allowed to address the crowd. A special committee of magistrates, chaired by Mr. Hulton has been assembled to break up the event. They appear to be in an upstairs room overlooking the gathering crowd. Norris, who urges restraint, is overruled. Byng has left his deputy in command of the soldiers, to attend a horse racing meet.

documents.title: Godzilla vs. Kong
documents.tagline: One Will Fall
documents.overview: In a time when monsters walk the Earth, humanity’s fight for its future sets Godzilla and Kong on a collision course that will see the two most powerful forces of nature on the planet collide in a spectacular battle for the ages.
documents.plot:
Godzilla vs. Kong is a 2021 American monster film directed by Adam Wingard, produced by Legendary Pictures, and distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures.

The story takes place on a remote island where the legendary creature Kong has been living for years. The island is home to a group of scientists who are studying Kong's behavior and trying to understand his origins. However, their research is disrupted when Godzilla, the King of the Monsters, arrives on the scene.

Godzilla is drawn to the island by the presence of a powerful artifact known as the "Heart of the Ocean," which has the ability to control and manipulate the emotions of those around it. The scientists believe that this artifact could be the key to understanding Kong's origins and potentially harnessing his power for human benefit.

As Godzilla begins to wreak havoc on the island, Kong emerges from the depths of the ocean to defend himself and his home. The two monsters engage in an epic battle, with Kong using his intelligence and agility to try and outsmart Godzilla.

However, as the fight rages on, it becomes clear that there is more at play than just a simple monster showdown. A group of humans, led by Dr. Ilene Andrews (Vera Farmiga), are secretly working to harness the power of the Heart of the Ocean for their own gain. They believe that this artifact could be the key to unlocking new technologies and advancing human civilization.

As the battle between Godzilla and Kong reaches its climax, it becomes clear that the true enemy is not the monsters themselves, but rather the humans who seek to exploit them for their own purposes. In the end, Kong emerges victorious, but not before Godzilla is severely injured.

The film ends with Kong standing victorious on the island, but also aware of the danger that he poses to humanity. The final shot is of Kong looking out at the ocean, hinting that he may one day be forced to confront his own destiny and the consequences of his actions.

Overall, Godzilla vs. Kong is a thrilling and action-packed film that explores themes of power, responsibility, and the dangers of playing with forces beyond human control.

documents.title: Alita: Battle Angel
documents.tagline: An angel falls. A warrior rises.
documents.overview: When Alita awakens with no memory of who she is in a future world she does not recognize, she is taken in by Ido, a compassionate doctor who realizes that somewhere in this abandoned cyborg shell is the heart and soul of a young woman with an extraordinary past.
documents.plot:
Alita: Battle Angel is a 2019 science fiction action film directed by Robert Rodriguez and based on the manga series "Gunnm" by Yukito Kishiro. The movie takes place in a post-apocalyptic world where humans have become extinct, and advanced technology has been left behind.

The story begins with Dr. Dyson Ido (played by Christoph Waltz), a brilliant scientist who discovers a severely damaged cyborg girl, Alita (played by Rosa Salazar), in an abandoned scrapyard. Alita is a "Gunnm," a being created from the remains of humans and advanced technology to serve as soldiers or assassins. However, Alita's creator, Dr. Ido, decides to spare her life and raise her as his own.

As Alita grows up, she begins to develop her own identity and desires, which often conflict with her programming. She becomes a skilled fighter and athlete, using her advanced technology to protect herself and those around her. Meanwhile, a powerful corporation called Iron City is seeking to exploit the remaining resources of the post-apocalyptic world.

The main antagonist, Vector (played by Mahershala Ali), is a ruthless mercenary who seeks to control Iron City and eliminate any opposition. He becomes obsessed with Alita, seeing her as a means to gain power and control over the corporation.

As Alita navigates this treacherous world, she discovers that she has a unique connection to the ancient technology of the pre-apocalyptic era. She also learns about her own past and the true nature of her existence as a Gunnm.

The plot thickens when Alita is forced to confront Vector and his allies in an epic battle. Along the way, she forms alliances with other characters, including Hugo (played by Jorge Lendeborg Jr.), a young hacker who helps her uncover the truth about her past.

Throughout the movie, Rodriguez weaves together themes of identity, humanity, and what it means to be alive. Alita's journey is a powerful exploration of self-discovery and empowerment, as she navigates a world that seeks to control and exploit her.

The film features stunning visuals, impressive action sequences, and a strong performance from Rosa Salazar as the titular character. While some critics noted that the movie deviated slightly from the original manga series, fans of the source material generally praised the adaptation's faithfulness to Kishiro's vision.

Overall, Alita: Battle Angel is a thrilling and emotionally resonant sci-fi epic that explores complex themes and features impressive action sequences. With its stunning visuals and strong performances, it's a must-see for fans of science fiction and action movies.

documents.title: Life of the Party
documents.tagline: Give life the old college try.
documents.overview: When her husband suddenly dumps her, longtime dedicated housewife Deanna turns regret into re-set by going back to college... landing in the same class and school as her daughter, who's not entirely sold on the idea. Plunging headlong into the campus experience, the increasingly outspoken Deanna – now Dee Rock – embraces freedom, fun and frat boys on her own terms, finding her true self in a senior year no one ever expected.
documents.plot: When her husband suddenly dumps her, longtime dedicated housewife Deanna turns regret into re-set by going back to college... landing in the same class and school as her daughter, who's not entirely sold on the idea. Plunging headlong into the campus experience, the increasingly outspoken Deanna – now Dee Rock – embraces freedom, fun, and frat boys on her own terms, finding her true self in a senior year no one ever expected.

documents.title: Daylight's End
documents.tagline: The Dead Rise When Daylight Ends
documents.overview: Years after a mysterious plague has devastated the planet and turned most of humanity into blood-hungry creatures, a rogue drifter on a vengeful hunt stumbles across a band of survivors in an abandoned police station and reluctantly agrees to try to help them defend themselves and escape to the sanctuary they so desperately need.
documents.plot:
Daylight's End is a 2016 American post-apocalyptic horror action film directed by William Kaufman and written by Chad Law. Johnny Strong stars as Thomas Rourke, a drifter who agrees to help a group of survivors, played by Lance Henriksen, Louis Mandylor, Hakeem Kae-Kazim, among others, to escape to safety. The mixed martial arts fighter Krzysztof Soszynski plays the leader of the vampire-like creatures that hunt them.

A plague has turned most of humanity into savage, vampire-like creatures that cannot survive in sunlight, and civilization has collapsed. The infected hide in dark places during the day and hunt at night. Rourke, a hardened loner traveling the empty highways of Texas in search of the creature responsible for the death of his wife, arrives in a small town where a woman named Sam and her companions are being attacked by looters. Rourke kills the attackers, and Sam tells him about a group of survivors holed up in an old police station in Dallas, which still has running water and electricity.

When they reach the station at sunset, the creatures attack, and Rourke glimpses a huge infected that appears to lead the pack. Inside, the survivors, many of them former police officers, are led by Chief Frank Hill, who distrusts the newcomer, disarms him and locks him in a cell for the night. Rourke learns that Sam's group has located a cargo plane and that the survivors plan to fly to a much larger colony in Baja California. With dawn their only window of safety, the group must make it from the station to the airfield, but a series of setbacks forces them to fight their way through hordes of infected, and Rourke's personal vendetta against the pack leader puts his own goals at odds with the survival of the others.

The film received a modest release and was well received by several genre critics. Mike Wilson of Bloody Disgusting wrote that it was neither cerebral nor original but still an enjoyable romp, Hugo Ozman of Screen Anarchy called it a solid thriller and suggested Kaufman deserved a big-budget project, and Mark L. Miller of Ain't It Cool News felt that its well-shot action made up for its debt to 1980s action films.

documents.title: The Nightingale
documents.tagline: Her song will not be silenced.
documents.overview: In 1825, Clare, a 21-year-old Irish convict, chases a British soldier through the rugged Tasmanian wilderness, bent on revenge for a terrible act of violence he committed against her family. She enlists the services of an Aboriginal tracker who is also marked by trauma from his own violence-filled past.
documents.plot: In 1825, Clare, a 21-year-old Irish convict, chases a British soldier through the rugged Tasmanian wilderness, bent on revenge for a terrible act of violence he committed against her family. She enlists the services of an Aboriginal tracker who is also marked by trauma from his own violence-filled past.

documents.title: Bright
documents.overview: In an alternate present-day where magical creatures live among us, two L.A. cops become embroiled in a prophesied turf battle.
documents.plot:
Bright is a 2017 American fantasy action film directed by David Yates and written by Max Landis. The movie takes place in a world where magic has been outlawed, and orcs have taken over the city of Portland.

The story follows two detectives, Daryl Ward (Will Smith), a human cop, and Nick Jakoby (Joel Edgerton), an orc cop, who are forced to work together to solve a murder case. The victim is a young girl named Beth Harmon (Lucy Fry), who was found dead in the woods with a magical amulet around her neck.

As Daryl and Nick delve deeper into the case, they discover that the amulet is one of five magical orbs created by the ancient elf king, King Elfhelm. The orbs are said to have the power to bring about peace between humans and orcs, but they also attract the attention of a powerful sorcerer named Berruk (Ed Skrein), who seeks to use their power for his own gain.

As the investigation unfolds, Daryl and Nick must navigate the complex web of human and orc politics in Portland, all while facing their own prejudices and biases. Along the way, they are aided by a wise old elf named Professor Stone (Michael Stuhlbarg) and a young elf named Elara Vex (Noomi Rapace).

Throughout the movie, Daryl and Nick's partnership is put to the test as they learn to trust each other and work together to solve the case. Along the way, they also discover that Beth Harmon was not just an innocent victim, but rather a key player in a larger conspiracy involving the magical orbs.

As the story reaches its climax, Daryl and Nick must face off against Berruk and his minions in a battle to control the magical orbs and bring about peace between humans and orcs. In the end, they succeed in defeating Berruk and shattering the magical orbs, but not before realizing that their partnership has changed them both forever.

Overall, Bright is a visually stunning film with a unique blend of fantasy and action elements. The movie explores themes of prejudice, trust, and redemption, and features a talented cast of characters. While it received mixed reviews from critics, fans of the genre have praised its originality and entertainment value.

documents.title: Resident Evil: Vendetta
documents.original_title: バイオハザード ヴェンデッタ
documents.tagline: Kill evil or die trying.
documents.overview: BSAA Chris Redfield enlists the help of government agent Leon S. Kennedy and Professor Rebecca Chambers from Alexander Institute of Biotechnology to stop a death merchant with a vengeance from spreading a deadly virus in New York.
documents.plot:
Resident Evil: Vendetta, released in Japan as Biohazard: Vendetta, is a 2017 English-language Japanese computer-animated action horror film set in the universe of Capcom's Resident Evil video games. It was directed by Takanori Tsujimoto, produced by Marza Animation Planet with Capcom producer Hiroyuki Kobayashi, and executive produced by the horror director Takashi Shimizu. The film brings together three of the series' best-known characters, Chris Redfield, Leon S. Kennedy and Rebecca Chambers, and it was released in Japanese cinemas on 27 May 2017, with a free PlayStation VR promotional experience released a few days earlier.

In 2014, Chris Redfield, an agent of the Bioterrorism Security Assessment Alliance, is pursuing Glenn Arias, a former CIA operative turned arms dealer. Arias blames the United States government for a drone strike that killed his friends and family, including his bride, at his own wedding, and he is now developing and smuggling biological weapons into the country. Chris leads a raid on a mansion in Mexico to rescue an undercover informant, but his team is wiped out by zombies and traps, and he survives only to discover that the informant has been turned into a zombie under Arias's control.

Months later, Professor Rebecca Chambers, a former member of the S.T.A.R.S. unit, is researching a new strain called the Animality Virus, which can remain dormant in a host until it is activated by a trigger. Arias's associate Maria Gomez attacks the laboratory and releases the virus, and Rebecca survives only by developing a vaccine. Recognising similarities with the parasite Las Plagas, she and Chris seek out Leon, who is struggling with guilt after a recent outbreak, to join the investigation. When Rebecca is captured and infected with a vaccine-resistant strain, Chris and Leon uncover Arias's plan for a massive viral attack on New York City and must race to rescue her and stop the outbreak.

The film emphasises action set pieces, including gunfights, close-quarters combat and a motorcycle chase, while its villain is motivated by grief and a desire for revenge. A scene involving zombie dogs was almost cut but was kept at the director's insistence.

Resident Evil: Vendetta received mixed reviews from the small number of critics who reviewed it, with about 43 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and it was praised mainly for its animation and action sequences while its story was considered thin.

documents.title: Hotel Transylvania 3: Summer Vacation
documents.tagline: Family vacation. It will suck the life out of you.
documents.overview: Dracula, Mavis, Johnny and the rest of the Drac Pack take a vacation on a luxury Monster Cruise Ship, where Dracula falls in love with the ship’s captain, Ericka, who’s secretly a descendant of Abraham Van Helsing, the notorious monster slayer.
documents.plot:
