Hotel Transylvania 3: Summer Vacation is a 2018 American animated monster comedy film directed by Genndy Tartakovsky and produced by Sony Pictures Animation. The movie serves as the third installment in the Hotel Transylvania franchise.

The story begins with Count Dracula (Adam Sandler) preparing for his daughter Mavis's (Selena Gomez) wedding to Jonathan (Andy Samberg). However, on the eve of the ceremony, a werewolf named Wayne (Kevin James) crashes the party and steals the bride. In an attempt to rescue Mavis, Dracula sets sail on a cruise ship called the "Dreadful Child" with his friends, including Frankenstein's monster (Steve Buscemi), the Invisible Man (David Spade), and the Wolfman (Robert Smigel).

As they embark on their journey, the group faces various obstacles, including sea monsters, pirates, and a rival cruise line run by the evil Captain Cutler (Peter Criss). Along the way, Dracula begins to reconnect with his daughter and learns to let go of his overprotectiveness.

Meanwhile, Mavis is being pursued by Jonathan's werewolf friend, Wayne. As they try to outsmart each other, they develop feelings for each other, but their love is put to the test when they are forced to confront their respective pasts.

Throughout the movie, Dracula and Mavis grow closer as they face various challenges together. They also learn valuable lessons about trust, acceptance, and embracing change. The film features a range of humor, from slapstick comedy to witty one-liners, making it an entertaining ride for audiences of all ages.

As the story unfolds, the group faces its greatest challenge yet: a showdown with Captain Cutler and his pirate crew. In the end, Dracula and Mavis successfully rescue their friends and find love in the process. The movie concludes on a heartwarming note, with the entire cast coming together to celebrate the power of friendship and acceptance.

Overall, Hotel Transylvania 3: Summer Vacation is a fun and lighthearted film that explores themes of family, love, and self-discovery. With its colorful characters, engaging storyline, and hilarious humor, it's sure to delight both kids and adults alike.

documents.title: Wonder Park
documents.tagline: Dream Bigger
documents.overview: A young girl named June with a big imagination makes an incredible discovery -- the amusement park of her dreams has come to life. Filled with the world's wildest rides operated by fun-loving animals, the excitement never ends. But when trouble hits, June and her misfit team of furry friends begin an unforgettable journey to save the park.
documents.plot:
Wonder Park is a 2019 American animated fantasy adventure comedy produced by Paramount Animation and Nickelodeon Movies, with animation by Ilion Animation Studios, from a screenplay by Josh Appelbaum and André Nemec. Brianna Denski voices the young heroine June Bailey, with Jennifer Garner and Matthew Broderick as her parents and Mila Kunis, John Oliver, Kenan Thompson, Ken Jeong, Norbert Leo Butz and Ken Hudson Campbell as the park's animals. Director Dylan Brown was dismissed by Paramount in early 2018, and the film was released without a credited director on March 15, 2019.

June is an imaginative girl who, with her mother, invents Wonderland, a magical amusement park run by talking animals: Boomer the blue bear, Greta the wild boar, the beaver brothers Gus and Cooper, the porcupine Steve, who secretly loves Greta, and the chimpanzee Peanut, who builds new rides from the ideas whispered to him by June's mother. When her mother falls ill and leaves for treatment, June abandons the game and burns her park plans. Sent off to maths camp, she fears her father cannot cope without her and escapes from the bus to head home.

Lost in the woods, she discovers a real Wonderland, now run-down and engulfed by a menacing cloud called the Darkness that is devouring the park. With the animals she tries to restart the Clockwork Swings, the machine at the heart of the park, but they are attacked by the Chimpanzombies, former plush toys that serve the Darkness. Separated from the others, June finds Peanut hiding in Zero-G Land, where he admits he is lost without the voice in his head. June realises that the Darkness grew out of her own despair over her mother's illness.

When she confesses this, the hurt animals turn their backs on her, and the Chimpanzombies seize Peanut. Discovering that she has been the source of the park's ideas all along, June repairs a ride, catches up with her friends and convinces them she wants to help. She plunges into the Darkness to rescue Peanut, promising to be his imaginative voice, and he conjures an escape slide. Realising that the Clockwork Swings are keyed to her own handwritten name, they restart the machine and clear the Darkness. June returns home to her recovered mother, and together they build a backyard Wonderland.

Wonder Park grossed about 124 million dollars worldwide against a budget estimated at 80 to 100 million dollars, and received generally negative reviews.

documents.title: The SpongeBob Movie: Sponge on the Run
documents.original_title: The SpongeBob Movie: Sponge on the Run
documents.tagline: They're Not in Bikini Bottom Anymore.
documents.overview: When his best friend Gary is suddenly snatched away, SpongeBob takes Patrick on a madcap mission far beyond Bikini Bottom to save their pink-shelled pal.
documents.plot:
The SpongeBob Movie: Sponge on the Run is a 2020 animated adventure comedy film directed by Tim Hill, based on the characters from the Nickelodeon television series SpongeBob SquarePants. The movie follows the story of SpongeBob and his pet snail Gary as they embark on an epic journey to save their home of Bikini Bottom.

The movie begins with SpongeBob (voiced by Tom Kenny) and Patrick Star (voiced by Bill Fagerbakke) trying to adopt a baby, but their plans are foiled when the adoption is rejected. Feeling defeated, SpongeBob decides to take Gary on a road trip to the Fry Cook Hall of Fame in Atlanta, Georgia, where he hopes to find inspiration for his life.

However, things quickly go awry as they get lost and kidnapped by King Poseidon (voiced by Rob Paulsen), who intends to use Gary's DNA to create an army of super-soldier snails. SpongeBob and Patrick must navigate through the underwater city of Atlantis, avoiding various obstacles and enemies along the way.

As they journey deeper into Atlantis, SpongeBob and Patrick meet a group of rebels led by Mermaid Man (voiced by Mr. Lawrence) and Barnacle Boy (voiced by Ernest Borgnine), who are fighting against King Poseidon's tyranny. The duo joins forces with the rebels to rescue Gary and stop King Poseidon's evil plans.

Throughout their adventure, SpongeBob and Patrick encounter various familiar characters from the show, including Sandy Cheeks (voiced by Carolyn Lawrence) and Squidward Tentacles (voiced by Rodger Bumpass). They also meet new characters, such as Mindy (voiced by Katie Layden), a young mermaid who becomes SpongeBob's love interest.

As the story unfolds, SpongeBob and Patrick face numerous challenges and setbacks, but their friendship and determination ultimately lead them to success. In the end, they successfully rescue Gary and defeat King Poseidon, saving Bikini Bottom from destruction.

The movie features stunning animation, witty humor, and a heartwarming storyline that celebrates the power of friendship and perseverance. With its colorful characters, engaging plot, and exciting action sequences, The SpongeBob Movie: Sponge on the Run is a fun and entertaining film that is sure to delight both old and new fans of the beloved Nickelodeon series.

[No additional information available]

documents.title: Sicario: Day of the Soldado
documents.tagline: No rules this time
documents.overview: Agent Matt Graver teams up with operative Alejandro Gillick to prevent Mexican drug cartels from smuggling terrorists across the United States border.
documents.plot:
Sicario: Day of the Soldado, also known as Sicario 2: Soldado, is a 2018 American action crime thriller directed by Stefano Sollima and written by Taylor Sheridan. A sequel to Sicario (2015), it sees Benicio del Toro, Josh Brolin, Jeffrey Donovan and Raoul Trujillo reprise their roles, with Isabela Merced, Manuel Garcia-Rulfo and Catherine Keener joining the cast.

After an ISIS suicide bombing kills fifteen people in a Kansas City grocery store, the government authorizes CIA officer Matt Graver to take extreme action against Mexican cartels suspected of smuggling the bombers across the border. Graver and the Department of Defense decide to ignite a war between the cartels, and he recruits operative Alejandro Gillick, using a private military contractor for deniability. Gillick assassinates a Matamoros cartel lawyer in Mexico City, while Graver's team kidnaps Isabel Reyes, daughter of rival Sonoran kingpin Carlos Reyes, in a false flag operation, then stages a DEA rescue in Texas. As they return her to Mexico, their corrupt police escort turns on them, and the Americans kill 25 Mexican police officers in the firefight. Isabel, suspecting the truth, flees into the desert, and Gillick follows her.

When investigators find that at least two of the bombers were domestic terrorists, the Secretary of Defense abandons the mission and orders Isabel and Gillick killed to hide American involvement. Gillick refuses and goes rogue to protect her, and the two pose as migrants and pay smugglers to cross into the U.S. At the border, Miguel, a young Mexican American recruited by the traffickers, recognizes Gillick from an earlier encounter, and the gang seizes them. As an initiation, Miguel is made to shoot the hooded Gillick in the head. Graver's team, having watched by satellite, wipes out the gang and, defying orders, takes Isabel to the U.S. to enter witness protection. Gillick, shot only through the cheek, survives and kills his pursuers. A year later, a heavily tattooed Miguel goes to meet his gang contact and finds Gillick waiting, ready to discuss his future as a sicario.

Sony Pictures Releasing distributed the film in North America from June 29, 2018, with Lionsgate handling most international markets; it is dedicated to the first film's composer, Jóhann Jóhannsson. It grossed $75.8 million worldwide. Critics found it less subversive than its predecessor but a stylish thriller, giving it 62% on Rotten Tomatoes and 61 on Metacritic.

documents.title: Tully
documents.tagline: See how the mother half lives.
documents.overview: Marlo, a mother of three, including a newborn, is gifted a night nanny by her brother. Hesitant at first, she quickly forms a bond with the thoughtful, surprising, and sometimes challenging nanny named Tully.
documents.plot:
Marlo is pregnant with an unplanned third child with her husband Drew. They have a daughter, Sarah, and a son, Jonah, who has an undiagnosed behavioral disorder. Trying to reduce his sensitivity to external stimuli, Marlo brushes his skin nightly. Craig, Marlo's wealthy brother, offers to pay for a night nanny as a baby gift, but she rebuffs him. Marlo has dreams of an underwater mermaid, and also of her son's tantrums.
After giving birth to a girl, Mia, Marlo quickly becomes even more overwhelmed and exhausted than before. After the principal of Jonah's school again recommends that he be placed in a different school because they cannot handle him, Marlo erupts at her and leaves angrily. Afterwards she gets out the phone number for the night nanny.
That night, Tully, the nanny, arrives at Marlo's house and immediately settles in to take control. Despite initial awkwardness, they develop a close friendship over the course of several nights. Tully proves to be an exceptional nanny and also cleans the house and bakes cupcakes for Jonah's class. Tully explains that she is there mostly not for Mia herself, but to help and support Marlo. Marlo begins re-engaging with her family and self, singing, cooking nice family meals, and having fun with her kids. When Marlo mentions that she and Drew have not had sex for some time, and that Drew has a fantasy about diner waitresses, Tully puts on a waitress uniform that Marlo had previously purchased but never used and, with Marlo coaching, has sex with Drew.
One night Tully arrives visibly distressed. She has fought with her "enmeshed" roommate, due to her roommate's anger over her bringing home men. Tully impulsively suggests going into the city for drinks, to which Marlo reluctantly agrees; they drive to Marlo's old neighborhood, Bushwick, Brooklyn. At a bar Tully suddenly tells her she can no longer work for her anymore, explaining that she was there only to "bridge a gap." Marlo yells at Tully for being immature and not understanding how aging is going to steal Tully's youthful body and demeanor. Marlo impulsively steals a bike and rides to her former girlfriend’s apartment, where Marlo herself used to live, but no one answers the door. Tully suggests she may be taking things too far. When Marlo's breast becomes painfully engorged with milk, Tully takes her into a bar bathroom and helps her express the milk. On their way home, Marlo falls asleep at the wheel, ends up in a river trapped underwater in the car, and Tully as a mermaid comes to rescue her.
She is taken to a hospital, where a psychiatrist informs a surprised Drew that Marlo was suffering from extreme sleep deprivation and exhaustion. Drew admits he does not know much about the nanny, and when asked for Marlo's maiden name, he says "Tully".
In flashbacks, events that Marlo and Tully experienced together now show Marlo alone. Tully comes to Marlo's hospital room to say goodbye, and each thanks the other for keeping her alive before Tully leaves.

documents.title: Prey
documents.tagline: On the loose... and he's hungry.
documents.overview: A zoo veterinarian gets caught up in a grisly adventure as she finds herself leading the city-wide hunt for a monstrous lion terrorizing the Dutch capital of Amsterdam.
documents.plot:
Prey (Dutch: Prooi), also known as Uncaged, is a 2016 Dutch action comedy horror film written and directed by Dick Maas about a man-eating lion loose in Amsterdam. It stars Sophie van Winden, Julian Looman and Mark Frost, with Rienus Krul, Theo Pont and Victor Löw, and was released on 13 October 2016.

When a family is found slaughtered on a farm outside Amsterdam, Chief Inspector Olaf Brinkers suspects that this is no ordinary crime and calls in Lizzy, a veterinarian at the ARTIS zoo who spent several years in Tanzania. She quickly confirms his fears: the victims were killed by a large male lion. Later that day a golfer is mauled in broad daylight, proving that the animal has moved into the city, but Police Commissioner Zaimberg refuses to accept the evidence until a delivery driver is also killed. Ignoring Lizzy's advice to hire a professional hunter, Zaimberg calls in his cousin Theo, an amateur whose experience is limited to game farms, and the hunt ends in disaster for Theo and his son. When the lion attacks passengers on a city tram, its presence can no longer be hidden, and the humiliated commissioner finally agrees to Lizzy's plan. She summons Jack Delarue, an eccentric English big game hunter who uses a wheelchair and who also happens to be her former boyfriend, a development that causes friction with her current partner Dave, a television news cameraman. Delarue immediately clashes with Zaimberg by proposing to use a victim's body as bait, while further deaths and a bungled police operation, in which armed officers mistakenly open fire on a group of army veterans conducting their own hunt, push the city toward panic. As Lizzy, Delarue and Dave pursue the lion through the streets and into the university's medical building, the hunters discover that their prey is cunning, relentless and seemingly everywhere at once.

Prey received mostly positive reviews from critics in the Netherlands. Floortje Smit of de Volkskrant called it an entertaining thriller and a fine addition to Maas's body of work, full of jabs at Dutch gossip and regulatory zeal, while Bart van der Put of Het Parool gave it a mixed review, finding it weaker than the director's earlier films. Despite the positive notices, the film was a box-office flop in the Netherlands, although it found success in China.

documents.title: Mary Poppins Returns
documents.tagline: Magic Always Returns.
documents.overview: Mary Poppins returns to the Banks family and helps them evade grave dangers by taking them on magical, musical adventures.
documents.plot:
Mary Poppins Returns is a 2018 musical fantasy film directed by Rob Marshall and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1964 original film, Mary Poppins, and continues the story of the beloved nanny.

The film takes place 25 years after the events of the original. Michael Banks (Ben Whishaw), now an adult, is struggling to cope with the loss of his father, George Banks (David Tomlinson). The family's life has become dull and grey, lacking the magic and wonder that Mary Poppins brought into their lives.

When the children begin to act out and rebel against their parents' strict rules, Michael realizes that he needs help. He turns to an old friend, Jack (Lin-Manuel Miranda), who is now a struggling artist and musician. Jack introduces Michael to his cousin, Topsy Kettering (Emily Blunt), a wealthy and eccentric woman who claims to be the long-lost sister of Mary Poppins.

Topsy reveals that she has been keeping an eye on the Banks children from afar and believes that they need Mary Poppins' unique brand of magic in their lives. Michael is skeptical at first, but eventually agrees to let Topsy find Mary Poppins for him.

As the story unfolds, we see flashbacks of Mary Poppins (Emily Blunt) returning to London after a long absence. She is still as magical and mysterious as ever, with a newfound sense of purpose and determination. With the help of her trusty umbrella, Mary Poppins sets out to bring joy and wonder back into the lives of the Banks children.

Throughout the film, Mary Poppins uses her unique brand of magic to teach the children valuable lessons about love, loss, and the importance of family. Along the way, she also helps Michael come to terms with his own grief and find a new sense of purpose in life.

As the story reaches its climax, Mary Poppins reveals that she has been searching for a special place where the magic can be shared with others. She takes the children on a fantastical journey through London, using her umbrella to transport them to different locations around the city.

In the end, Mary Poppins helps the Banks family find closure and healing, and Michael comes to terms with his own emotions. The film ends on a hopeful note, with the entire family coming together to celebrate the magic of life and the power of love and connection.

Overall, Mary Poppins Returns is a heartwarming and visually stunning film that pays tribute to the original while also introducing new characters and themes. With its memorable songs, impressive choreography, and Emily Blunt's iconic performance as Mary Poppins, this movie is sure to delight audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Flatliners
documents.tagline: You haven't lived until you've died
documents.overview: Five medical students, hoping to understand the mystery of what lies beyond life, embark on a dangerous experiment. When their hearts are stopped for a short period of time, they have a near-death experience…
documents.plot:
Courtney is a medical student who is obsessed with the afterlife. She invites her classmates, Jamie and Sophia, to join her in an experiment, in an unused hospital room: using defibrillation to stop her heart for sixty seconds while recording her brain. She assures them they would not be held responsible for any accidents. Sophia is against this, but Jamie does it anyway. After sixty seconds, they are unable to revive her until a fellow student, Ray, steps in to help. Marlo, another medical student, arrives and learns of the experiment.
Courtney begins to recall experiences about increased intelligence and euphoria. Envious, Jamie flatlines, and has a disturbing near-death experience as he meets his ex-girlfriend. Marlo and Sophia follow suit, increasing the duration of time they are down. During Sophia's turn they are nearly caught and flee the hospital.
The visions experienced by those who flatlined are: Courtney sees her sister Tessa, who died in a car crash Courtney caused; Jamie sees the baby he begged his ex-girlfriend to abort; Marlo sees a patient named Cyrus, who died when she accidentally mixed up his medication; and Sophia sees Irina, whose life she ruined out of spite, allowing Sophia to become valedictorian. Everyone keeps their visions to their individual selves.
Courtney, traumatized by her visions, records a message apologizing and admitting that her interest in flatlining was due to the death of her sister, not for scientific discovery. She dies having been pushed off a fire escape by the ghost of her sister. The others are devastated. They think they may be implicated if their experiments are discovered. They attempt to clean Courtney's apartment of all evidence. Marlo goes to the morgue to find Courtney's phone, where she is disturbed by more visions.
On his boat, Jamie again hears the cries of a baby and a woman weeping. He falls out of his boat and swims to the dock where a figure stabs his hand.
Courtney's recording discloses they all had similar visions. They admit the mistakes they made and come to the conclusion that their haunting experiences are hallucinations owing to guilt from their sins, not the paranormal. The only one who did not flatline, Ray, initially disbelieves what is happening.
Sophia's apology to Irina is accepted. Jamie discovers his ex-girlfriend has kept their baby and pledges to provide for his son. Ray and Marlo get into a fight when he uncovers her attempt at hiding Cyrus' cause of death and she refuses to confess. Marlo hallucinates being suffocated while driving and crashes her car. Tired of being haunted by her hallucinations, Marlo flatlines on her own in the hope of asking Cyrus for forgiveness. She sees Courtney, who tells Marlo that she needs to forgive herself. Ray, Sophia and Jamie arrive to resuscitate Marlo.
Marlo confesses to the Dean and is held on probation. Marlo, Ray, Sophia and Jamie meet to reminisce about Courtney.

documents.title: Gifted
documents.tagline: How do you create an ordinary life for an extraordinary girl?
documents.overview: Frank, a single man raising his child prodigy niece Mary, is drawn into a custody battle with his mother.
documents.plot:
In St. Petersburg, Florida, seven-year-old Mary Adler, a mathematical genius, lives with her uncle and de facto guardian, Frank. Her best friend is her 43-year-old neighbor, Roberta Taylor. Frank, a former philosophy professor and now boat mechanic, feels strongly that Mary should attend a normal elementary school so she can have a normal childhood.
In first grade, Mary shows remarkable mathematical talent, which impresses her teacher, Ms. Stevenson. It emerges that Mary's mother, Diane, had been a promising mathematician, dedicated to the Navier–Stokes problem (then, one of the unsolved Millennium Prize Problems) before taking her own life when Mary was six months old. Mary has lived with Frank ever since.
Despite Mary's initial disdain for average children her own age, and her boredom with their classwork, she begins to bond with them when she brings her one-eyed cat, Fred, for show-and-tell. Later, she defends a classmate from a bully on the school bus. The principal, having discovered Mary's math talent, encourages Frank to send Mary to a private school for gifted children, offering the opportunity of a scholarship. Frank turns it down, based on his family's experiences with similar schools.
The principal contacts Frank's estranged mother and Mary's maternal grandmother, Evelyn. Evelyn, a former mathematician herself, believes that people with capabilities such as Mary's have an obligation to use their talents to help further society, and feels that Mary should be specially tutored in preparation for a life devoted to mathematics, as Diane was. But Frank is adamant that his sister would want Mary to be in a normal school and have the childhood she did not have.
Evelyn sues Frank for full custody. While she is on the stand in court, it is revealed that not only did Evelyn homeschool Diane, she kept her socially isolated, so that she could be completely focused on mathematics. When Diane and her teenage boyfriend ran away to a ski resort, Evelyn pressed kidnapping charges and filed a lawsuit against his parents until he cut ties with Diane. Diane attempted suicide for the first time shortly after, something Evelyn argues was an isolated incident. When Frank takes the stand, he admits working at a low-paying job without health insurance. His lawyer, worried that the judge will side with Evelyn due to her financial resources, convinces Frank to take a deal orchestrated by Evelyn's lawyer.
Mary is placed in foster care, where she can attend the private school. Evelyn waits until her 12th birthday, when she will be able to decide where she wants to live. The foster parents live near Frank, and he is entitled to scheduled visits. Mary is devastated and refuses to see Frank when he tries to visit. Thanks to a tip from Ms. Stevenson, Frank rescues Fred from the pound moments before he is about to be put down. Frank realizes that Evelyn, who is allergic to cats, is overseeing Mary's education in the guest house of the foster home.

While the few sailors who are still alive barely manage to survive, their families push for accurate information and a British officer struggles to obtain from the Russian government a permit to attempt a rescue before it is late. But general incompetence are against all their efforts.

documents.title: The Square
documents.overview: A prestigious Stockholm museum's chief art curator finds himself in times of both professional and personal crisis as he attempts to set up a controversial new exhibit.
documents.plot:
Christian is the curator of the X-Royal art museum in Stockholm, formerly the Royal Palace. He is interviewed by journalist Anne, struggling to explain museum parlance. Later, Christian is pulled into a confrontation at a pedestrian zone, after which he notices that his smartphone and wallet are missing, along with his cufflinks, presumably stolen in a confidence trick. Christian is able to track the position of his phone on his computer, which he and his assistant Michael trace to a large apartment block.
They write a threatening anonymous letter demanding the return of the phone and wallet by depositing them at a nearby 7-Eleven. Christian puts a copy of the letter through each apartment mailbox that night. Several days later, a package for him is deposited at the store, containing the phone and the completely untouched wallet.
Euphoric after the success of his plan, Christian goes to a party where he meets Anne again, before ending up in her apartment. After the two have sex, Anne offers to throw away a used condom but he steadfastly refuses to hand it over to her. They argue over the situation, as she believes he does not trust her to dispose of the semen rather than take it. Several days later, Anne meets Christian in the museum and states she is looking for more than casual sex. She asks him if he feels the same, but Christian is evasive. When Anne later tries to call him, he does not pick up the phone.
The day after picking up the package, Christian is informed that a second one has arrived for him at the 7-Eleven. Suspicious, he sends Michael to pick it up. In the store, Michael is confronted by a young Arab boy who states that his parents believe that he is a thief because of the letter and demands that Christian apologizes to him and his family. Otherwise, the boy threatens to create "chaos" for him.
Later, the boy visits Christian's home and confronts him, along with his two young daughters, on the staircase. Christian tries to send him away but the boy begins to knock on doors and screaming for help. In a fit of frustration, Christian pushes the boy down the stairs, though no one comes to his aid. Disturbed, Christian desperately searches the trash outside the house for a note which contains the boy's phone number. After finding it and unsuccessfully trying to call him, Christian records an apologetic video message.
In the midst of these troubles, Christian has to manage the promotion of a new exhibition centered on an art piece called The Square by Lola Arias, which is described in the artist's statement: "The Square is a sanctuary of trust and caring. Within it we all share equal rights and obligations."
The advertising agency commissioned by the museum to promote The Square states that they need to harness social media attention with something other than the uncontroversial and bland artist's statement.

documents.title: Death Race: Beyond Anarchy
documents.overview: Black Ops specialist Connor Gibson infiltrates a maximum security prison to take down legendary driver Frankenstein in a violent and brutal car race.
documents.plot:
Death Race: Beyond Anarchy is a 2018 American science fiction action film directed by Don Michael Paul. It is the fourth and final entry in the Death Race series that began with the 2008 remake of Death Race 2000, and it serves as a direct sequel to the 2008 film. Zach McGowan stars as Connor Gibson, with Danny Trejo returning as Goldberg, and Danny Glover, Frederick Koehler and Christine Marzano in supporting roles. The film was released on DVD and digital platforms on 2 October 2018.

The story takes place in the Sprawl, an enormous privately run prison that holds hundreds of thousands of inmates. Inside, the brutal Death Race competition, in which convicts drive armoured vehicles in deadly races, has been outlawed by a new warden appointed by the prison's corporate owner, Weyland International. The warden's mission is to eliminate Frankenstein, the masked Death Race champion who effectively rules the prison. When a prison SWAT team attempts to take him down, Frankenstein's loyal army of inmates massacres them, and he warns the warden that every man sent after him will meet the same fate.

A helicopter carrying new prisoners arrives, and most of the newcomers are killed by a gang known as the Cops, led by the racer Johnny Law. Two survivors fight off the entire gang: one of them is Connor, a former special forces operative who has been secretly sent into the Sprawl to assassinate Frankenstein. Inside the prison, Connor learns to navigate its lawless society, which is controlled by gangs and a black market economy, with help from veteran inmates including Goldberg and Baltimore Bob. He also grows close to Jane, the bartender at a bar run by Frankenstein, who introduces him to Baltimore Bob. To get close to his target, Connor must enter the Death Race himself, and as he competes he discovers that the authorities' motives are far from clear-cut.

The film continues the series' formula of vehicular combat, gang warfare and graphic violence, set in a more anarchic environment than the earlier prison-based instalments.

Reviews were generally negative. DVD Talk felt that it offered a mixture of old and new elements that would please fans of the series without winning over anyone who disliked the previous films, while The A.V. Club described the Death Race franchise as a younger, dumber and cheaper version of Fast & Furious.

documents.overview: The year 2050 the planet has become overpopulated, to help control population the government develops a race. The Death Race. Annually competitors race across the country scoring points for killing people with their vehicles.

documents.title: Everybody Knows
documents.tagline: Who did it?
documents.overview: Laura, a Spanish woman living in Buenos Aires, returns to her hometown outside Madrid with her Argentinian husband and children. However, the trip is upset by unexpected events that bring secrets into the open.
documents.plot:
Everybody Knows (Spanish: Todos lo saben) is a 2018 Spanish-language mystery drama written and directed by the Iranian filmmaker Asghar Farhadi. Penélope Cruz plays Laura, Javier Bardem her old friend Paco and Ricardo Darín her husband Alejandro, with Bárbara Lennie as Paco's wife Bea and Inma Cuesta as Laura's younger sister Ana. It opened the 2018 Cannes Film Festival in competition.

Laura, a Spanish woman living in Buenos Aires, returns with her teenage daughter Irene and young son Diego to her hometown near Madrid for Ana's wedding. In the town square she reunites with Paco, now a vineyard owner, while Irene flirts with a local boy. After the reception Irene goes upstairs feeling unwell, and later that night Laura finds her gone. A text message demands €300,000 and warns the family not to involve the police. As the family scrambles for the money, old resentments surface: some relatives believe Paco owes them because Laura sold him the land for his vineyard cheaply, though he was the son of the family's servants. A retired police officer advises the family privately and suggests that even relatives should be suspects.

Alejandro, a recovering alcoholic facing bankruptcy, arrives from Argentina to a cold welcome. Bea reveals that she has received the same ransom messages, and Laura confesses to Paco that Irene is his biological daughter, conceived sixteen years earlier. Despite Bea's anger and suspicion, Paco sets out to raise the ransom by selling his land, while Alejandro discovers that everyone in town already knows the truth about Irene's father. The kidnapping was arranged by Laura's niece Rocío, her estranged husband Gabriel and an accomplice, and as the plan spins out of control Rocío begs them to let Irene go. Paco delivers the money and finds Irene tied up in his car. He brings her back to her parents but returns home to find that Bea has left him. As Laura's family leave for Argentina, Rocío's suspicious mother Mariana tells her husband that they need to talk.

Everybody Knows was released in Spain in September 2018 and in the United States in February 2019, distributed internationally by Focus Features. Reviews were generally positive, with a 78% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, though its consensus called it less than the sum of its parts despite an outstanding cast.

documents.title: The Most Hated Woman in America
documents.original_title: The Most Hated Woman in America
documents.overview: The true story of Madalyn Murray O'Hair -- iconoclast, opportunist, and outspoken atheist -- from her controversial rise to her untimely demise.
documents.plot:
In 1995, Madalyn Murray O'Hair is kidnapped along with her son Garth and granddaughter Robin by three men: David Waters, Gary Karr and Danny Fry. The three abductees recognize Waters.
The scene shifts to the early 1960s. Madalyn has become a single mother of two sons, Garth and the older William J. "Billy Boy" Murray Jr., and is a proud atheist, which outrages her Christian parents. Madalyn is outraged to learn that Billy is being forced to recite the Lord's Prayer in school, so she launches a campaign to ban school prayer, ultimately resulting in a Supreme Court ruling making mandatory prayer in schools illegal. She quickly becomes labeled one of the most hated figures in America. She forms the atheist advocacy group American Atheists, recruiting Garth and Billy. Billy's devotion to his mother destroys his relationship with his wife, and he becomes a bitter alcoholic after she divorces him. He eventually quits drinking and becomes a born-again Christian, causing a deep rift with Madalyn.
Madalyn begins profiting from spirited debates with a local pastor, putting the money in offshore accounts. She hires Waters to manage the American Atheists branch; he becomes her trusted ally, especially after he confides in her about having murdered someone as a young man. Eventually, Waters has a falling out with Madalyn and is fired from American Atheists. In 1995, he demands one million dollars from Madalyn, which she refuses. Waters devises the kidnapping as a way to get the money he feels she owes him. Reporter Jack Ferguson begins covering the kidnapping and questions Billy. He gets a sketch artist to draw a picture of Fry. Ferguson joins forces with Madalyn's assistant and they slowly unravel the plot.
Back at the safe house, Karr kills Robin after she refuses his sexual advances. Panicked, Waters and Karr then kill Garth and Madalyn. Finally, Karr kills Fry after forcing him to dismember the bodies. Ferguson finally catches Waters and gets him to confess to the triple murder. Waters and Karr are both arrested and tried. Closing text reports that Karr received a life sentence; Waters received 68 years but died in prison in 2003. Billy now chairs the Religious Freedom Coalition and works to return mandated prayer to public schools, and the American Atheists continues to exist.

documents.title: Can You Ever Forgive Me?
documents.tagline: Her greatest work will be her biggest crime.
documents.overview: When a bestselling celebrity biographer is no longer able to get published because she has fallen out of step with current tastes, she turns her art form to deception.
documents.plot:
In 1991, following the critical and commercial failure of her biography of Estée Lauder, author Lee Israel struggles with financial troubles, writer's block, and alcoholism. Her only friend is her cat, which has a health issue. Lee hopes to write a biography of comedian Fanny Brice, who died in 1951, but her literary agent, Marjorie, sharply rejects the idea, noting that Brice’s life no longer interests people. Marjorie bluntly adds that Lee is not remotely successful enough to act like she does, which is to say miserable and angry all the time.
With Marjorie unable to secure her an advance for a new book regardless of subject matter, Lee resorts to selling her possessions to cover her living expenses. She sells a personal letter she received long ago from Katharine Hepburn to Anna, a used bookstore merchant and autograph dealer. Lee begins spending time with old acquaintance Jack Hock after a chance encounter with him at a gay bar called Julius’, where he reveals he has been banned from all Duane Reade locations for shoplifting.
Lee visits a Manhattan library's special collections department to research Fanny Brice and discovers two letters typewritten by Brice. She removes one of them from the building, takes it to Anna's store, and shows it to her. Anna makes Lee an offer that is lower than what she was expecting, due to the letter's bland content. Lee returns home and uses a typewriter to add a postscript to the letter, then returns to the store where Anna, now amused by what "Fanny Brice" wrote "several decades ago", offers Lee $350. She also asks Lee for advice on whether her short stories are worth publishing, but Lee, who is socially phobic, replies cautiously. Lee uses some of the $350 to pay for her cat's treatment by a veterinarian.
Emboldened by her success with selling the Brice letter, Lee starts forging and selling letters supposedly written by deceased celebrities, incorporating intimate details to command high prices. Anna, a fan of Lee's biographies, tries to initiate a romantic relationship with Lee, while also hoping for Lee's input regarding her short stories, but Lee rebuffs her.
In some of Lee's forged letters, she has Noël Coward make references to his social life that reflects his homosexuality. Paul, a used-book dealer, buys one of them from Lee and sends it to a friend of his who knew Coward. The recipient doubts Coward would have risked his privacy and relays his suspicions to Paul, who warns others, leading to Lee's customers blacklisting her. Unable to sell more forgeries, she has Jack sell them on her behalf, since the customers do not know he has a connection to Lee. She also starts stealing authentic letters from libraries and archives for Jack to sell, replacing them with forged duplicates. While Lee is out of town committing one such theft, she lets Jack stay in her apartment. Jack spends the night with a young waiter from Julius’, when Lee's cat dies.

documents.title: Thelma
documents.tagline: Unleash Your True Self. Unleash Your True Power.
documents.overview: A college student starts to experience extreme seizures. She soon learns that the violent episodes are a symptom of inexplicable abilities.
documents.plot:
Thelma is a lonely and repressed young woman from an ultra-religious Christian family who has lived a sheltered life under the protection of her father, Trond, and disabled mother, Unni. She struggles to make friends and soon after moving to Oslo to attend university begins to experience unexplained psychogenic non-epileptic seizures. When she meets another student, Anja, she discovers that her feelings for Anja trigger uncontrollable psychokinetic powers. Thelma suffers much guilt over her feelings for Anja, and wishes she was not in love with her.
While undergoing a brain tomography test to find the cause of her seizures, she begins to think about Anja and as she focuses on her, Thelma's power is set in motion and she unconsciously and unwittingly makes Anja vanish into empty space. Distraught and confused by Anja's sudden disappearance, Thelma returns home and soon remembers that when she was a little girl, she had a baby brother. Once, when feeling neglected and jealous of the attention given to her younger sibling, and wishing him to be quiet and gone, she involuntarily caused him to teleport from his crib and reappear underneath the sofa. In a final tragic incident, she caused him to disappear from his bath, and he was found trapped below the ice of a frozen lake by her father. Traumatised, Thelma's mother tried to take her own life by jumping off a bridge, but instead the failed attempt left her paraplegic. Thelma had forgotten these events. Realising her utter distress, her parents tell her the truth, which is that she is somehow able to manifest whatever she deeply wants and that she inherited the same inexplicable ability from her grandmother (who blamed herself for the disappearance of Thelma's grandfather and was kept sedated in a psychiatric nursing home by Trond). Thelma perceives that her parents have a similar fate in mind for her as her grandmother. Though Trond expresses some misgivings about drugging Thelma, Unni tells him it is their responsibility to stop Thelma.
Earlier, while visiting Anja, Thelma had recalled how her father once held her hand over a lit candle until it almost burned so that she could feel what Hell's eternal fire was like. She causes the death of her father by telekinetically making him self-combust while out boating on the unfrozen lake. Thelma realises that her power can also restore life when she revives a small dead bird. She begins to understand that her supernatural ability is also a gift and uses it to heal her mother, making her able to walk again. Along with the realisation that she can summon her power, Thelma is able to finally control it, and brings Anja back to existence. She returns to college, now with Anja as her girlfriend.

documents.title: Fahrenheit 451
documents.tagline: Knowledge is a dangerous thing
documents.overview: In an oppressive future, a 'fireman' whose duty is to destroy all books begins to question his task.
documents.plot: In an oppressive future, a 'fireman' whose duty is to destroy all books begins to question his task.

documents.title: Red Sparrow
documents.tagline: Seduce. Deceive. Repeat.
documents.overview: Prima ballerina, Dominika Egorova faces a bleak and uncertain future after she suffers an injury that ends her career. She soon turns to Sparrow School, a secret intelligence service that trains exceptional young people to use their minds and bodies as weapons. Dominika emerges as the most dangerous Sparrow after completing the sadistic training process. As she comes to terms with her new abilities, she meets a CIA agent who tries to convince her that he is the only person she can trust.
documents.plot:
In modern-day Russia, famous ballerina Dominika Egorova supports her infirm mother. Her career abruptly ends after her dance partner injures her during a performance. After the Bolshoi cuts her off, Dominika's Uncle Ivan, the deputy director of the SVR, reveals that her ex-partner, Konstantin, and a rival dancer, Sonya, who were lovers, deliberately injured her. Dominika seeks retribution by ambushing them in the Bolshoi showers and beating them with her cane, injuring both. To avoid prosecution and receive financial support, she agrees to help Ivan. She is tasked with seducing Dimitri Ustinov, a Russian gangster, in exchange for her mother's continued medical care.
Meeting at a bar, the two go to her private hotel room, where Dimitri rapes her but is quickly interrupted and garroted by Sergei Matorin, an SVR operative authorized by Ivan. They flee to a safehouse and Ivan offers Dominika a choice: become an SVR operative, or be executed for witnessing Ustinov's assassination.
Nate Nash is a CIA operative working in Moscow. While meeting with a Russian mole code-named Marble in Gorky Park, they are confronted by the police. Nash creates a diversion to ensure his contact escapes unidentified while reaching the U.S. Embassy. Nash is reassigned to the U.S. but insists he is the only person Marble will work with. Since he cannot return to Russia, he is assigned to Budapest to reestablish contact with Marble, which the SVR also deduce.
Dominika is sent to State School 4, a brutal specialist training school for "Sparrows"—operatives capable of seducing their targets with sexpionage— where she's given the alias, Katya, and revealing her true identity and profession is forbidden. She excels in her training, despite some friction with her trainer, 'the Matron'. Against Matron's recommendation, Ivan and General Vladimir Korchnoi, a high-ranking official, decide that Dominika is ready for an assignment in Budapest—to gain Nash's trust and expose Marble's identity.
In Budapest, Dominika lives with fellow "sparrow" Marta, and is supervised by station chief Maxim Volontov. She makes contact with Nash, who quickly determines she is a Russian intelligence operative and attempts to convince her to defect.
Dominika inspects Marta's room and finds she has been assigned to buy classified intelligence from Stephanie Boucher, chief of staff to a U.S. Senator. When Ivan pressures her about her slow progress with Nash, Dominika claims to be helping Marta with Boucher as well.
Marta is brutally killed by Sergei Matorin after Dominika told her about the earlier incident with Ustinov. Dominika is then warned by Sergei that the same fate would befall her should she open her mouth about that again. She contacts Nash, agrees to become a double agent in exchange for protection for her and her mother, and has sex with him.

documents.title: Ben 10 Generator Rex Heroes United
documents.tagline: Two Heroes. One Epic Battle.
documents.overview: Ben Tennyson falls through a wormhole and encounters Rex. The two heroes must unite against a foe that can absorb their powers.
documents.plot:
Ben 10/Generator Rex: Heroes United is an animated crossover special uniting Ben 10: Ultimate Alien and Generator Rex, written by Man of Action, the creative team behind both series. Structured as a double-length episode of Generator Rex, covering the third and fourth episodes of its third season, it brings Ben Tennyson into Rex's universe and redraws him and his alien forms in that show's art style. It premiered at New York Comic Con 2011 before airing in a one-hour slot on Cartoon Network on November 25, 2011, the network's second crossover special after 2007's The Grim Adventures of the KND.

A mysterious rift opens over Manhattan, and Rex Salazar, a former agent of the peacekeeping organization Providence, arrives with Agent Six and Bobo. Something comes through: Ben, transformed into Humungousaur. Mistaking him for an EVO, a human mutated by rogue nanites, Rex fights him across the city as Ben shifts into Diamondhead, Lodestar and Rath, while a strange metallic creature that also emerged from the rift slips away. Back in human form, Ben is stunned that nobody knows him. The creature self-destructs in front of Six, leaving him in a coma, and Rex blames Ben. Doctor Holiday finds the creature was nanite-based but unlike any EVO. Ben escapes confinement as Big Chill, and he and Rex meet Caesar, who admits he created the creature, Alpha, to manufacture adaptable nanites, then banished it to another dimension after it became sentient and began seizing human bodies. Ben realizes Caesar sent it into the Null Void, the alien prison where it took a cyborg body before returning.

Alpha now aims to absorb EVOs and capture Rex's Omega Nanite, the key to its perfection. At the Bug Jar, a quarantined city of EVOs, Ben fights as XLR8, Four Arms and the new Shocksquatch, but Alpha copies the Ultimatrix and takes Rex's Omega Nanite, becoming the giant Alpha-Omega. Ben merges with Rex as Upgrade and together they compress Alpha into a dense sphere. Caesar recovers the Omega Nanite and opens a rift home for Ben, who, as Upchuck, swallows the compacted Alpha before leaving. Six recovers, Caesar restores Rex's nanite, and Alpha stirs in the Null Void, hinting at a return.

Daryl Sabara voices Rex, with Yuri Lowenthal as Ben, Wally Kurth as Six, Grey DeLisle as Holiday, John DiMaggio as Bobo, J. K. Simmons as White Knight, Michael Emerson as Alpha and Freddy Rodriguez as Caesar. Fans of both series embraced the special, which reached the iTunes top 100.

documents.title: Denial
documents.tagline: The whole world knows the Holocaust happened. Now she needs to prove it.
documents.overview: Acclaimed writer and historian Deborah E. Lipstadt must battle for historical truth to prove the Holocaust actually occurred when David Irving, a renowned denier, sues her for libel.
documents.plot:
Denial is a 2016 biographical drama film directed by Mick Jackson and written by David Hare, adapted from Deborah Lipstadt's 2005 book History on Trial: My Day in Court with a Holocaust Denier. It dramatizes Irving v Penguin Books Ltd, the libel case brought against Lipstadt by the Holocaust denier David Irving. Rachel Weisz stars as Lipstadt, with Timothy Spall as Irving, Tom Wilkinson as the barrister Richard Rampton, Andrew Scott as the solicitor Anthony Julius, Alex Jennings as Justice Charles Gray and Mark Gatiss as the historian Robert Jan van Pelt, with Jack Lowden and Caren Pistorius.

Lipstadt, an American professor of Holocaust studies, has a lecture disrupted by Irving, a British writer on Nazi Germany, who sues her and her publisher for libel in England over her description of him as a Holocaust denier. Because English libel law puts the burden of proof on the defendant, Lipstadt's team, headed by Julius and Rampton, must show that Irving deliberately lied about the Holocaust. Preparing the defense, Lipstadt and Rampton visit the site of Auschwitz, where van Pelt explains how the gas chambers operated. Lipstadt bristles at Rampton's seemingly irreverent manner, and her lawyers sideline her, believing her involvement would hurt the case, while British Jewish leaders urge her to settle. The team scores an early success by flattering Irving into accepting a trial before a judge rather than a jury he might sway. Representing himself, Irving tries to twist the evidence, and his claim that the gas chamber roofs had no holes for introducing Zyklon B ("no holes, no Holocaust") dominates the press. Lipstadt wants survivors to testify, but Julius fears Irving would humiliate them. Rampton wins her trust, then dismantles Irving in cross-examination, while historians such as Richard J. Evans expose the distortions in his work. At the close, Gray unsettles the defense by asking whether Irving can be lying if he sincerely believes his claims, but Rampton argues that Irving's antisemitism proves his falsifications were deliberate. Gray finds for the defense, and her lawyers remind her that her writing was the basis of the victory. Irving later claims on television that the trial largely went his way.

Shot in London and at the Auschwitz-Birkenau State Museum, Denial premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on 11 September 2016. It received positive reviews, with an 82% Rotten Tomatoes rating that particularly praised Weisz's performance.

documents.title: Hard Target 2
documents.tagline: It's hunting season again...
documents.overview: Forced into a deadly cat-and-mouse game, a disgraced mixed martial arts fighter is hunted through the jungles of Southeast Asia.
documents.plot:
Hard Target 2 is a 2016 American action film directed by Roel Reiné, starring Scott Adkins with Robert Knepper, Temuera Morrison, Rhona Mitra and Ann Truong. Billed as a follow-up to the 1993 film Hard Target, in which Jean-Claude Van Damme played a drifter battling a human hunting operation in New Orleans, it has no narrative connection to the original and reworks its premise of people hunted for sport in a new setting.

Professional mixed martial arts fighter Wes Baylor faces Jonny Sutherland for a welterweight championship in Las Vegas. Angry at the judges' scoring, Baylor tries for a knockout and accidentally kills Sutherland in the ring. Consumed by guilt, he goes into self-imposed exile in Thailand. Six months later, he is still haunted by the tragedy and scraping by in underground fights when he attracts the attention of Jonah Aldrich, a wealthy man who offers him $1 million for a private bout in Myanmar.

On arrival, Baylor learns that there is no fight: he is to be the prey in a lethal hunt organized by Aldrich for a group of rich clients. He is given a water bottle and a money belt that secretly contains a GPS tracker. The hunters include Sofia, a bullfighter named Esparto, a video game designer, a sharpshooter, a Texan and his son Tobias, and Aldrich's right-hand man Madden, supported by a unit of corrupt soldiers. Baylor kills his first pursuer at a waterfall and then meets Tha, a local woman who agrees to guide him to the border. As Aldrich escalates the hunt with armed motorcycles and rocket launchers, Baylor and Tha fight back, picking off hunters one by one. They make their way through a minefield, where an explosion buys them time to hide in a cave in which Tha finds her missing brother, an earlier target of Aldrich's game who had managed to survive in hiding. Baylor then turns the tables on the remaining hunters for a final confrontation with Aldrich, finding a measure of redemption along the way.

The film was released direct to video in 2016. Reviewers frequently noted that it could not match the original, which had been made with a much larger budget by the acclaimed director John Woo, but many judged it a respectable addition to Adkins's catalogue. Critics at HighDef Digest and MMA Torch were particularly enthusiastic, praising the fight scenes, Reiné's slick visuals and the cast of villains surrounding Adkins's sympathetic hero.

documents.title: Edge of Winter
documents.tagline: Nothing is more dangerous than a father's love.
documents.overview: When two brothers are stranded by a brutal winter storm with an unpredictable father they barely know, the boys begin to suspect their supposed protector may be their biggest threat.
documents.plot:
Edge of Winter is a 2016 Canadian psychological thriller drama film directed and written by Rob Connolly and Kyle Mann. Joel Kinnaman stars as Elliot Baker, a recently divorced father whose anger gradually takes control of him while he is stranded with his two sons in the wilderness, with Tom Holland as his teenage son Bradley and Percy Hynes White as his younger son Caleb. Rossif Sutherland and Shiloh Fernandez play Luc and Richard, two hunters, and Rachelle Lefevre plays Karen. The film was produced by Kyle Mann and Jonathan Bronfman and shot in and around Sudbury, Ontario.

Elliot, who has just been fired for punching his boss, eagerly seizes a chance to spend time with his sons, Bradley and Caleb, when their mother drops them off for a visit. When the boys find his shotgun, he decides to turn the discovery into a bonding lesson in firearm safety and takes them to his old lumber yard in the snowy wilderness, but the trip is strained from the start; Elliot finds messages on Bradley's phone complaining about spending time with him and hides the phone. On the way home, with Bradley at the wheel because Elliot has been drinking, an argument between the brothers sends the car off the road, where it becomes stuck. During the night in the car, Caleb lets slip that their stepfather has been promoted and the family will soon be moving to London, and Elliot reacts with fury. Facing the risk of freezing or starving if they try to walk to the main road, they make for a hunting cabin, where Elliot rescues Bradley after he falls through the ice. Their uneasy refuge is disturbed when two hunters, Richard and Luc, arrive seeking shelter. Increasingly paranoid and desperate not to lose his sons, Elliot treats the strangers as a threat, and his behavior turns violent, leaving the boys to realize that the greatest danger they face may be their own father as they try to find a way to escape and bring help.

Edge of Winter received mixed reviews, with scores of 50% on both Rotten Tomatoes and Metacritic. Frank Scheck of The Hollywood Reporter praised Kinnaman's superb performance and the boys' quietly terrified reactions, while finding that the film ultimately succumbed to tired thriller conventions.

documents.title: All Eyez on Me
documents.tagline: Legends never die
documents.overview: All Eyez on Me chronicles the life and legacy of Tupac Shakur, including his rise to superstardom as a hip-hop artist, actor, poet and activist, as well as his imprisonment and prolific, controversial time at Death Row Records. Against insurmountable odds, Tupac rose to become a cultural icon whose career and persona both continue to grow long after his passing.
documents.plot: All Eyez on Me chronicles the life and legacy of Tupac Shakur, including his rise to superstardom as a hip-hop artist, actor, poet and activist, as well as his imprisonment and prolific, controversial time at Death Row Records. documents.title: The Death of Stalin
documents.tagline: In the Kremlin, no one can hear you scheme
documents.overview: When dictator Joseph Stalin dies, his parasitic cronies square off in a frantic power struggle to become the next Soviet leader. As they bumble, brawl and back-stab their way to the top, the question remains — just who is running the government?
documents.plot:
For 20 years, Stalin's NKVD security forces have imposed The Great Terror. Those on Stalin's list of 'enemy' names are arrested, exiled or shot.
On the night of 1 March 1953, Josef Stalin demands the director of Radio Moscow provide a recording of a live recital of Mozart's Piano Concerto No. 23 after the show has concluded. The director recalls the audience and orchestra and records the recreated concert. Pianist Maria Yudina, who hates the cruel dictator, only complies after being bribed and slips a note into the recording before it is couriered to Stalin.
Stalin is hosting a tense, but rowdy, gathering of Central Committee members at Kuntsevo Dacha. As Foreign Minister Vyacheslav Molotov leaves, NKVD head Lavrentiy Beria reveals to Nikita Khrushchev and Deputy Chairman Georgy Malenkov that Molotov is to be part of the latest purge. The concert recording arrives and Maria's note, admonishing Stalin and wishing him dead, causes him to suffer a cerebral haemorrhage as he laughs at the note. Stalin's guards hear him fall in his office but fear disturbing him.
Stalin's housemaid discovers him unconscious the next morning and members of the Central Committee rush to the dacha. Beria finds Maria's note but only after Malenkov, Khrushchev, Lazar Kaganovich, Anastas Mikoyan, and Nikolai Bulganin arrive, does the Committee finally decide to send for medical help. The best doctors in Moscow have been arrested after the "Doctors' plot". When Stalin dies under the care of mediocre doctors, Beria orders the NKVD to relieve the Soviet Army of control of Moscow.
Beria and Khrushchev vie for the support of Molotov and of Stalin's children, Svetlana and her unstable, alcoholic brother Vasily. Beria removes Molotov's name from the impending purge and releases Polina Zhemchuzhina, Molotov's wife, from prison. The Committee names Malenkov, a puppet of Beria, as chairman. He hijacks Khrushchev's proposed reforms, such as releasing political prisoners and loosening clerical restrictions, relegating Khrushchev to planning Stalin's funeral.
Beria threatens Khrushchev with Maria's note, and Khrushchev reverses Beria's order to halt all transport into Moscow. When 1,500 arriving mourners are killed, the Committee wants to blame junior NKVD officers. In an effort to deflect blame, Beria threatens his colleagues with documents detailing their involvement in various purges.
Angered by the NKVD's takeover of security from the Army, Marshal Georgy Zhukov supports Khrushchev in launching a coup against Beria after Stalin's funeral. Khrushchev gets support from the rest of the Committee save Malenkov, and on Zhukov's orders the Army reclaims its posts from the NKVD. Zhukov, Kiril Moskalenko and Leonid Brezhnev storm a meeting of the Committee and arrest Beria.
Malenkov reluctantly signs Beria's death warrant. At Beria's emergency trial, Khrushchev finds him guilty of counter-revolutionary activities, sexual assault, and paedophilia.

documents.title: Ocean's Eight
documents.tagline: The plan is priceless.
documents.overview: Debbie Ocean, a criminal mastermind, gathers a crew of female thieves to pull off the heist of the century at New York's annual Met Gala.
documents.plot:
Ocean's Eight is a heist comedy-drama film released in 2018, directed by Gary Ross and written by Olivia Milch. The movie serves as a spin-off to the Ocean's franchise, with Sandra Bullock taking on the lead role of Debbie Ocean, the sister of Danny Ocean (played by George Clooney in the previous films).

The story begins with Debbie Ocean, who has just been released from prison after serving time for a crime she didn't commit. She sets out to plan and execute a massive heist at the Met Gala, one of the most prestigious events in New York City's social calendar.

Debbie assembles a team of eight women, each with their unique skills and expertise: Cate Blanchett as Lou, the tough-as-nails ex-con; Anne Hathaway as Daphne, a talented thief; Mindy Kaling as Amita, an expert hacker; Sarah Paulson as Tammy, a skilled pickpocket; Awkwafina as Constance, a street-smart thief; Rihanna as Nine Ball, a charismatic and deadly thief; Helena Bonham Carter as Rose, a quirky and artistic forger; and Richard Armitage as Claude Becker, the wealthy businessman who has hired Debbie to pull off the heist.

As the team prepares for the Met Gala, they must navigate their personal demons and learn to work together in order to succeed. Along the way, they discover that Claude's true intentions are not what they seem, and that the heist is just a cover for something much more sinister.

The movie takes the audience on a thrilling ride through the world of high-stakes thievery, with plenty of twists and turns along the way. The team faces numerous challenges as they try to stay one step ahead of Claude's security team and the police, all while dealing with their own personal struggles and relationships.

As the night of the Met Gala approaches, Debbie and her team put their plan into action, using their unique skills to infiltrate the event and steal a priceless necklace. However, things don't go exactly as planned, and the team must use all their wits and cunning to escape with their lives and the loot.

In the end, Debbie and her team emerge victorious, but not without some unexpected surprises and revelations about Claude's true intentions. The movie ends on a high note, with Debbie and her team celebrating their success and looking forward to their next adventure together.

Overall, Ocean's Eight is a fun and entertaining heist movie that features a talented ensemble cast and plenty of twists and turns along the way. With its strong female lead and diverse cast of characters, it's a great addition to the Ocean's franchise and a must-see for fans of the genre.

documents.title: 1898: Our Last Men in the Philippines
documents.tagline: There are men who want medals and men who want to come back.
documents.overview: The Philippines, 1898. Fifty Spanish soldiers arrive in the small village of Baler to rebuild an outpost. Although the war against the Filipinos and their American allies is almost lost, as is the Spanish Empire, the garrison will endure a cruel siege for eleven months. They will be the last to surrender.
documents.plot:
1898, Our Last Men in the Philippines (Spanish: 1898, Los últimos de Filipinas) is a 2016 Spanish war drama directed by Salvador Calvo. It dramatises the Siege of Baler of 1898 to 1899, in which a Spanish detachment held out for almost a year inside the church of San Luis Obispo de Tolosa against Filipino revolutionaries, unaware that the war had ended. The cast includes Luis Tosar, Javier Gutiérrez, Álvaro Cervantes, Karra Elejalde and Carlos Hipólito. It was released on December 2, 2016.

During the Philippine Revolution, rebels attack the Spanish garrison in the coastal town of Baler and kill most of its soldiers. A detachment of young recruits under Captain Enrique de las Morenas and Lieutenant Martín Cerezo is sent from Manila to reoccupy the town. They are welcomed by the parish priest, Brother Carmelo. Among the recruits is Carlos, a sensitive young man who dreams of studying art, and who begins to share the priest's opium.

News arrives that the United States has declared war on Spain and destroyed its fleet, cutting the garrison off from supplies. When the revolutionaries attack, the soldiers barricade themselves in the church. Months pass under siege as beriberi, caused by poor rations, kills many of them, including de las Morenas and Brother Carmelo, leaving the rigid Cerezo in command. One recruit deserts to the enemy and urges his comrades to give up a lost cause, and offers of peace, including newspapers reporting Spain's defeat, are dismissed by Cerezo as tricks.

The men grow desperate, and violence and paranoia spread. Carlos, suffering from withdrawal after his opium is discovered, is locked up. Even when a Spanish officer arrives with orders to surrender, Cerezo refuses to believe that Spain has lost its colonies. Carlos goes out to verify the news and learns from the Filipino commander that Spain has ceded the islands to the Americans, but Cerezo still holds out, and deserters are brutally punished.

Only when Cerezo reads a minor item in a newspaper about the posting of a friend, a detail no enemy could have invented, does he accept the truth. The garrison surrenders in June 1899, and the Filipino forces, impressed by their resistance, allow the survivors to leave with honour rather than as prisoners. Carlos, disillusioned, discards his drawings as the men depart.

The film was shortlisted as Spain's possible Academy Award submission. The Hollywood Reporter called it spectacular and striking, if not subtle.

documents.title: Headshot
documents.tagline: They should have killed him.
documents.overview: A young man washes ashore, his memory gone - but his past comes back to haunt him after he is nursed back to health and his killing ability is needed when he takes on a powerful drug lord.
documents.plot:
A comatose man of unknown identity and origin is being cared by Dr. Ailin in a rural hospital on a small island. The man eventually wakes up after two months with no clear memory of how he was injured or even his identity. He adopts the name Ishmael from Moby-Dick, which Ailin is reading. The man learns that he was found on the beach by a man named Romli.
Meanwhile, a mobster named Lee and his henchmen Rika and Besi violently eliminate a rival gang. One of the gang's survivors tells Lee about Ishmael and Lee sends the man to investigate. Ishmael and the thug have a brief altercation after the man threatens Ailin. Ailin travels to the mainland to seek better care for Ishmael, but her bus is stopped by Lee's men, who are looking for Ishmael (whom they call Abdi). They slaughter all the passengers except Ailin and a young girl, whom they abduct. Called by Ailin, Ishmael and Romli hurry to the scene of the bus attack. Ishmael kills a few of Lee's thugs, but Romli is also killed. An Interpol agent tells Ishmael about children abducted by Lee's syndicate and bred to be devoted smugglers and criminal enforcers; Ishmael was one of those children.
The agent is killed when a group of Lee's assassins attack the police station in an attempt to take out Ishmael/Abdi. Ishmael puts down the attackers instead and escapes. Ishmael must then go to war with the syndicate to save Ailin. While traveling, Ishmael encounters Besi near a well, and it is revealed that he, Besi and Rika trained together. Lee would put children in the well and starve them for a few days and the child, who killed all the others to get the food would be freed. Ishmael tries to persuade Besi to not be on Lee's side, but Besi refuses out of loyalty. They then begin to fight and Ishmael manages to gain the upper hand, killing Besi with a strong hit to the head. After Besi dies, Rika discovers his corpse and attacks Ishmael on the beach.
Ishmael eventually defeats Rika despite receiving multiple wounds from the latter, and it is revealed that Rika was the one who shot Ishmael and gave him amnesia in the first place. Rika takes advantage of the distraction and holds Ishmael at gunpoint, but she can't bring herself to shoot Ishmael again, where she instead shoots away from him, wasting her bullets. In the confusion, Ishmael accidentally mortally injures Rika by reflexively throwing a knife. After comforting Rika in her dying moments, Ishmael finds Lee's hideout, where he and Ailin meet each other during the chaos, with Ailin initially hostile to Ishmael due to their relationship resulting in her kidnapping. Ishmael manages to convince her and they mutually embrace.
However, Lee arrives and gets enraged that Ishmael killed both Besi and Rika, whom he had considered as his "favorite children". They then enter a brutal fight, with Lee gaining the upper hand due to his strength. However, Ishmael finally beats Lee outside, and impales him on the sharp branch of a tree trunk.

documents.title: Ralph Breaks the Internet
documents.tagline: Who Broke the Internet?
documents.overview: Video game bad guy Ralph and fellow misfit Vanellope von Schweetz must risk it all by traveling to the World Wide Web in search of a replacement part to save Vanellope's video game, Sugar Rush. In way over their heads, Ralph and Vanellope rely on the citizens of the internet — the netizens — to help navigate their way, including an entrepreneur named Yesss, who is the head algorithm and the heart and soul of trend-making site BuzzzTube.
documents.plot:
Ralph Breaks the Internet is a 2018 American animated comedy-adventure film produced by Walt Disney Animation Studios. The movie serves as a sequel to Wreck-It Ralph, released in 2012.

The story begins with Ralph (voiced by John C. Reilly), the lovable but destructive villain from the classic arcade game Fix-It Felix, who has become an unlikely hero after saving the arcade from an evil virus known as "Sugar Rush." To celebrate his victory, Ralph and his new friend Vanellope von Schweetz (voiced by Sarah Silverman) are invited to a high-tech gaming convention called Slaughter Race.

However, things take a turn when Ralph becomes fascinated with the world of online gaming and decides to explore the internet. He and Vanellope embark on a journey through various websites, including YouTube, eBay, and Amazon. Along the way, they encounter new characters, such as Shank (voiced by Gal Gadot), a tough-as-nails driver from the racing game Crash Bandicoot.

As Ralph delves deeper into the internet, he becomes increasingly obsessed with his online persona and the validation it provides. He starts to neglect his friendship with Vanellope and his responsibilities in the arcade. Meanwhile, Shank's true intentions are revealed, and she is determined to take down Ralph and claim the championship title for Crash Bandicoot.

As Ralph struggles to balance his online life with his real-life relationships, he must also confront the darker side of the internet. He discovers that the world of online gaming can be cruel and unforgiving, where players are often pitted against each other in a never-ending cycle of competition.

In the end, Ralph realizes that true friendship and connection cannot be found online but rather through shared experiences and genuine relationships. With Vanellope's help, he finds a way to reconcile his online persona with his real-life identity and saves the arcade from Shank's evil plans.

The movie features stunning animation, witty humor, and a talented voice cast. The film's exploration of the internet's impact on society is both thought-provoking and entertaining, making it a must-see for audiences of all ages. Overall, Ralph Breaks the Internet is a heartwarming and hilarious adventure that celebrates the power of friendship and the importance of staying true to oneself.

documents.title: A Street Cat Named Bob
documents.tagline: Sometimes it takes nine lives to save one
documents.overview: James Bowen, a homeless busker and recovering drug addict, has his life transformed when he meets a stray ginger cat.
documents.plot:
A Street Cat Named Bob is a 2016 British biographical drama directed by Roger Spottiswoode and written by Tim John and Maria Nation, based on James Bowen's memoirs A Street Cat Named Bob and The World According to Bob. Luke Treadaway stars as Bowen, with Ruta Gedmintas, Joanne Froggatt and Anthony Head, while Bob the cat plays himself in most scenes. The title is a play on A Streetcar Named Desire. The film premiered in London on 3 November 2016 and went on general release the following day.

James Bowen is a homeless former heroin addict busking on the streets of London and struggling to survive. After a near-fatal overdose, his support worker Val finds him a council flat and puts him on a methadone programme in the hope of getting him off the streets for good. On his first night in the flat, James discovers a ginger cat raiding his food. He assumes the cat belongs to someone nearby and tries to send him home, but the cat returns, this time with an infected wound on his leg. James's neighbour Betty, an animal lover, tells him about a charity veterinary clinic where she volunteers, and gives the cat the name Bob.

James spends what little money he has on Bob's treatment and then lets him go, but Bob refuses to leave and follows him onto the bus and into central London. The sight of a busker with a cat perched on his shoulders draws crowds, and James begins to earn more money than ever before, eventually becoming a well-known figure in the area and selling The Big Issue magazine. His friendship with Betty grows, and caring for Bob gives him the motivation to stay clean. But his path to recovery is not easy: he faces hostility from other vendors, trouble with authorities, the temptation of his old life and a painful attempt to reconcile with his estranged father, and he must undergo the ordeal of withdrawal from methadone to finally free himself from addiction.

The film was a success in the United Kingdom and won Best British Film at the National Film Awards UK in 2017. Critics praised Treadaway's performance and Bob's natural screen presence, though some found it sentimental. A Christmas sequel, A Gift from Bob, was released in 2020, after the real Bob had died earlier that year.

documents.title: From a House on Willow Street
documents.original_title: From a House on Willow Street
documents.tagline: Evil has an address...
documents.overview: After a young woman is kidnapped, her captors soon come to realize that in fact they may be the ones in danger and this young woman has a dark secret inside her.
documents.plot:
Hazel, her boyfriend Ade, Ade's cousin James, and Mark plot to kidnap diamond heiress Katherine within the next six weeks. The expedited time frame worries Mark, who believes it may cause them to make mistakes. Hazel and Ade are adamant about the time frame, as Ade will soon go on trial for the accidental death of his brother George. They stress the importance of both the timing and the need for a flawless execution. Left with no other option, Mark agrees. Six weeks later, the four break into Katherine's house, encountering no resistance and finding the alarm already deactivated. After grabbing Katherine, they return to their headquarters in an abandoned warehouse and chain up Katherine. They are surprised by her dirty and sickly appearance but continue with their plan regardless.
Katherine warns them to let her go free and initially refuses to play along in making a ransom video. Hazel convinces her by promising the ordeal will end faster if she cooperates. However, the kidnappers can not contact her parents to make their demands. Hazel sends Ade and James back to Katherine's house to investigate. Less distracted, they realise the house is full of decaying food and smells horrible. James finds two dead, mutilated priests in the cellar, and Ade realises that Katherine's parents have been gruesomely murdered. Both are haunted by apparitions from their past. Worried they will be blamed for the murders, they flee the house after grabbing videotapes from the cellar. On the way back, Ade swerves to miss an apparition of George, and James is assaulted by his dead mother.
Back at the warehouse, Hazel and Mark are also haunted. Hazel sees her own dead mother, and Mark sees his dead daughter Sarah. James' condition steadily deteriorates, and the others leave him in a room to rest while they watch the videotapes. The first videotape is by Katherine and details the history of her house and its many unexplained deaths, including that of Hazel's mother. The others are annoyed that Hazel kept this detail quiet, but they continue watching. On the next videotape, a priest says a demon that feeds on grief is responsible for the deaths and has subsequently possessed Katherine. The demon has chosen this house because it is the furthest point in the world from a holy relic kept in the Vatican. Panicked by the demon's growing power, the priests attempt to immolate Katherine, but she kills everyone in the house.
Disturbed by the videotapes, Hazel, Ade, and Mark confront Katherine, who, as the demon, reveals that she only needs to possess two more people to be set free from hell. James, infected by his mother's apparition, attempts to infect the others. Katherine appeals to Mark, telling him that if he betrays Hazel and Ade, she will spare his soul and allow him to be with Sarah again. Mark frees Katherine from her chains and delivers the others to her. After hearing their anguished cries, he sacrifices himself to give them time to escape and becomes infected.

documents.overview: Master car thieves square off against French gangsters in the South of France with money, women and lives all on the line.
