documents.overview: When architect-turned-recluse Bernadette Fox goes missing prior to a family trip to Antarctica, her 15-year-old daughter Bee goes on a quest with Bernadette's husband to find her.
documents.plot: When architect-turned-recluse Bernadette Fox goes missing prior to a family trip to Antarctica, her 15-year-old daughter, Bee, goes on a quest with Bernadette's husband to find her.

documents.title: My Little Pony: Equestria Girls - Legend of Everfree
documents.original_title: My Little Pony: Equestria Girls - Legend of Everfree
documents.overview: When Canterlot Highschool goes on a trip to Camp Everfree, they’re surprised to find a magical force is causing strange things to happen around camp. With the help of the Mane 6 and especially Sunset Shimmer, Twilight Sparkle must confront the dark “Midnight Sparkle” within herself  and embrace her newfound magical abilities to save the camp.
documents.plot:
The students of Canterlot High School attend a field trip to Camp Everfree, a nature camp owned by Gloriosa Daisy and her brother, Timber Spruce. During the bus ride, transfer student Twilight Sparkle has a nightmare of being overtaken by "Midnight Sparkle", a malevolent alter ego of herself produced while temporarily corrupted by Equestrian magic. Her friend Sunset Shimmer is supportive, relating to her own similar experience of transforming into a demon. Shortly upon arrival at the camp, Twilight develops telekinetic powers, which she worries is a sign of Midnight's lingering presence.
That night, Timber tells a campfire story about a forest spirit named Gaea Everfree being angered by the camp's construction and threatens to unleash a plague of natural disasters upon it. The next day, a sailboat crashes into a dock the campers are building to use as a fashion show runway. The terrified campers spot glittering gem dust that matches the description of Gaea's presence in Timber's story, convincing them that Gaea is real. Twilight, however, believes her magic to be responsible for the accident and distances herself from her friends.
Later, Twilight's friends begin developing superpowers which they can only use within the camp's boundaries (Rainbow Dash gains super speed, Fluttershy gets the ability to communicate with animals, Pinkie Pie can create explosions using sprinkles, Rarity can make diamonds out of thin air, and Applejack receives super strength). Now believing her magic is infecting her friends, Twilight prepares to run away from the camp. Sunset follows Twilight into the woods and, discovering her power of telepathic empathy, convinces her to stay. As Timber leads them back to the camp, Sunset notices gem dust falling from his pocket and suspects him of staging Gaea's attacks. She later overhears him arguing with Gloriosa about abandoning what Sunset assumes to be the camp. Remembering his earlier statements of longing for urban life, Sunset concludes that Timber means to shut the camp down by terrorizing the campers.
Sunset brings Twilight and Spike with her to investigate a nearby cave kept off-limits by Timber, where they find geodes infused with Equestrian magic. The three are confronted by Gloriosa, who reveals herself to be the true cause of the natural disasters. Sunset learns through her visions that Gloriosa, desperate to prevent the camp's closure, has been wearing the geodes as a necklace to harness their power, with the "disasters" resulting from her reckless attempts at using magic to improve the campers' experience; Timber, anticipating this, invented the story of Gaea Everfree to cover for her.
Gloriosa adds more geodes to the necklace and is completely corrupted by their power, taking on an appearance resembling Gaea. Crashing the campers' fashion show rehearsal, Gloriosa enacts her intent to "protect" them by trapping the camp in a bramble cage.

documents.overview: Five years after an ominous unseen presence drives most of society to suicide, a survivor and her two children make a desperate bid to reach safety.

documents.title: Don't Kill It
documents.overview: Demon hunter, Jebediah Huntley teams up with an FBI agent to battle a supernatural force in the southern state of Mississippi.
documents.plot:
Don't Kill It is a 2016 American comedy horror film directed and edited by Mike Mendez from a screenplay by Dan Berk and Robert Olsen. Dolph Lundgren stars as Jebediah Woodley, an eccentric demon hunter who travels to a small Mississippi town to destroy an ancient, murderous demon. Kristina Klebe, Tony Bentley, James Chalke, Billy Slaughter and Miles Doleac appear in supporting roles. The script was originally set in Alaska, but filming was moved to Mississippi for financial reasons, and the film was made for less than $1 million, part of it raised through crowdfunding on Indiegogo.

While hunting deer in southern Mississippi, a man named Gabriel follows his dog to a small golden box, which the dog opens. The animal begins to act strangely and attacks Gabriel, who is forced to shoot it. Gabriel returns home with the same black eyes and erratic behavior, murders his family and then begins killing his neighbors until he is shot dead by a neighbor named Marcus, who immediately develops black eyes himself and carries on the slaughter. The demon, it turns out, passes into whoever kills its current host.

Days later, Jebediah Woodley, a weathered demon hunter who has spent decades tracking this particular entity, hears about the killings on the radio and comes to town. At the same time, FBI agent Evelyn Pierce, who grew up in the area, has been sent to investigate the massacres as a possible case of domestic terrorism. Pierce and the local police chief dismiss Woodley's talk of demons and have him detained, but when the killings continue, Pierce is forced to accept that he is right. Woodley explains that the demon cannot simply be killed, since its killer becomes the next host, and that it must be trapped instead. As panic spreads and the townspeople start to turn on one another, Woodley and Pierce try to stop the demon without letting anyone kill it, a task that becomes increasingly difficult as it jumps from body to body.

The film played on the genre festival circuit before its release and was generally well received by horror critics, who enjoyed its sense of humor, its gory effects and Lundgren's relaxed, self-mocking turn as the gruff hunter.

documents.title: An Ordinary Man
documents.overview: A war criminal in hiding forms a relationship with his only connection to the outside world - his maid.
documents.plot:
A war criminal is hiding in plain sight in an unnamed Balkan country. He is wanted internationally for ethnic cleansing and war crimes, but his country pretends his whereabouts to be unknown despite international pressures to turn him in. A retinue of loyalists watches over him and ensures his safety as he goes about his life in a city where his face is well known. He begins to form a relationship with his newly hired maid, Tanja, after he expresses loneliness to her. Initially treating her abusively, he gradually forms an awkward friendship with her. She is later revealed to be an agent who is hired to protect him. She reluctantly drives him to the cemetery in his home village. His driver, who had been waiting for them, kills her on the spot, and drives the General back to his apartment in the city. The last scene shows him awaiting his arrest, seated at his kitchen table, with a handgun and bullets laid out in front of him.
The character of the General is based on Ratko Mladić, who was ultimately sentenced to life in prison for war crimes committed in the Bosnian war.

documents.title: Mostly Ghostly 3: One Night in Doom House
documents.original_title: Mostly Ghostly 3: One Night in Doom House
documents.overview: Just one enchanted jewel stands between earth and an army of evil spirits led by the devious ghoul, Phears. With the help of his new girlfriend and ghost pals, Max Doyle races to find the crystal and save the world.
documents.plot:
Mostly Ghostly 3: One Night in Doom House, released as R.L. Stine's Mostly Ghostly: One Night in Doom House, is a 2016 American family fantasy horror comedy written and directed by Ron Oliver. It is the third feature film based on R. L. Stine's Mostly Ghostly book series, following Mostly Ghostly: Who Let the Ghosts Out? (2008) and Mostly Ghostly: Have You Met My Ghoulfriend? (2014), and was made by Universal 1440 Entertainment. To keep the characters at the same ages, the main roles were recast: Corey Fogelmanis plays Max Doyle, with Sophie Reynolds as Cammie, Blake Michael and Olivia Ryan Stern as the ghosts Nicky and Tara, Adam Tsekhman as Phears, Danny Trejo as Mr. Morgo and Jamie Kennedy as a television ghost hunter. Morgan Fairchild also appears.

Max is a teenage stage magician who shares his home with Nicky and Tara, two young ghosts who are counting on him to help them find their missing parents. To raise money for his girlfriend Cammie's school dance crew, he stages a public séance. The ghosts supply genuine spectral effects, but everyone assumes they are Max's tricks, and when the ghost of a French maid interrupts the show with information about Nicky and Tara's parents, the evening ends in embarrassment and Cammie breaks up with him. At the same time, his ghost friends complain that he treats them more like pets than friends.

Max turns for help to Simon Drake, the self-obsessed host of a ghost-hunting television show who is filming an episode in town, only to discover that he is a fraud. The evil ghost Phears, working with the sinister Mr. Morgo, takes possession of Drake as part of a new attempt to release an army of evil spirits on the world and plunge it into darkness. The key is a dark crystal that turns up in Max's house, which Max has tried to use to win Cammie back. Hampered by fame, family squabbles, a rich rival for Cammie's affections and an anxious dance choreographer, Max has to recover the jewel and rescue Nicky and Tara before Phears succeeds, in a showdown at a derelict mansion, the Doom House of the title.

The film was released directly on DVD, digital download and on demand on 6 September 2016. Common Sense Media described it as a low-budget, harmless fright-fest with nonstop action and over-the-top villains, enlivened by Kennedy's send-up of a reality television star, but lacking in depth.

documents.title: League of Gods
documents.overview: During the reign of King Zhou, an official enters his bedchamber, and is devoured by the monstrous tails of Daji, his concubine. Outside their city, several warriors within a metal wagon discuss their strategies to free the Invisible People and their Chief, when Jiang Ziya appears to them. He tells them that when King Zhou was younger, he let himself become possessed by the Black Dragon for his quest for power.

documents.title: Insidious: The Last Key
documents.tagline: Fear comes home.
documents.overview: Parapsychologist Elise Rainier and her team travel to Five Keys, NM, to investigate a man’s claim of a haunting. Terror soon strikes when Rainier realizes that the house he lives in was her family’s old home.
documents.plot:
Insidious: The Last Key is a supernatural horror film directed by Adam Wingard and written by Leigh Whannell. The movie serves as the fourth installment in the Insidious franchise.

The story begins with Elise Rainier (Lin Shaye), a paranormal investigator, who has been institutionalized for her supposed mental illness due to her experiences with the spirit world. However, it is revealed that she was actually being held captive by a group of people who were trying to exploit her abilities.

Elise escapes from her captors and returns home, where she reunites with her friends Specs (Leigh Whannell) and Tucker (Angus Sampson). They inform Elise that her sister, Sally (Haley Murphy), has been experiencing terrifying visions and nightmares, which they believe are connected to their family's dark past.

As the story unfolds, it is revealed that their family's history is filled with tragedy and loss. Their father, Josh (Derek Johnson), died under mysterious circumstances when Elise was a child, and their mother, Lorraine (Rose Byrne), has been struggling to cope with her grief ever since.

Elise decides to investigate the source of Sally's visions, which leads her to an abandoned asylum in New Orleans. There, she discovers that the asylum was once home to a malevolent spirit known as "The Key," which is responsible for the family's dark past.

As Elise delves deeper into the mystery, she realizes that The Key is connected to her own traumatic experiences and that it has been manipulating her sister's visions in an attempt to lure her back to the asylum. Elise must use her skills and knowledge of the spirit world to defeat The Key and free Sally from its grasp.

Throughout the movie, Elise faces numerous challenges and obstacles as she navigates the treacherous world of spirits and demons. She is aided by Specs and Tucker, who provide comedic relief and technical support throughout the investigation.

The climax of the movie features an intense showdown between Elise and The Key, which culminates in a dramatic confrontation that will determine the fate of Sally and the entire Rainier family.

Ultimately, Elise emerges victorious, but not without scars. She realizes that her experiences have left her with emotional baggage and that she must find a way to heal and move forward. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, as Elise begins to rebuild her life and reconnect with her sister.

Insidious: The Last Key received mixed reviews from critics, who praised the film's visuals and atmosphere but criticized its predictable plot and lack of originality. Despite this, the movie has developed a loyal fan base and is widely regarded as one of the best entries in the Insidious franchise.

documents.title: Moonfall
documents.tagline: Humanity will face the dark side of the Moon.
documents.overview: A mysterious force knocks the moon from its orbit around Earth and sends it hurtling on a collision course with life as we know it.
documents.plot:
"Moonfall" is a 2022 science fiction disaster film directed by Roland Emmerich, produced by Centropolis Entertainment, and written by Drew Pearce.

The movie follows two main storylines that eventually intersect. The first storyline revolves around Sam Bell (played by Patrick Wilson), an astronaut who wakes up on the Moon with no memory of how he got there or what happened to his crew. As he tries to piece together his past, he discovers a mysterious message from an unknown sender that sets him on a mission to prevent a catastrophic event.

The second storyline takes place in 2055, where we meet J.T. O'Grady (played by Halle Berry), the daughter of Sam Bell, who is now a renowned astrophysicist. She's recruited by a team of scientists and engineers, including her colleague Brian Harper (played by John Bradley), to prevent a massive asteroid from colliding with Earth.

As the story unfolds, we learn that the asteroid is not just any ordinary rock - it's actually a piece of the Moon that has broken off due to an unknown cataclysmic event. The team discovers that the Moon was once part of a larger celestial body called Kaltain, which was destroyed in a catastrophic collision with Earth millions of years ago.

The movie takes a thrilling turn as Sam Bell and J.T. O'Grady embark on a perilous journey to prevent the asteroid from colliding with Earth. Along the way, they encounter numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, malfunctioning equipment, and personal demons.

Throughout the film, Emmerich's signature style of explosive action sequences and heart-pumping suspense is on full display. The movie's climax features an intense showdown between Sam and J.T., as they work together to prevent the asteroid from destroying Earth.

While "Moonfall" received mixed reviews from critics, it has its fans who appreciate the film's over-the-top action sequences and thrilling plot twists. However, some viewers may find the pacing a bit uneven and the scientific explanations lacking in depth.

Overall, "Moonfall" is an entertaining sci-fi disaster film that will keep you on the edge of your seat. With its breakneck pace and mind-bending plot twists, it's sure to appeal to fans of Roland Emmerich's signature style.

documents.title: Hotel Artemis
documents.tagline: No guns. No cops. No killing the other patients.
documents.overview: Los Angeles, June 21st, 2028. While the streets are being torn apart by riots, the Nurse, who runs a clandestine hospital for criminals in the penthouse of the Artemis, a closed old hotel, has a rough night dealing with troublemaker clients: thieves, assassins, someone from the past and the one who owns the place and the whole city.
documents.plot:
On June 21, 2028, a riot breaks out in Los Angeles over the city's water privatization. Taking advantage of the chaos, professional criminal Sherman attempts a bank robbery that leaves half his team dead with his brother Lev and another accomplice critically wounded. During the robbery, Lev takes a fancy pen from a well-dressed bank customer (amongst gardeners and maids) who tells Lev he is making a terrible mistake. They escape to the nearby Hotel Artemis, an underground hospital funded by its criminal clientele, which is run by Jean "The Nurse" Thomas. Confined inside the hotel for 22 years by her severe agoraphobia and grief over the death of her son, Beau, Thomas adheres to the strict set of rules for the hospital, including "No weapons", "No non-members", and "No killing of other guests".
Sherman and Lev are admitted while their accomplice is forcibly ejected by Thomas' orderly, Everest. Lev, given the codename "Honolulu", undergoes the hotel's technologically advanced treatment, including robot-assisted surgery and 3D printed transplant organs. Thomas shows Sherman evidence that his brother Lev is a drug addict.
Sherman encounters the hotel's other guests: "Acapulco", an obnoxious arms dealer, and "Nice", an international assassin and old acquaintance. As the riot draws nearer, Thomas receives word that notorious crime lord Orian "The Wolf King" Franklin, who is also the owner of the Artemis, is en route with a Code Red. Thomas' preparations are complicated by the arrival of a wounded police officer named Morgan, a childhood friend of Thomas' late son, begging for help. Against Everest's warnings and Thomas' own rules, they admit Morgan.
Through aid from Nice, Sherman discovers the pen Lev stole is marked with the Wolf King's symbol and conceals diamonds worth over $18 million. The Wolf King has a strict policy of killing those who steal from him by drowning them in the ocean. Acapulco learns that Nice has been hired to kill the Wolf King; she incapacitates Acapulco and plants a bomb on the hotel's door lock power generator.
The wounded Wolf King arrives and is admitted, but his men and son Crosby must wait in the lobby's gated ante-room. Everest sneaks Morgan out of the hotel after finishing treatment of her wounds. Fearful of being discovered, Sherman prepares to fight the Wolf King's men until his brother is stable enough to move.
While administering to the Wolf King, Thomas discovers that he was responsible for her son's death. The police reported he died due to an overdose, instead of the truth, her son was killed after attempting to steal the Wolf King's car. The Wolf King paid the police to lie about her son's death and he used the tragedy to recruit Nurse Thomas to run Hotel Artemis. Thomas prepares to kill the Wolf King, but is diverted when Nice's bomb disrupts the power and Lev's life support. While Thomas struggles to save Lev, Nice kills the Wolf King.

documents.title: What Happened to Monday
documents.tagline: Seven sisters. One identity.
documents.overview: In a world where families are limited to one child due to overpopulation, a set of identical septuplets must avoid being put to a long sleep by the government and dangerous infighting while investigating the disappearance of one of their own.
documents.plot:
In a dystopian 2073, overpopulation has resulted in a strict one-child policy, enforced by the European Federation's Child Allocation Bureau. Any illegal children found by the C.A.B. are taken and placed in indefinite cryosleep.
After the death of his daughter during childbirth, Terrence Settman secretly raises his identical septuplet granddaughters. To conceal their existence, he names each child after a day of the week and trains them to live a shared life under a single identity, "Karen Settman". Each sister is allowed to go outside only on the day corresponding to her name to ensure their secret remains undiscovered.
One night, Monday fails to return home after work. The next day, Tuesday retraces her steps and discovers Monday received the promotion they were up for and met their co-worker Jerry at a bar. Before she can investigate further, C.A.B. agents detain her.
At the C.A.B. facility, Tuesday meets presidential candidate and head of the bureau Nicolette Cayman. Cayman reveals she is aware of the sisters' existence and dispatches C.A.B. agents to their apartment to eliminate them. The sisters manage to kill the agents, but Sunday is killed in the process. Learning the agents used Tuesday's severed eyeball to bypass the building's retinal scan, the sisters suspect Jerry may have disclosed their secret.
The next day, Wednesday leaves without disguising herself and confronts Jerry. He reveals that "Karen" received the promotion after transferring millions of euros to Cayman to fund her campaign. After a C.A.B. sniper kills Jerry, Wednesday flees his apartment.
The sisters remotely guide Wednesday to safety but are interrupted when C.A.B. agent Adrian Knowles arrives at their apartment, concerned about "Karen". Surmising that Adrian is in a relationship with one of them, Thursday convinces Saturday to accompany Adrian. At his apartment, Saturday, a virgin, learns which sister Adrian had been seeing. She covertly links their bracelets while sleeping with him, allowing Friday to hack into the C.A.B. surveillance system; the sisters believe they have found Monday in a holding cell. Meanwhile, C.A.B. agents corner and kill Wednesday. After Adrian leaves his apartment, C.A.B. agents arrive and kill Saturday after she tells her siblings Monday was dating Adrian. The sisters' apartment is raided simultaneously by a C.A.B. squad led by Joe, the bureau's head of security. Admitting that she cannot survive on her own, Friday sacrifices herself by detonating their apartment to allow Thursday to escape and rescue Monday.
After learning about the attack, Adrian rushes back to the sisters' apartment, where Thursday confronts him in his car and blames him for her sisters’ deaths. Adrian insists that he knew nothing about the sisters' existence and that he loves 'Karen' without knowing her true name Monday, and agrees to help rescue her.

documents.title: Better Watch Out
documents.tagline: You might be home but you're not alone
documents.overview: On a quiet suburban street tucked within a 'safe neighborhood', a babysitter must defend a twelve-year-old boy from strangers breaking into the house, only to discover that this is far from a normal home invasion.
documents.plot:
Better Watch Out, originally titled Safe Neighborhood, is a 2016 Christmas psychological horror film directed by Chris Peckover, who co-wrote the script with Zack Kahn. It stars Olivia DeJonge as the babysitter Ashley, Levi Miller as twelve-year-old Luke Lerner, Ed Oxenbould as Luke's friend Garrett, Aleks Mikic as Ashley's boyfriend Ricky, Dacre Montgomery as her ex-boyfriend Jeremy, and Patrick Warburton and Virginia Madsen as Luke's parents, Robert and Deandra Lerner.

At Christmas, seventeen-year-old Ashley babysits Luke, a precocious boy with a crush on her, who tries and fails to seduce her as they watch a horror film. Strange noises outside unnerve her, but they seem to come from Luke's best friend Garrett, who drops by. When a brick reading "U leave and U die" smashes through an upstairs window, Garrett panics, runs out the back and appears to be shot dead. Ashley and Luke hide, first in the attic, where he saves her from a dangerous fall, and then in his closet, as a masked figure with a shotgun enters. Recognizing the mask as Luke's, Ashley demands that the intruder remove it, revealing Garrett, and she realizes that Luke staged the attack to frighten her so he could play the hero. When she scolds him, Luke knocks her out. He ties her up with duct tape and makes her play truth or dare, and Ricky, lured by a text that Luke sent from her phone, arrives and senses something wrong. With Garrett holding him at gunpoint, Ricky is subdued and tied up next to Ashley. As Ashley cuts herself free with a piece of glass, Luke kills Ricky by dropping a paint can on him. She points the gun at Luke, but it is unloaded, and as she tries to reach carolers outside, Luke knocks her out again with the brick. Luke then gets Jeremy to write Ashley an apology note and hangs him from a tree, making the letter look like a suicide note. When a remorseful Garrett starts to free Ashley, Luke kills him, then stabs Ashley in the neck and arranges the scene to frame Jeremy before going to bed to await his parents, who call the police. Ashley, however, survives, having sealed her wound with duct tape, and she gives Luke the finger from her stretcher as he watches from his window.

Shot in Sydney in early 2016 on a $3 million budget, the film premiered at Fantastic Fest on 22 September 2016 and was released in the United States on 6 October 2017. Critics responded positively, giving it an 89% Rotten Tomatoes rating and praising the young cast, though it grossed only $188,756.

documents.title: Sniper: Ghost Shooter
documents.overview: Elite snipers Brandon Beckett and Richard Miller are tasked with protecting a gas pipeline from terrorists looking to make a statement. When battles with the enemy lead to snipers being killed by a ghost shooter who knows their exact location, tensions boil as a security breach is suspected. Is there someone working with the enemy on the inside? Is the mission a front for other activity? Is the Colonel pulling the strings?
documents.plot: Elite snipers Brandon Beckett and Richard Miller are fighting extremists in the Middle East when the Colonel gives them a new mission: to protect a gas pipeline stretching from the Republic of Georgia to Western Europe from extremists eager to make a political statement. But when skirmishes with the enemy lead to U.S. snipers being killed by a ghost shooter who locks into their exact location, a security breach is suspected. Fingers are pointed and battle lines are drawn, all leading up to an explosive climax.

documents.title: Mowgli: Legend of the Jungle
documents.tagline: The greatest journey is finding where you belong
documents.overview: A human child raised by wolves, must face off against a menacing tiger named Shere Khan, as well as his own origins.
documents.plot:
In the jungles of India, the gigantic Indian python seer Kaa watches as Shere Khan, a sadistic Bengal tiger, breaks "jungle law" by killing a family of humans. The black panther Bagheera finds a surviving infant boy and takes him to Nisha and Vihaan's family of Indian wolves, but the child is spotted by Shere Khan's striped hyena assistant Tabaqui.
The "man-cub" is brought before the wolf council, where Bagheera strong-arms Baloo, a Himalayan brown bear, into serving as his fellow guardian. Shere Khan arrives to kill the child, but Akela, leader of the wolves, declares that the boy is under the pack's protection. Shere Khan warns that when Akela misses his prey, he will return to kill the boy.
The child, now known as Mowgli, is adopted by Nisha and raised by the wolves, Baloo and Bagheera. Years pass, and Mowgli encounters Shere Khan, who has antagonized the nearby "man-village" by killing and slaughtering their cattle. Mowgli falls into a tiger trap set by the villagers, but is saved by Hathi, an Indian elephant missing half a tusk.
That night, Bagheera reveals to Mowgli that he is human, but Mowgli is determined to complete "the Running" – the trial to earn full membership in the pack. Bagheera urges Mowgli to leave the jungle for the village, where he will be safe from Shere Khan; watching the village from afar, Mowgli learns of the existence of fire.
The next day, during the Running as Bagheera chases the young wolves to prove their skill, Mowgli uses his ability to climb and run upright to gain the lead. Desperate to keep him safe, Bagheera unfairly foils Mowgli. After stating to Mowgli that he let his guard down, an enraged Baloo angrily confronts and berates Bagheera for his actions. After running off, Mowgli is kidnapped by the Bandar-log tribe of monkeys and brought to Shere Khan. Baloo and Bagheera arrive to save him. They are overwhelmed by the monkeys and Mowgli is rescued by Kaa. After Baloo heals him, Bhoot, Mowgli's albino wolf friend, attempts to cheer Mowgli up, but Mowgli, furious that he hadn't completed the Running, angrily lashed out at him, causing Bhoot to run away in tears before Mowgli, who felt remorseful for hurting his friend's feelings, can apologize to him. Later, he goes to visit Kaa, who believes he can restore harmony to the jungle.
While hunting, the elderly Akela fails to bring down a water buffalo, leading Shere Khan to remind the pack they must now challenge him for the role of leader. As the wolves fight, Mowgli steals a burning branch from the village and repels Shere Khan and the challengers, but shames Akela who regrettably advises him to leave. Mowgli is soon captured by the villagers and John Lockwood, a British hunter. One night, Bagheera visits Mowgli and tells him that he must stay with the villagers and gain their trust as he once did to escape captivity himself.

documents.title: Mary Magdalene
documents.tagline: Her story will be told
documents.overview: In the first century, free-spirited Mary Magdalene flees the marriage her family has arranged for her, finding refuge and a sense of purpose in a radical new movement led by the charismatic, rabble-rousing preacher named Jesus.
documents.plot:
Mary Magdalene is a 2018 biographical drama film directed by Garth Davis and written by Roseanne Powell. The film tells the story of Mary Magdalene, one of Jesus' twelve apostles, and her journey from being a sinful woman to becoming a devoted follower of Christ.

The film begins with Mary (played by Rooney Mara) as a young woman living in Capernaum, a small fishing village on the shores of the Sea of Galilee. She is portrayed as a complex character, struggling with her own demons and feeling isolated from society due to her past mistakes. The story then shifts to Jesus' (played by Juno Temple) arrival in Capernaum, where Mary meets him and becomes drawn to his teachings.

As Mary spends more time with Jesus, she begins to see the world through new eyes and finds a sense of purpose and belonging. She is introduced as one of Jesus' twelve apostles, alongside other notable figures such as Peter (played by Yul Vazquez) and John (played by Louis Hunter). The film depicts their early days together, exploring the teachings of Jesus and witnessing his miracles.

However, Mary's past mistakes continue to haunt her. She is shown to have been involved with a group of men who were using her for their own gain, leading to her feelings of shame and guilt. Despite this, she finds solace in her relationship with Jesus, who accepts her unconditionally and helps her to confront her demons.

As the story unfolds, Mary becomes increasingly devoted to Jesus' teachings and is present at many key events in his life, including the Last Supper and the Crucifixion. The film's portrayal of these events is poignant and powerful, highlighting the depth of Mary's love for Jesus and her willingness to follow him even into death.

The film's climax features Mary standing by Jesus' side as he dies on the cross, a moment that has been depicted in many other films and artworks throughout history. However, this version offers a fresh perspective on the event, emphasizing Mary's role as a witness and follower of Jesus rather than simply a bystander.

Throughout the film, the cinematography is stunning, capturing the beauty of the natural world and the emotional intensity of the characters' experiences. The score by Jed Kurzel adds to the overall sense of drama and tension, perfectly capturing the mood of each scene.

Overall, Mary Magdalene offers a powerful and moving portrayal of one of Jesus' most devoted followers. By exploring her complex character and her journey towards redemption, the film provides a unique perspective on the life of Christ and his disciples.

documents.title: Euphoria
documents.tagline: It's never too late.
documents.overview: The story of two sisters on a journey, where they try to get close to each other and approach the tough questions in life. Euphoria is a contemporary drama about responsibility and reconciliation, in a world where these concepts are gradually being lost.
documents.plot:
Emilie (Eva Green) and Ines (Alicia Vikander) Thompson are two sisters with very different characters who live far apart and rarely see each other. Now Ines, an artist trying to cope with unfavourable reviews of her latest exhibition, has accepted Emilie's invitation to accompany her on a short trip to an unknown place in the heart of Europe. The hotel Emilie has chosen for the first few days of her stay is very luxurious, as is the restaurant where she plans to dine; she evasively explains to her sister that she has sold her flat because she wants to go back to studying. During dinner, she agrees to dance with a stranger, to whom she confides that she is convinced Ines is only with her because her career is on the decline, adding that she "has no more time to lie". She therefore rejects the man's advances on the grounds that she would like to have an adventure but that this is not possible for her; immediately afterwards she feels very uncomfortable, which she attributes to the champagne she has drunk.
Their destination, which Emilie describes as "the most beautiful place in the world", turns out to be an estate lost in the woods beyond an unspecified country border, where they are met by an elderly woman, Marina (Charlotte Rampling), who describes herself as Emilie's "personal companion". For the unsuspecting Ines, it is the moment of truth: Emilie reveals to her that she has cancer, has been undergoing unsuccessful treatment for three years, and has therefore chosen assisted suicide; the place to which she has taken her is actually an exclusive clinic where patients can spend their last six days in complete peace before taking their own lives by poisoning themselves after a simple ritual. Ines is distraught and cannot accept that Emilie has kept everything from her, but her sister bitterly claims that she did it because it was the only way she could accompany her on her final journey. In fact, during their stay, the two will repeatedly confront each other harshly about their conflicting life choices: Emilie has remained close to her mother, who fell into depression because of her separation from her husband, until her suicide; Ines soon distanced herself from her, accused her of weakness and victimhood, and did not even go to the funeral, building a nice career as an excuse for her constant absence and creating a kind of armour of rationality and self-preservation. At the clinic, the two women not only meet but also the charming Mr Daren (Charles Dance), also terminally ill, a wealthy playboy who is now an old man and organises a party on his last night, and Brian (Mark Stanley), a former footballer who has been paralysed and rendered impotent by a car accident and who, attracted to Emilie, spends a night with her, arousing her anger that he has decided to leave life behind despite his health.

documents.title: Detroit
documents.tagline: It's time we knew
documents.overview: A police raid in Detroit in 1967 results in one of the largest citizens' uprisings in the history of the United States.
documents.plot:
On July 23, 1967, the Detroit Police Department stage a raid on an unlicensed club during a celebration for some African American veterans returning from the Vietnam War. While suspects are being arrested, a mob forms and begins throwing rocks at the officers before looting nearby stores and starting fires, beginning the 12th Street Riot. With local authorities, elected representatives, and emergency services unable to maintain order, Governor George W. Romney authorizes the National Guard and President Lyndon B. Johnson authorizes Army paratroopers to enter Detroit to provide assistance. On the second day of rioting, officers Krauss and Flynn pursue a fleeing looter, and Krauss kills the man with a shotgun against orders, but is allowed to remain on duty while his superiors debate filing murder charges.
Seconds before The Dramatics, a black R&B vocal group, take the stage for a performance that they hope will lead to a recording contract with Motown, the police shut down the venue due to rioting outside. The bus the group gets on is attacked by rioters, and, in the ensuing chaos, they get split up. Larry, the lead singer, and his friend, Fred, rent a room in the nearby Algiers Motel—in a detached annex building—to get off the streets. They meet two young white women, Julie and Karen, who introduce them to Carl, Lee, Aubrey, and Michael. Carl and Lee stage a prank using a starter pistol, upsetting Julie and Karen, who go to the room of Greene, a Vietnam War veteran, while Larry and Fred return to their own room.
Melvin Dismukes, a private security guard, is at a grocery store near the Algiers to protect it from rioters. Some guardsmen pull up outside, and Carl decides to fire several blanks at the troops to frighten them. The shots are mistaken for a sniper attack, and members of the National Guard and the state and local police descend upon the Algiers annex to investigate. Krauss guns down a fleeing Carl immediately upon entering the building and plants a knife next to the body.
The task force lines up everyone they find in the annex against the wall, demanding to know who the sniper was. No weapon is found, but Krauss begins to terrorize and beat the suspects while interrogating them. Dismukes arrives and, although he does not like what he sees, does not challenge Krauss openly. As the situation spirals out of control, most of the state police and national guardsmen leave to avoid being associated with it, but no one intervenes or reports the abuse.
One by one, Krauss orders several suspects to be moved to different rooms and subjected to mock executions in order to terrify the others into confessing. Julie and Karen are taken to an upstairs room when Karen begins screaming, and Julie's clothes get torn off. Disgusted, one of the remaining Guardsman gets them released from custody.

documents.title: A Cinderella Story: If the Shoe Fits
documents.original_title: A Cinderella Story: If the Shoe Fits
documents.tagline: A magical musical treat for the dreamer in all of us.
documents.overview: A contemporary musical version of the classic Cinderella story in which the servant step daughter hope to compete in a musical competition for a famous pop star.
documents.plot:
A Cinderella Story: If the Shoe Fits is a 2016 American musical teen comedy film directed by Michelle Johnston in her directorial debut, the fourth installment in the A Cinderella Story series. It stars Sofia Carson as Tessa, a young mechanic who secretly competes for the lead in a musical, Thomas Law as the star Reed West, and Jennifer Tilly as her stepmother, Divine, with Nicole Fortuin and David Ury.

Since her father's death, Tessa has lived with Divine and her stepsisters, Athena and Olympia. She goes along as their assistant to auditions at a luxury hotel for a musical based on Cinderella, directed by Freddie Marks and starring Reed, with whom she is instantly smitten. Freddie announces that auditions are open to everyone and that the actress cast as the lead will receive a recording contract. Tessa befriends Georgie, the show's make-up artist, and helps the stagehands repair a motorcycle for the production; Reed, seeing her work, takes her for a man. Inspired by the hotel staff's performances, Tessa decides to audition, and since her stepfamily forbids it, Georgie gives her a makeover and a fake identity. Her singing impresses Reed and Freddie, but when her stepfamily bursts into the dance audition, she flees, leaving a dance shoe behind.

Reed announces that whoever brings the matching shoe by midnight will win the role, and Divine orders Tessa to forge a copy for her daughters. Fixing the motorcycle, Tessa bonds with Reed and tells him about her father, then hands in her real shoe and wins the part under the stage name Bella Snow, secretly attending rehearsals. Told by Freddie that Reed is engaged to his co-star Harper Halston, she distances herself from him. Her stepsisters discover her secret and lock her away on opening day to steal the lead, but she escapes through an air vent. As chaos erupts onstage, Reed confronts Freddie for meddling and declares that he and Harper are only friends and that he loves someone else. Tessa appears without her disguise, the show succeeds, she receives her record contract and rejects Divine, and she and Reed ride off on the motorcycle she repaired.

The film was released digitally on August 2, 2016, alongside its soundtrack album from WaterTower Music, and on DVD that month. Its Freeform premiere in November 2016 drew 1.11 million viewers, and a Disney Channel airing in January 2017 drew 2.13 million. A Cinderella Story: Christmas Wish followed in 2019.

documents.title: Throne of Elves
documents.overview: In the mythical Elven world of Altera, an epic battle unfolds between the beautiful Princess Liya and the Dark Elf Elena, who has gained possession of a jewel so powerful it allows its holder complete authority over all Alterans.
documents.plot:
Throne of Elves, also known as Dragon Nest 2: Throne of Elves, is a 2016 Chinese animated adventure romance directed by Song Yuefeng and the sequel to the 2014 film Dragon Nest: Warriors' Dawn, itself based on the video game Dragon Nest. The English dub features Ryan Potter as Little Fish, Ashley Boettcher as Princess Liya, Anika Noni Rose as Meyla, Julie Nathanson as Queen Mayre, Gavin Hammon as Prince Alyan, Kevin Michael Richardson as Barnac and Enn Reitel as the blacksmith Berlin.

Years after the first film, Liya's brother Alyan is to marry her friend Mayre, queen of the Elves, and Liya invites her human sweetheart, Little Fish, now apprenticed to Berlin, despite Mayre's reluctance. Meanwhile, Mayre's long-lost sister Meyla, consumed by evil, plots to rule all Elves by seizing the Gem of Life, the counterpart and power source of her own dark gem, and raises Elven ghosts from an ancient battlefield as her army. Sensing the threat, Mayre entrusts the gem to Liya, warning her to keep it from Fish because humans are prone to greed. Fish arrives with Berlin and Barnac to a cold welcome from the Elves, including Alyan, who distrust humans.

During the wedding, Meyla attacks, and failing to find the gem on Mayre, abducts her, infecting Fish with dark magic when he intervenes. She demands the gem from Alyan as ransom at the ancient battlefield. Alyan pursues her with Liya and his guards, and Fish follows on Berlin's hoverboard, but their attempt to free Mayre from Meyla's flying ship fails, and Meyla invades Fish's mind. She imprisons Mayre in the Dark Valley, a black mountain ringed by lava furnaces, and travels north to merge with the soul of a great dragon frozen in ice. Fish resists her control and rejoins Alyan's party, rescuing the few survivors of a ghost ambush, but Meyla later forces him to try to seize the gem from Liya. When they shoot at each other, his love lets him break free, and he fires a headless arrow while hers mortally wounds him; Liya heals him with the gem. United, humans and Elves head for the Dark Valley, where Liya sends the gem to Mayre by arrow. Meyla takes a demonic form, and Fish lures her into a lava furnace, killing them both. The Gem of Life then frees the ghosts, turns the furnace into a tree and revives Fish, convincing Alyan that humans can be selfless, while the overlooked Meyla also returns to life, cleansed of darkness.

Beijing Enlight Pictures released the film in China in 2D and 3D, where it grossed CN¥23.4 million.

documents.title: The Last Princess
documents.tagline: Based on the true story of the last princess of the last empire.
documents.overview: Under the oppressive Japanese colonial rule, Deok-hye, the last Princess of the declining Joseon Dynasty, is forced to move to Japan. She spends her days missing home, while struggling to maintain dignity as a princess. After a series of failed tries, Deok-hye makes her final attempt to return home with help of her childhood sweetheart, Jang-han.
documents.plot:
The Last Princess (Korean: Deokhye Ongju, literally "Princess Deokhye") is a 2016 South Korean period drama directed by Hur Jin-ho and based on the best-selling 2009 novel by Kwon Bi-young. Son Ye-jin stars as Princess Deokhye, the last princess of the Joseon dynasty, with Park Hae-il as Kim Jang-han, her childhood friend. The film depicts Deokhye's life in Japan after she was forced to move there as a teenager under Japanese colonial rule, and her long struggle to return home. Son had previously worked with Hur on the 2005 film April Snow.

In 1925, Korea is under Japanese rule, and thirteen-year-old Deokhye, the daughter of Emperor Gojong, is sent to Japan, officially to study but in reality as part of the colonial authorities' efforts to assimilate the Korean royal family. Homesick and isolated, she tries repeatedly to return to Korea after finishing school, but her attempts are blocked by Han Taek-soo, a pro-Japanese Korean official who serves the colonial government.

Deokhye is reunited with Kim Jang-han, her childhood friend, who is now an officer in the Japanese army but secretly working with the Korean independence movement. He plans a covert operation to smuggle Deokhye and her brother, Crown Prince Yi Un, to Shanghai, where the Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea is based. The plan fails when Han discovers it, and Deokhye and Kim lose contact. In 1931, Deokhye is forced to marry the Japanese aristocrat Count Sō Takeyuki, and after the birth of their daughter she suffers a severe mental illness. Decades later, Kim, now a newspaper journalist, discovers her confined in a Japanese psychiatric hospital and campaigns to persuade the South Korean government to allow her to come back. In 1962, Deokhye finally returns to her homeland.

The film portrays Deokhye as a symbol of the suffering of the Korean people under colonial rule. Its story mixes historical events with fiction: Kim Jang-han is an invented character, and the film takes dramatic liberties with the historical record.

The Last Princess was a commercial success, drawing about 5.6 million admissions in South Korea, and Son Ye-jin won Best Actress at both the Grand Bell Awards and the Baeksang Arts Awards.

documents.title: Teen Titans: The Judas Contract
documents.tagline: The young fight hard for justice.
documents.overview: Tara Markov is a girl who has power over earth and stone; she is also more than she seems. Is the newest Teen Titan an ally or a threat? And what are the mercenary Deathstroke's plans for the Titans?
documents.plot:
Teen Titans: The Judas Contract is a 2017 American animated superhero film directed by Sam Liu from a screenplay by Ernie Altbacker, based on the storyline by Marv Wolfman and George Pérez. The 29th DC Universe Animated Original Movie and a sequel to Justice League vs. Teen Titans (2016), it features Miguel Ferrer as Deathstroke, in his final film role, and Christina Ricci as Terra, with Stuart Allan, Jake T. Austin, Taissa Farmiga and Brandon Soo Hoo.

In a flashback set five years earlier, the original Teen Titans, led by Dick Grayson as Robin, rescue the alien princess Starfire from captors sent by her sister Blackfire and offer her a home on Earth, and Dick falls for her. In the present, Dick, now Nightwing, rejoins the Titans as they pursue Brother Blood, the leader of a terrorist cult who plans to capture the team and absorb their powers with a machine. Blood hires the mercenary Deathstroke to deliver them, and Deathstroke, who still wants revenge on Damian Wayne, the new Robin, monitors the team through a double agent: Terra, whom he rescued after her village turned against her, and who joined the Titans a year earlier. Although she initially keeps her distance, Terra warms to the team and begins a relationship with Beast Boy. When Damian grows suspicious of her, she captures him.

Deathstroke and Terra then abduct Beast Boy at a convention where he is recording a podcast with Kevin Smith, Blue Beetle at a soup kitchen, Starfire at her apartment and Raven at Titans Tower. Nightwing escapes an ambush by faking his death. Terra reveals her betrayal to her captive teammates, but because the machine needs a sixth Titan, Deathstroke hands her over to Blood as well. Nightwing interrupts the ritual and frees the team, and Terra, enraged by Deathstroke's betrayal, turns against him and Blood. Raven depowers Blood by unleashing her demonic side, Terra buries Deathstroke under rocks, and Blood is shot dead by his lover, Mother Mayhem, to prevent his capture. Ashamed, Terra brings down the fortress on herself and dies in Beast Boy's arms. Later, Beast Boy tells Kevin Smith that he will always miss her, and a post-credits scene reveals that Jericho survived being shot by Mother Mayhem.

The film premiered at WonderCon on March 31, 2017, and was released digitally on April 4 and on home media on April 18 by Warner Home Video, three months after Ferrer's death. Reviews were generally positive, with 83% approval on Rotten Tomatoes from a small sample.

documents.title: Batman and Harley Quinn

documents.overview: Batman and Nightwing are forced to team with the Joker's sometimes-girlfriend Harley Quinn to stop a global threat brought about by Poison Ivy and Jason Woodrue, the Floronic Man.

documents.title: RE:BORN
documents.tagline: Zero Range Combat
documents.overview: A legend covert soldier with a mysterious past decides to unleash once again his beast within to stand up for what he cares about.
documents.plot:
RE:BORN is a Japanese action film directed by Yuji Shimomura and written by Benio Saeki, starring Tak Sakaguchi (credited as TAK∴) in his return to acting. The cast also includes Yura Kondo, Takumi Saitoh, Hitomi Hasebe, Mariko Shinoda, Masaya Kato, Issei Ishida and Akio Otsuka, and the score is by Kenji Kawai. The film is built around close-quarters combat: Sakaguchi spent about a year training under Yoshitaka Inagawa, founder of the "Zero Range Combat" system, who served as the film's tactical supervisor and also plays the assassin Abyss Walker.

At a training ground deep in the mountains, a platoon of thirty special forces soldiers rehearsing an exercise against a lone enemy is wiped out by a single unknown attacker. Toshiro Kuroda, once a member of an elite mercenary unit where he was known as the Ghost, now works in a convenience store in Kaga and lives with Sachi, a young girl related to him whom he rescued from the brainwashing experiments of his former commander, Phantom. Toshiro keeps his urge for violence in check with medication and counselling, but the strain is growing. When he kills an assassin sent to murder him, he realizes that Phantom, whose unit he destroyed when he turned against it, wants him dead and has hired Abyss Walker, Toshiro's former partner and his equal in combat. Kenji Makabe, a former comrade left blind and paralysed when he shielded Toshiro, sends his men Max and Masaru to help.

After Sachi is kidnapped, Toshiro reveals that he has allowed it in order to find the enemy's base. He, Max and Masaru then advance as hunters into a forest held by more than 200 of Phantom's soldiers. Masaru hesitates in front of Casper, a girl soldier who survived the same experiments as Sachi, and is killed, while Toshiro defeats Phantom's lieutenants Fox, Eagle and Casper. He rescues Sachi, entrusts her to Max and goes on alone, overcoming Abyss Walker in a brutal duel before narrowly defeating Phantom and collapsing. Later, as Sachi buries a book Toshiro gave her on a beach, he is seen watching from a distance.

The film premiered at the Bucheon International Fantastic Film Festival in 2016, screened at Fantastic Fest and opened in Japan on August 12, 2017. In The Japan Times, Mark Schilling found Sakaguchi still a convincingly lethal presence but compared the story to a video game in which the hero faces a series of bosses.

documents.title: Scooby-Doo! and WWE: Curse of the Speed Demon
documents.original_title: Scooby-Doo! and WWE: Curse of the Speed Demon
documents.overview: When Scooby and Mystery Inc. visit an off-road racing competition, it's not long before strange events start to occur. A mysterious phantom racer, known only as Inferno, is causing chaos and is determined to sabotage the race. It's up to Scooby-Doo, Shaggy and their new driving partner, The Undertaker, to save the race and solve the mystery.
documents.plot:
Scooby-Doo! and WWE: Curse of the Speed Demon is an animated film that combines the classic mystery-solving adventures of Scooby-Doo with the world of professional wrestling. The movie follows Shaggy, Velma, Daphne, Fred, and Scooby as they team up with WWE Superstar John Cena to solve a supernatural mystery.

At its core, the film explores themes of friendship, teamwork, and embracing one's unique strengths and weaknesses. The characters must put aside their differences and work together to overcome the challenges they face, learning valuable lessons about trust, loyalty, and communication along the way.

The movie also touches on the idea of identity and self-discovery, as Shaggy struggles to find his place in the world beyond being Scooby's best friend. Through his interactions with John Cena's character, he begins to discover new aspects of himself and develop a sense of confidence and purpose.

Furthermore, the film pokes fun at the conventions of both Scooby-Doo and professional wrestling, using humor and satire to comment on the tropes and clichés that define these genres. This self-awareness adds a layer of depth and cleverness to the story, making it a fun and entertaining ride for audiences of all ages.

Overall, Scooby-Doo! and WWE: Curse of the Speed Demon is a lighthearted, family-friendly film that celebrates the power of friendship, teamwork, and embracing one's individuality.

documents.title: A Dark Song
documents.tagline: Not everything can be forgiven.
documents.overview: A determined young woman and a damaged occultist risk their lives and souls to perform a dangerous ritual that will grant them what they want.
documents.plot:
A bitter and grieving Sophia Howard rents an isolated house in rural Wales to convince short-tempered occultist Joseph Solomon to lead her in a gruelling, months-long rite dictated from The Book of Abramelin to summon her guardian angel, whom Sophia can then ask to speak with her dead seven-year-old son. Solomon explains that once they begin, if they leave the house before the ritual is finished, they will be in grave peril, and that Sophia must endure months of punishing exercises in which they will deal with real demons and angels. She agrees. She then complies with dozens of painful, harrowing exercises, but refuses to do the forgiveness ceremony. To compensate for her refusal, Solomon insists she must drink his blood, and also says they must have sex as part of the ritual. After manipulating her into taking off her clothes, he masturbates, then tells her it was just for his own release, not for ritualistic purposes. Sophia gets revenge by urinating in his breakfast the next day.
They begrudgingly get to know one another over time. However, after months, a frustrated Sophia complains that it’s taking too long, and Solomon accuses her of impairing the ritual by not being honest about something. She admits that the real favour she will ask the angel is revenge upon whoever kidnapped and killed her son. That night he awakens her and says that because her dishonesty has made her impure, a re-birthing ritual in the tub is required. However, he drowns her, recites a spell, and revives her with CPR. Angered, she pushes him and he accidentally falls on a large kitchen knife, impaling him in the side. As she treats the wound with their meagre medical supplies, he explains that this is a sign that the ritual is beginning to work, and that she will have her revenge. He discloses that he will ask the angel to make him invisible for the rest of his life, to be away from people as he “want some quiet before the howl.”
As Solomon soldiers on with the wound, Sophia begins seeing and hearing menacing presences in the house, including the voice of her son. When Solomon's wound becomes infected, he begins to fail and eventually dies in his sleep. When Sophia goes back to his books for further instruction, everything has been crossed out, unreadable. She steps beyond the perimeter of the house but her car won't start. After walking down an empty road, she is disturbed to realise that she has arrived back at the mansion.
She re-enters to discover various demons appearing. They drag her to the basement, torment her, and cut off a finger as she tells them how sorry she is. They retreat as a brilliant white light fills the house. She finds a massive, beatific angel in armour awaiting her. She asks it for the power to forgive, and it smiles. Later, she performs a water burial of Solomon, then drives away.

documents.title: Blame!
documents.overview: In the distant technological future, civilization has reached its ultimate Net-based form. An "infection" in the past caused the automated systems to spiral out of order, resulting in a multi-leveled city structure that replicates itself infinitely in all directions. Now humanity has lost access to the city's controls, and is hunted down and purged by the defense system known as the Safeguard. In a tiny corner of the city, a little enclave known as the Electro-Fishers is facing eventual extinction, trapped between the threat of the Safeguard and dwindling food supplies. A girl named Zuru goes on a journey to find food for her village, only to inadvertently cause doom when an observation tower senses her and summons a Safeguard pack to eliminate the threat. With her companions dead and all escape routes blocked, the only thing that can save her now is the sudden arrival of Killy the Wanderer, on his quest for the Net Terminal Genes, the key to restoring order to the world.

documents.title: I'm Not Ashamed
documents.tagline: Her faith would touch the world.
documents.overview: Based on the inspiring and powerful true story and journal entries of Rachel Joy Scott- the first student killed in the Columbine High School shooting in 1999.
documents.plot:
In Littleton, Colorado, a young Rachel Joy Scott witnesses her father leave her family in the middle of the night. Her mother then struggles financially and encourages her children to pray for financial help. Rachel begins to embrace the Christian faith.
By 1998, Rachel is a sophomore at Columbine High School; she becomes rebellious and begins sneaking out to hang out with her friends, Madison, Gabby, and Celine. During the summer, Rachel's mother sends her to her cousins in Louisiana, where her journey with Christianity grows. By around the first day of her junior year, Rachel witnesses the jocks picking on Eric Harris and Dylan Klebold. Eric then threatens to harm them.
Later that year, Rachel begins to get involved with the head of the drama club, Alex Dickerson, and during a rehearsal, the two kiss. Later on, at a breakthrough meeting, Rachel meets Nathan Ballard, a homeless youth whose mother is a heroin addict. With Rachel's help, Nathan is able to be put up at another kid's house. Nathan is grateful.
One day, Rachel's stepfather, Larry, finds a beer bottle from a party in the car, and Rachel loses her right to the car, becoming rebellious again. At the first performance of the school play, Nathan arrives and begins to fight with Alex, embarrassing Rachel. At a party that night, Rachel discovers Alex cheating on her with Madison. She then begins to be bullied more often by others and even considers suicide at one point. However, with Nathan's encouragement, Rachel turns back to her faith and inspires other Christian students to not give up hope, despite being bullied. Meanwhile, Eric and Dylan plan their revenge on the school.
Meanwhile, Rachel tries to help Celine with family issues but is rebuffed. The day before prom, Celine reconciles with Rachel, revealing that she has issues with her mother. Not long after at prom, Alex tries to reconcile with Rachel, but she declines his apology.
On April 20, 1999, Rachel reconciles with Madison, and the two make plans to hang out the next day. At lunch, Rachel has an emotional conversation with a fellow student, Dave Rogers, about family issues. Rachel calms him by saying that everything happens for a reason. Just then, Eric and Dylan come out of the parking lot and begin shooting at Rachel and Richard Costaldo. Richard is knocked unconscious, while Rachel struggles to get away. Eric and Dylan corner her, with Eric tauntingly asking her if she still believes in God, and when Rachel tells him that she does, he points his gun to her head and shoots her. The assailants then storm the school offscreen, killing 11 other students and one teacher before taking their own lives. In the aftermath, U.S. President Bill Clinton (via archive footage) says that citizens must do more to reach out to our children teach them to express anger and resolve their conflicts with words, not weapons before addressing the nation that the prayers of the American people are with Littleton.

documents.title: 7 Guardians of the Tomb
documents.tagline: Unearth the legend. Unleash the curse.
documents.overview: An innocent discovery of a well-preserved mummified Emperor from 200 BC China unearths a 2000 year old nightmare - a secret that should have remained buried.
documents.plot:
7 Guardians of the Tomb, also released as Guardians of the Tomb, is a 2018 Australian-Chinese science fiction horror adventure film written and directed by Kimble Rendall. Li Bingbing stars as Jia, a venom specialist, with Kellan Lutz, Kelsey Grammer, Wu Chun, Stef Dawson and Shane Jacobson in supporting roles. Described as the largest co-production between China and Australia at the time, it was released on 19 January 2018.

The film opens in ancient China, where the emperor commands his court physician to find the secret of immortality, a quest that briefly takes the doctor to Australia and an encounter with its Aboriginal people before he returns home. In the present day, Luke and Ethan, two researchers working for the businessman Mason, are investigating the legend of the emperor and eternal life in a remote part of China. Exploring a cave, they are attacked by swarms of spiders, and Luke manages to send a distress signal before apparently succumbing.

Mason persuades Luke's estranged sister Jia, an expert in venom and dangerous animals, to join a rescue expedition. In China they meet the rest of the team, including the adventurer Jack, Milly, Chen and Gary, and set off quickly to reach the location of the signal before a lightning storm arrives. Jia notices that Mason has brought several vials of antivenom, a sign that he knows more than he is admitting. Inside the mountain the team discovers a vast ancient tomb and a labyrinth of tunnels guarded by millions of aggressive, venomous funnel-web spiders, as well as deadly traps left by the emperor's builders. As members of the expedition are picked off one by one, Jia uncovers the real purpose of Mason's mission and the connection between the spiders' venom and the ancient search for eternal life, and she must find her brother and escape before the guardians of the tomb overwhelm them all.

The film drew largely unfavorable notices from Western reviewers, who found its script and characters thin and compared it unfavorably with earlier creature features. It was one of a number of large-scale co-productions of the period that paired Chinese and Western stars in the hope of reaching audiences in both markets, and it was later distributed internationally on home video and streaming.

documents.title: Killing Ground
documents.tagline: A remote campsite. An abandoned tent. A romantic getaway to die for.
documents.overview: A couple's camping trip turns into a frightening ordeal when they stumble across the scene of a horrific crime.

documents.title: The Loud House Movie
documents.tagline: The Louds are about to rule.
documents.overview: The Loud family travel to Scotland and discover they are descendants of Scottish royalty as they move into their giant ancestral castle.
documents.plot:
The Loud House Movie is a 2021 American animated musical fantasy comedy based on the Nickelodeon series The Loud House. Produced by Nickelodeon Movies and written by Kevin Sullivan and Chris Viscardi, with Dave Needham making his directing debut, it features David Tennant as Angus, Michelle Gomez as Morag and Katy Townsend as Lucille Loud and Old Aggie, alongside the series' regular voice cast, led by Asher Bishop as Lincoln Loud.

Lincoln, the only boy among eleven children, helps his ten sisters through their busy schedules, but when the girls are celebrated for their achievements at the family restaurant, he feels overlooked. Inspired by his best friend Clyde, who has discovered family roots in Paris, Lincoln asks about his own ancestry, and his sister Lisa traces their father's line to Scotland. The family sets off for a week's holiday, while Lori's boyfriend Bobby, misunderstanding a broken phone call as a break-up, follows her. At Loch Loud the Louds learn that they descend from the local royal family, and the groundskeeper Angus shows them a portrait of ancestors who look just like them, explaining that the Duke was the most special member of the family. Lynn and Lana find an egg that hatches into a baby dragon, Lela, who grows whenever she eats, and the family meets the ghost of their ancestor Lucille.

Lincoln wins over the villagers, persuades his family to move to Scotland and is invested as Duke, to the fury of the caretaker Morag. Lucille reveals that the Louds' forebears were driven out by Morag's ancestor, Old Aggie, and Morag plans to repeat the feat using the Dragon Stone, a gem that can control dragons when set in the royal sceptre. She tricks Lincoln into riding Lela during a performance, then hypnotises the dragon, which wrecks the town. Disgraced, the Louds leave, and Morag crowns herself duchess, planning to use the ever-growing Lela to drive out everyone else. Warned by Lucille, Lincoln and his sisters sail back. While Lincoln distracts Morag, baby Lily swaps the sceptre for a burrito; Lela destroys the stone and saves them when Morag pushes them off a cliff. Lincoln hands the title of Duke to Angus, Lela strands Morag on an island of noisy seals, and the family sails home just as Bobby arrives.

Originally planned as a theatrical release by Paramount Pictures, the film was instead released digitally on Netflix on August 20, 2021. Reviews were mixed to positive.

documents.title: Lady Macbeth
documents.overview: Rural England, 1865. Katherine, suffocated by her loveless marriage to a bitter man and restrained by his father's tyranny, unleashes an irresistible force within her, so powerful that she will stop at nothing to get what she wants.
documents.plot:
In 1865, a young woman named Katherine joins the landed gentry by marrying Alexander Lester. His domineering father Boris bought Katherine to produce a legitimate heir with Alexander. They live on Boris's rural estate in Northumberland, England. Little of the couple's backstory emerges. She and her late mother shared an interest in walking and nature. He has a colliery and an illegitimate child across the county in Amble,
and a repressed hatred of Boris.
Katherine prepares for the wedding night with her maid Anna, who serves the household with a younger maid and a cook. Alexander arrives and tells Katherine she should stay indoors despite her interests. He has a voyueristic interest in her but refuses to consummate their marriage, and she tires of her solitary indoor routine. One day, Alexander leaves for Amble, while Boris travels to London. In their absence, Katherine enjoys walking around the estate. Katherine finds the estate workmen abusing Anna in an outbuilding, where the men live. Having freed Anna, Katherine is intrigued by the ringleader Sebastian, and they soon begin an overt affair. Anna becomes concerned by Katherine's behaviour, while Katherine suspects Anna has shared her concerns with their priest.
Boris returns. Katherine has drunk his stock of Beaujolais, but Anna takes the blame, and Boris humiliates her. Boris hears about the affair. He beats Sebastian then locks him up. Having argued over Sebastian's release and the lack of an heir, Boris strikes Katherine across her face. The next day, she poisons his breakfast which includes mushrooms foraged by Anna. As Boris struggles in an adjacent room, Katherine orders Anna to sit with her until he falls silent. His death is not generally regarded as suspicious, but Anna is traumatized and goes mute. Alexander refuses to attend Boris's funeral.
Katherine moves Sebastian into the house. Late one night, she wakes as Alexander returns unexpectedly. They meet in their bedroom, while Sebastian hides in the closet. Having promised to dishonor Boris at his grave, Alexander confronts Katherine over the affair and the damage to his reputation. He says Sebastian will be dismissed, and she will live indoors. Katherine responds by fetching Sebastian for sex. As the men fight, Katherine arms herself with a poker then bludgeons Alexander to death.
Evidence of Alexander's return is disposed of in woodland: Sebastian buries his body, while Katherine kills his horse with a shotgun. They live together as mistress and master. Enough time passes that Alexander is generally regarded as missing presumed dead.
A young boy and his grandmother, Teddy and Agnes, arrive to live in the house. Agnes explains that Alexander stayed with them in Amble then left to return home to Katherine. Teddy is his illegitimate son with her late daughter. Alexander made the boy his ward so, as Teddy's legal guardian, Agnes replaces Katherine as mistress. Sebastian resumes his working life but is resentful and avoids Katherine.

documents.title: ARQ
documents.overview: Two old friends living in a dystopic future become trapped in a mysterious time loop — one that may have something to do with an ongoing battle between an omnipotent corporation and a ragtag band of rebels.
documents.plot:
ARQ is a 2016 American and Canadian science fiction action thriller written and directed by Tony Elliott in his feature debut. Robbie Amell stars as an engineer caught in a time loop during a home invasion, with Rachael Taylor as his former lover and Gray Powell, Jacob Neayem and Shaun Benson as the intruders. The film was selected for the Discovery section of the 2016 Toronto International Film Festival, where it premiered on September 9, before Netflix released it worldwide on September 16, 2016.

In a dystopian near future ravaged by an energy war, Renton wakes in bed beside Hannah, a woman he once loved. Masked men burst into the bedroom, and when Renton breaks his neck trying to escape, he wakes again a moment earlier. This time the intruders tie the couple up. Their leader, called Father, says they represent the Bloc, a rebel group opposed to the powerful Torus Corporation, and demands the "scrips," a form of currency Renton is accused of stealing from Torus. Renton reveals that he built and stole a device called the ARQ, which appears to be a perpetual motion machine, while working for the corporation.

Each time Renton dies, the loop resets and the morning begins again. He tries escape, deceit and poison gas, discovering along the way that Hannah is herself a member of the Bloc and resents him for abandoning her to Torus, which tortured her. Soon Hannah also begins to remember previous loops, and Renton realizes that the ARQ is not producing endless energy at all but is generating the time loop itself. As alliances shift with every iteration, it emerges that one of the intruders, Sonny, is secretly a mercenary working for Torus, and he too becomes aware of the repetition. Renton and Hannah must use everything they have learned across the loops to keep the ARQ from falling into the corporation's hands and to find a way out of the cycle.

Elliott, a writer on the series Orphan Black, shot the film in Toronto over 19 days on a budget he described as under $2 million. John DeFore of The Hollywood Reporter called it a tricky little time twister that makes the most of limited resources, comparing its concept to Groundhog Day and Edge of Tomorrow and praising how it resolves its paradoxes. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds a 43% rating from seven reviews.

documents.title: A Wish for Christmas
documents.overview: Sara Shaw is the type of woman who prefers to sit on the sidelines at work, but when her big idea for a Christmas initiative is stolen, she makes a wish to Santa that she'll finally have the courage to stand up for herself. Santa grants her wish, but only gives her 48 hours. As the clock ticks, Sara will discover how to channel the Christmas magic and speak her mind all on her own.
