documents.title: Pinocchio
documents.tagline: The most beloved fairy tale comes to life.
documents.overview: In this live-action adaptation of the beloved fairytale, old woodcarver Geppetto fashions a wooden puppet, Pinocchio, who magically comes to life. Pinocchio longs for adventure and is easily led astray, encountering magical beasts, fantastical spectacles, while making friends and foes along his journey. However, his dream is to become a real boy, which can only come true if he finally changes his ways.
documents.plot:
Pinocchio is a 2019 fantasy film co-written, directed and co-produced by Matteo Garrone, based on Carlo Collodi's 1883 book The Adventures of Pinocchio. Federico Ielapi plays the title character, with Roberto Benigni as Geppetto, Gigi Proietti as Mangiafuoco, Rocco Papaleo and Massimo Ceccherini as the Cat and the Fox, and Marine Vacth as the adult Fairy with Turquoise Hair. A passion project for Garrone, who drew his first storyboard of the story at the age of six, it was Benigni's second live-action Pinocchio film after his own 2002 adaptation.

The poor carpenter Geppetto carves a wooden puppet he hopes will earn him a living by touring the country, names it Pinocchio and, when it comes to life, calls it his son. Ignoring the advice of a Talking Cricket, Pinocchio burns his feet off by the fire, and Geppetto promises new ones if he goes to school. Instead the puppet is lured to a puppet theatre and ruins the show, and the furious Mangiafuoco carries him off; touched when Pinocchio offers to be burned in another puppet's place, he frees him with five gold coins for Geppetto. The scheming Fox and Cat persuade Pinocchio to plant the coins in the Field of Miracles, attack him disguised as assassins and leave him hanging from a tree, where he is rescued by the Fairy as a little girl, whose questions make his nose grow with each lie. Tricked again, he loses the coins, and when he reports the theft to a gorilla judge he is jailed until he gains release by claiming to have committed a crime. Learning that Geppetto has gone overseas to find him, Pinocchio is shipwrecked on the Island of the Busy Bees, where the grown-up Fairy promises to make him a real boy if he studies and behaves. He becomes a model pupil, but his friend Lucignolo tempts him to the Land of Toys, where both turn into donkeys. Sold to a circus and lamed, Pinocchio is thrown into the sea, where fish nibble away his donkey skin, and he is swallowed by a huge sea monster, inside which he finds Geppetto. They escape while the asthmatic monster sleeps with its mouth open and reach shore with a friendly tuna. Pinocchio works for a farmer to earn milk for his ailing father, resists the Fox and the Cat, and is finally made a real boy.

Released in Italy by 01 Distribution on 19 December 2019, it grossed €15 million domestically, Garrone's biggest domestic success, and received positive reviews. It won six Nastro d'Argento Awards and earned Academy Award nominations for costume design and makeup.
production_companies: MEDIA Programme of the European Union

documents.title: Dear Zindagi
documents.overview: An unconventional thinker helps a budding cinematographer gain a new perspective on life.
documents.plot:
Kaira is an aspiring cinematographer who dreams of directing her own films and works in Mumbai at a small firm. Blunt and cynical, she is most comfortable with her four best friends, Fatima, Jackie, Raunaq and Ganju. Kaira's life takes a downturn when she sleeps with her friend Raghuvendra, a film producer, and then breaks up with her childhood sweetheart Sid, a pub owner. Raghuvendra later gets engaged to another woman. Kaira's landlord evicts her because the building residents' association is annoyed by her bohemian lifestyle and has requested he only rent apartments to married couples and families. Kaira reluctantly returns to Goa to live with her parents, with whom she has unresolved issues. She spends many sleepless nights in unhappiness and uncertainty.
While in Goa, Kaira seeks out Dr. Jehangir "Jug" Khan, a psychiatrist, for her insomnia after inadvertently having heard him speak at a Mental Health Awareness conference. She warms up to Jug's unconventional methods during their sessions, trying to use them to understand herself. Meanwhile, she meets and starts a relationship with Rumi, a musician, but they quickly break up after she realizes they may not be right for each other. Subsequently, Kaira reunites with her younger brother, Kabir "Kiddo", the only person in her family to whom she confides. Matters with her family come to a head when Kaira has an outburst at a family event, where she confronts her parents about them abandoning and neglecting her as a child for years at her grandparents' house.
Kaira finally narrates the story of her abandonment to Jug. Her parents had left her as a child with her grandparents after their business failed and had neglected her while they tried to rebuild their business and after Kiddo was born, before suddenly taking her back years later. She lost her trust in her parents after overhearing her mother arguing with her grandfather over lying to Kaira about their situation to spare her from the difficult truth. Jug notes she tremendously fears desertion and does not allow herself to commit to relationships, leaving them before they can leave her. He advises her to see her parents as two regular people who are capable of making mistakes instead of focusing on the need to forgive them. Afterwards, Kaira tries to reconcile with her parents and works to finish her short film.
At their last session, Kaira admits to Jug that she has grown to have feelings for him. Jug responds it is normal for a patient to feel this way about their therapist, and while he likes her platonically, a relationship would not be possible between them. The two share a hug before Kaira leaves. Kaira finally completes her short film, which she had worked on for years. At the premiere, her friends, family, and previous partners are present to cheer her on. Kaira meets a furniture designer and initiates a conversation with him.

documents.title: Sword Art Online: The Movie – Ordinal Scale
documents.original_title: 劇場版 ソードアート・オンライン -オーディナル・スケール-
documents.tagline: It was just a game...or so I thought
documents.overview: In 2026, four years after the infamous Sword Art Online incident, a revolutionary new form of technology has emerged: the Augma, a device that utilizes an Augmented Reality system. Unlike the Virtual Reality of the NerveGear and the Amusphere, it is perfectly safe and allows players to use it while they are conscious, creating an instant hit on the market. The most popular application for the Augma is the game Ordinal Scale, which immerses players in a fantasy role-playing game with player rankings and rewards.  Following the new craze, Kirito's friends dive into the game, and despite his reservations about the system, Kirito eventually joins them. While at first it appears to be just fun and games, they soon find out that the game is not all that it seems...
documents.plot:
In the year 2026, the Augma is released to the public as an alternative system to the AmuSphere, as it projects a game layer on top of reality while the player is conscious, rather than using FullDive. The most prominent combat-based game is Ordinal Scale, in which a player's abilities are ranked by ordinal numbers.
Asuna, Lisbeth and Silica encourage Kirito to play OS upon hearing that Aincrad bosses have appeared. Kirito joins Asuna and Klein in a boss fight against Kagachi the Samurai Lord at Akihabara, where the game's mascot, AI idol singer Yuna, appears and gives players buff effects as she sings. Kirito fails to achieve anything due to lack of real world physical strength and agility. Eiji, the number-two ranked player, aids the group in defeating the boss. Before Asuna makes the killing blow, Eiji whispers the word "Switch", a game mechanic from SAO that she recognizes.
The next night, Asuna joins Klein and his group for another boss fight at Yoyogi Park while waiting for their last group member, unaware that he was injured by Eiji the night before. Asuna leaves Klein and his guild behind and proceeds to the fight against the Storm Griffin, which is again presided over by Yuna. Klein and his guild are surprised by the sudden appearance of a second boss, Zanghi the Flame Caller, and shockingly supported by Eiji, who physically attacks and defeats Klein and his entire guild in the real world using superior reflexes and seemingly superhuman strength. When Asuna returns to where she left them, Klein and his guild are nowhere to be seen. The following morning, as Kirito practices with OS in Yoyogi Park, a girl he doesn't know appears in a white hood, mouths something wordlessly and points off into the distance before disappearing. A confused Kirito is surprised by Asuna who has arrived to have lunch with him. While eating together, Asuna theorizes that Eiji was a former member of the Knights of the Blood Oath named Nautilus, while Yui deduces that the spawn locations of the Aincrad bosses line up with the SAO dungeon maps. Noting the absence of Klein, Kirito tries to check up on him.
Asuna, Lisbeth and Silica join the boss fight against Strict Hermit at Yebisu Garden Place, where Yuna and Eiji appear again. At the same time, Agil contacts Kirito and tells him that Klein has been hospitalized with a broken arm; Kirito, alarmed, rushes to protect Asuna and their friends. During the boss battle, a second boss, Dorz'l the Chaos Drake, suddenly appears and fixates on Silica. Eiji blocks Silica's escape by pushing her into the path of a lethal boss attack, and Asuna is defeated while protecting her; an orange orb materializes from Asuna and is quickly collected by one of the OS drones. After the battle, Asuna begins to suffer memory loss, and goes to the hospital for examination.
Asuna learns that the Augma device scanned her brain specifically for SAO memories and that the memory loss could worsen.

documents.title: The Son of Bigfoot
documents.tagline: Meet the wildest family around!
documents.overview: Teenage outsider Adam sets out on an epic and daring quest to uncover the mystery behind his long-lost dad, only to find out that he is none other than the legendary Bigfoot! He has been hiding deep in the forest for years to protect himself and his family from HairCo., a giant corporation eager to run scientific experiments with his special DNA. As father and son start making up for lost time after the boy's initial disbelief, Adam soon discovers that he too is gifted with superpowers beyond his imagination. But little do they know, HairCo. is on their tail as Adam's traces have led them to Bigfoot!
documents.plot:
The Son of Bigfoot, released in some territories as Bigfoot Junior, is a 2017 animated fantasy comedy directed by Ben Stassen and Jeremy Degruson and produced by the Belgian studio nWave Pictures. Bob Barlen and Cal Brunker wrote the screenplay, based on their own original script. Pappy Faulkner voices Adam Harrison, a lonely thirteen-year-old, with Chris Parson as his father, Marieve Herington as his mother Shelly, and Terrence Stone as the villainous businessman Wallace Eastman.

The film opens with a helicopter belonging to HairCo, a vast corporation devoted to hair-care products and run by Eastman, chasing a scientist named Dr. Harrison, who escapes by leaping into a river. Twelve years later, Harrison's son Adam lives with his mother in Portland, believing that his father died long ago. At school he is bullied, though a kind classmate named Emma likes him. Adam begins to undergo strange changes: his hearing and eyesight become extraordinarily sharp, and his hair and feet grow at an alarming rate.

Searching through a box that his mother has kept hidden, Adam discovers that his father is alive and learns where he is living. He sneaks away into the forest and finds that his father is none other than Bigfoot, his appearance the result of a genetic mutation, who has been hiding for years to protect himself and his family from Eastman, a man determined to experiment on his unique DNA for the benefit of his hair products. Spending time with his father, Adam discovers that he shares Bigfoot's abilities, including heightened senses, superhuman speed when barefoot, the power to heal and the ability to communicate with animals, and he meets his father's animal friends. However, a truck driver photographs Bigfoot rescuing Adam from an accident and sells the image to the newspaper, alerting Eastman, whose agents descend on the forest, forcing father and son to work together to escape capture and protect Adam's mother.

The film is a family adventure about an absent father reconnecting with his son, about accepting one's differences and about corporate greed, combined with slapstick humour and animal sidekicks.

The Son of Bigfoot received generally positive reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds an approval rating of about 75 percent; the consensus says it lacks innovation but provides entertaining fodder for younger viewers. It grossed about 47 million dollars worldwide against a budget of 20 million and was followed by a sequel, Bigfoot Family, in 2020.

documents.title: The Warriors Gate
documents.overview: After a mysterious chest opens a gateway through time, teen gamer Jack is transported to an ancient empire terrorized by a cruel barbarian king. Jack will need all of his gaming skills as he battles to defeat the barbarian, protect a beautiful princess, and somehow find his way back home.
documents.plot:
The Warriors Gate (Chinese: 勇士之門), also released as Enter the Warriors Gate, is a 2016 Chinese-French fantasy action-adventure directed by Matthias Hoene and written by Luc Besson and Robert Mark Kamen. Uriah Shelton stars as the teenage gamer Jack Bronson, with Mark Chao as the warrior Zhao, Ni Ni as Princess Su Lin, Dave Bautista as the barbarian king Arun the Cruel and Francis Ng as a wizard. It was released in China on 18 November 2016 in 2D and 3D formats, and on video on demand in the United States in May 2017.

Jack is an American teenager who spends his free time playing warrior-themed video games and works part-time at a Chinese antiques shop run by Mr. Cheng. His mother is struggling to sell their house before it goes into foreclosure, and Jack is regularly harassed by a neighborhood bully, Travis. One day an heirloom known as the Warriors Gate arrives at the shop from Mr. Cheng's cousin in Beijing, and Cheng gives it to Jack as a gift. That night Jack wakes up to find a sword at his throat: Zhao, a warrior from another realm, has come through it and believes Jack is the "Black Knight," the champion from Jack's video game. Zhao entrusts him with protecting the most precious thing in his kingdom, Princess Su Lin, who stays with Jack overnight.

The next morning barbarians arrive from the other realm to capture the princess. She fights them off, wrecking the house in the process, but they drag her back through the gate. Jack follows, finding himself in an ancient land, where he meets a wizard who freezes time and explains that Zhao was one of seven warriors raised to protect the emperor, and that their only match was Arun the Cruel, king of the barbarians, who poisoned the warriors and killed the emperor. Arun intends to marry Su Lin and seize the kingdom. Jack must use the skills he learned in gaming to train as a real warrior and, together with Zhao, rescue the princess and defeat Arun.

The Hollywood Reporter compared the film to The Last Starfighter, finding Hoene's direction competent rather than creative and lacking the flair of his debut Cockneys vs Zombies, while suggesting that its familiar story might appeal to young audiences fond of 1980s adventure films.

documents.title: Monster High: Welcome to Monster High
documents.original_title: Monster High: Welcome to Monster High
documents.tagline: Welcome to the most clever, quirky and exciting monster-filled school imaginable!
documents.overview: Monsters once lived in hiding—even from each other—because they were afraid they would be in danger if humans knew they existed. But Draculaura, the daughter of Dracula, along with her best ghoulfriends, dreamt of a school where everyone was welcome and accepted for who they are. Determined to make their dream come true, the ghouls travel the world on an epic adventure to recruit new students. But even in this amazing place, there's drama: a villainess zombie is spreading trouble rather than friendship, and every student must live with the fear that their secret will be revealed. Now the ghouls must save their school so that every monster has a place where they belong and their uniqueness is celebrated!
documents.plot:
Monster High: Welcome to Monster High (also titled Welcome to Monster High: The Origin Story) is a 2016 American computer-animated fantasy film that rebooted Mattel's Monster High franchise with redesigned characters and a new origin story. Directed by Stephen Donnelly, Olly Reid and Jun Falkenstein from a screenplay by Donnelly, Dana Starfield and Shane Amsterdam, it was the first second-generation special and was animated by the British studio Flaunt Productions, with music by Paul Robb and Michael Kotch. It received a limited US theatrical release on 27 August 2016 before arriving on streaming and DVD that September.

Draculaura, the daughter of Count Dracula, has spent her life in her father's mansion, forbidden to mingle with humans and dreaming of friends and a normal life. One night Frankie Stein, daughter of Frankenstein's creature, knocks at the door, having seen Draculaura turn into a bat. The two decide to open a school for monsters, who have always lived in hiding, even from one another. In the forest they recruit the werewolf Clawdeen Wolf, whose mother and brothers move in, and the mansion is converted into Monster High. Draculaura's blog, posted on the secret Monster Internet, draws thousands of followers, and with a magical amulet that teleports them to any monster whose name they know, the ghouls travel the world, recruiting the mummy Cleo de Nile in Egypt, Lagoona Blue in Australia, Deuce Gorgon and Venus McFlytrap.

Draculaura and Frankie run for student council presidents, promising a world where humans and monsters can coexist and rashly vowing to bring Draculaura's favourite pop star, Tash, to the school dance. Their rival is Moanica D'Kay, a zombie who commands an army of "Zomboyz" and wants monsters to rule over humans. She mocks the girls' dream, and Tash rejects Draculaura in horror at the sight of her fangs. Draculaura and Frankie nonetheless win the election, but Moanica crashes the dance with Tash as her hostage, planning to turn her into a zombie. Draculaura defeats Moanica in bat form, and when Moanica lunges at the singer and passes straight through her, Tash reveals that she is in fact a ghost named Ari Hauntington, who had disguised herself to live among humans, and she finally accepts being a monster.

The voice cast includes Debi Derryberry as Draculaura, Cassandra Lee Morris as Frankie, Salli Saffioti as Clawdeen and Cleo, Cristina Milizia as Moanica, Michael Sorich as Dracula and Jonquil Goode as Tash.

documents.title: Pottersville
documents.tagline: It's a magical life
documents.overview: Maynard, a beloved local businessman is mistaken for the legendary Bigfoot during an inebriated romp through town in a makeshift gorilla costume. The sightings set off an international Bigfoot media spectacle and a windfall of tourism dollars for a simple American town hit by hard times. When Brock Masterson, reality TV’s “Monster Hunter,” arrives to hunt the beast, Maynard agonizes over whether to come clean, destroying the rebirth of his beloved town, or perpetuate the inadvertent hoax.
documents.plot: Maynard, a beloved local businessman is mistaken for the legendary Bigfoot during an inebriated romp through town in a makeshift gorilla costume. The sightings set off an international Bigfoot media spectacle and a windfall of tourism dollars for a simple American town hit by hard times. When Brock Masterson, reality TV’s “Monster Hunter,” arrives to hunt the beast, Maynard agonizes over whether to come clean, destroying the rebirth of his beloved town, or perpetuate the inadvertent hoax.

documents.title: Sweet Virginia
documents.overview: A former rodeo star, now a motel manager, meets a young man who is responsible for the violence that suddenly has seized his small town.
documents.plot:
Sweet Virginia is a 2017 neo-noir thriller directed by Jamie M. Dagg and written by Benjamin and Paul China. It stars Jon Bernthal as Sam, a former bull riding champion who manages a motel in a small town, and Christopher Abbott as Elwood, a volatile drifter, with Imogen Poots as Lila, Rosemarie DeWitt as Bernadette, Odessa Young and Jared Abrahamson. The film is a slow-burning character study set around a brutal crime in a quiet community.

One night, three men are playing poker in a closed bar when a stranger enters and asks to be served. When he is turned away, he returns with a gun and kills all three. The next morning, Sam, a former bull rider whose career-ending injuries have left him with a limp and tremors, reads about the shootings while running the motel. He is having an affair with Bernadette, the widow of one of the victims. Meanwhile, it emerges that Lila, the wife of another victim, hired the killer to murder her husband, but the man killed the others as well when the plan went wrong. He now demands his payment, but Lila discovers that her late husband was bankrupt and left her nothing.

The killer, Elwood, checks into Sam's motel and begins to befriend him, praising him as a famous bull rider whom his late father admired. Sam, unaware of who Elwood is, introduces him to Lila, who pretends not to know him. As Elwood grows increasingly desperate for money and his volatile behavior escalates into further violence, he poses a growing threat to Lila, Bernadette and the gentle Sam, leading to a tense final confrontation at the motel.

The film draws on film noir and the western, contrasting the fragile, decent Sam with the menacing Elwood, and was praised for its atmosphere and performances.

Sweet Virginia premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival on April 21, 2017, and was released by IFC Films on November 17, 2017. It received favorable reviews, with 79 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it a smart, well-acted and atmospheric thriller, and a Metacritic score of 72. Dagg was nominated for the Directors Guild of Canada's Discovery Award.

documents.title: My Cousin Rachel
documents.tagline: Did she or didn't she?
documents.overview: A young Englishman plots revenge against his mysterious, beautiful cousin, believing that she murdered his guardian. But his feelings become complicated as he finds himself falling under the beguiling spell of her charms.
documents.plot:
In the 1830s, a young orphaned Philip is adopted by his older cousin Ambrose, who raises him as a son on his large estate in Cornwall. Philip grows up with no women in the household. When Philip is a young man, Ambrose travels to the sunnier climate of Florence for his health. Ambrose writes Philip that he has married their widowed, distant cousin Rachel in Florence. Later, Ambrose's letters grow increasingly paranoid, indicating he is becoming more ill and distrusts his doctors. Concerned, Philip travels to Italy, only to be informed by Rachel's friend Enrico Rainaldi that Ambrose has died and Rachel has left. Philip is convinced that Rachel caused Ambrose's death and vows revenge.
Under the terms of Ambrose's will, Philip will inherit the estate when he turns 25, and with no provision for Rachel. Philip returns to Cornwall and later learns Rachel has followed. She arrives at the estate and, while he vows to confront her, he becomes infatuated by the older woman's beauty and charm as they share the herbal tea she brews. They accompany each other on riding excursions and, no longer suspecting her of foul play, he throws an accusatory letter on the fire. Philip arranges a generous allowance for Rachel, which she is initially upset about, saying she did not come to Cornwall to beg for money. Rachel also reveals that Ambrose had fallen out of love with her after she had a miscarriage. Philip and Rachel's relationship grows deeper and more affectionate.
Rachel stays for Christmas celebrations and wears the family pearl necklace. Philip's godfather, Nick Kendall, learns Rachel has drastically overdrawn her bank account and warns Philip that Rachel was notorious in Florence for her extravagance and lust. Despite this, Philip gets a document drawn up to turn over the estate to Rachel as soon as he inherits it on his 25th birthday. His birthday arrives and he goes to her room at midnight and gives her the family jewels.
He asks her for what he lacks, and she draws him willingly to bed. The following morning, she reads the document giving her the entire estate and goes to Kendall to confirm its intent. When she returns, Philip takes her to the wood and they have sex again, but this time she does not welcome the intimacy. At dinner with friends, Philip declares that Rachel is to be his wife, which she denies. In private, she tells him she had sex with him merely as a form of thanks. He had viewed it as a confirmation they would marry, as this was what he lacked. They get into a violent argument and he grips her throat, after which Rachel professes fear of him.
Soon after, Philip falls ill and Rachel nurses him back to health. He discovers a letter from Ambrose claiming Rachel was poisoning him. Suspicious, Philip starts refusing her herbal tea, which she also made for Ambrose. He also finds that Rachel was secretly meeting her friend Rainaldi, whom he hates.
One day, Philip suggests Rachel ride along a clifftop path he knows is dangerous.

documents.title: Our House
documents.tagline: The dead are sending you a signal
documents.overview: Ethan is suffering enormous guilt after his parents are killed in a car accident. He quits a promising future at MIT and work on a revolutionary experiment in order to care for his younger siblings.
documents.plot:
Our House is a 2018 supernatural horror film directed by Anthony Scott Burns from a screenplay by Nathan Parker. A remake of Matt Osterman's 2010 film Ghost from the Machine, it stars Thomas Mann as a young inventor, with Nicola Peltz, Kate Moyer and Percy Hynes White. It was released in the United States and Canada on July 27, 2018, by IFC Midnight and Elevation Pictures.

Ethan, a gifted college student, visits his parents and younger siblings, Matt and Becca, but leaves early to work on his invention. His project, a machine designed to transmit electricity wirelessly, lacks university approval, so he sneaks into a campus lab with his girlfriend, Hannah, and a friend to test it. The experiment causes a blackout across the campus. The next morning, Ethan learns that his parents have been killed in a car accident. He returns home to care for his siblings and keeps working on the machine.

When he runs it in the house, strange phenomena begin to occur, and the siblings become convinced that the device is allowing their dead parents to reach out to them. A presence communicates that the machine is drawing on spiritual energy and that more power will let both parents appear. Ethan enlists his neighbor Tom, a grieving widower, to illegally tap into the street's power supply. Becca speaks of a new friend, Alice, who is afraid of a man named Henry, and the activity grows increasingly menacing. An elderly neighbor, Marie, tells Ethan that a girl named Alice vanished from the house years earlier and was believed to have been killed by her foster father, Henry.

Becca is lured into the basement and disappears. Realizing that the spirits are not his parents, Ethan tries to shut the machine off, but discovers that Tom has taken it to contact his late wife, and the two men fight. Meanwhile Matt and Hannah find Becca in a hidden room beneath the house, where they are attacked by hostile ghosts. Ethan persuades Tom that the spirit he hears is not his wife, and the ghost turns on Tom before Ethan smashes the machine, ending the haunting and saving his family. As the siblings move to a new home, Becca returns a doll she had left behind to keep Alice company, but the doll is later seen peering out of a packing box.

Critical reception was mixed. Rotten Tomatoes reported 62% approval, while Metacritic gave it a score of 45.

documents.title: Mudbound
documents.overview: In the post–World War II South, two families are pitted against a barbaric social hierarchy and an unrelenting landscape as they simultaneously fight the battle at home and the battle abroad.
documents.plot:
In the Mississippi Delta, white brothers Henry and Jamie McAllan dig a grave during a rainstorm and struggle to lower their deceased father's coffin into it. When the Jacksons, a black tenant farmer family pass by in a wagon, Henry asks the father, Hap Jackson, for help. Henry seems uncomfortable asking and Hap hesitates to reply.
A few years prior, Henry is conned out of renting a home and is forced to live near sharecroppers on a farm outside the town of Marietta, Mississippi and moves there with his wife Laura, their daughters, and his virulently racist father, Pappy. The Jackson family, led by tenant farmer Hap and his wife Florence, work the farm's cotton field and dream of owning their own land one day. As World War II begins, Jamie and the Jacksons' eldest son, Ronsel, join the United States Army Air Corps and U.S. Army, respectively. Both men experience severe war trauma in the European theater as Jamie flies B-25 bombers and Ronsel commands tanks. Ronsel also falls in love with a white German woman.
Meanwhile, in Mississippi both families continue to live in poverty and support each other out of necessity. Florence also helps the McAllan family when their two young daughters fall ill with whooping cough; and then Laura offers Florence work to help care for her daughters permanently. When the Jacksons' mule has to be euthanized, Henry offers to rent out his mule but exacts half of the Jacksons' crop in payment. Leaving the Jacksons nearly no choice but to accept, the proposed arrangement would diminish them from tenant farmers to the lower economic and social status of sharecroppers. Hap, who serves as the preacher for the local Black community, falls while helping to build a church, breaking his leg and rendering him unable to work his fields. Laura sneaks money from her husband's safe so Hap can be properly treated by a doctor, much to Henry's disapproval and causing their passionless marriage to worsen. Hap recovers and prevents his family from further social decline.
When the war ends, Ronsel and Jamie return home and realize that they have changed but the Mississippi Delta has not. Jamie becomes an alcoholic and has PTSD. Ronsel, accustomed to the relative lack of racism among Europeans, struggles with racism in Mississippi. They become aware of each other's difficulties and bond over their war experiences. Ronsel questions why Jamie treats him with respect, and Jamie recounts that on a bomber mission a Black fighter pilot saved his life. Jamie grows close to Laura but his alcoholism worsens and he drunkenly crashes his truck. Henry leaves on a trip and tells Jamie to depart from the farm before he returns. Ronsel receives a letter and photo from the German woman with whom he had been romantically involved and learns that they had a child together and she wants him to come to Europe. The photo is of her and their biracial child.

documents.title: Columbus
documents.tagline: In the middle of all the mess... there was this.
documents.overview: When a renowned architecture scholar falls suddenly ill during a speaking tour, his son Jin finds himself stranded in Columbus, Indiana - a small Midwestern city celebrated for its many significant modernist buildings. Jin strikes up a friendship with Casey, a young architecture enthusiast who works at the local library.
documents.plot:
In Columbus, Indiana, Jin Lee arrives from South Korea to watch over his estranged father who, while visiting the town to give a lecture about architecture, has fallen into a coma and is now in a local hospital. One day, Jin meets Casey, a young woman who works in a library near the hospital. Casey lives with and takes care of her mother, a recovering drug addict.
Casey and Jin quickly build a rapport as she guides him around Columbus for several days. The two discuss the local architecture while simultaneously opening up about themselves to each other. Jin reveals his feelings of resentment toward his father, whom Jin believes to have cared more about work than for him. Casey also opens up about her dream of getting a job in architecture. However, she confesses that she cannot leave her mother in order to pursue it. Jin advises that it is her life and that Casey is holding herself back.
One night, Casey and Jin are wandering around Columbus when Casey discovers that her mother had been lying to her and has possibly relapsed, though later learns she has just been seeing a new partner. Following this incident, Casey comes to the conclusion that it is in her best interest to move on and decides to leave Columbus in order to pursue her dream. Jin and Casey share a tender hug goodbye and Casey leaves, while Jin stays behind to watch over his ailing father.

documents.title: The Batman
documents.tagline: Unmask the truth.
documents.overview: In his second year of fighting crime, Batman uncovers corruption in Gotham City that connects to his own family while facing a serial killer known as the Riddler.
documents.plot:
On Halloween, Gotham City mayor Don Mitchell Jr. is murdered by a masked serial killer, the Riddler. Reclusive billionaire Bruce Wayne, who has operated for two years as the vigilante Batman, investigates the murder alongside Lieutenant Jim Gordon, much to the disdain of the Gotham City Police Department (GCPD); the Riddler leaves a message for Batman at the crime scene. The following night, the Riddler kills the police commissioner, Pete Savage, and leaves another message for Batman. Batman and Gordon discover that the Riddler left a thumb drive in Mitchell's car; it contains images of Mitchell's affair with a woman, Annika Kosolov, at the Iceberg Lounge—a nightclub operated by the Penguin, crime boss Carmine Falcone's lieutenant. While questioning the Penguin, who pleads ignorance, Batman notices that Annika's roommate, Selina Kyle, works at the club as a waitress. Annika disappears; while searching for answers, Batman and Selina discover that Savage and Mitchell were on Falcone's payroll, as is district attorney Gil Colson.
The Riddler abducts Colson, straps a timed collar bomb to his neck, and sends him to interrupt Mitchell's funeral. When Batman arrives, the Riddler calls him via a phone duct-taped to Colson and threatens to detonate the bomb if Colson cannot answer three riddles. Colson refuses to answer the third—the name of the informant who gave the GCPD information that led to a historic drug bust ending mob boss Salvatore Maroni's operation—and is killed. Batman and Gordon deduce that the informant may be the Penguin and track him to a drug deal. They discover that Maroni's operation was transferred to Falcone, with many corrupt officers involved. Selina inadvertently exposes them when she arrives to steal money and discovers Annika's corpse in the trunk of a car. Batman captures the Penguin after a car chase, but he and Gordon learn that the Penguin is not the informant.
Batman and Gordon follow the Riddler's trail to the ruins of an orphanage initially funded by Bruce's deceased parents, Thomas and Martha Wayne, where they learn that the Riddler holds a grudge against the Wayne family for failing the orphanage. Bruce's butler and caretaker, Alfred Pennyworth, is hospitalized after opening a letter bomb addressed to Bruce. The Riddler leaks evidence that Thomas, who was running for mayor before he was murdered, hired Falcone to kill a journalist whom Maroni controlled and who was writing a story about Martha's family history of mental illness. Bruce confronts Alfred, who maintains that Thomas only asked Falcone to threaten the journalist into silence; upon learning that Falcone had murdered the journalist, Thomas planned to turn both himself and Falcone over to the police. Alfred suspects that Falcone had Thomas and Martha killed to silence them.
Selina reveals to Batman that Falcone is her father.

documents.title: Ravenous
documents.overview: In an isolated rural community of Quebec, Canada, some inhabitants attack other people, hungry for human flesh. A few survivors gather and go deep into the forest to escape them.
documents.plot:
Ravenous (French: Les Affamés) is a 2017 French-language Canadian horror film written and directed by Robin Aubert. The cast includes Marc-André Grondin, Monia Chokri, Brigitte Poupart, Luc Proulx, Charlotte St-Martin, Micheline Lanctôt and Marie-Ginette Guay. Set in rural Quebec, the film follows a handful of ordinary people struggling to survive after an outbreak turns most of the population into ravenous, zombie-like creatures, and it uses the genre to explore loneliness, grief and community.

Following the outbreak, the countryside has been emptied of most of its inhabitants. Bonin and his friend Vézina patrol the area with shotguns, killing infected and passing the time telling each other jokes, until Vézina is drawn into the forest and attacked. Elsewhere, Céline, a wife and mother who has lost her family, roams alone, fighting off the infected with a machete. She arrives at the farm of Thérèse and Pauline, two armed elderly women who check her for bites before taking her in.

Bonin meets Tania, a young woman bitten on the arm who insists the wound came from a dog, and he frees her and flees with her when the infected attack. Along the way they take in Zoé, a silent little girl. Bonin notices that the infected behave strangely: rather than simply hunting, they gather in fields around towers of household objects they have piled up, standing motionless as if taking part in a ritual. The survivors join up with the women at the farm, but the house lies in the path of the advancing horde, and they are forced to flee. They are joined by Réal, a retired insurance agent, and Ti-Cul, a boy armed with a rifle. As the group moves through forests and abandoned farms, they must decide whom they can trust, and the losses they suffer reveal how fragile their makeshift community is.

Ravenous received positive reviews, holding an 89 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. T'cha Dunlevy of the Montreal Gazette praised it as a successful reinvention of the zombie genre that was funny, philosophical, frightening and boldly cinematic, and Robert Everett-Green of The Globe and Mail read it as an allegory. It won the Toronto International Film Festival award for Best Canadian Film and was nominated for five Canadian Screen Awards, including Best Motion Picture, winning for Best Make-Up.

documents.title: Operation Mekong
documents.overview: Chinese narco-cops take their mission to the Golden Triangle following the Mekong River massacre of innocent fishermen by the region's drug lord.
documents.plot: The Chinese government launches a daring operation to arrest a violent drug cartel following the discovery of thirteen Chinese crew members' bodies on two ships sailing through the Mekong River.

documents.title: Barbie: Star Light Adventure
documents.tagline: A new kind of princess!
documents.overview: Barbie is a cosmic princess who flies high on her hoverboard through a far-off universe with her adorable and devoted pet sidekick, Pupcorn. One day, everything changes when the twinkling stars start to dim and slow their dance in the sky. Barbie travels to a beautiful new planet to join a special rescue team on a mission to save the stars. Once there, she teams up with a group of talented new friends who work together to save the galaxy through exciting hoverboarding adventures. Barbie soon discovers that if she listens to her heart, and with the help of her friends, she might be the leader the whole universe has been waiting for!
documents.plot:
Barbie: Star Light Adventure is a 2016 computer-animated children's adventure film directed by Andrew Tan and written by Kacey Arnold, with Kate Boutilier assisting on the script. The 33rd entry in the Barbie film series, it was the first produced under Mattel's new Mattel Creations banner and the first to open with the doll brand's message sequence. After a one-day Fathom Events screening, it was released on home video by Universal and later aired on Nickelodeon. Its voice cast includes Erica Lindbeck, Dwight Schultz and Robbie Daymond.

A prophecy foretells that one day the stars will stop their cosmic dance and go dark unless "the One" can make them shine again, and the sky is indeed growing darker. The rigid, orderly King Constantine, convinced despite repeated failures that he is the One, recruits a team of gifted young people for his latest plan. On the wildlife preserve planet of Para-Den, Barbie is an enthusiastic but impulsive hoverboarder who can communicate with animals and objects through telekinesis. Encouraged by her widowed father, she accepts the king's invitation and travels to the Capital Planet.

There she meets her teammates: Sal-Lee, a sarcastic, competitive hoverboarder with super speed; Prince Leo, a shy and awkward but brilliant pilot; and the kindly alien twins Kareena and Sheena, who share a psychic link and can make things lighter or heavier. Barbie's free-spirited ways repeatedly clash with Constantine's insistence on order, and when she persuades the team to release a Starlian creature they were meant to capture, believing he wants it for a zoo, he fires her, explaining that the creature was needed to guide them to the centre of the galaxy. Barbie apologises for misjudging him but not for following her conscience, and uses her powers to ask the Starlian for help. Under pressure from her teammates, Constantine reinstates her as leader.

Guided by the Starlian, the team reaches the galaxy's central planet, where Barbie and her friends clear a path to the core for Constantine and his machine. Ignoring Barbie's advice, he uses the device to force the stars into order, and they go out at once. Sensing that the stars have stopped dancing out of sadness and loneliness, Barbie begins a new dance with them, restoring their light and proving herself the One. Humbled, Constantine takes Barbie and her father in as his wards, and the film ends with Princess Starlight and her friends teaching the king to dance.

documents.title: Hotel Mumbai
documents.tagline: November 26, 2008… Terror struck the heart of India.
documents.overview: Mumbai, India, November 26, 2008. While several terrorists spread hatred and death through the city, others attack the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel. Both hotel staff and guests risk their lives, making unthinkable sacrifices to protect themselves and keep everyone safe while help arrives.
documents.plot: Mumbai, India, November 26, 2008. While several terrorists spread hatred and death through the city, others attack the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel. Both hotel staff and guests risk their lives, making unthinkable sacrifices to protect themselves and keep everyone safe while help arrives.

documents.title: Arctic Dogs
documents.tagline: Time to run with the big dogs!
documents.overview: Animals band together to save the day when the evil Otto Von Walrus hatches a sinister scheme to accelerate global warming and melt the Arctic Circle.
documents.plot:
Swifty is an Arctic fox who works in the mailroom of Taigasville's Arctic Blast Delivery Service, who dreams of become the top dog of the company, but is unfit of doing so due to his breed. One day, while on his first time delivering packages, he ends up at a hidden fortress overseen by Otto Von Walrus, along with his puffin henchmen. Visiting his red fox friend, Jade, he shares his discoveries to her and about his first job. That night, the delivery service's top dogs, Siberian Huskies Duke, Dakota, and Dusty, are abducted by some of Walrus' henchmen. The following day, the delivery service mourns over their disappearance.
That day, Swifty is visited by two otters named Bertha and Leopold, who warn him about Walrus' henchmen. Magda, the service's head caribou, allows Swifty to take the top dogs place for delivering packages. During his job, he visits Walrus again. Sneaking into the fortress, he discovers Walrus' plan to drill into the surface at Taigasville's surface to unleash masses of ancient gas to melt the Arctic. Returning to the delivery service, he tries to warn their crew members about Walrus' plan, but to no avail. Meanwhile, Jade is abducted by Walrus' henchmen, and taken to his fortress. Walrus then forces her to complete his drill. The following day, Swifty learns about Jade's kidnapping, and tells P.B., his best friend, about the fortress and the kidnapping of the top dogs and Jade.
He is again visited by Bertha and Leopold, who explain to him about the Walrus' plan. That night, they capture photos of their plans, and warn the citizens of Taigasville about their plan. Magda explains that Walrus once worked at the delivery service after being kicked out from his original work place at the ocean. However, Walrus was fired from the service after trying to invent a pneumatic tube system powered by the gas, deeming it to be dangerous. Determined to stop him, Swifty rallies his friends to storm Walrus' fortress. However, during their plan, they end up imprisoned by Walrus. There, they reconcile with the top dogs and Jade. Swifty tearfully admits to her about her being an engineer, but she does admit for being back with him. Walrus descends their cage into an vat of boiling water to try to execute the group, before setting out to Taigasville. Upon arrival, he activates his drill to try to unleash the gas, terrorizing the city in the process.
The group manages to escape, and return to Taigasville. While his friends take out most of Walrus' henchmen, Swifty is able to reach the control panel and stop the drill, causing it to explode. Walrus is then sent to prison by the citizens of Taigasville. His friends hail him for being a hero and a top dog. The next day, the delivery service has been changed by Swifty, while he and Jade become a couple.

documents.title: Godard Mon Amour
documents.tagline: This movie is a “stupid, stupid idea.”
documents.overview: In 1967, during the making of “La Chinoise,” film director Jean-Luc Godard falls in love with 19-year-old actress Anne Wiazemsky and marries her.
documents.plot:
Godard Mon Amour, released in France as Le Redoutable (Redoubtable), is a 2017 French biographical comedy-drama written and directed by Michel Hazanavicius, adapted from Un an après, Anne Wiazemsky's 2015 memoir. Louis Garrel plays the filmmaker Jean-Luc Godard and Stacy Martin plays Wiazemsky, while the supporting cast includes Bérénice Bejo (Michèle Rosier), Micha Lescot (Jean-Pierre Bamberger), Grégory Gadebois (Michel Cournot) and Guido Caprino (Bernardo Bertolucci). Structured in nine chapters with an epilogue, the film playfully imitates Godard's own techniques, including black-and-white passages, voice-over, characters addressing the camera, title cards and ironic subtitles.

In Paris in 1967, Godard, the celebrated 37-year-old figurehead of the French New Wave, falls in love with the 20-year-old Anne while directing her in La Chinoise, and asks her to marry him on the day the radio reports news of the submarine Le Redoutable. His growing commitment to Maoism shapes his work, but the film is rejected by the Chinese embassy and poorly received by critics and audiences. A year later the events of May 1968 erupt. Godard joins the often violent street protests, is pestered by fans who want him to return to lighter films such as Breathless and Pierrot le Fou, is shouted down at the occupied Sorbonne and mocked in graffiti, and meets the same scorn at a conference in Rome hosted by Bertolucci. He and friends travel to the Cannes Film Festival, which they help shut down in solidarity with the strikes, and then find themselves stranded without fuel during the general strike.

Back in Paris, Godard founds the Dziga Vertov Group with Jean-Pierre Gorin to make radical political cinema, but he becomes increasingly isolated, accused by others of being incomprehensible. As Anne pursues her own acting career, their marriage deteriorates and Godard attempts suicide with an overdose. Anne falls out of love, and they separate during the collective shoot of Wind from the East, where Godard is confronted with his own contradictions.

Produced by Les Compagnons du Cinéma with Wild Bunch and France 3 Cinéma and photographed by Guillaume Schiffman, the film premiered in competition for the Palme d'Or at the 2017 Cannes Film Festival. Reviews were mixed, with a Rotten Tomatoes approval rating of 54% and a Metacritic score of 55.

documents.title: The Quake
documents.tagline: The Wave Was Only The Beginning
documents.overview: A geologist races against time to save his estranged wife and two children when a devastating earthquake strikes Oslo, Norway.
documents.plot:
The Quake (Norwegian: Skjelvet) is a 2018 Norwegian disaster film directed by John Andreas Andersen and the sequel to the 2015 film The Wave. Kristoffer Joner returns as geologist Kristian Eikjord, with Ane Dahl Torp, Jonas Hoff Oftebro, Edith Haagenrud-Sande and Kathrine Thorborg Johansen in the main cast. It was released in Norwegian cinemas on 31 August 2018.

Three years after he was hailed as a hero for his actions during the Geiranger tsunami, Kristian is a broken man. He blames himself for the 250 people who died, keeps a hidden room devoted to the disaster, and has become estranged from his wife Idun, who is divorcing him, and their children Sondre and Julia, who have moved to Oslo, where Idun works at the Radisson Blu Plaza Hotel. When a fellow geologist, Konrad Lindblom, is killed in a collapse in the Oslofjord Tunnel, Kristian travels to the capital to find out why. Konrad's supervisor, Johannes Løberg, assures him that the tremors Konrad had been monitoring were nothing more than construction blasting, but Kristian, working with Konrad's daughter Marit, finds core samples, maps of alarming seismic activity and video of laboratory rats killed by gas escaping from the ground. Kristian concludes that a massive earthquake, as strong as 8.5 on the Richter scale, is about to strike Oslo. A smaller rift that damages the Oslo Opera House during Julia's ballet recital proves he is right, but no one in authority will listen. As the city goes about its business, Kristian races to warn his family, calling in a fake bomb threat to clear Sondre's university and hurrying to Idun's office high in the hotel tower. The earthquake hits while they are still inside, devastating the city and leaving Kristian, Idun, Julia and Marit fighting to survive in the collapsing skyscraper.

The Quake was well received by critics. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds an 85% approval rating based on 40 reviews, with a consensus describing it as a satisfyingly smart action thriller that delivers nail-biting tension without sacrificing character development or common sense, and on Metacritic it has a score of 70 out of 100, indicating "generally favorable reviews".

documents.title: Winchester
documents.tagline: Terror is building.
documents.overview: San Jose, California, 1906. Isolated in her labyrinthine mansion, eccentric firearm heiress Sarah Winchester believes that she is being haunted by the souls of those killed by the guns manufactured by her company.
documents.plot:
Sarah Winchester is the widow of famed gun manufacturer William Wirt Winchester. Her husband's sudden death and the previous death of their child Annie have left her in grief and convinced she is cursed by the ghosts of those who died at the hands of Winchester firearms.
After seeking advice from a medium, she spent her twenty million dollars inheritance to build an enormous, seemingly never-ending mansion in San Jose, California that would eventually be named the Winchester Mystery House. The house is under constant construction and Sarah's niece Marion Marriott lives in the house with her son Henry. At night, Henry is possessed by a mysterious entity.
In 1906, the Winchester company hires Doctor Eric Price to stay at the house and assess Sarah, believing she is mentally unfit to remain in charge of the company. Still grieving the death of his wife Ruby, Eric is reliant on drugs. He arrives at the house and has a ghostly vision that he believes is the drugs' side-effect. Later, he spots a ghost in the basement. Witnessing a possessed Henry jump off the roof, Eric saves him.
The next day, Eric begins to conduct his assessment of Sarah's mental well-being. Sarah admits her fear of ghosts and believes she can help them move on. She reveals that she knows about Eric's drug problem and confiscates his supply of laudanum. That night, Eric witnesses a seemingly possessed Sarah draw a plan for a new room. He is startled by an entity and flees back to his room. The next day, Sarah shows Eric that she keeps records of people killed by Winchester rifles. It is revealed that Eric had actually been shot and killed by a Winchester rifle before being revived, and he keeps the refurbished bullet with him. Sarah explains how thirteen nails keep spirits sealed in rooms.
A possessed Henry attempts to kill Sarah with a rifle, but is stopped by Eric and Marion. Realizing how violent this spirit is, Sarah sends her staff away and decides to personally remove the ghost from her home. Eric encounters a butler who reveals himself to be a ghost. He and Sarah identify the ghost as Benjamin Block, a Confederate States Army soldier who lost his two brothers in the American Civil War to Winchester rifles. A devastated Ben proceeded to shoot up a Winchester office, massacring the workers before being shot dead by police. Ben has been the one possessing Henry; the constructed room with the Winchester guns is the room where he was shot dead.
A violent earthquake takes place, devastating the house and separating Eric and Sarah. In the chaos, a possessed Henry escapes, pursued by Marion. Eric encounters several ghosts before seeing the ghost of Ruby. It is revealed that Ruby could see and hear ghosts but was misdiagnosed as "delusional" by Eric. Eventually, the unstable Ruby shot Eric before killing herself with a Winchester rifle. Ruby's ghost comforts Eric, inspiring him to help Sarah.
Eric reunites with Sarah and they manage to trap Ben in the room.

documents.title: The Big Sick
documents.tagline: An awkward true story.
documents.overview: Pakistan-born comedian Kumail Nanjiani and grad student Emily Gardner fall in love but struggle as their cultures clash. When Emily contracts a mysterious illness, Kumail finds himself forced to face her feisty parents, his family's expectations, and his true feelings.
documents.plot:
Kumail is a struggling standup comedian, who hooks up with a UChicago grad student, Emily, after a performance at the local comedy club. Despite being from different races (Kumail is ethnically Pakistani while Emily is Caucasian), they start dating. After a few months, Emily confronts Kumail about photographs of other women she found in his apartment. Kumail says it's 'just a cultural thing' (these are women he has met for an arranged marriage), but Emily rejects the idea and breaks up with him.
Deciding to focus on his career, Kumail targets a spot at the Montreal Comedy Festival. He is offered to audition, and hooks up with an audience member that same night. Lying in bed, Kumail receives a distress call, informing him that Emily needs help after being admitted to the hospital.
Kumail goes to check on her, where doctors use his signature to place Emily in a medical coma, then asking him to inform her family. The next day, Terry and Beth arrive from North Carolina. They are cold towards Kumail, but he continues checking in on Emily. Eventually, the three bond when doctors prepare Emily for surgery. Terry and Beth defend Kumail from racial hecklers at the comedy club, and spend the night with him at Emily's apartment, playing drinking games.
Kumail ignores his family's calls, as they attempt to set him up with other women for an arranged marriage. His parents show up at his apartment, leading to an argument in which they threaten to disown him. That evening, Emily's condition worsens, and Kumail bombs his Montreal audition as a result.
Miraculously, Emily responds to anti-inflammatory treatment the next morning, and awakens from coma. She is diagnosed with a rare adult-onset Still's disease, but will fully recover. Unaware that Kumail was by her side throughout, she refuses to meet him and rejects his idea to get back together.
Dejected, Kumail decides to leave for New York with his comedian friends, and start over in pursuit of a career in standup. Emily hears the news and is disappointed. Kumail's parents are shocked by his decision, but bid him farewell nonetheless, showing that they mean to patch things up with him.
In New York, Kumail performs a new set at a local club. He is heckled/cheered by an audience member, who turns out to be Emily. She announces she is there to see 'someone'. During the credits, photographs of the wedding between Kumail and Emily are shown, showing that Kumail's parents and family attended.

documents.title: Barbie & Her Sisters in a Puppy Chase
documents.original_title: Barbie & Her Sisters in a Puppy Chase
documents.tagline: A fun-filled tropical adventure!
documents.overview: Barbie and her sisters go to an island paradise for a dance competition, but they must work together as a team to find their pets after their furry friends go missing at a horse festival.
documents.plot:
Barbie & Her Sisters in a Puppy Chase is a 2016 American computer-animated adventure film and the 34th entry in the Barbie film series. Directed by Conrad Helten with Michael Goguen from a screenplay by Amy Wolfram and Kacey Arnold, it was produced by Mattel Playground Productions with animation by Rainmaker Entertainment, with music by Steven Argila and The Math Club. It was released direct to video in the United States in October 2016 and made its television debut on Nickelodeon that November. Its theme song is "Live in the Moment".

Barbie (Erica Lindbeck) and her sisters Skipper, Stacie and Chelsea fly with their puppies Taffy, DJ, Rookie and Honey to a tropical island, where Chelsea is to compete in a dance competition against her rival, Lindsay. Chelsea wants to go straight to the hotel to rehearse, but Barbie has planned a surprise. With most rental cars taken, the sisters set off in a golf cart, send their luggage ahead and head to Banyan Tree Park for the Dancing Horse Festival, where the trainers Vivian and Marco present the nervous young horse Beauty in her debut. While the girls watch, the puppies explore a horse trailer belonging to a show dog, Archibald, and are unwittingly driven away when the trainers leave.

Trying to follow, Barbie gets the cart stuck in the arch of the great banyan tree, and with no internet signal the sisters must spend the night in the park, passing the time with imagination games and learning of a macaw constellation once used by local fishermen for navigation. The next day, finding the road washed out, they climb a mountain, take a zip-line to a village and rent a camper, only to run out of fuel near the beach campground where the trainers have stopped. Meanwhile the puppies, cared for by Vivian and Marco, enjoy their own adventure, running with the horses and learning to surf.

As her worries mount, Chelsea snaps at Barbie for being relentlessly positive, and Barbie reassures her that doing her best matters more than winning. The sisters are reunited with their pets, and when another washed-out road blocks the way, the horses carry the girls across. Barbie admits that she hid her own worries to seem dependable, and her sisters tell her she can share them. Guided north by the macaw constellation, they reach the competition. The voice cast also includes Kazumi Evans as Skipper, Claire Margaret Corlett as Stacie, Alyssya Swales as Chelsea and Mark Oliver as Archibald.

documents.title: Forever My Girl
documents.tagline: Find your way back home
documents.overview: After being gone for a decade, a country star returns home to the love he left behind.
documents.plot:
In St. Augustine, Louisiana, Josie is left at the altar by her fiancé Liam to pursue fame and fortune. Eight years later, he is a successful country singer.
The morning after a concert in New Orleans, Liam wakes up to discover the girl he brought home jumping excitedly on and breaking his cell phone. Panicked after realizing, he takes the phone to an electronics store where the manager fixes it for him. Asked why he still has the damaged phone, Liam tells him it has an important message on it.
While watching TV, Liam learns that Mason, his childhood best friend, has been killed in a car accident. He returns to St. Augustine to attend the funeral. Although Liam attempts to be discreet, Josie bumps into him. After the burial, she punches him in the gut.
Liam stays with his father, Pastor Brian, although he's bitter that Liam also cut off contact with him. While reacquainting himself with the town, he encounters Josie at her flower shop. Liam learns that she has a seven-year-old daughter, Billy, and that he is the father. Josie confesses that she found out she was pregnant two weeks after he left her at the altar. Although she tried to contact him, Liam never returned her call, so she decided to raise Billy alone.
Liam is surprised to learn that his father also tried to tell him that Josie was pregnant at one of his concerts seven years ago. However, he was too absorbed in his fame and didn't listen to him. Liam eventually persuades Josie to let him spend time with Billy, albeit on her terms. Billy quickly realizes Liam is her father, much to Josie's surprise, and agrees to get to know each other.
Liam and Billy bond as she displays musical ability. Josie agrees to let her stay the night with him. As Liam tucks her in, Billy asks him why he left her mom. He admits he was young and confused, and regrets it, which both Josie and Brian overhear.
After Billy falls asleep, Josie asks Liam out saying she wants to have a date with "the Liam Page" as she'd never experienced his fame with him. He flies her to New Orleans for their date, and when they are briefly questioned by the press as to who Josie is, he answers "She's the one".
After returning to St. Augustine, Liam and Billy continue to bond. She chokes on her lunch but Liam freezes after having a flashback to his mother's death. Jake, Josie's brother, saves Billy. Guilt-ridden, Liam gets drunk at a bar. Jake finds him to say Josie and Billy would be better off without him.
While bandaging a wound Liam sustained that evening, Brian reveals that when Liam's mother died, he was so absorbed in his own grief that he overlooked his son's, so apologizes to him for it. Brian theorizes that he became famous and cut contact with him as his way of dealing with the grief over his mother's death, to which Liam agrees.
Liam goes the next morning without saying goodbye to Josie and Billy, leaving a note telling Brian that they are better off without him. Returning to his tour, he performs in London.

documents.title: Scary Stories to Tell in the Dark
documents.original_title: Scary Stories to Tell in the Dark
documents.tagline: Stories taken from true urban legends
documents.overview: Mill Valley, Pennsylvania, Halloween night, 1968. After playing a joke on a school bully, Stella and her friends decide to sneak into a supposedly haunted house that once belonged to the powerful Bellows family, unleashing dark forces that they will be unable to control.
documents.plot:
Scary Stories to Tell in the Dark is a 2019 supernatural horror film directed by André Øvredal and based on Alvin Schwartz's children's book series. Dan and Kevin Hageman wrote the screenplay from a story by Guillermo del Toro, Patrick Melton and Marcus Dunstan, and del Toro also produced. CBS Films acquired the rights in 2013, del Toro came aboard in 2016 and Øvredal was hired in late 2017. A co-production of the United States, Canada and Mexico, it was shot in Ontario between August and November 2018 and released by Lionsgate on August 9, 2019. Del Toro explained that he avoided an anthology format because such films are only as good as their weakest segment.

On Halloween night in 1968, in the fictional town of Mill Valley, Pennsylvania, teenagers Stella, Auggie and Chuck and the newcomer Ramón explore the supposedly haunted Bellows house. They find a book of horror stories by Sarah Bellows, an outcast girl blamed for the deaths of local children who reportedly killed herself in 1898, and Stella takes it home. New stories begin writing themselves in blood, and each comes true. The bully Tommy is turned into the scarecrow Harold, and Auggie is dragged away by a corpse searching for its missing toe. Chuck's sister Ruth survives a swelling that bursts with spiders but is left traumatized.

Investigating, the friends learn that Sarah actually hanged herself in a hospital where her brother, a doctor, had subjected her to electroshock to make her confess, and that the children had really died because the family's paper mill poisoned the water with mercury. Chuck is absorbed by the Pale Lady, and after Police Chief Turner arrests Stella and Ramón, exposing Ramón as a draft dodger, the Jangly Man kills Turner. Back at the Bellows house, Stella relives Sarah's abuse and promises to tell the truth if she stops the killings, then writes the true story in her own blood, and the monsters vanish. Ramón leaves for Vietnam, while Stella searches for a way to bring Chuck and Auggie back.

The cast includes Zoe Colletti, Michael Garza, Gabriel Rush, Austin Zajur, Natalie Ganzhorn, Austin Abrams, Dean Norris, Gil Bellows and Lorraine Toussaint, with Javier Botet also joining the cast. Reviews were generally positive, with 78% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, praise for its faithful re-creations of the books' scares and some complaints about filler. It grossed $104.5 million worldwide, and a sequel is in development.

documents.title: Wildlife
documents.overview: 14-year-old Joe is the only child of Jeanette and Jerry — a housewife and a golf pro — in a small town in 1960s Montana. Nearby, an uncontrolled forest fire rages close to the Canadian border, and when Jerry loses his job (and his sense of purpose) he decides to join the cause of fighting the fire, leaving his wife and son to fend for themselves.
documents.plot:
In 1960, Jeannette and Jerry Brinson have recently moved to Great Falls, Montana, with their teenage son Joe. Tensions build after Jerry is fired from a job as a golf pro at a country club. He is offered his old job back but refuses out of pride, and instead of looking for work, he sleeps in his car and watches the local firefighting efforts against a forest fire raging in nearby mountains. To support the family as Jerry looks for a job, Jeannette takes a job as a swimming instructor (although she tries first to get a job teaching at school). Joe gives up football after school to work part-time at a local photography studio. One day, Jerry decides to take a low-paying job fighting the forest fire, which upsets Jeannette and worries Joe. Jeannette speaks openly about her strained marriage with Jerry to Joe, and the stress of the situation takes a minor toll on Joe's school life.
While Jerry is away, Jeannette tells her son they may have to move to a smaller place as they cannot afford their small rented house. She introduces Joe to Warren Miller, a prosperous older man who owns an automobile dealership. She says she taught him to swim and he has offered her a job.
Joe is repeatedly left alone as Jeannette spends time with Miller and Jeannette opens up about her dissatisfaction with her husband's restlessness. Joe wakes one morning and his mother is absent. He goes to Miller's car dealership, but the receptionist does not know who his mother is.
One night, after a dinner hosted by Miller, Miller dances with a drunken Jeannette and kisses her; he spends the night at Joe's house, which a shocked Joe discovers later that night. After Miller leaves, Joe confronts Jeannette about the affair. Jeannette does not admit to caring about Miller or no longer loving Jerry, but concedes that the affair will make their life financially better, and she implores Joe to think of a better plan for her. He tells her that he cannot. The next morning, Joe packs up some of his belongings and heads to a bus stop. As the bus arrives it begins to snow, signaling the end of the wildfires, and Joe returns home.
Jerry returns and is met with a lukewarm reception by Jeannette, who reveals that she has begun renting an apartment in town, and Joe is free to stay with her. Devastated and suspecting an affair, Jerry asks Jeannette to admit to her relationship. Furious upon hearing that Miller slept with Jeannette in the family house, Jerry drunkenly goes to Miller's house and tries to set it ablaze. Miller catches him in the act and confronts him, admonishing him about his behavior with Joe present. When an injured Jerry pleads with Joe to help him escape before the police arrive, Joe flees on foot to the police station, where he discovers his father has not been arrested. Returning to the house, he learns from Jerry that Miller will not press charges, but his parents' marriage is over.

documents.title: Diary of a Wimpy Kid: The Long Haul
documents.original_title: Diary of a Wimpy Kid: The Long Haul
documents.tagline: Hitting the road in a whole new direction.
documents.overview: A Heffley family road trip to attend Meemaw's 90th birthday party goes hilariously off course thanks to Greg's newest scheme to get to a video gaming convention.
documents.plot:
Diary of a Wimpy Kid: The Long Haul is a 2017 American road comedy film directed by David Bowers, who co-wrote it with the series' author Jeff Kinney. It is the fourth installment in the Diary of a Wimpy Kid film series and is based on the ninth book of the same name, with elements of the seventh, eighth and tenth books. The film recast the Heffley family, with Jason Ian Drucker as Greg, Alicia Silverstone as his mother Susan, Tom Everett Scott as his father Frank, Charlie Wright as his older brother Rodrick and Owen Asztalos as his best friend Rowley.

At a family restaurant, Susan announces that the Heffleys will take a road trip to attend Meemaw's 90th birthday party, to the dismay of Greg and Rodrick. Before they leave, Greg suffers a public humiliation when he gets stuck in the restaurant's ball pit with a dirty diaper stuck to his hand. Someone films his panic, and the clip goes viral online as the "Diaper Hands" meme, making him infamous. When Greg discovers that a video game convention, the Player Expo, is taking place near Meemaw's home in Indianapolis, and that his favorite online gamer, Mac Digby, will appear there, he decides to secretly sneak off during the trip, hoping that a video with Digby will make people forget about Diaper Hands.

Susan has declared the trip "technology-free" and confiscates everyone's phones, but Greg retrieves his and enlists Rodrick's help with his plan. Along the way the family endures a long series of disasters. At a county fair, Greg wins a piglet that the family is forced to take along, and they repeatedly cross paths with a menacing family who become convinced the Heffleys have wronged them. Their trip includes a seedy motel, a flock of seagulls, car trouble and other mishaps, as Greg's schemes to reach the Expo keep backfiring and threaten to ruin the family vacation entirely.

Released by 20th Century Fox in May 2017, the film was a critical and commercial failure, grossing about $40 million worldwide. Fans objected strongly to the recasting of the familiar characters, and critics found the humor crude and the story thin. It was the last live-action film in the franchise, which later continued with animated adaptations on Disney+.
