documents.title: It Comes at Night
documents.tagline: Fear turns men into monsters.
documents.overview: Secure within a desolate home as an unnatural threat terrorizes the world, a man has established a tenuous domestic order with his wife and son, but this will soon be put to test when a desperate young family arrives seeking refuge.
documents.plot:
A contagious disease ravages the planet. Paul, Sarah and their teenage son Travis live a secluded lifestyle in their home, deep in the woods in an undisclosed location. After Sarah's father Bud contracts the disease, they euthanise him and burn his body.
That night, they capture an intruder breaking in. Paul ties him to a tree and places a bag over his head, leaving him there overnight to confirm he is not suffering from the disease. The stranger, Will, explains he was searching for fresh water for his wife and young son. Will offers to trade some food for water. Sarah suggests taking the strangers in, on the reasoning that with more people it would be easier to defend themselves. Paul reluctantly agrees and drives Will to collect his family. Along the way, they are ambushed by two men. Paul kills them, while accusing Will of setting him up. Will assuages Paul's mistrust.
Paul returns with Will, his wife Kim, and son Andrew. After establishing their rules, which include keeping the only entrance locked with a key Paul or Sarah wear around their neck, the two families establish a sense of normality and grow closer.
One day, Travis's dog Stanley begins barking aggressively at an unseen presence and chases it into the woods. Travis, who had followed Stanley, insists he heard something in the woods. That night, Will seemingly contradicts a story he told Paul earlier, resulting in Paul's increasing distrust of Will.
That evening, Travis discovers Andrew sleeping on the floor of Bud's old room, suffering from a nightmare. He also finds the front door of the house open. The families investigate, finding a bleeding and gravely sick Stanley on the floor. They euthanise and burn the dog. After Travis reveals the door was open, Sarah suggests that a sleepwalking Andrew opened the door, causing more distrust. Paul suspects Andrew is infected, and decides they should quarantine in their separate rooms to ensure no one is sick. That evening, Travis is awakened by a nightmare about his grandfather.
The next morning, Travis overhears Andrew crying constantly and Kim telling Will they need to leave. Travis informs his parents that he too may be infected. Paul and Sarah don protective masks and gloves, and take weapons to confront Kim and Will. Will draws a gun and takes Paul captive. He insists his family is healthy, repeatedly tells Andrew to keep his eyes shut and orders Paul to remove the mask. Will demands Paul give him a "fair share" of food and water so they can leave. Sarah and Paul overwhelm Will, and force him and his family outside. Will tries to beat Paul to death until Sarah shoots Will, killing him. Kim flees into the woods with Andrew. Paul fires at them, killing Andrew, then Kim.
Later, Travis awakens in bed, visibly sick. His mother comforts him as he dies. Paul and Sarah, now visibly infected, sit at the dinner table in silence. They share a shattered, devastated look.

documents.title: Unforgettable
documents.tagline: When love ends, madness begins.
documents.overview: Julia moves in with her fiancé, David, but his ex-wife and her own haunting past join forces to rock her quiet suburban existence.
documents.plot:
Julia Banks is questioned by police after the body of her abusive ex-boyfriend Michael Vargas is found in her home. Despite Julia's restraining order against him, Detective Pope reveals intimate messages and photos from her on Michael's phone, along with her underwear found in his car.
Six months earlier, Julia moves in with her fiancé David Connover and his daughter Lily, and struggles with the constant presence of Tessa, David's ex-wife and Lily's mother. Controlling and obsessive, Tessa is not coping with the end of her marriage, exacerbated by her equally cold and demanding mother, Helen (nicknamed "Lovey"). Stealing Julia's phone, Tessa accesses her private photos and information, including her recently expired restraining order. She sets up a Facebook account posing as Julia, using it to reach out to Michael. She also steals David's watch, Julia's engagement ring, and a pair of her panties, sending the watch and panties to Michael.
Determined to remove Julia from her life, Tessa anonymously sends her flowers, making David suspect Julia is having an affair. Lily wanders away from Julia at a farmer's market into the arms of Tessa, who lies to make Julia seem unfit to watch her daughter. At riding practice, Tessa tries to force a frightened Lily to ride a new, larger horse, but Julia takes Lily home, humiliating Tessa in front of Lovey.
Tessa cuts Lily's long hair as punishment, leading to a heated argument with Julia. As David arrives home, Tessa throws herself down the stairs, pretending Julia pushed her. David assures Julia that he loves her, but refuses to see the truth about his ex.
Julia and her friend Ali discover police records of Tessa's obsessive and violent tendencies as a child, which led her to burn down her father's home. As “Julia”, Tessa enjoys sexually explicit messages with Michael, inviting him to visit Julia for sex. Finding the real Julia alone at home, he attacks her, but a badly beaten Julia wounds him with a kitchen knife and escapes. Tessa, waiting outside, stabs Michael in the chest, framing Julia for his murder. Julia is released after being questioned by Detective Pope, who shows David the social media conversations with Michael.
At Tessa's home, David notices her burned gloves in the fireplace and the stolen ring on her finger. He realizes the whole truth, but an enraged Tessa knocks him unconscious with a fireplace poker, and ties him up. Julia arrives, taking Lily to her car, and returns to rescue David but is attacked by Tessa.
In the ensuing fight, Tessa is halted by the sight of her bleeding face in a mirror, and by a picture of Lily. As Julia holds her at bay with a knife, Tessa commits suicide by pulling herself onto the blade; dying, she asks Julia not to let Lily remember her like this.
Six months later, David and Julia have married and moved into a new house with Lily far from his home town, in San Francisco. Julia is horrified by the arrival of Lovey, asking to see her granddaughter.

documents.title: Three Christs
documents.overview: Dr. Alan Stone breaks new ground for treatment of the mentally ill through an experiment on three paranoid schizophrenic patients who believe they are Jesus Christ.
documents.plot:
Dr. Alan Stone, a progressive and idealistic psychologist, dropped out of New York University in 1954 to work directly with patients at the Ypsilanti State Mental Asylum. Stone, whose focus is on schizophrenic patients, is widely considered a critic of the system. In the 1950s, people with mental illnesses were mostly kept in institutions and sedated when needed. Treatments with insulin shock therapy and the use of electric shocks were common, while talk therapy was limited.
In Ypsilanti, Stone meets two patients who both believe they are Jesus Christ: the short intellectual Joseph Cassell and the gruff Clyde Benson. Stone develops a format of group talk therapy. He has another patient transferred to Ypsilanti who also believes he is Christ, Leon Gabor, and brings the three men together to study their behavior. He finds out that the problems of the three are completely different. Gabor suffered all his life from his deeply religious mother, and he was also traumatized by multiple rapes by a man he had been exposed to as a soldier. Benson could not cope with the death of his wife from an abortion. Cassell is prone to outbursts of anger. Once admitted to the institution, he was repeatedly sedated with electric shocks, which he developed a great fear of. Contrary to the skepticism of many colleagues, including the head of the institution, Dr. Orbus, Stone dispenses with physical punishment. He gets through to the patients by talking to them and writing them letters.
When he makes the cover of a professional journal with his new approach, it arouses the envy of Dr. Orbus, who wants a share of the fame and to be involved in the treatment. Orbus lets Cassell be taken alone to his office for an interview. It is revealed that Stone wrote the letters to Cassell on Orbus' behalf since the head of the asylum originally declined the task. Cassell feels betrayed by Stone and stalled by Orbus. Despite good behavior, he sees his hopes of leaving the clinic dwindling. Angry, he becomes abusive again, so Orbus orders renewed electric shocks for him. Stone tries to stop it but fails. In a skirmish with another doctor, he injures both of them. Orbus then has him expelled from the institution.
Orbus takes over his patients; however, Cassell, who noticed that Stone wanted to save him, no longer trusts Orbus. During a conversation in the chapel's bell tower with Orbus, he jumps out of the window and dies.
In the later hearing, Stone accuses Orbus of making negligent decisions. He also deciphers Cassell's last words, according to which Cassell not only committed suicide to be free but gave his life to justify the sins of Orbus as Jesus did the sins of humankind. The hearing ends with Stone being fired. However, he is granted permission and funds to continue his study (including of the two remaining patients) in New York. Orbus remains in his post but without decision-making powers until his retirement. The film closes with a summary.

documents.title: Dear Dictator
documents.tagline: She thought she was a rebel... Until she met a real one
documents.overview: When political turmoil forces a British-Caribbean dictator to flee his island nation, he seeks refuge and hides with a rebellious teenage girl in suburban America, and ends up teaching the young teen how to start a revolution and overthrow the "mean girls" in her high school.
documents.plot:
Dear Dictator is a 2018 American satirical comedy film written and directed by Lisa Addario and Joe Syracuse. It stars Michael Caine as Anton Vincent, the deposed dictator of a Caribbean island nation, and Odeya Rush as Tatiana Mills, the American teenager who becomes his pen pal, with Katie Holmes, Seth Green and Jason Biggs. The script appeared on the 2006 Black List of unproduced screenplays, and Alfred Molina, Robert De Niro and Anthony Hopkins were at various times attached to the title role before Caine was cast in 2016.

Sixteen-year-old Tatiana lives a chaotic life with her single mother, Darlene, who is involved with her married boss, Dr. Charles, a dentist with a foot fetish. For a letter-writing assignment from her social studies teacher, Mr. Spines, Tatiana becomes the pen pal of Anton Vincent, a notorious strongman who rules an island nation. When his people rise up against his violent, oppressive regime and overthrow him, Vincent vanishes, and Tatiana worries about his safety. A few days later he turns up unexpectedly in the United States and hides in her family's suburban garage.

There, Anton forms a grandfatherly bond with Tatiana and her struggling mother, making himself useful around the house while secretly coordinating with loyalist forces back home to plot his return to power. He also turns his attention to Tatiana's troubles at high school, where she is bullied by a clique of popular girls. Making her a dictator-in-training, he teaches her to seize power at school using the same methods that brought him to power in the Caribbean. His schemes eventually go too far, turning Tatiana against him, and the security services, having intercepted Anton's messages to his loyalists, suspect that she is involved in terrorism. The police question Tatiana and Darlene and search their home without realizing that the old man living with them is the missing dictator. No evidence is found and they are released, but Tatiana then tells the police who he is, and Anton is arrested pending extradition.

Screened at several festivals under its working title, Coup d'Etat, the film was released in North America by Cinedigm in theaters and on video on demand on March 16, 2018. Reviews were negative, although Caine's and Rush's performances were praised; Rotten Tomatoes reported 16% approval, with critics finding that it squandered its wildly silly premise and talented cast.

documents.title: Goodbye Christopher Robin
documents.overview: The behind the scenes story of the life of A.A. Milne and the creation of the Winnie the Pooh stories inspired by his son Christopher Robin.
documents.plot:
During World War II in 1941, Alan Alexander Milne – nicknamed "Blue" by his friends and family – and his wife Daphne receive a distressing telegram at their home. The story then flashes back to 1916 during World War I with Blue fighting in the Battle of the Somme. Blue resumes his life with Daphne in England while suffering shell shock with occasional flashbacks to his battle experiences, and has a child with Daphne. Daphne appears traumatised by the birth as the midwife says "she didn't understand the mechanics" of giving birth. She was also hoping for a girl and is disappointed to instead have a son. They name the baby Christopher Robin Milne, but generally call him "Billy Moon". They hire a nanny, Olive Rand, whom Billy calls "Nou". At Olive's job interview, Daphne says how wonderful it is that whilst the war killed so many men, it means there are a great number of women such as Olive who will never marry and can therefore be of service to others.
Blue is having difficulty resuming his writing – he wants to draft a compelling treatise against war – and relocates the family to a house in the country with wooded acreage. Daphne resents the move and returns to London for an extended period. During that time, Olive goes to care for her dying mother and the cook takes some time off, leaving Blue and Billy to fend for themselves. Reluctantly at first, Blue takes Billy along on walks in the woods and begins making up stories about the boy's adventures with the plush toy animals the parents have bought for him.
Blue invites his illustrator friend Ernest to join them at the house, and together they begin to develop the Winnie-the-Pooh books. Daphne returns to the house after Blue sends her a poem, "Vespers", that she has had published for him in Vanity Fair. Olive returns following her mother's death. After the Winnie-the-Pooh books become a success, Daphne manages their new-found celebrity and readily accepts extra opportunities to generate publicity and income, for example, a line of Winnie the Pooh bears, or an opportunity to have tea with 'Christopher Robin'. As Christopher Robin, Billy makes frequent public appearances, which he finds confusing and frustrating.
When Billy learns that Olive has a beau, Alfred Brockwell, he tells his parents, after which Daphne feels betrayed and confronts Olive nastily. Olive becomes angry with Blue and Daphne, resigns, and admonishes them for what they have been putting Billy through. Blue resolves to stop writing about the boy and his imaginary friends. Olive leaves and Billy's mother tells him not to cry.
Blue ends Billy's publicity activities and enrolls him at a boarding school. However, "Christopher Robin" is bullied at the school and emerges bitter toward his father.

documents.title: The Current War
documents.tagline: Power changes everything
documents.overview: Electricity titans Thomas Edison and George Westinghouse compete to create a sustainable system and market it to the American people.
documents.plot:
The Current War is a historical drama inspired by the 19th-century rivalry between Thomas Edison and George Westinghouse over which electrical system would power the United States, known as the "war of the currents." Directed by Alfonso Gomez-Rejon from a screenplay by Michael Mitnick, with Martin Scorsese and Steven Zaillian among the executive producers, it stars Benedict Cumberbatch as Edison, Michael Shannon as Westinghouse, Nicholas Hoult as Nikola Tesla and Tom Holland as Samuel Insull, alongside Katherine Waterston, Tuppence Middleton and Matthew Macfadyen.

In the 1880s, Edison is already famous as the inventor of the practical incandescent light bulb and is racing to electrify American cities with his direct current system. The industrialist Westinghouse, convinced that alternating current is cheaper and able to carry power over far greater distances, enters the business as Edison's rival after Edison snubs him. The competition soon turns personal and ruthless. Edison, struggling to balance his ambition with his devotion to his wife Mary and their children, launches a public campaign to brand alternating current as deadly, staging electrocutions of animals to frighten the public. Meanwhile, the brilliant Serbian immigrant Tesla, who briefly works for Edison before leaving in frustration, struggles to fund his own inventions until Westinghouse acquires his designs for an alternating current motor.

The contest escalates through patent battles and secret dealings, including Edison's covert involvement in the development of the electric chair, which is used for the first time to execute a man with alternating current. The rivalry comes to a head with the competition to light the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition in Chicago, a showcase of the future in which the winner will define how the nation is powered.

The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2017, but its release was derailed when The Weinstein Company collapsed amid the sexual abuse allegations against Harvey Weinstein. Lantern Entertainment acquired the film and sold US rights to 101 Studios, and Gomez-Rejon, with Scorsese's backing, carried out reshoots and trimmed the running time. This director's cut was released in the United States in October 2019. Reviewers judged it an improvement over the festival version; Metacritic gave it 55 out of 100.

documents.title: Get Out
documents.tagline: Just because you're invited, doesn't mean you're welcome.
documents.overview: Chris and his girlfriend Rose go upstate to visit her parents for the weekend. At first, Chris reads the family's overly accommodating behavior as nervous attempts to deal with their daughter's interracial relationship, but as the weekend progresses, a series of increasingly disturbing discoveries lead him to a truth that he never could have imagined.
documents.plot:
Get Out is a psychological horror film written and directed by Jordan Peele, released in 2017 by Blumhouse Productions. The movie tells the story of Chris Washington, a young African American photographer who agrees to visit his white girlfriend's family estate in upstate New York.

The film begins with Chris (played by Daniel Kaluuya) and his girlfriend Rose (played by Allison Williams) discussing their relationship and the fact that she has invited him to meet her family. Despite some initial reservations, Chris decides to attend the weekend getaway, hoping it will be a chance for them to take their relationship to the next level.

Upon arrival at the Armitage estate, Chris is greeted by Rose's parents, Dean (played by Bradley Whitford) and Missy (played by Catherine Keener), as well as her brother Jeremy (played by Caleb Landry Jones). Initially, Chris feels a sense of unease due to the family's strange behavior and the fact that they seem to be hiding something from him.

As the weekend progresses, Chris begins to notice that the family is treating him with an unusual level of hospitality, almost to the point of being overly accommodating. He also discovers that the family has a fascination with black culture, which he initially attributes to their enthusiasm for his photography work. However, as the days go by, Chris starts to uncover a sinister plot involving hypnosis, mind control, and a sinister secret that the Armitage family is hiding.

The turning point in the film comes when Chris discovers that the family has been using their wealth and influence to lure black people into their home, where they are subjected to a form of psychological manipulation. The family's true intention is to harvest the bodies of these individuals for use as vessels for their own white consciousness, essentially allowing them to experience life through the eyes of a black person without actually having to live it.

As Chris tries to escape and expose the truth, he realizes that he has become trapped in the Armitage estate. The film builds up to a tense climax, where Chris must use his wits and resourcefulness to outsmart the family and break free from their clutches.

Ultimately, Chris manages to escape the estate, but not before discovering that Rose is complicit in her family's sinister activities. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Rose has been using her relationship with Chris as a way to experience black culture without actually having to live it herself.

The film ends with Chris driving away from the Armitage estate, finally free from his ordeal. However, the final shot of the film suggests that Chris may not be entirely safe, leaving the audience with a sense of unease and uncertainty about his future.

Get Out is a thought-provoking and deeply unsettling film that explores themes of racism, privilege, and the fetishization of black culture. The movie's clever script, combined with its masterful direction and performances, make it a standout in contemporary horror cinema.

documents.title: Midnight Sun
documents.tagline: Love will light the way.
documents.overview: Katie, a 17-year-old, has been sheltered since childhood and confined to her house during the day by a rare disease that makes even the smallest amount of sunlight deadly. Fate intervenes when she meets Charlie and they embark on a summer romance.
documents.plot:
Midnight Sun is a 2018 American romantic fantasy film directed by Julie Yoe and written by Josh Campbell, Matt Stuecken, and Michael H. Weber. The movie is based on the novel of the same name by Stephenie Meyer.

The story revolves around Isabella "Bella" Swan (played by Elle Fanning), a teenage girl who moves to Forks, Washington to live with her father, Charlie (played by Kyle MacLachlan). Bella starts at a new high school, where she is immediately drawn to a mysterious and handsome boy named Edward Cullen (played by Robert Pattinson).

As Bella spends more time with Edward, they develop an intense connection, but their relationship is threatened by the danger that comes with being in love with a vampire. The Cullens are revealed to be a family of vampires who have been living among humans for years, and they must keep their true nature hidden from the rest of the world.

The movie takes a unique approach to telling the story, as it focuses on Bella's inner thoughts and feelings through a series of flashbacks and diary entries. This allows the audience to experience the story from Bella's perspective, making her emotions and struggles more relatable and intimate.

As Bella and Edward's relationship deepens, they face numerous challenges, including the threat of James (played by Cam Gigandet), a rogue vampire who is determined to destroy Bella. The Cullens work together to protect Bella, but their efforts are hindered by the fact that Bella is still learning about her own supernatural abilities.

Throughout the movie, the romance between Bella and Edward is portrayed as intense and all-consuming, with a deep emotional connection between the two characters. However, the film also explores themes of isolation, loneliness, and the difficulties of being in love with someone who is fundamentally different from oneself.

Ultimately, the movie ends on a hopeful note, with Bella and Edward's relationship still intact despite the many obstacles they have faced. The ending sets the stage for the rest of the Twilight Saga, which follows the further adventures of Bella and Edward as they navigate their supernatural world together.

Overall, Midnight Sun offers a fresh take on the Twilight franchise, focusing on Bella's inner world and emotions rather than the action-packed plot of the original movies. With its unique storytelling approach and beautiful cinematography, the film provides a captivating and romantic viewing experience for fans of the series.

documents.title: The Babysitter
documents.tagline: Dream girls can be a nightmare.
documents.overview: When Cole stays up past his bedtime, he discovers that his hot babysitter is part of a Satanic cult that will stop at nothing to keep him quiet.
documents.plot:
The Babysitter is a 2017 American supernatural horror film written and directed by Christian Stevens. The movie follows Cole, a teenager who has been babysitting for his family's wealthy neighbors, the Smiths, since he was eight years old.

Cole (played by Judah Lewis) is now 17 and feels suffocated by his mundane life in suburban Chicago. He spends most of his free time playing video games and hanging out with his friends. However, when he meets Bee (played by Samara Weaving), a new babysitter hired by the Smiths, Cole's life takes an unexpected turn.

Bee is charming, beautiful, and seems to be everything Cole has ever wanted in a girl. As they spend more time together, Cole becomes increasingly smitten with Bee, but he also starts to notice that she's not like other babysitters. She's always on her phone, and when Cole asks her about it, she brushes him off.

As the night progresses, Cole discovers that Bee is part of a coven of teenage witches who are using their babysitting job as a cover for their dark rituals. The coven, led by Bee, has been manipulating the Smiths' children, turning them into mindless drones who do their bidding.

Cole soon realizes that he's in grave danger and must find a way to escape from Bee and her cohorts. He enlists the help of his friends, Ben (played by Owen Vaccaro) and Max (played by Hana Mae Lee), but they're not much help. In fact, they seem to be under some sort of mind control as well.

As Cole tries to outsmart Bee and her coven, he discovers that she's been using a magical artifact to control the minds of those around her. The artifact is hidden in a mysterious box that Bee keeps locked away.

In a thrilling climax, Cole manages to break into the Smiths' house and confronts Bee. He uses his knowledge of magic and some quick thinking to outwit her and destroy the artifact. However, not before Bee reveals that she's been using the coven to exact revenge on the Smiths for their wealth and privilege.

In the end, Cole emerges victorious but shaken by the experience. He realizes that he's been living in a bubble of ignorance and that there's more to life than what he thought. The movie ends with Cole reflecting on his newfound understanding of the world and his place in it.

Overall, The Babysitter is a tense and suspenseful horror film that explores themes of teenage angst, rebellion, and the struggle for identity. While it may not be the most original plot, the movie's clever twists and turns keep viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

documents.title: LEGO Jurassic World: The Indominus Escape
documents.original_title: LEGO Jurassic World: The Indominus Escape
documents.overview: The scientists of Jurassic World create a captivating and terrifying new creature that loves hot dogs. But what happens when the hot dogs run out?
documents.plot:
LEGO Jurassic World: The Indominus Escape is a 2016 American animated comedy short produced by Universal and the LEGO Group as part of the toy line tied to the Jurassic World franchise. It first appeared in October 2016 as a five-part online series and was then released on DVD later that month as a single 24-minute film, packaged with the short LEGO Jurassic World: Employee Safety Video. Set before the events of Jurassic World (2015), it reimagines most of that film's characters as minifigures and is regarded as the first animated spin-off of the Jurassic Park franchise. The voice cast includes Bryce Dallas Howard, A.J. LoCascio, Jake Johnson, Lauren Lapkus, Zachary Levi, BD Wong, Fred Tatasciore and Sendhil Ramamurthy.

The story opens with park owner Simon Masrani flying Claire Dearing to the island and showing off with aerial stunts, until he crashes into the aviary and tumbles out of his helicopter. Owen Grady rescues him with the help of a trained Pteranodon. Before he is driven away in an ambulance, Masrani tells Claire that Jurassic World will need a new attraction. Meanwhile, the security chief Vic Hoskins goes hunting in the woods and mistakes a park employee in a dinosaur costume for the real thing, chasing him through the jungle for much of the film.

Claire resolves to create a brand-new dinosaur. Owen doubts it can be done, but Dr. Henry Wu proves otherwise by combining Velociraptor and Carnotaurus DNA, and Owen later discovers a whole collection of earlier hybrids kept in an old section of the island. Wu's newest creation, the Indominus rex, turns out to have an insatiable appetite for hot dogs. When it spots the same costumed employee, now dressed as a hot dog mascot, it breaks out of its enclosure and pursues him. Claire calls in the containment unit, rams the beast with a truck and uses a trail of hot dogs to lure it, while Owen's raptors briefly turn against the soldiers because the Indominus shares their DNA. Eventually Owen arrives with the old Tyrannosaurus and the hybrids, and together they drive the Indominus into a pit. The next day visitors enjoy the new attraction, dinosaurs kicking a gyrosphere like a ball with Hoskins still trapped inside, while in a closing scene Wu feeds a second Indominus.

documents.title: Daddy's Home 2
documents.tagline: More Daddies. More Problems.
documents.overview: Brad and Dusty must deal with their intrusive fathers during the holidays.
documents.plot:
Daddy's Home 2 is a 2017 American Christmas comedy film directed by Sean Anders and John Morris, and produced by Paramount Pictures.

The movie takes place two years after the events of the first film. Brad Whitaker (Will Ferrell) and Dusty Mayron (Mark Wahlberg) are still co-parenting their children, but they're struggling to balance their own relationships with their wives, Sara (Linda Cardellini) and Megan (Catherine Keener), respectively.

As Christmas approaches, the Whitakers and the Mayrons decide to spend the holiday together as a blended family. However, things quickly become complicated when Brad's estranged father, Don Whitaker (Mel Gibson), shows up unexpectedly with his own son, Ryan (Wes Bentley). Don is a gruff, old-school man who clashes with Dusty and the rest of the family.

As the two families try to come together for Christmas, they face various challenges. Brad and Dusty struggle to assert their authority as co-parents, while Sara and Megan try to keep the peace between their husbands. Meanwhile, Don's presence sparks tension among the group, particularly with Dusty, who feels like he's being replaced by his father.

As the story unfolds, we see flashbacks of Don's past, which reveal a complex and troubled relationship with Brad. We also learn more about Ryan, who is struggling to find his place in the world after serving in the military.

Throughout the film, the characters' relationships are put to the test as they navigate their differences and try to come together for Christmas. In the end, the Whitakers and Mayrons learn to put aside their differences and work together as a blended family.

One of the standout aspects of Daddy's Home 2 is its exploration of complex themes such as family dynamics, masculinity, and identity. The film tackles these issues with humor and heart, making it a relatable and entertaining watch for audiences of all ages.

Overall, Daddy's Home 2 is a fun and lighthearted holiday film that explores the ups and downs of blended families. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and heartfelt moments, it's a great addition to any Christmas movie marathon.

documents.title: Sandy Wexler
documents.overview: When a hapless but dedicated talent manager signs his first client who actually has talent, his career finally starts to take off.
documents.plot: When a hapless but dedicated talent manager signs his first client who actually has talent, his career finally starts to take off.

documents.title: Ad Astra
documents.tagline: The answers we seek are just outside our reach
documents.overview: The near future, a time when both hope and hardships drive humanity to look to the stars and beyond. While a mysterious phenomenon menaces to destroy life on planet Earth, astronaut Roy McBride undertakes a mission across the immensity of space and its many perils to uncover the truth about a lost expedition that decades before boldly faced emptiness and silence in search of the unknown.
documents.plot:
In the early 22nd century, mysterious cosmic-ray bursts emanating from Neptune cause power surges that threaten to destroy all life in the Solar System. Major Roy McBride is informed that the surge is antimatter in origin and may be connected to the Lima Project, a space station in orbit around Neptune, sent twenty-nine years earlier to search for intelligent life and fuelled by antimatter. Roy's father, Clifford McBride, was the project's leader, a man considered a hero in SpaceCom history. Contact was lost sixteen years into its mission. Roy agrees to travel to Mars to use the last active communications station unaffected by the bursts in an effort to contact Clifford aboard the Lima.
At the Moon SpaceCom base, Roy is told in secret by Colonel Pruitt that should he fail to make contact with the Lima Project, the station will have to be destroyed. Roy obtains passage to Mars on the cruiser Cepheus.
On the way to Mars the Cepheus attends a distress call from a research station, where the captain is killed. The ship continues to Mars but is hit by a surge as it is landing, Roy assumes command from the overwhelmed (but now in charge) First Officer, and calmly lands the ship. After securing himself in the underground SpaceCom complex, Roy begins recording officially pre-written voice messages and transmitting them to the Lima Project in hopes that his father will respond. Following several failed attempts, Roy ends up ignoring the official message and sends a personal message to his father stating that he hopes he will see him one day. Roy is then told he will be returning to Earth as his 'personal connection' makes him unsuitable for further service.
Roy is visited by facility director Helen Lantos, who reveals that her parents were Lima Project team members. She shows him classified footage revealing that Clifford's team mutinied and attempted to return to Earth, causing him to shut off their life-support systems; her parents were among those killed. She also states that the Cepheus is carrying a nuclear weapon and has now been requisitioned for a secret 'seek and destroy' mission without Roy. Seeing that the 'hero' story was fabricated to hide the truth, Roy decides that he should deal with his father. Lantos facilitates Roy getting to the rocket as it prepares to depart.
Roy climbs aboard as the rocket takes off and is immediately discovered by the crew, who are unintentionally killed in the confrontation. During the 79-day journey to Neptune, a solitary Roy reflects on his relationship with his father and with his estranged wife, Eve. He finally arrives at the station and plants the nuclear bomb before encountering Clifford, the sole survivor of the Lima Project. Clifford explains that the surges are coming from an antimatter meltdown caused by the mutiny. He also admits to Roy that he never really cared about his family and does not consider Earth his home.

documents.title: Disobedience
documents.tagline: Love is an act of defiance
documents.overview: A woman learns about the death of her Orthodox Jewish father, a rabbi. She returns home and has romantic feelings rekindled for her best childhood friend, who is now married to her cousin.
documents.plot:
New York photographer Ronit Krushka, known as Ronnie in the United States, returns to her childhood home in North London after her father, the old Rav, succumbs to pneumonia. Ronit is uncomfortable seeing everyone again since she was banished from the community for behaving in a manner not conforming to Orthodox culture.
Ronit is shocked to learn that her childhood friends Dovid, a chosen disciple of her father, and Esti, are now married. Dovid invites Ronit to stay with them. They attend Shabbat dinner at her uncle Moshe's house where she is questioned by the guests about changing her name, and they tell her she should get married, because that is what is right. Ronit tells them if she had stayed in London she probably would have been married off, but she would have been suicidal.
Ronit visits Moshe at his office to discuss the disposition of her father's house and discovers her father has left all of his possessions to the synagogue. Ronit and Esti run into each other on the street while Ronit is on her way to visit her father's house. While inspecting items left in the house, Ronit becomes frustrated and expresses that she wishes to cut her trip short and return to the United States. Upset, Esti tenderly kisses Ronit, who initially resists before reciprocating. Esti confesses to having asked Ronit to be notified of her father's death out of a desire to see her again. She also reveals her unhappiness with her life choices, taken based on the Rav's advice and her strong belief in HaShem. It is revealed that Ronit and Esti were caught in a romantic tryst when they were younger, leading Ronit to leave the United Kingdom; neither has been with another woman since and Esti admits being attracted to only women.
On the way home, they stop at a nearby park and kiss again, but are spotted by a couple from the congregation. The next day Esti, who works as a teacher at the local Jewish school, is called into the headmistress' office after the couple deliver a complaint about what they saw. Meanwhile, Dovid is asked to take over the Rav's duties. Ronit tells Esti she is leaving London, and the two of them sneak away to a hotel room in central London for passionate sex.
When Esti arrives home, she turns down Dovid when he tries to initiate intimacy. She later tells him the truth about her feelings for Ronit, causing him to leave. Esti later purchases a pregnancy test and discovers she is pregnant. The next morning, Dovid calls Ronit and says that Esti is missing. They spend the day looking for her and, when they return home, Esti has come back; she asks Dovid for her freedom, stating that she wants to give her unborn child a chance to decide whether or not to be part of their community.
Ronit and Esti attend the Rav's hesped (eulogy gathering), which is to be given by Dovid. Under the guise of addressing the congregation, he releases Esti from their marriage and then publicly turns down the offer of becoming the congregation's new spiritual guide.

documents.title: I Kill Giants
documents.tagline: I find giants, I hunt giants
documents.overview: Sophia, a new high school student, tries to make friends with Barbara, who tells her that “she kills giants,” protecting this way her hometown and its inhabitants, who do not understand her strange behavior.

documents.title: Don't Knock Twice
documents.tagline: Pray she doesn't answer.
documents.overview: A mother desperate to reconnect with her troubled daughter becomes embroiled in the urban legend of a demonic witch.
documents.plot:
In Wales, Jessica "Jess" Webb-Thomas, an American sculptor and former drug addict, meets with her estranged daughter Chloe (from Jess's prior marriage and sent to foster care due to the former's drug addiction) and invites her to come live with her and her second husband, Ben Thomas. Chloe declines. That night, Chloe goes out with her friend Danny to a house where legend says a witch lived. The two knock twice on the door and leave. Danny starts experiencing paranormal occurrences and is later dragged away by an unseen force. When the demonic spirit frightens Chloe, she accepts Jess' offer and moves in with her.
Chloe is initially hostile to her family. Strange events unfold, beginning when Chloe finds a human molar in her carrot and coriander soup. Jess suffers from a nightmare about an old woman crying in her house. In her nightmare, the woman looks at Jess and says "Przepraszam" ("I'm sorry" in Polish), before slitting her own throat. Jess tells Chloe about her dream and, finding this description familiar, Chloe tells her about Mary Aminov, a supposed witch that used to live next door. After her death by suicide, an urban legend started that she would come and get you if you knocked twice on her door. While sculpting, Jess's model Tira is disturbed by Chloe's presence and leaves. Chloe believes to be haunted by Baba Yaga, a demonic witch from Slavic folklore.
Chloe slowly warms up to her mother. One day, Jess discovers her workshop in shambles with "She's mine" scrawled on the floor. That night, the two are terrorized by the witch. The next day, a portal opens and Chloe is almost dragged inside but is saved by Jess. They meet with Tira, who says that Mary was never a witch. Because Chloe helped spread the false rumor of witchcraft, Mary's spirit wants revenge. Chloe flees in panic, convinced that the disappearances were her fault. She is found and returned to the foster home. Jess goes to retrieve her and has an epiphany that the true culprit of the disappearances was not Mary but Detective Boardman. Chloe is taken by the witch.
Jess breaks into Mary's abandoned house, injuring her foot on an old nail. She is caught and sent to the police station, but not before knocking twice at the door. When she is alone in her prison cell, she is taken through the same portal. She wanders into a cave where she finds a cage with Chloe in it. Jess gets her out and Baba Yaga pursues them; meanwhile, Boardman arrives at the witch's home. The pair are able to escape through the front door, but Boardman is dragged inside by the witch.
Ben returns home and is confronted by a mysterious figure in their bedroom. Jess and Chloe arrive home but find Ben missing. Tira is shown leaving the property covered in blood with Ben's dead body in the trunk of her car. The "Slave of Baba Yaga" symbol is shown on her chest.

documents.title: Terrifier
documents.tagline: There is nothing more frightening than a clown after midnight.
documents.overview: On Halloween night, a young woman finds herself as the obsession of a sadistic murderer known as Art the Clown.
documents.plot:
Terrifier is a 2016 American horror film written, directed, and edited by Damien Leone. The film stars David Howard Thornton as Art the Clown, a sadistic and murderous clown who terrorizes a small town on Halloween night.

The story begins with Art, a seemingly ordinary clown, being left behind by his owner, Reverend Henry (played by Jeff Daniel Phillips), at a children's birthday party. However, it becomes clear that Art is not your average clown. He has a twisted and sadistic personality, and he takes great pleasure in causing pain and terrorizing those around him.

As the night progresses, Art begins to stalk and murder a group of teenagers who are out trick-or-treating. The film's pacing is fast-moving and intense, with a focus on building tension and suspense through its use of long takes and close-ups.

Throughout the film, Art's backstory is slowly revealed through a series of flashbacks, which show him being abused by Reverend Henry as a child. This traumatic experience has left Art with deep emotional scars, and he seeks revenge against those who wronged him.

One of the standout aspects of Terrifier is its use of practical effects to bring Art to life. David Howard Thornton's performance as the titular character is chilling and unsettling, and his physicality and presence on screen are truly unnerving.

The film has received widespread critical acclaim for its originality and effectiveness in building tension and suspense. It has also spawned a sequel, Terrifier 2, which was released in 2022.

Overall, Terrifier is a masterclass in building tension and suspense through its use of long takes, close-ups, and practical effects. The film's unique blend of horror and dark humor makes it a must-see for fans of the genre.

documents.title: Cage Dive
documents.tagline: First you find the sharks. Then they find you.
documents.overview: Three friends from California are filming an audition tape for an extreme reality game show. They document their journey to Australia where they will be doing their most dangerous activity.... Shark Cage Diving. A catastrophic turn of events leaves them in baited water full of Great White Sharks, turning their recording into a blood chilling diary of survival... and death.
documents.plot:
Open Water 3: Cage Dive is a 2017 Australian found-footage survival horror film written and directed by Gerald Rascionato. Presented as a mockumentary about supposedly true events, it follows three American tourists recording an audition tape for an extreme reality show when their shark cage diving boat capsizes. The cast includes Joel Hogan, Megan Peta Hill and Pete Valley. Although billed as the third Open Water film, it is a standalone story linked to the earlier entries only by theme.

A news report from October 2015 describes a capsized shark diving boat off Australia and a search for three missing passengers from Laguna Beach, California. A week later a diver finds an underwater camera lodged in a reef, its memory card intact, and posts the footage online. The recordings show brothers Josh and Jeff and Jeff's girlfriend, Megan, arriving in Sydney to stay with the brothers' cousin Greg before flying to Adelaide for their dive, and reveal that Megan is secretly having an affair with Josh. During the excursion, as the three enter the cage, a rogue wave overturns the boat. They escape to the surface amid wounded passengers, and sharks soon kill several people nearby.

Drifting for hours, the trio clings to tangled life preservers while Jeff, who has a heart condition and needs regular medication, weakens. That night they find an inflatable emergency raft with supplies, and Josh rescues an unconscious, hypothermic woman from floating debris. During an argument Megan and Josh accidentally fire a flare inside the raft, which burns, killing the woman. The quarrel exposes the affair, and soon afterward a shark drags Megan under. The next morning Jeff taunts Josh about Megan's death until he loses consciousness from his heart condition, and Josh eventually lets his brother's body sink. With the camera battery nearly exhausted, Josh films a rescue helicopter in the distance, but as he waves and shouts, the camera captures a great white rising beneath him, and the footage ends as he is pulled under.

Lionsgate acquired the independent production in early 2017 and rebranded it as part of the Open Water series after the success of Open Water 2: Adrift, releasing it across multiple platforms on August 11, 2017. It bears similarities to 47 Meters Down, another 2017 film about a cage dive gone wrong. It received a 25% score on Rotten Tomatoes from eight critics, although Starburst Magazine reviewed it positively.

documents.title: Maleficent: Mistress of Evil
documents.tagline: Go beyond the fairy tale
documents.overview: Maleficent and her goddaughter Aurora begin to question the complex family ties that bind them as they are pulled in different directions by impending nuptials, unexpected allies, and dark new forces at play.
documents.plot:
Maleficent: Mistress of Evil is a 2019 American dark fantasy film directed by Michelle MacLaren, written by Michelle MacLaren and Christina Hodson, and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The film serves as a sequel to the 2014 film Maleficent.

The story begins with Princess Aurora (Ella Balinska) now a young woman, preparing for her wedding to Prince Philip (Benedict Walker). However, Maleficent (Angelina Jolie), who has been watching over Aurora from afar, senses that something is amiss. She discovers that the royal family's advisor, King Stefan (Harris Dickinson), plans to use dark magic to ensure his daughter's happiness and secure the throne.

Maleficent sets out to stop the wedding, knowing that it will lead to a catastrophic outcome for all of them. Along the way, she meets Morgan (Jemaine Clement), a powerful sorcerer who claims to be her long-lost brother. As they journey together, Maleficent learns more about her past and the reason behind her curse.

Meanwhile, Prince Philip's mother, Queen Grimhilde (Lesley Manville), is revealed to be the one responsible for casting the original curse on Aurora as a child. The queen's true intentions are to use Aurora's blood to gain ultimate power and control over the kingdom.

As Maleficent navigates her complicated past and confronts her enemies, she must also face her own morality and the consequences of her actions. Alongside Morgan, she forms an unlikely alliance with the fairy godmother, who helps them in their quest to stop the wedding and save Aurora from a terrible fate.

The film's climax features an epic battle between Maleficent and Queen Grimhilde, with the two powerful women engaging in a magical duel that will determine the future of the kingdom. In the end, Maleficent emerges victorious, but not without scars and a newfound understanding of her own strength and vulnerability.

Throughout the film, Angelina Jolie's performance as Maleficent is both captivating and nuanced, bringing depth to the character's complexities. The supporting cast delivers solid performances, particularly Ella Balinska as Aurora, who shines in her breakout role.

Overall, Maleficent: Mistress of Evil offers a thrilling and emotionally resonant sequel that expands on the original story while introducing new characters and themes. With its stunning visuals, engaging storyline, and strong performances, this film is sure to delight fans of fantasy and adventure movies alike.

documents.title: Christopher Robin
documents.tagline: Don't underestimate the value of doing nothing.
documents.overview: Christopher Robin, the boy who had countless adventures in the Hundred Acre Wood, has grown up and lost his way. Now it’s up to his spirited and loveable stuffed animals, Winnie The Pooh, Tigger, Piglet, and the rest of the gang, to rekindle their friendship and remind him of endless days of childlike wonder and make-believe, when doing nothing was the very best something.
documents.plot:
Christopher Robin is a 2018 American fantasy drama film directed by Marc Forster and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie is based on the Winnie-the-Pooh stories created by A.A. Milne.

The story begins with Christopher Robin (played by Ewan McGregor), now a grown man, who has lost touch with his childhood imagination and the magical world of Winnie-the-Pooh. He is struggling to find meaning in his life as a successful businessman, but feels unfulfilled and disconnected from his past.

One day, while on vacation at the Hundred Acre Wood, Christopher Robin reunites with his old friends Pooh (voiced by Jim Cummings), Piglet (voiced by Nick Mohammed), Eeyore (voiced by Brad Garrett), Tigger (voiced by Jim Cummings), Rabbit (voiced by Peter Capaldi), Owl (voiced by Toby Jones), and Kanga (voiced by Nicole Scherzinger). The friends are delighted to see Christopher Robin again, but they also sense that he has lost his way.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Christopher Robin's adult life is marked by stress, anxiety, and a lack of creativity. He feels like he's losing himself in the process of becoming a successful businessman. Meanwhile, Pooh and the other animals are struggling to cope with the changing world around them, including the loss of their home due to urban development.

Through his interactions with his friends, Christopher Robin begins to rediscover the joys of childhood imagination and creativity. He starts to see the world through the eyes of a child again, and finds inspiration in the simple pleasures of life. The movie features stunning animation, bringing the beloved characters to life in a way that is both nostalgic and fresh.

As the story reaches its climax, Christopher Robin must confront his own fears and doubts in order to find his true purpose in life. With the help of his friends, he learns to let go of his adult responsibilities and rediscover the magic of childhood. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Christopher Robin returning home to his family, but this time with a renewed sense of wonder and imagination.

Throughout the film, there are also flashbacks that show Christopher Robin's childhood adventures in the Hundred Acre Wood, which serve as a reminder of the power of imagination and friendship. The movie features a talented voice cast, including Emily Blunt as Christopher Robin's wife, Jane, and Hayley Atwell as his mother.

Overall, Christopher Robin is a heartwarming and visually stunning film that celebrates the importance of childhood imagination and creativity. It's a story about finding one's true purpose in life and rediscovering the magic of childhood through the power of friendship and imagination.

documents.title: Aladdin
documents.tagline: Choose Wisely.
documents.overview: A kindhearted street urchin named Aladdin embarks on a magical adventure after finding a lamp that releases a wisecracking genie while a power-hungry Grand Vizier vies for the same lamp that has the power to make their deepest wishes come true.
documents.plot:
Aladdin is a 2019 American fantasy adventure film directed by Guy Ritchie and produced by Jerry Bruckheimer. The movie is a live-action remake of the 1992 animated film of the same name, which was based on the Middle Eastern folk tale "Aladdin's Wonderful Lamp".

The story begins in the bustling streets of Agrabah, where we meet our protagonist, Aladdin (played by Mena Massoud), a poor but kind-hearted street urchin who lives with his pet monkey, Abu. One day, while exploring the marketplace, Aladdin stumbles upon a mysterious cave where he finds a magic lamp containing the Genie (played by Will Smith). The Genie is an ancient being who has been trapped in the lamp for thousands of years and is eager to be released.

The Genie grants Aladdin three wishes, which he uses to become a prince to win the heart of Princess Jasmine (played by Naomi Scott), the beautiful daughter of the Sultan. However, their romance is threatened when the evil Jafar (played by Marwan Kenzari), the Royal Advisor, discovers that the magic lamp and its Genie are real.

As Aladdin navigates his new life as a prince, he must also confront the dark secrets of Agrabah's past and the true intentions of Jafar. The Genie, who has grown attached to Aladdin, becomes a valuable ally in the battle against Jafar.

Throughout the film, Ritchie's signature style is evident in the witty banter, clever wordplay, and fast-paced action sequences. The movie also features stunning visuals, with intricate sets and costumes that transport viewers to the vibrant world of Agrabah.

As the story unfolds, Aladdin must confront his own identity and the consequences of his wishes. In a thrilling climax, he faces off against Jafar in an epic battle to save the kingdom and win Jasmine's heart.

Ultimately, Aladdin emerges victorious, but not without sacrifices. The film concludes with Aladdin and Jasmine sharing a romantic moment, while the Genie is finally able to rest in peace. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Aladdin embracing his true identity as a street urchin who has become a hero.

Overall, the 2019 live-action remake of Aladdin is a visually stunning and action-packed adventure that stays true to the spirit of the original tale while introducing new elements to captivate modern audiences.

documents.title: The Lion King
documents.tagline: The King has Returned.
documents.overview: Simba idolizes his father, King Mufasa, and takes to heart his own royal destiny. But not everyone in the kingdom celebrates the new cub's arrival. Scar, Mufasa's brother—and former heir to the throne—has plans of his own. The battle for Pride Rock is ravaged with betrayal, tragedy and drama, ultimately resulting in Simba's exile. With help from a curious pair of newfound friends, Simba will have to figure out how to grow up and take back what is rightfully his.
documents.plot:
The Lion King is a 2019 American musical drama film and a photorealistically animated remake of Disney's traditionally animated 1994 film. Directed by Jon Favreau and written by Jeff Nathanson, it was produced by Walt Disney Pictures and Fairview Entertainment. The voice cast includes Donald Glover as Simba, Beyoncé Knowles-Carter as Nala, Chiwetel Ejiofor as Scar, Seth Rogen and Billy Eichner as Pumbaa and Timon, John Oliver as Zazu, John Kani as Rafiki and Alfre Woodard as Sarabi, with James Earl Jones reprising his role as Mufasa.

In the Pride Lands, King Mufasa and Queen Sarabi present their newborn son Simba to the gathered animals, while Mufasa's younger brother Scar resentfully covets the throne. Mufasa teaches Simba about the responsibilities of a king and the "circle of life" that connects all living things. Scar tricks the curious cub into exploring a forbidden elephant graveyard, where Simba and his best friend Nala are chased by hyenas led by Shenzi before Mufasa, alerted by the hornbill Zazu, comes to their rescue. Scar then strikes a deal with the hyenas, promising them hunting rights in exchange for their help in killing Mufasa and Simba. He lures Simba into a gorge and has the hyenas drive a stampede of wildebeest toward him; Mufasa saves his son but is thrown to his death by Scar, who convinces Simba that he was to blame and urges him to run away and never return. Scar claims the throne and lets the hyenas into the Pride Lands. Rescued in the desert by the meerkat Timon and the warthog Pumbaa, Simba grows up carefree in their oasis, living by their motto "hakuna matata". Years later he is reunited with Nala, who tells him that the kingdom has fallen into drought and ruin under Scar's rule. Still burdened by guilt, Simba refuses to return, until the wise mandrill Rafiki and a vision of his father's spirit remind him of who he is, and he heads home to confront Scar and reclaim his place in the circle of life.

The film received mixed reviews, with many critics praising its visuals but faulting its lack of originality and near-identical retelling of the original; it holds a 52% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. It nevertheless grossed more than $1.6 billion worldwide and broke several box-office records, including becoming the highest-grossing animated film of all time until 2024.

documents.title: Chip 'n Dale: Rescue Rangers
documents.tagline: It's not a reboot. It's a comeback.
documents.overview: Decades since their successful television series was canceled, Chip has succumbed to a life of suburban domesticity as an insurance salesman. Dale, meanwhile, has had CGI surgery and works the nostalgia convention circuit, desperate to relive his glory days. When a former cast mate mysteriously disappears, Chip and Dale must repair their broken friendship and take on their Rescue Rangers detective personas once again to save their friend’s life.
documents.plot:
Chip 'n Dale: Rescue Rangers is a 2022 American live-action and animated action-adventure comedy based on Disney's chipmunk duo and serving as a follow-up to the 1989 animated series of the same name. It was directed by Akiva Schaffer from a screenplay by Dan Gregor and Doug Mand. John Mulaney voices Chip and Andy Samberg voices Dale, with KiKi Layne, Will Arnett, Eric Bana, Seth Rogen and J. K. Simmons. It premiered at the El Capitan Theatre and was released on Disney+ on May 20, 2022.

In a world where humans and cartoon characters live side by side, Chip and Dale become best friends in elementary school and later move to Hollywood, where they rise from bit parts to stardom with the hit series Chip 'n Dale: Rescue Rangers. When Dale is offered a solo spin-off, the pair fall out bitterly and the show is cancelled. Thirty years later, Chip is a cautious, jaded insurance salesman, while Dale, who has undergone "CGI surgery" to look three-dimensional, works the fan convention circuit.

Their old co-star Monterey Jack, deep in debt to the criminal Valley Gang because of his addiction to cheese, warns them of a ring that kidnaps cartoons, alters their appearance and forces them to star in cheap bootleg films overseas. When Monty disappears, the estranged chipmunks reluctantly reunite to find him, helped by Ellie Steckler, an eager police officer and devoted fan of their show.

Their investigation leads to the gang's leader, Sweet Pete, a grown-up, embittered Peter Pan who was cast aside by the industry when he aged, and his henchmen. The chipmunks trace the operation to a warehouse containing a machine for reshaping toons, and realise that someone in the police is working with Pete. During a chase at a fan convention Chip is captured, and Ellie discovers that her captain is in league with the villain.

Dale rallies their old co-stars Gadget and Zipper, now married with a large family, and stops the machine before it can be used on Chip. In the chaos, Pete is transformed into a monstrous amalgam of cartoon parts. Using a trick from one of their old episodes, the chipmunks trap him, and the FBI, led by Ugly Sonic, arrests the gang. When Dale survives a cannon blast thanks to a keepsake Chip once gave him, the friends reconcile, free Monty and the other captive toons and go on to make a successful reboot of their show.

Critics responded warmly, with 81% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and the film later won the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Television Movie.

documents.title: The Return of Godzilla
documents.tagline: Breaking 30 years of silence comes the anticipated-worldwide latest "Godzilla" work!
documents.overview: After a fishing boat is attacked, the sole surviving crew member realizes it is none other than a resurrected Godzilla. However, efforts to bring the story to light are suppressed by the Japanese government amid growing political tensions between the United States and the Soviet Union, who are both willing to bomb Japan to stop the monster.
documents.plot:
The Return of Godzilla is a 1984 Japanese science fiction kaiju film directed by Kazuki Ōmori and produced by Tomoyuki Tanaka. It is the 15th film in the Godzilla franchise.

The movie begins with a series of mysterious earthquakes occurring around the world, which are later revealed to be caused by the return of Godzilla, also known as "Gigantis" or "Godzilla's Return". The story takes place two years after the events of Godzilla vs. Biollante (1989), where Godzilla is awakened from its slumber in the depths of the ocean.

The film starts with a series of strange occurrences happening around the world, including earthquakes and tidal waves. As the earthquakes intensify, it becomes clear that Godzilla has returned to wreak havoc on humanity. The Japanese government assembles a team of scientists and military personnel to deal with the crisis.

The main character, Dr. Yamane (played by Takeshi Kusao), is a renowned paleontologist who had previously studied Godzilla's DNA. He is recruited by the government to lead the team that will study and stop Godzilla. The team includes his daughter, Emiko (played by Yuriko Hoshi), a young scientist who has grown up studying her father's work.

As Godzilla begins its rampage across Japan, the team discovers that it is not just a mindless beast, but a creature with a complex intelligence and a desire to destroy humanity. The team also learns that Godzilla's return is linked to the discovery of a new species of giant lizard in the depths of the ocean.

The plot thickens as the team discovers that Godzilla's DNA has been altered by its encounter with a new species of giant lizard, which has given it enhanced strength and intelligence. This revelation raises questions about the nature of Godzilla's existence and whether it is truly a monster or a creature worthy of respect.

As the story unfolds, the team faces numerous challenges in trying to stop Godzilla. They use various tactics, including nuclear missiles and sonic devices, but nothing seems to work. The film builds towards an epic showdown between Godzilla and the team, which culminates in a dramatic confrontation on the streets of Tokyo.

In the end, Dr. Yamane comes up with a plan to use a device that can disrupt Godzilla's DNA, rendering it unable to reproduce. However, this plan is complicated by the fact that Emiko has fallen in love with Godzilla and wants to protect it. The film ends with a bittersweet conclusion, as Emiko sacrifices herself to save her father and the world from Godzilla.

The Return of Godzilla is a thought-provoking film that explores themes of nature vs. nurture, humanity's relationship with technology, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond our control. It is also a thrilling adventure that showcases Godzilla's iconic status as a symbol of Japanese popular culture.

documents.title: Flower
documents.tagline: Bad decisions. Good intentions.
documents.overview: Rebellious, quick-witted Erica Vandross is a 17-year-old firecracker living with her single mom, Laurie, and her mom's new boyfriend, Bob, in L.A.'s San Fernando Valley. When Bob's mentally unbalanced son, Luke, arrives from rehab to live with the family, Erica finds her domestic and personal life overwhelmed. With Luke and her sidekicks Kala and Claudine in tow, Erica acts out by exposing a high school teacher's dark secret.
documents.plot:
Flower is a 2017 American romantic comedy-drama directed by Max Winkler from a screenplay he wrote with Alex McAulay and Matt Spicer. Zoey Deutch stars as Erica Vandross, a brash and sexually curious seventeen-year-old, with Kathryn Hahn as her mother Laurie, Tim Heidecker as Laurie's boyfriend Bob, Joey Morgan as Bob's troubled son Luke, and Adam Scott as a former teacher. Dylan Gelula, Maya Eshet and Eric Edelstein complete the cast. The film premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival in April 2017 and was later released by The Orchard.

Erica and two friends run a reckless scheme in their Los Angeles suburb: Erica seduces older men while her friends secretly film the encounter, then the trio extort money by threatening to expose the men for involvement with a minor. Erica is saving the money to pay bail for her father, who is in jail awaiting trial for attempting to rob a casino. Her mother tolerates her behaviour but is frustrated that Erica refuses to warm to her new partner, Bob.

When Bob's son Luke, an anxious and emotionally fragile eighteen-year-old, returns from rehab and moves into the household, Erica first tries to provoke him but soon develops an unexpected friendship with him. At a bowling alley, Luke suffers a panic attack upon seeing Will Jordan, a former middle-school teacher he once accused of sexual abuse, a case that was dropped because of inconsistencies in his account. Shortly afterwards, Erica stops Luke from attempting suicide. Determined to punish the man she believes hurt him, Erica decides to make Will her group's next target, and Luke reluctantly agrees to help. As she pursues the teacher, however, the plan grows more dangerous and the truth about what happened between Will and Luke turns out to be more complicated than she assumed, forcing Erica to confront the consequences of her impulsive sense of justice.

The film moves between raunchy teen comedy and darker territory involving abuse, depression and family dysfunction, with the relationship between Erica and Luke at its centre.

Reviews were mixed. On Rotten Tomatoes the film holds an approval rating of about 48 percent; the consensus credits Deutch with bringing even a preposterously written character vividly to life, while finding the film's tonal shifts and treatment of its serious subject matter uneven.

documents.title: Above Suspicion
documents.tagline: The devil always comes as everything you wanted
documents.overview: The chilling true story of a newly married FBI poster boy assigned to an Appalachian mountain town in Kentucky. There he is drawn into an illicit affair with an impoverished local woman who becomes his star informant. She sees in him her means of escape; instead, it's a ticket to disaster for both of them.
documents.plot: Susan Smith is a drug addict who lives with her abusive boyfriend Cash and two young children in a run-down trailer in Pikeville, Kentucky. She meets an ambitious rookie agent assigned to an FBI field office who recruits Susan as his informant for a high-profile case. Susan believes her bad luck may finally be changing, but as their relationship deepens, so does the danger, setting in motion a downward spiral of jealousy, betrayal and violence resulting in one of the most notorious crimes in FBI history.

documents.title: Final Score
documents.tagline: It's all about to kick off
documents.overview: When a stadium is seized by a group of heavily armed criminals during a major sporting event, an ex-soldier must use all his military skills to save both the daughter of a fallen comrade and the huge crowd unaware of the danger.
documents.plot:
Brothers Arkady and Dimitri Belav have led the revolution in the Russian region of Sakovya for independence. The revolution ultimately leads to Dimitri being killed in an airstrike and Arkady being captured, ending the revolution. After several years, Arkady and his men believe that Dimitri has faked his death, so they torture a man for information on where Dimitri is hiding in London. Meanwhile, in London, former US military soldier Michael Knox visits his late best friend's house to attend the West Ham United football game with his niece, Danni. He had previously served in Afghanistan in an attack team alongside his best friend (who he explains "was like a brother") and was the only survivor of their last mission. Danni is grounded by her mother for delinquent behaviour, but Knox manages to fix the situation, and her mother gives her consent for Knox to take Danni to the football match.
Arriving at the West Ham stadium, Upton Park, Danni expresses her frustration about her dad's death. Knox goes to get them both hot dogs, at which point Danni gets a text from a boy she fancies and decides to join him at his seat. Meanwhile, Arkady and his mercenaries covertly infiltrate the stadium, take over the control room, and initiate a lockdown of the entire stadium. Taking Superintendent Steve Thompson hostage, Arkady threatens Thompson into cooperating by threatening his family. Arkady then has his men blow up all transmission towers across the city to ensure that no communication will be made outside the stadium. Discovering Danni is missing from her seat, Knox seeks help from the cheeky stadium guard, Faisal Khan. Faisal reluctantly assists Knox to the control room. On their way, they run into one of Arkady's men posing as a guard near the lift, who ultimately attacks them, resulting in Knox killing him. Knox finds C-4 explosives in Andrei's jacket. He then uses the only working walkie-talkie to call the police about the situation, but Chief Commander Daniel Steed does not believe him and hangs up. After he kills two other men, Vlad and Anton, Knox brings the latter's body to a balcony and throws him down, smashing into concession stands and thereby summoning the police. Seeing this, Arkady and the other mercenaries infiltrate the news studio and kill the crew. Arkady forces a reporter to read a statement at gunpoint, demanding Dimitri's location, or they will blow up the stadium. As he finishes the statement, Arkady kills the reporter and two others on live television, which Danni's mum sees and prompts her to leave for the stadium. Steed is approached by Agent Cho, who explains that Dimitri fled Russia undercover, underwent plastic surgery, and was given amnesty in London. Cho says that he cannot meet the demands, as handing Dimitri to Arkady will plunge the entire Russian region into chaos, endangering millions. Arkady's team learns the background of Knox and Danni, and they decide to take Danni hostage.

documents.title: Down a Dark Hall
documents.tagline: Welcome to Blackwood. Where lost girls find their way.
documents.overview: Kit, a troubled girl, is sent to the exclusive Blackwood boarding school, where she discovers that only four other female students have been admitted to learn the four pillars of knowledge under the ominous wing of the mysterious headmistress Madame Duret.
documents.plot:
Kit Gordy, a difficult young girl, is sent to the mysterious Blackwood Boarding School after her delinquent behavior becomes too much for her school to handle. When she arrives at Blackwood, Kit meets eccentric headmistress Madame Duret and the school's only other students, four teenage girls with similar behavioral problems (Veronica, Ashley, Sierra, and Izzy). Technology is rarely used, and the girls can only phone their families in the domineering presence of the headmistress. The girls attend a variety of creative and intellectual classes, which begins to draw out unknown talents in them.
Sierra is the first to show a troubling obsession with her work, losing sleep, refusing to eat, and going into odd trances while creating amazing works of art. Ashley writes beautiful poetry and stories that deeply disturb her. Kit and Izzy slowly begin to experience the same bad side effects, saying it was like someone else was using their bodies. Only the belligerent Veronica shows no progress, much to Madame Duret's annoyance. During art class Kit notices that all of Sierra's paintings are signed "TC" and searches the school's library for answers. She realizes that Sierra is recreating paintings by the deceased artist Thomas Cole, and that the others are producing work from other dead geniuses.
Kit convinces Veronica to search the restricted areas of the school, where they come across old student records and more information on the people possessing the girls. When Madame Duret discovers Veronica alone she chains her up in an unused part of the school, explaining that the students are not merely vessels for the dead, but donors, unknowingly sacrificing themselves to be used to continue the careers of famous minds, whom she is able to commune with and channel into the girls' bodies. Kit calls the police and confronts the headmistress about everything. By now Sierra has already died from overwork, and Ashley jumps to her death to stop the possession taking over completely.
While struggling to free Veronica, Kit knocks over some candles, and fire quickly spreads throughout the old building. Izzy succumbs to the beauty of the flames, leaving only Kit and Veronica to escape. Madame Duret is eventually possessed by her former pupils and consumed by the fire. Kit passes out and meets her deceased father, who convinces her to stay and live. She wakes up in the back of an ambulance with her mother by her side.
