documents.title: Angel Has Fallen
documents.tagline: Loyalty is under fire
documents.overview: After a treacherous attack, Secret Service agent Mike Banning is charged with attempting to assassinate President Trumbull. Chased by his own colleagues and the FBI, Banning begins a race against the clock to clear his name.
documents.plot:
Angel Has Fallen is a 2019 American action thriller film directed by Ric Roman Waugh and written by Jeff Nathanson. The movie stars Gerard Butler, Morgan Freeman, Jai Courtney, and Lance Reddick.

The story begins with Mike Banning (Gerard Butler), the former head of the Secret Service, who has retired to a quiet life in Virginia with his wife, Shannon (Molly R. Quinn). However, their peaceful existence is disrupted when Shannon is kidnapped by a group of terrorists led by the ruthless and cunning assassin, Ortega (Lance Reddick).

As Mike frantically searches for his wife, he discovers that she has been taken to the White House, where President James Sawyer (Morgan Freeman) is hosting a high-profile event. The kidnappers demand that the President be killed in exchange for Shannon's safe return.

Mike soon realizes that Ortega is not just any ordinary terrorist but a former Secret Service agent who was thought to have been killed years ago. As Mike navigates the complex web of intrigue and deception, he must also confront his own demons and the personal costs of his past actions as a Secret Service agent.

As the story unfolds, Mike teams up with his old friend and fellow Secret Service agent, Tobin (Jai Courtney), to take down Ortega and rescue Shannon. Along the way, they encounter a range of characters, including a mysterious woman named Rachel (Pati Callahan) who may hold the key to unlocking the truth about Ortega's past.

As the plot thickens, Mike finds himself in a cat-and-mouse game with Ortega, who will stop at nothing to achieve his goals. The action unfolds at breakneck speed, with Mike facing off against Ortega and his henchmen in a series of intense and suspenseful confrontations.

In the end, Mike is able to outsmart Ortega and rescue Shannon, but not before he suffers a serious injury that leaves him questioning his own mortality. As the movie concludes, Mike reflects on the personal costs of his actions as a Secret Service agent and the sacrifices he has made for his country.

Throughout the film, Gerard Butler delivers a strong performance as the rugged and charismatic Mike Banning, bringing depth and nuance to the character. Morgan Freeman provides a sense of gravitas and authority as the President, while Jai Courtney brings a youthful energy to the role of Tobin.

Overall, Angel Has Fallen is a tense and thrilling action movie that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats from start to finish. With its breakneck pace, intricate plot twists, and memorable performances, it's no wonder this film has become a fan favorite among action movie enthusiasts.

documents.title: Mass
documents.overview: Two couples meet for a painful and raw conversation in the aftermath of a violent tragedy.
documents.plot:
Mass is a 2021 American drama film written and directed by Fran Kranz in his directorial debut. Reed Birney, Ann Dowd, Jason Isaacs and Martha Plimpton star as two couples who meet years after a school shooting in which the son of one couple killed the son of the other. Set almost entirely in one room, it premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 30, 2021, and was released by Bleecker Street on October 8, 2021.

Six years after a high school shooting, Jay and Gail Perry, whose son Evan was among those killed, agree to meet Richard and Linda, the parents of the teenage gunman, Hayden, who killed himself after the attack. Their meeting is arranged in a quiet back room of an Episcopal church, with a church worker nervously preparing the space. The couples have met before, during the legal proceedings that followed the shooting, when Jay and Gail spoke harshly to the other parents, and Jay has since become a public advocate for gun control.

After awkward small talk and memories of their sons as young children, the conversation turns to how the tragedy happened. Jay and Gail press for details of Hayden's upbringing beyond what the public already knows. Richard and Linda describe his growing depression after the family moved, his isolation, and the bullying he suffered, and they argue briefly over the influence of violent video games. While noting that schools and therapists failed to act on warning signs, they acknowledge their own guilt at not seeing what their son was becoming.

The talk grows heated. Jay and Gail admit they wanted Richard and Linda to suffer as much as the victims' families did. When the other couple reveal that Hayden had friends who were also bullied, one of whom had access to guns, Jay explodes, suggesting that Hayden was simply a psychopath, before breaking down as he describes how Evan died. Linda tells them about a notebook in which Hayden planned the attack, and explains that she and Richard held a funeral to mourn the boy they had loved before his crime.

When Linda asks to hear about Evan, Gail shares a happy memory of him at twelve and finally forgives Hayden and his parents, and the four hold hands in silence. As they leave, Linda returns to tell Gail how afraid she once was of Hayden. Jay is overcome by the sound of a choir rehearsing nearby. The film was acclaimed for its acting and writing, with 95% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and Dowd received a BAFTA nomination for Best Supporting Actress.

documents.title: Never Look Away
documents.overview: The story of Kurt, a young art student who falls in love with fellow student, Ellie. Ellie’s father, Professor Seeband, a famous doctor, is dismayed at his daughter’s choice of boyfriend, and vows to destroy the relationship. What neither of them knows is that their lives are already connected through a terrible crime Seeband committed decades ago.
documents.plot: German artist Kurt Barnert has escaped East Germany and now lives in West Germany, but is tormented by his childhood under the Nazis and the GDR regime.

documents.title: In the Fade
documents.overview: Katja's life collapses after a senseless act impacts her. After a time of mourning and injustice, she seeks revenge.
documents.plot:
In the Fade (German: Aus dem Nichts) is a 2017 German drama thriller written and directed by Fatih Akin. Diane Kruger stars as Katja Şekerci, a German woman whose Kurdish husband and young son are killed in a bombing carried out by neo-Nazis, with Denis Moschitto as her lawyer, Numan Acar as her husband, Johannes Krisch as the defense attorney and Ulrich Tukur. The film competed for the Palme d'Or at the 2017 Cannes Film Festival, where Kruger won the award for Best Actress, in her first major German-language role.

Nuri Şekerci, a Kurdish-German man who served time in prison for drug dealing and studied business while inside, now lives a happy life in Hamburg with his German wife, Katja, and their six-year-old son, Rocco, running a small office. One day Katja leaves Rocco with Nuri while she spends the afternoon with a friend. As she leaves, she warns a young blonde woman who has parked a new bicycle in front of the office that it might be stolen if she does not lock it. Returning that evening, Katja finds the street cordoned off: a nail bomb has exploded, killing Nuri and Rocco.

Katja tells the police about the woman with the bicycle and becomes convinced the attack was the work of neo-Nazis, but investigators focus on Nuri's past and possible links to drug traffickers. Overwhelmed by grief, Katja turns to drugs and attempts suicide, but she is stopped by news that suspects have been arrested: a young neo-Nazi couple, André and Edda Möller, whose own father reported his son to the police. The trial in the film's second part becomes a painful ordeal, as the defense attacks Katja's credibility because of her drug use and a Greek neo-Nazi provides the couple with an alibi. When the court acquits them for lack of evidence, Katja, abandoned by the justice system, follows the couple to Greece and contemplates taking justice into her own hands.

In the Fade received generally favorable reviews, with a 77 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus praised Kruger's ability to carry the film, though some felt it did not match her remarkable work. It won the Golden Globe Award for Best Foreign Language Film and was shortlisted for the Academy Award. The film was inspired in part by the murders committed by the National Socialist Underground in Germany.

documents.title: Victoria & Abdul
documents.tagline: History's most unlikely friendship.
documents.overview: Queen Victoria strikes up an unlikely friendship with a young Indian clerk named Abdul Karim.
documents.plot:
Abdul Karim, a young prison clerk from a Muslim, Urdu-speaking family in Agra, British India, is instructed to travel to Britain for Queen Victoria's Golden Jubilee in 1888 to present her with a mohur, a gold coin that has been minted as a token of appreciation from British-ruled India.
The Queen, lonely and tired of her fawning courtiers, develops an interest in and then a friendship with Abdul. She spends time with him alone and gives him a bejewelled locket with her photograph. She promotes him to be her Munshi and asks him to teach her Urdu and the Quran. She in fact learns Urdu for 14 years. When Victoria discovers he is married, she has him bring his wife to England. His wife and his mother-in-law both wear black burqas, much to the consternation of the household—and the fascination of Victoria.
As Victoria's interest in India grows, she has the Durbar Room built at her Isle of Wight home of Osborne House for state functions. It is elaborately and intricately decorated, with a carpet from Agra, formal portraits of renowned Indians, a replica of the Peacock Throne and carvings by Bhai Ram Singh.
While Victoria treats Abdul as a son, his preferment is resented by her household and inner circle, including her son, Bertie, and the prime minister, Lord Salisbury. The household plots to undermine their relationship, hoping that Abdul will be sent home. When Victoria embarrasses herself by recounting Abdul's one-sided account of the Indian Rebellion of 1857 to the court, Victoria's faith and trust in him are shaken. She decides he must return to India, but soon changes her mind and asks him to stay.
The prime minister is adamant that the royal household must be rid of Abdul. They research his family background in India and present Victoria with a dossier showing that his family is more ordinary and poor than Abdul claimed. When Victoria insists that her doctor examine Abdul to learn why his wife has not become pregnant, he discovers that Abdul has gonorrhea. He expects the Queen will dismiss Abdul in disgust, but Victoria remains loyal to him, orders his medical treatment and admonishes her courtiers for plotting against him. She announces her intention to give Abdul a knighthood.
Eventually, the household decides that Victoria must break with Abdul. If not, they all will resign and have Victoria declared insane. When Victoria is told, she angrily summons her family and the entire household and demands that anyone who wishes to give up their place should step forward. When no-one does, she says she has decided against making Abdul a knight. She will instead include him in her next honours list as a Commander of the Royal Victorian Order.
When Victoria falls ill, she urges Abdul to return to India while she can still protect him and warns him that the court will turn on him after her death. Abdul insists that he will stay until her death.

documents.title: Kill Switch
documents.tagline: Worlds will collide
documents.overview: A pilot battles to save his family and the planet after an experiment for unlimited energy goes wrong.
documents.plot:
Kill Switch, also known as Redivider, is a 2017 science fiction film and the feature directorial debut of Tim Smit, from a screenplay by Charlie Kindinger and Omid Nooshin. Dan Stevens stars as Will Porter, a former NASA pilot turned physicist who is sent into a parallel world to undo the damage caused by tapping an unlimited source of quantum energy, and who must choose which of two Earths will survive. Bérénice Marlohe, Tygo Gernandt, Charity Wakefield, Bas Keijzer, Mike Libanon and Mike Reus co-star.

In the near future, Porter is recruited by Alterplex, a power company that has built an enormous tower drawing on limitless quantum energy. The energy comes from a mirror version of Earth known as "the Echo", which was never supposed to harbour life; a malfunction, however, created a true duplicate planet, populated and with a tower of its own. As the Alterplex tower siphons off its power, the Echo is plagued by strange gravitational anomalies and unexplained deaths, and the link between the worlds now threatens to destroy both within less than a day unless one of them is eliminated. Porter is dispatched into the Echo carrying a cube-shaped device called the Redivider, which he has been told will rebalance the flow of energy between the two universes and restore order. Once there, he discovers that the device is in fact a kill switch designed to annihilate the Echo, leaving him to decide which world must be sacrificed so the other can live. The Echo's armed forces are aware of his mission and hunt him, seeking to capture or kill him, while a band of anti-tower rebels wages its own war against the soldiers guarding the towers.

Stevens plays Porter, with Marlohe as Abigail Vos, Gernandt as Michael, Wakefield as Mia Porter, Gijs Scholten van Aschat as Reynard, Keijzer as Bektman, Libanon as Hugo and Reus as Dr. Klintsen. The casting of Stevens and Marlohe, with Smit directing, was announced in February 2016, and Aaron Ryder produced through FilmNation Entertainment; Don Diablo wrote, scored and performed the theme song, "Echoes". Saban Films acquired distribution rights in February 2017 and released the film theatrically on June 16, 2017, followed by a video-on-demand release from Lionsgate Home Entertainment on August 22. Critics were largely negative, giving it a 9% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 31, and it earned only about $163,000 worldwide at the box office, with home video sales adding roughly $140,000.

documents.title: Apostle
documents.tagline: Your god can't help you.
documents.overview: In 1905, a man travels to a remote island in search of his missing sister who has been kidnapped by a mysterious religious cult.
documents.plot:
In 1905, Thomas Richardson travels to a remote Welsh island to rescue his sister, Jennifer, who has been kidnapped and held for ransom by a mysterious cult led by Malcolm Howe. Posing as a convert, Thomas encounters Howe, who founded the cult with two other convicts, Frank and Quinn. They claim that the barren island was rendered fertile through blood sacrifice. Thomas discovers Frank's son Jeremy and Quinn's daughter Ffion sneaking home after a tryst. He forces Jeremy to admit that Jennifer was kidnapped for ransom, as the cult does not have the resources to pay for the continuous animal sacrifices needed to maintain the island's fertility.
One of the newcomers attempts to assassinate Malcolm, but Thomas intervenes and is wounded. The same night, Malcolm parades Jennifer through the village, claiming she will be killed if her co-conspirator does not come forward. Thomas flees from an old woman who chases him, and escapes to a beach cave covered in markings, depicting a deity. Malcolm visits a barn where the old woman, who is in fact the island's deity, is imprisoned in tree roots; he reprimands her for appearing to Thomas before feeding her his blood, causing the vegetation imprisoning her to bloom. Thomas tells Malcolm's daughter Andrea that he was a Christian missionary who was persecuted in Beijing during the Boxer Rebellion for introducing Christianity to China, and lost his faith after his god failed to intervene. She takes him to a shack in a wheat field to hide.
Ffion reveals to Jeremy that she is pregnant, and the pair make plans to elope. Infuriated, Quinn mutilates Ffion in a forced abortion. Jeremy stabs Quinn, who frames Jeremy for Ffion's murder, and uses a "purification" ritual to publicly murder him by hollowing out the back of his head. Quinn calls Malcolm a false prophet and demands that he prove himself by executing Thomas. Frank, enraged by the death of his son, attacks Quinn, enabling Thomas to escape.
Frank and Thomas flee and arrive at the barn where The Goddess is being held. Frank enters, intent on killing The Goddess, but is killed by a masked figure, The Grinder, whom Thomas witnesses force-feeding Jeremy's body to The Goddess. Sneaking past, he finds Jennifer alive but strung up in a sack. As he releases her, he is knocked unconscious by the Grinder. He finds himself tethered to a meat-grinding table by hooks embedded into his hands and legs. He escapes and kills The Grinder.
Quinn reveals to a captive Jennifer and Andrea that he imprisoned The Goddess after he and Malcolm realized her powers and that he plans to repeatedly impregnate them and use their offspring as blood sacrifices. The Goddess shows Thomas her history with the cult, and begs him to set her free; he grants her wish by unexpectedly immolating her. The village also catches fire while villagers flee to boats. Thomas, Andrea, and Jennifer overpower and kill Quinn, with Thomas sustaining heavy stab wounds.

documents.title: Halloween
documents.tagline: Face Your Fate.
documents.overview: Laurie Strode comes to her final confrontation with Michael Myers, the masked figure who has haunted her since she narrowly escaped his killing spree on Halloween night four decades ago.
documents.plot:
Halloween is a 2018 American slasher film directed by David Gordon Green, who co-wrote it with Jeff Fradley and Danny McBride. The eleventh installment in the Halloween series, it is a direct sequel to John Carpenter's 1978 original that disregards every other film in the franchise. Jamie Lee Curtis reprises her role as Laurie Strode, and James Jude Courtney plays Michael Myers, with Nick Castle returning to the role for a cameo; Judy Greer, Andi Matichak, Will Patton and Haluk Bilginer co-star.

On October 29, 2018, Michael, confined at Smith's Grove psychiatric hospital for four decades, is about to be transferred to another facility. True crime podcasters Aaron Korey and Dana Haines visit him. In Haddonfield, Laurie still lives in fear, drinking heavily inside her fortified house. Her daughter, Karen, was taken from her by the state at age twelve and remains estranged, while Laurie's granddaughter, Allyson, tries to stay close to her. On the night of October 30, the transfer bus crashes and Michael escapes. The next day he murders the podcasters at his sister Judith's grave, kills a mechanic for his overalls and recovers his mask.

That Halloween night, Allyson leaves a party after finding her boyfriend cheating; Michael kills her best friend. Laurie and Deputy Frank Hawkins, who arrested Michael in 1978, respond to the scene, and Laurie shoots Michael before he escapes. Karen and her husband, Ray, are taken to Laurie's house for protection. Hawkins subdues Michael and tries to kill him, but Michael's psychiatrist, Dr. Ranbir Sartain, who secretly arranged Michael's escape to study him in the wild, attacks Hawkins and drives toward Laurie's home with Michael and Allyson in the back seat. Michael wakes, kills Sartain, the officers guarding the house and Ray. In the final confrontation, he stabs Laurie and throws her from a balcony, but when he looks down her body has vanished, echoing their first encounter. Karen shoots him, and the three women trap him in the basement safe room and set the house on fire. A post-credits scene suggests Michael survived.

The film premiered in the Midnight Madness section of the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2018 and was released on October 19. It grossed $259.9 million worldwide. Critics responded favorably, with 79% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 67, praising its return to basic but effective ingredients.

documents.title: Annette
documents.tagline: As dangerous, as intense, as love.
documents.overview: The story of Henry, a stand-up comedian with a fierce sense of humour and Ann, a singer of international renown. In the spotlight, they are the perfect couple, healthy, happy, and glamourous. The birth of their first child, Annette, a mysterious girl with an exceptional destiny, will change their lives.
documents.plot: In present-day Los Angeles, controversial stand-up comedian Henry McHenry and internationally renowned opera singer Ann Defrasnoux form the façade of a happy couple in the spotlight. Ann gives birth to a baby girl named Annette, who possesses an exceptional gift that will change all of their lives forever.

documents.title: Megan Leavey
documents.tagline: Based on the true story of a marine's best friend.
documents.overview: The true story of Marine Corporal Megan Leavey, who forms a powerful bond with an aggressive combat dog, Rex. While deployed in Iraq, the two complete more than 100 missions and save countless lives, until an IED explosion puts their faithfulness to the test.

documents.title: Bohemian Rhapsody
documents.tagline: Fearless lives forever
documents.overview: Singer Freddie Mercury, guitarist Brian May, drummer Roger Taylor and bass guitarist John Deacon take the music world by storm when they form the rock 'n' roll band Queen in 1970. Hit songs become instant classics. When Mercury's increasingly wild lifestyle starts to spiral out of control, Queen soon faces its greatest challenge yet – finding a way to keep the band together amid the success and excess.
documents.plot:
Bohemian Rhapsody is a biographical drama film that tells the story of the life of Queen's lead vocalist, Freddie Mercury. The film stars Rami Malek as Mercury and follows his journey from his early days as a musician to the band's rise to fame.

The film begins with Freddie Mercury (Rami Malek) growing up in Zanzibar, Tanzania, where he is born Farrokh Bulsara. He moves to India with his family at a young age and later attends art college in London, where he discovers his passion for music. Mercury forms a band called Ibex, which eventually becomes Queen.

The film then cuts to the early days of Queen, with Mercury meeting Brian May (Gwilym Lee) and Roger Taylor (Ben Hardy). The three musicians form a strong bond and begin to develop their unique sound. They are later joined by John Deacon (Joe Mazzello), who completes the classic lineup.

As Queen gains popularity, they start to tour and perform in front of large crowds. Mercury's charisma and stage presence quickly make him a fan favorite. The film depicts the band's struggles with fame, including their tumultuous relationship with their record label, EMI.

One of the most pivotal moments in the film is Queen's performance at Live Aid in 1985. The band takes the stage to perform "Bohemian Rhapsody," which becomes an instant classic. The film captures the energy and excitement of the event, as well as Mercury's emotional response to performing his iconic song.

Throughout the film, Malek delivers a critically acclaimed performance as Mercury, capturing the singer's flamboyant personality, wit, and vulnerability. The supporting cast, including Lucy Boynton as Mercury's girlfriend Mary Austin, also deliver strong performances.

As Queen's popularity continues to grow, Mercury becomes increasingly reclusive and struggles with his personal life. He is openly gay in a time when it was not widely accepted, which puts him at odds with his record label and the public.

The film's climax depicts Queen's performance at Live Aid, as well as their subsequent tour of Japan. The film ends with Mercury's final performance with Queen, which takes place on November 24, 1991, just months before his death from complications related to AIDS.

Overall, Bohemian Rhapsody is a triumphant and emotional tribute to Freddie Mercury's life and legacy. The film features stunning performances, impressive music sequences, and a gripping narrative that captures the highs and lows of Queen's incredible journey.

documents.title: Sorry to Bother You
documents.tagline: Destiny Is Calling
documents.overview: In an alternate present-day version of Oakland, black telemarketer Cassius Green discovers a magical key to professional success – which propels him into a macabre universe.
documents.plot:
In a dystopian near future, Cassius "Cash" Green and his artist girlfriend Detroit live in the garage of Cash's uncle Sergio. Struggling to pay rent, Cash gets a job as a telemarketer for RegalView. He struggles with customers until his older co-worker Langston teaches him how to use his "white voice" and adopt a blithe, affluent persona during calls, at which Cash excels.
Cash's co-worker Squeeze forms a union and recruits Cash, Detroit, and their friend Sal. When Cash participates in a protest, he expects to be fired but is instead promoted to an elite "Power Caller" position within the company. In the luxurious Power Caller suite, the lead Power Caller known as Mr. _______ tells Cash to always use his white voice. He learns that RegalView secretly sells military arms and cheap labor from the megacorporation WorryFree, through which employees sign lifetime contracts to work and be housed in factories, i.e. slave labor.
Though Cash is initially uncomfortable with the job, he is celebrated at work and can now afford a new apartment and a flashy car while paying off Sergio's house, keeping him from joining WorryFree in the process. Through his newfound success, he initially improves his relationship with Detroit and boosts his sex life significantly. He stops participating in the union push and Detroit quits her RegalView job to avoid conflicting loyalties between the two, while secretly participating in the Left Eye Faction, an anti-WorryFree activist group. She eventually breaks up with Cash, arguing that his immoral job has changed him, while he insists he has the right to be proud of his success.
As Cash is escorted through the union's picket line one morning, a picketer throws a can of soda at his head and injures him. Footage of the incident becomes a popular Internet meme, and even the woman who threw the can profits from it when she signs a sponsorship with the soda brand she threw. Cash attends Detroit's art exhibit and artistic performance uninvited, at which she uses a white voice of her own. He tries to stop the event, but that only motivates Detroit to kick him out, and she later has "everything but sex" with Squeeze.
Cash is invited to a debaucherous party with WorryFree CEO Steve Lift, where he is goaded into rapping for the predominantly white guests. Later, in a private meeting, Steve offers Cash a powdered substance which Cash snorts, believing it is cocaine. Cash looks for the bathroom but takes a wrong turn and discovers a shackled half-horse, half-human hybrid who begs him for help. Steve explains that WorryFree plans to make their workers stronger, more obedient, and more profitable by transforming them into human-horse "Equisapiens" through snorting a powder that modifies their DNA. Cash fears that he just ingested the substance, but Steve assures him it was cocaine. Cash refuses an offer of $100 million to become an Equisapien for five years to act as a false revolutionary figure to keep the employees in line.

documents.title: Bumblebee
documents.tagline: Every hero has a beginning.
documents.overview: On the run in the year 1987, Bumblebee finds refuge in a junkyard in a small Californian beach town. Charlie, on the cusp of turning 18 and trying to find her place in the world, discovers Bumblebee, battle-scarred and broken.  When Charlie revives him, she quickly learns this is no ordinary yellow VW bug.
documents.plot:
Bumblebee is a 2018 American science fiction action film directed by Travis Knight and produced by Paramount Pictures. The movie takes place in 1987, during the height of the Transformers franchise's popularity.

The story begins with Charlie Watson (Hailee Steinfeld), a high school student who lives on the outskirts of a small town in California. Charlie is struggling to cope with her mother's death in a car accident and her father's absence due to his work as an oil rig worker. She spends most of her time alone, tinkering with cars and daydreaming about adventure.

One night, while out running from her troubles, Charlie stumbles upon a damaged Chevrolet Camaro that has crash-landed on the outskirts of town. As she approaches the car, it transforms into Bumblebee, an Autobot scout sent to Earth to protect its secrets from the Decepticons.

Initially, Charlie is frightened by the giant robot, but as she observes Bumblebee's behavior, she realizes that it is not a threat. Instead, she begins to form a bond with the Autobot, and they start to communicate through a series of beeps and chirps.

As Charlie spends more time with Bumblebee, she learns about its mission to find its long-lost friend, Jazz (Josh Duhamel), who has been captured by the Decepticons. The Autobots have sent Bumblebee to rescue Jazz, but it needs Charlie's help to navigate the human world and evade the Decepticon forces.

The plot thickens as Charlie becomes embroiled in a series of events that put her life at risk. She is pursued by the Decepticons, led by Shatter (Angus Macfadyen), who will stop at nothing to capture Bumblebee and exploit its advanced technology.

As Charlie and Bumblebee work together, they develop a strong bond, with Charlie learning about the Autobot's values of loyalty, friendship, and sacrifice. In return, Bumblebee learns about human emotions and experiences, which helps it to better understand its mission.

The movie culminates in an action-packed showdown between Charlie, Bumblebee, and the Decepticons. With the help of her father, who has been hiding a secret of his own, Charlie is able to outsmart the Decepticons and help Bumblebee rescue Jazz.

In the end, Charlie says goodbye to Bumblebee as it departs to continue its mission, but not before they share a heartfelt moment that leaves Charlie with a newfound sense of purpose and belonging. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that even in the darkest times, there is always the possibility for connection and redemption.

Overall, Bumblebee is a heartwarming and action-packed film that explores themes of friendship, loyalty, and self-discovery. With its blend of humor, adventure, and sci-fi excitement, it has become a beloved entry in the Transformers franchise.

documents.title: The Case for Christ
documents.tagline: One man's journey to solve the biggest mystery of all times
documents.overview: Based on the true story of an award-winning investigative journalist -- and avowed atheist -- who applies his well-honed journalistic and legal skills to disprove the newfound Christian faith of his wife... with unexpected, life-altering results.
documents.plot:
In 1980, Lee Strobel is an atheist journalist and investigative reporter for the Chicago Tribune. He and his wife Leslie have a daughter named Alison and are expecting their second child. After getting a very special recognition, Lee and his family go out for dinner to celebrate, and Alison chokes on a piece of candy. One of the patrons, a nurse named Alfie, intervenes and saves Alison. She credits the event to God's will, which Leslie takes to heart.
Leslie and Alfie become friends and start attending a Christian church together. Irritated, Lee unsuccessfully tries to dissuade Leslie. Due to advice from his mentor, Lee sets out to find evidence that the resurrection of Jesus did not happen. Meanwhile, Leslie gives birth to a son, Kyle.
Lee starts gathering information and evidence. Next, he tries to prove that the witnesses were hypnotized, but a psychologist proves him wrong. Lee then tries to gather evidence that Jesus may have not actually died on the Cross, or was taken off, but again, a physician proves him wrong, saying Jesus had to have died on the Cross.
Meanwhile, Lee's estranged father tries to reconcile with him, but Lee brushes him off. His father dies soon after, and then Lee learns that his father truly loved him, which surprises Lee.
Simultaneously with Lee's pursuit to disprove the resurrection of Jesus, he is also investigating a case of the shooting of a police officer. At first, it looks like the convicted man is guilty and an informant for a gang, but Lee proves that the cop shot himself with a secret gun disguised as a pen, and the convict is freed.
Lee tries to get more evidence for his religious investigation, but his mentor explains that whether he chooses to believe or not believe, the last part of proving Jesus' real existence is faith. When a colleague gives him a speech, Lee decides to take the leap of faith and believe. When he tells Leslie about it, they have a happy reconciliation and pray together.

documents.title: Show Dogs
documents.tagline: Unleashed and undercover
documents.overview: Max, a macho, solitary Rottweiler police dog is ordered to go undercover as a primped show dog in a prestigious Dog Show, along with his human partner, to avert a disaster from happening.
documents.plot:
Show Dogs is a 2018 buddy cop comedy directed by Raja Gosnell from a screenplay by Max Botkin and Marc Hyman, mixing live action with talking animals. Filming began on November 28, 2016, at Pinewood Studio Wales in Great Britain, with further scenes shot on location in Las Vegas. The film was released in the United States on May 18, 2018, and reached DVD and Blu-ray that August.

Max, a tough Rottweiler serving as a police dog, tries to rescue Ling-Li, a baby giant panda that an animal smuggling ring is preparing to sell. In doing so he accidentally ruins an FBI sting run by his human partner, Frank, who blames the dog for letting the criminals escape. Forced to cooperate despite their mutual dislike, the two go undercover as a show dog and his handler at the prestigious Canini Invitational dog show in Las Vegas, hoping to unmask the smugglers from inside the competition.

Ludacris voices Max and Will Arnett plays Frank, with Natasha Lyonne as Mattie and Omar Chaparro as Señor Gabriel. The voice cast also includes Stanley Tucci as the Papillon Philippe, Jordin Sparks as Daisy, an Australian Shepherd, Gabriel Iglesias as the Pug Sprinkles, Shaquille O'Neal as the Komondor Karma, RuPaul as Persephone and Alan Cumming as Dante.

Reviews were negative. Rotten Tomatoes gave it a 16% approval rating and Metacritic a score of 31, although CinemaScore audiences awarded an A−. Christy Lemire gave it half a star, Peter Hartlaub gave it none, and Mark Kermode later named it the worst film of 2018, while The Hollywood Reporter was more forgiving of its self-aware script. Shortly after release, critics and parents' groups objected to a subplot in which Max must let a judge touch his genitals and is told to go to his "happy place", arguing that it normalized child grooming. Botkin said the script had been heavily rewritten by other writers, and the distributor Global Road Entertainment apologized, removed two scenes and sent a revised cut to theaters for the second weekend. The British Board of Film Classification considered the scene non-sexual and the US concerns a misinterpretation. Made for $5.5 million, the film grossed $40 million worldwide.

documents.title: Loving Pablo
documents.tagline: A gangster. A princess. The true story of a most unlikely love affair.
documents.overview: The film chronicles the rise and fall of the world's most feared drug lord Pablo Escobar and his volatile love affair with Colombia's most famous journalist Virginia Vallejo throughout a reign of terror that tore a country apart.
documents.plot: Between 1981 and 1987, Colombian drug lord Pablo Escobar had a romantic relationship with the journalist and the television presenter, Virginia Vallejo.

documents.title: The Miracle Season
documents.tagline: Every point. Every game. Every match. Was for her....
documents.overview: After the tragic death of star volleyball player Caroline "Line" Found, a team of dispirited high school girls must band together under the guidance of their tough-love coach in hopes of winning the state championship!
documents.plot:
Caroline "Line" Found is the star volleyball player on the Iowa City West High School volleyball team and well-loved by members of the community. With Line as the captain, the Trojans have been undefeated and everyone in the city has high hopes for them to win the championship against their long-time rival, City High. During a party at her house, Line sneaks off to visit her mother Ellyn, who is being treated for cancer in a hospital. Line is killed in a moped accident, leaving the entire community in mourning. At Line's wake, Ellyn insists on walking to her daughter's casket to pay her respects; Ellyn dies from cancer days after the wake, leaving her husband and Line's father Ernie grieving over the loss of his wife and his daughter.
The Trojans' coach, Kathy "Brez" Bresnahan, continues to hold volleyball practice. She asks Line's best friend, Kelley Fliehler, to return to the team, saying Line would have wanted them to continue. Kelley initially refuses, but Brez persuades her. The Trojans forfeited their most recent match and Kelley encourages the entire school to continue for Line.
West High struggles in practice and loses their first game badly, still discouraged by Line's death. Brez runs the team through grueling drills and names Kelley the new captain. Kelley initially struggles in the role, but improves as the weeks go by. The team begins to win and is motivated to win the state championship for Line. They need to win the fourteen remaining games to be eligible for the state championship, which they do.
Before the tournament begins, Kelley receives a gift from Line's father, that encourages her not just to play for Line, but to "Live Like Line". At West High, Kelley and boyfriend Alex paint the windows to read "Live Like Line". T-shirts with the catchphrase are given out to players, staff, and fans. The Trojans win the quarter-final game with ease, but struggle to win their semi-final game. They move on to the championship against City High, who are heavily favored to win. Before the game, Brez gives a tribute to Line, deciding not to have a moment of silence, but encourages the crowd to meet someone new, as Line always was kind to everyone. City takes the lead early, but West ties the score and forces the fifth and final set, which the Trojans win. As the crowd cheers, "Sweet Caroline" plays in honor of Line and Kelley holds Line's picture up high and proud.
During the closing credits, images, videos, and footage show the real life Caroline Found and her family, Kelley Fliehler, Kathy Bresnahan, and the Iowa West High volleyball team. On-screen subtitles show how Caroline Found's death inspired the real Iowa West High volleyball team to repeat their win for the 2011 Iowa State Championship. The Founds climbed Mount Monadnock. Over 4,000 students from across Iowa attended Line's funeral. Kathy "Brez" Bresnahan was voted National Coach of the Year for 2011; she retired from coaching in 2014 but remains in contact with the 2011 team.

documents.overview: A young boy finds a powerful otherworldly weapon, which he uses to save his older adoptive brother from a crew of thugs. Before long, the two of them are also pursued by federal agents and mysterious mercenaries aiming to reclaim their asset.

documents.title: Ghostbusters: Afterlife
documents.tagline: Discover the past. Protect the future.
documents.overview: When a single mom and her two kids arrive in a small town, they begin to discover their connection to the original Ghostbusters and the secret legacy their grandfather left behind.
documents.plot:
Ghostbusters: Afterlife is a 2021 supernatural comedy film directed by Jason Reitman, written by Gil Kenan and Greg Russo, and produced by Ivan Reitman, Dan Aykroyd, and Chris Columbus. The movie serves as a direct sequel to the original Ghostbusters (1984) and Ghostbusters II (1989), ignoring the events of the 2016 reboot.

The story takes place in 2021, 30 years after the events of the first two films. We meet Callie Spengler (Carrie Coon), a single mother who lives on a farm with her son Trevor (Finn Wolfhard) and granddaughter Phoebe (Mckenna Grace). The family is struggling to cope with the loss of their father, Raymond Stantz (Dan Aykroyd), who was one of the original Ghostbusters.

One day, Callie receives an unexpected visit from a mysterious woman named Phoebe's grandmother, Janine Melnitz (Annie Potts), who reveals that she is Phoebe's mother and has been keeping her identity a secret. Janine informs Phoebe about her family's history as Ghostbusters and the reason for their disappearance.

As Phoebe begins to uncover the truth about her family's past, she discovers an old proton pack in the attic of her grandfather's house, which leads her on a journey to find the lost city of Stay Puft, where her father and his team were last seen. Along the way, she meets Trevor, who becomes her ally in uncovering the secrets of their family's legacy.

As they delve deeper into the mystery, Phoebe and Trevor encounter a new generation of Ghostbusters, led by Dr. Zoey Frankel (Mckenna Grace), who is determined to revive the original team's work. Together, they face off against a powerful entity known as Gozer, an ancient Sumerian deity that was defeated by the original Ghostbusters.

Throughout the film, Reitman pays homage to the original Ghostbusters while introducing new characters and themes. The movie explores the idea of legacy, family, and the power of tradition. The special effects are impressive, with a blend of practical and CGI elements that bring the supernatural world to life.

Overall, Ghostbusters: Afterlife is a heartwarming and entertaining film that honors the spirit of the original while introducing a new generation to the beloved franchise.

documents.title: Cargo

documents.overview: After being infected in the wake of a violent pandemic and with only 48 hours to live, a father struggles to find a new home for his baby daughter.

documents.title: Beach Rats
documents.overview: An aimless teenager on the outer edges of Brooklyn struggles to escape his bleak home life and navigate questions of self-identity, as he balances his time between his delinquent friends, a potential new girlfriend, and older men he meets online.
documents.plot:
Frankie is an aimless 19-year-old Brooklynite who spends his days hanging out and getting high with his macho friends as an escape from his troubled home life. His family includes his little sister and a mother who is mostly occupied with caring for his terminally ill father. At night, Frankie cruises Brooklyn Boys, a webcam site for gay men, but partially obscures his face with a hat.
When Frankie and his friends are at the Coney Island boardwalk watching fireworks, he catches the attentions of local girl Simone. Simone accompanies Frankie back to his place and tries to initiate sex with him, asking, "Am I pretty?" Frankie cannot perform and tries to make small talk instead, mocking and imitating her question. Insulted, Simone leaves. A few days later, Frankie and his friends are at the beach when they spot Simone with another guy. Frankie goes to apologize to Simone for his behavior the other night, and she tentatively forgives him. Meanwhile, Frankie uses the chat site to arrange hookups, particularly with older men as they are less likely to run into his friends and give away his double life. When a male partner asks about his penchant for older men, Frankie replies, "I don't really know what I like."
Frankie suffers a loss when his father succumbs to his terminal cancer. Frankie takes his father's pills, which he and his friends have been abusing. On a day out with Simone, Frankie casually asks her if she has ever made out with a girl. Simone replies she has, and makes an offhand comment that it is "hot" when girls make out, but when guys make out, it is "gay". That night, Frankie forces himself to have sex with her. Later, after a hookup with a gay man at a motel, Frankie is asked about his orientation. Frankie says he is not gay and reasons he has a girlfriend.
On a night out with his friends and Simone, they take drugs and party but when Frankie sees that the man from the motel works as a bartender he panics, he attempts to have sex with Simone but can't bring himself to do it and leaves her aggressively, he causes a fight on the dance floor and storms out. He meets up with an older man after. Much to his liking, when he gets home he is questioned by his mother for his behavior.
Frankie tries to apologize to Simone, who rejects him, telling him he needs to work on his personal issues and they stop seeing each other. Frankie runs into his friends on his way to meet with a guy his age named Jeremy. His friends, running out on their drug supply ask Frankie to come up with a plan and he tells them he uses a gay dating site to meet with men who have weed, his friends don't take him seriously but tag along with him when he tells them Jeremy is bringing weed with him. But when Jeremy meets them, he becomes wary of Frankie's crew and leaves. His friends insist that he finds another guy and they go back to Frankie's home, where he shows them the site and attempts to talk to men.

documents.title: Lords of Chaos
documents.tagline: Based on truth and lies
documents.overview: A teenager's quest to launch Norwegian Black Metal in Oslo in the 1990s results in a very violent outcome.
documents.plot:
Lords of Chaos is a 2018 biographical horror film directed by Jonas Åkerlund, who co-wrote the screenplay with Dennis Magnusson. Adapted from the 1998 book of the same name by Michael Moynihan and Didrik Søderlind, it offers a fictionalised account of the early 1990s Norwegian black metal scene, told from the perspective of guitarist Øystein "Euronymous" Aarseth, co-founder of the band Mayhem. Rory Culkin plays Euronymous, with Emory Cohen as Varg Vikernes, Jack Kilmer as Per "Dead" Ohlin, Sky Ferreira as Ann-Marit and Valter Skarsgård as the drummer Faust. Åkerlund was himself a former drummer of the Swedish band Bathory.

The story begins in 1984, when the young Euronymous forms Mayhem in Norway, recruiting bandmates and eventually the Swedish vocalist known as Dead. Dead's self-harm and macabre stage antics help build the band's extreme reputation. At one concert the group meets Kristian, a shy and awkward fan whom Euronymous initially treats with condescension, and Euronymous begins a relationship with Ann-Marit from the local metal community. When Dead takes his own life, Euronymous photographs the body rather than calling the police and turns the tragedy into part of the band's dark mythology.

Kristian reinvents himself as Varg Vikernes, the frontman of the one-man project Burzum, and gravitates toward Euronymous's record shop, Helvete, which becomes the centre of a small circle of musicians determined to prove they are the most extreme. What begins as provocative posturing escalates into real violence, including a series of church burnings and a murder, while a bitter rivalry develops between Euronymous, who cultivates an image he does not fully live up to, and the increasingly fanatical Varg. The conflict culminates in the 1993 killing of Euronymous.

The film presents its subjects as alienated young men caught up in their own myth-making, and it combines dark humour with brutally graphic depictions of violence, which drew criticism from some members of the real scene who disputed its accuracy.

Lords of Chaos premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in 2018. On Rotten Tomatoes about 73 percent of critics' reviews are positive, with the consensus describing it as a grimly compelling dramatisation of a music scene whose nihilistic aesthetic spilled over into real-life tragedy.

documents.title: Fullmetal Alchemist
documents.overview: Two alchemist brothers go on a quest for the Philosopher's Stone after an attempt to revive their dead mother goes horribly wrong.
documents.plot:
Fullmetal Alchemist (Hagane no Renkinjutsushi) is a Japanese science fantasy action film of 2017 directed by Fumihiko Sori and adapted from Hiromu Arakawa's manga. Ryosuke Yamada stars as Edward Elric, with Atomu Mizuishi as his brother Alphonse, Tsubasa Honda as their friend Winry Rockbell, Dean Fujioka as Colonel Roy Mustang, Ryuta Sato as Maes Hughes and Yasuko Matsuyuki as Lust. Warner Bros. released it in Japan on 1 December 2017.

In the land of Amestris, Edward and Alphonse grow up in a rural town with their mother Trisha. When she dies of illness, the boys attempt the forbidden art of human transmutation to bring her back, and pay the price of equivalent exchange: Edward loses his left leg and Alphonse is pulled into the Gate of Truth. Edward gives up his right arm to recover his brother's soul and bind it to a suit of armor, and Winry's family fits him with automail prostheses. Recruited by Mustang, Edward becomes the youngest State Alchemist, the Fullmetal Alchemist, and the brothers begin searching for the legendary Philosopher's Stone that could restore their bodies.

Years later, Major General Hakuro introduces the teenage brothers to Shou Tucker, who earned his state license by creating a talking chimera. Tucker sends them to Dr. Tim Marcoh, a former stone-maker in hiding, who is killed by the assassin Lust. Returning to Tucker's home, the brothers discover that he has fused his little daughter Nina with the family dog to keep his credentials; they have him arrested, but not before he sows a bitter quarrel between them. Hughes finds something alarming in Marcoh's notes and is murdered by Lust's partner Envy.

Marcoh's research leads Edward to the secret Fifth Laboratory, where the now-deranged Tucker is holding Alphonse and Winry. There Edward learns that Philosopher's Stones are made from human lives and breaks down. Lust kills Tucker, revealing herself as a homunculus, and Hakuro, her ally, admits the military made stones from human captives; he unleashes an army of artificial Mannequin Soldiers powered by stones, which kill him. As the army destroys them, Mustang kills Lust and gives Edward the stone from her body, but the brothers refuse to use it to restore Alphonse. Instead Edward uses it to reach his brother's real body at the Gate of Truth and vows to find another way.

It was shot in Italy and Japan in 2016. Netflix released the film internationally in February 2018. Reviews were mixed, and two sequels followed in 2022.

documents.title: Roma
documents.tagline: There are periods in history that scar societies and moments in life that transform us as individuals.
documents.overview: In 1970s Mexico City, two domestic workers help a mother of four while her husband is away for an extended period of time.
documents.plot:
In 1970, Cleodegaria "Cleo" Gutiérrez is a Mixtec live-in maid in an upper-middle-class household in Mexico City's Colonia Roma neighborhood. The household consists of the mother, Sofía; the father, Antonio; their four school-aged children, Pepe, Sofi, Toño and Paco; and Sofía's mother, Teresa. Antonio, a medical doctor, often leaves for business conferences, but Sofía's distressed reactions to his absences suggest he is having an extramarital affair.
Meanwhile, Cleo believes she might be pregnant. She tells her boyfriend, Fermín, who pretends to be supportive but immediately abandons her at a movie theatre. She nervously reveals her news to Sofía, who provides emotional comfort and takes her to the hospital, confirming her pregnancy. Sofía then takes Cleo and the children to a family friend's hacienda for New Year celebrations. Recent tensions over land in the area arise, and a large forest fire erupts that the partygoers help extinguish.
Back in the city, Cleo sees Antonio and a young woman flirting on the street. She looks for Fermín, traveling to an impoverished district on the edge of the city, where she finds him training at a military-style camp run by Professor Zovek. Fermín denies that her baby is his, threatening to beat Cleo and their child if she talks to him again.

Cleo returns to the city, and the increasingly distraught Sofía tries unsuccessfully to conceal her husband's infidelity from their children. With the baby almost due, Teresa takes Cleo shopping for a crib downtown. Suddenly a student protest outside the store turns into the Corpus Christi massacre of 10 June 1971 as a paramilitary group, Los Halcones ("the Falcons"), attacks the protesters. The militants chase a student into the store and murder him. Fermín, appearing as one of Los Halcones, points a gun at Cleo and Teresa before wordlessly exiting. Then Cleo's water breaks. The violence in the streets slows traffic and her attempt to get to the hospital. When she arrives, Antonio briefly appears, reassures her, then makes an excuse to leave. She cries in agony as her baby girl is delivered stillborn.
Later, Sofía takes Cleo and the children on a family outing to the beaches at Tuxpan. Sofía tells her children that she and their father are separating and that the outing is giving him time to collect his belongings from their home. At the beach, a strong current almost drowns Sofi and Paco, but Cleo wades in and saves them, despite not knowing how to swim. Sofía and the children affirm their love for Cleo, all of them holding each other and crying, while Cleo confesses that she did not want her baby to be born. The group returns home to find the house reorganized, and Cleo prepares a load of clothes for washing.

documents.title: The Nutcracker and the Four Realms
documents.original_title: The Nutcracker and the Four Realms
documents.tagline: Let the mystery unfold.
documents.overview: When Clara’s mother leaves her a mysterious gift, she embarks on a journey to four secret realms—where she discovers her greatest strength could change the world.
documents.plot:
The Nutcracker and the Four Realms is a 2018 American Christmas fantasy film directed by Lasse Hallström and Joe Johnston from a screenplay by Ashleigh Powell, retelling E. T. A. Hoffmann's 1816 tale The Nutcracker and the Mouse King and Tchaikovsky's 1892 ballet. It stars Mackenzie Foy as Clara Stahlbaum, Keira Knightley as the Sugar Plum Fairy, Jayden Fowora-Knight as Captain Philip Hoffman, Helen Mirren as Mother Ginger and Morgan Freeman as Drosselmeyer, with Eugenio Derbez, Matthew Macfadyen, Richard E. Grant and Misty Copeland. Johnston directed a month of reshoots after Hallström's principal photography at Pinewood Studios.

On Christmas Eve in Victorian London, Clara receives a locked egg-shaped box left to her by her late mother, Marie, with a note saying that everything she needs is inside. At the party of her godfather, the engineer Drosselmeyer, she follows a string bearing her name into a parallel world, where a mouse steals the key. With the help of Captain Philip, a nutcracker soldier, she reaches a palace and meets the regents of three realms: the Sugar Plum Fairy of the Land of Sweets, Shiver of the Land of Snowflakes and Hawthorne of the Land of Flowers, who say they are at war with Mother Ginger and the Fourth Realm. Clara learns that Marie created this world and was its queen, making Clara a princess, and that a machine Marie used to bring toys to life could defend the realms if activated with the key.

Clara and Philip retrieve the key from Mother Ginger, ignoring her warning, but the egg turns out to be a music box. The Sugar Plum Fairy then reveals her treachery: resentful at feeling abandoned by Marie, she uses the machine to create an army of toy soldiers to conquer all four realms and imprisons Clara and her allies. Finding a mirror inside the music box, Clara realizes she needed only herself. She escapes, wins Mother Ginger's help and reverses the machine, turning the Sugar Plum Fairy back into a doll. Clara returns to London, reconciles with her father and dances with him to the music box, which plays the first song he and Marie danced to.

Released by Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures in November 2018, the film grossed $174 million worldwide but was a box office flop, with an estimated loss of $75-90 million. Critics found it lovely to look at but hollow, and it received 32% approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: A Cinderella Christmas
documents.tagline: One Night Changes Everything
documents.overview: Angie works hard to run her uncle’s events business while her cousin Candace takes the credit. When Angie takes a night off to have fun at the Christmasquerade Ball, the mask and gown allow her to let loose, and she quickly catches the eye of Nicholas, a wealthy local bachelor. But then Angie has to go before revealing her identity, leaving Nicholas searching for his mystery woman in this modern take on the classic fairy tale.

documents.title: The Domestics
documents.tagline: In the end, defend.
documents.overview: A young husband and wife must fight to return home in a post-apocalyptic mid-western landscape ravaged by gangs.
documents.plot:
The US Government conducts a catastrophic chemical weapons attack on the American populace to "reset" society. The surviving population of America divides into two groups. The Gangs, who name themselves Gamblers, Sheets, Plowboys, Nailers, and Cherries, control territory. The Domestics are unaffiliated with the Gangs and wish to live in peace rather than give in to violence. The story is interspersed with snippets from a talk show by DJ Crazy Al, who provides updates and commentaries about America.
Married couple Mark and Nina West, whose divorce was put on hold because of society's breakdown, travel to Nina's parents in Milwaukee. They rest in an abandoned house along the way, catching the attention of some Nailers. Two break in, prompting Mark to kill them. Later, while scavenging for supplies at a store, they are met by Nathan Wood and his son Steven, who save them from a group of pursuing Nailers. Nathan invites Mark and Nina to his home to meet his family for a meal. They accept, and encounter members of the Plowboys along the way. During the meal, Nathan tells Mark about a rumored new gang consisting of children.
The conversation takes a turn for the worse when Nathan informs Mark that they had eaten human flesh. A Nailer from the prior home invasion, having survived and followed them, holds Nathan's daughter hostage and demands a trade for Mark and Nina. Steven ambushes the Nailer and chaos ensues. Nina and Mark flee, leaving Nathan's family behind, where the Nailer kills Nathan's wife and daughter. Nathan kills the Nailer but swears revenge on the Wests. He calls his Plowboy contacts on his CB Radio. As they drive away, Mark and Nina get into a heated argument before Nina is shot and passes out.
The couple reach an abandoned house, unwittingly followed by Betsy, a deserter Cherry who is fascinated by Nina. Betsy had earlier killed her way out of the Plowboys' captivity. After treating Nina's wound, Mark looks for supplies in another house. When Nina awakens, she removes her wedding ring and contemplates leaving before finding Mark's notes pleading her to give their relationship another chance. She then finds a box of records and a bottle of alcohol, puts on her favorite Heavy Metal record and begins dancing.
Mark encounters William Cunningham, a flamboyant madman. He discovers William has captured Nathan and Steven, who has caught up to them. William holds him at gunpoint and forces him to fight a large slave. While fighting, Mark is thrown into William, and takes the opportunity to kill him then free the slave. Nathan decides to forgive Mark and depart with Steven, ending his quest for vengeance.
Mark reunites with Nina at the house and the two rekindle their relationship. However, they are captured by Gamblers, brought to their clubhouse and forced to play Russian Roulette. After Mark is shot in the shoulder, Nina breaks free, grabs a gun and shoots the game's host. The two escape on a stolen car.

documents.title: UFO
documents.tagline: Sightings are never a coincidence. The cover-up ends here.
documents.overview: A college student, who sees a UFO, uses his exceptional math skills to investigate the sighting with his friends while the FBI follows closely behind.
documents.plot:
UFO is a 2018 American science fiction film written and directed by Ryan Eslinger. Alex Sharp stars as a gifted mathematics student determined to prove that an alien craft has visited Earth, with Gillian Anderson as his professor, David Strathairn as a federal official, and Ella Purnell. Unusually for the genre, its story turns on mathematics and physics rather than spectacle. Sony released it directly to video on September 4, 2018, promoting it with a trailer on UFO Day.

Derek Echevaro, a student at the University of Cincinnati, has been haunted since childhood by what he believes was a UFO sighting. In 2017 an unidentified object briefly hovers over Cincinnati's international airport, disrupting air traffic control radio. The authorities first describe it as a drone and later as a Gulfstream jet, but Derek's calculations prove both explanations impossible. Analysing the interference, he finds that it encodes the fine-structure constant, a fundamental number of physics, broken into chunks of digits.

When a mysterious program starts running on his computer, Derek reformats the signal into binary, and his obsession increasingly strains his relationships with his friends and roommates, Lee and Natalie. His work comes to the attention of Franklin Ahls, a senior official of a secret FBI committee on aerial phenomena, who is leading a team of scientists in Ohio trying to cover up the incident and decode the signal, which he believes comes from an advanced civilisation.

Sensing that time is short, Derek asks his professor, Dr. Rebecca Hendricks, for help. Sceptical at first, she joins him in analysing mobile phone disruptions recorded during the incident, but they realise that a unit of measurement is missing from their calculations. During a lecture on eigenvalues, Hendricks realises that the missing unit is 21 centimetres, the wavelength of radiation emitted by neutral hydrogen, which allows the signal to be read as coordinates.

Borrowing Lee's car, Derek drives to the location and briefly sees the craft, which sends out a new signal before vanishing. He is seized by armed agents and taken to Ahls, who confirms that the visitors used the fine-structure constant to establish a shared mathematical language and that the new message, more complex, appears to describe their location in three dimensions. Ahls confirms that humanity is not alone and invites Derek to help refine the calculations. Reviews were muted, Starburst giving it five out of ten.

documents.title: Scooby-Doo! Shaggy's Showdown
documents.overview: When the Scooby gang visits a dude ranch, they discover that it and the nearby town have been haunted by a ghostly cowboy, Dapper Jack, who fires real fire from his fire irons. The mystery only deepens when it’s discovered that the ghost is also the long lost relative of Shaggy Rogers!

documents.title: Rampage
documents.tagline: Big meets bigger
documents.overview: Primatologist Davis Okoye shares an unshakable bond with George, the extraordinarily intelligent, silverback gorilla who has been in his care since birth.  But a rogue genetic experiment gone awry mutates this gentle ape into a raging creature of enormous size.  To make matters worse, it’s soon discovered there are other similarly altered animals.  As these newly created alpha predators tear across North America, destroying everything in their path, Okoye teams with a discredited genetic engineer to secure an antidote, fighting his way through an ever-changing battlefield, not only to halt a global catastrophe but to save the fearsome creature that was once his friend.
documents.plot:
Rampage is a 2018 science fiction monster film directed by Brad Peeters and written by Ryan Condal. The movie stars Dwayne Johnson, Naomie Harris, Malin Åkerman, Jake Lacy, and Jeffrey Dean Morgan.

The story begins with Davis Okoye (Dwayne Johnson), a primatologist who works at the San Diego Zoo. He is particularly close to his genetically engineered gorilla, George, whom he has raised since childhood. However, their peaceful life is disrupted when a biotech company called UAC (United Animal Corporation) announces its plans to create genetically modified super-soldiers using DNA from various animals.

The CEO of UAC, Robert K. Ross (Jeffrey Dean Morgan), reveals that the company's goal is to create an army of super-intelligent and powerful creatures to fight in a war against China. The plan involves injecting DNA from different species into various animals, making them stronger and more aggressive.

As the story unfolds, Davis discovers that UAC has been secretly experimenting on his gorilla, George, without his knowledge or consent. When he confronts Ross, he is met with hostility and eventually loses control of George, who escapes and wreaks havoc on San Diego.

Meanwhile, a genetically modified wolf named Ruby (Naomie Harris) and an elephant named Ralph (Jake Lacy) also escape from UAC's facility. The three creatures, including George, begin to terrorize the city, causing destruction and chaos.

As Davis tries to find a way to stop his creations, he teams up with Dr. Kate Caldwell (Malin Åkerman), a geneticist who helped create the super-soldiers. Together, they embark on a mission to find a cure for George's DNA and prevent further destruction.

Throughout the movie, Davis struggles with his feelings of guilt and responsibility towards George, whom he considers a friend. He also grapples with the consequences of playing God and creating life forms that are beyond human control.

As the story reaches its climax, Davis and Kate devise a plan to use a virus to reverse the effects of the DNA injection on George and the other creatures. In the final battle, Davis confronts Ross and his team, who have been using the super-soldiers for their own gain.

In the end, Davis is able to stop George and the other creatures from causing further destruction, but not before they wreak havoc on San Diego. The movie concludes with Davis reflecting on the consequences of his actions and the importance of responsible scientific research.

Overall, Rampage is an action-packed monster film that explores themes of responsibility, friendship, and the dangers of playing God. While it received mixed reviews from critics, it has become a cult classic among fans of science fiction and monster movies.

documents.title: Iron Mask
documents.overview: Commissioned to map the Far East territories of the Russian Empire, cartographer Jonathan Green sets off on a long journey of unbelievable adventures—making breath-taking discoveries and meeting mysterious creatures, Chinese princesses, deadly masters of oriental martial arts, and even the King of Dragons.
documents.plot:
Iron Mask, released in Russia as Тайна печати дракона (The Mystery of the Dragon Seal) and in China as 龙牌之谜, and also known as Viy 2: Journey to China, is a fantasy adventure of 2019 directed by Oleg Stepchenko, sequel to the 2014 film Viy. Jason Flemyng returns as the English cartographer Jonathan Green and Charles Dance as Lord Dudley, joined by Jackie Chan as the White Wizard Master Et Al, Arnold Schwarzenegger as James Hook, the warden of the Tower of London, Helen Yao as his daughter Chen-Lan, Anna Churina as Jonathan's beloved Emma and Rutger Hauer as an ambassador.

In ancient China, White Wizards guard a magical dragon whose eyelashes yield a tea that cures any illness. Some turn greedy, becoming Black Wizards who stop trimming the lashes to harvest more tea, sending the dragon into a deep sleep. Et Al is exiled to the Tower of London, and his daughter Chen-Lan to a Russian prison. There she meets Jonathan, jailed because Tsar Peter the Great, who commissioned his last map, has been replaced by an impostor while the real tsar is held in the Tower alongside Et Al. Released through family influence but sent to map Russia's Far East so that he cannot expose the fraud, Jonathan takes Chen-Lan along as his assistant, mistaking her for a boy, and she agrees to guide him to China.

In London, Peter and Et Al alert Emma to their presence through one of Jonathan's letters and stage an escape; Et Al stays behind to fight Hook, giving Peter a magical medallion to lead him to his daughter, and Peter and Emma stow away on a ship bound for China. At the dragon's tower, Jonathan finds the Black Wizards' leader, a two-faced queen who has taken Chen-Lan's appearance, oppressing the townspeople and faking control of the dragon with tricks. Jonathan is caught spying, and he and Emma are about to be executed when Cossack allies wreck the queen's mechanical dragon. Chen-Lan revives the real dragon and duels the queen, who falls to her death once Jonathan sees through her disguise. Chen-Lan takes the throne, and Et Al, pardoned, travels to China with Hook.

Shot in 2015-2017 and delayed by censorship approval, the film opened in China on 16 August 2019. It was panned, scoring 22% on Rotten Tomatoes, and Schwarzenegger received a Golden Raspberry nomination for Worst Supporting Actor.

documents.title: Mortal Engines
documents.tagline: Some scars never heal
documents.overview: Many thousands of years in the future, Earth’s cities roam the globe on huge wheels, devouring each other in a struggle for ever diminishing resources. On one of these massive traction cities, the old London, Tom Natsworthy has an unexpected encounter with a mysterious young woman from the wastelands who will change the course of his life forever.
documents.plot:
Mortal Engines is a 2018 science fantasy adventure film directed by Christian Rivers and written by Fran Walsh, Philippa Boyens, and Peter Jackson. The movie is set in a post-apocalyptic world where cities are on wheels and roam the land, preying on smaller towns to sustain themselves.

In the year 2256, London is one of the largest and most powerful mobile cities, known as Cogtopolis. The city is ruled by the tyrannical Mayor, who controls its citizens through a complex system of gears and machinery. The story follows Hester Shaw (Hera Hilmar), a young woman with a prosthetic leg, who seeks revenge against the man responsible for her father's death.

Hester's father was killed by the leader of the city, Thaddeus Valentine (Robert Sheehan), who is also the inventor of the "mangler" - a machine that can crush and devour smaller cities. Hester sets out on a perilous journey to find Valentine, accompanied by her friend Anubis (Jorge Lendeborg Jr.), a skilled engineer.

As they travel across the land, they encounter other mobile cities, including New London, which is ruled by the ruthless Mayor of London, and the nomadic tribes that live outside the city walls. The group also meets Shangdu, a Chinese city that has been destroyed by Valentine's mangler.

The story takes a dramatic turn when Hester and Anubis discover that Valentine is planning to destroy all the smaller cities in order to create a new world order. They must use their skills and ingenuity to stop him and save the world from destruction.

Throughout the movie, the action unfolds at a breakneck pace, with thrilling chases and battles between the mobile cities. The special effects are impressive, bringing the post-apocalyptic world to life in stunning detail.

One of the standout aspects of Mortal Engines is its unique world-building. The concept of mobile cities roaming the land is both fascinating and terrifying, and the movie does an excellent job of exploring the consequences of such a society. The characters are also well-developed, with Hester being a particularly compelling protagonist.

The ending of the movie sets up a potential sequel, as Hester and Anubis face off against Valentine in a final showdown. However, the conclusion is bittersweet, leaving some questions unanswered and setting the stage for further adventures in this richly imagined world.

Overall, Mortal Engines is an exciting and visually stunning film that will appeal to fans of science fiction and adventure movies. With its unique world-building and compelling characters, it's a must-see for anyone looking for a thrilling ride.

documents.title: Napping Princess
documents.original_title: ひるね姫 ～知らないワタシの物語～
documents.tagline: There's a reason why I can see in dreams
documents.overview: Japan, 2020, a few days before the opening of the Tokyo Olympics. Although she should be studying for her final exams, Kokone, a schoolgirl who lives in a small town with her widowed father, a mysterious and talented mechanic, falls asleep often, anywhere, anytime, entering, over and over, a dream-world where a squad of fantastic motorized contraptions fights against magic, a world close to reality where she will find out the keys of her true past.
documents.plot:
In a near-future Japan, Kokone Morikawa has strange dreams of the fantastical realm called Heartland while taking naps. In these dreams, Heartland is a society entirely revolving around cars; the King's castle is a car factory, and his subjects all come to it to make a constant stream of new cars. His daughter, Ancien (who appears as a younger Kokone), has a "magic tablet" computer she uses to give life to various machines: notably, a blue toy dog named Joy, and a motorcycle named Heart. The king disapproves of Ancien bringing Heart to life, however, and confiscates her tablet and Heart and orders Ancien to be confined to her tower. Additionally, the society of Heartland is under threat from a gigantic monster of molten metal called the Colossus. The king builds giant robots to face the Colossus. Ancien, spying a motorcycle-driving subject of the king's named Peach, decides to ally with him and seek to defeat the Colossus together with him, while the king's chief adviser Bewan plots against the king and Ancien alike.
In normal Japan, Kokone is finishing up her school term, considering where to go to college, and reconnecting with old friend Morio who has returned from Tokyo from his first year in college. Kokone lives with her single father Momotarō; her mother perished in an accident while Kokone was still young, and Kokone complains that her father never told her much about her mother. Momotarō is an eccentric car mechanic and has a jacket similar to Peach's, a blue stuffed dog, a motorcycle, and a cracked tablet, all similar to the ones seen in Kokone's dreams. The situation takes a turn for the worse when Momotarō is unceremoniously arrested three days prior to the 2020 Tokyo Olympics and accused of stealing the car company Shijima Motors' secrets. A suited figure who looks identical to the Heartland king's evil adviser visits the Morikawa home, and is overheard to be searching for both the tablet and Kokone. Via text message from jail, Momotarō warns his daughter not to trust the adviser, who is named Watanabe. The message includes a picture of a younger Momotarō, his wife, and Watanabe. With Morio's help, Kokone evades Watanabe and his men and recovers the stolen tablet and bear doll, driving away in the family's motorcycle. They also discover a business card for Isshin Shijima, the chairman of Shijima Motors, and consider visiting him for help after Kokone is told that her mother, Ikumi, was the daughter of the chairman. The two take a nap in the motorcycle, visit Heartland where they dream of the motorcycle soaring through the sky, and are surprised to find on waking up that the motorcycle has driven itself to Osaka overnight before running out of gas. Kokone's attempts to contact her father via the tablet seemingly fail, but surprisingly enough, the "magic" seems to work in the real world when a request to the tablet's e-Heart chat for train tickets results in an attendant giving them paid-for Shinkansen tickets to Tokyo.
