documents.title: Minions: The Rise of Gru
documents.tagline: A villain will rise.
documents.overview: A fanboy of a supervillain supergroup known as the Vicious 6, Gru hatches a plan to become evil enough to join them, with the backup of his followers, the Minions.
documents.plot:
Minions: The Rise of Gru is a 2022 computer-animated comedy film produced by Illumination Entertainment and Universal Pictures.

The movie takes place in the 1970s, where we meet our protagonist, Young Gru (voiced by Evan Albertson), a young boy who lives with his mother, Bella (voiced by Miranda Tate), in a small village. Gru is an orphan who has been living on the streets and survives by stealing food from the local market.

One day, Gru meets Kevin, Stuart, and Bob, three Minions who are on a mission to find their next "supervillain" leader. The Minions are drawn to Gru's unique energy and decide to recruit him as their new leader. However, Gru is hesitant at first, but eventually joins the group.

As Gru becomes more confident in his leadership skills, he sets out to become the greatest supervillain of all time. He adopts a new persona, "Gru," and starts to build an army of Minions. Along the way, he meets a young girl named Valerie (voiced by Camila Cabello), who becomes his love interest.

However, Gru's plans are threatened when he discovers that his idol, the infamous supervillain, Vector (voiced by Dolph Lundgren), is actually his long-lost father. Vector has been searching for Gru and wants to recruit him as his new sidekick.

As Gru navigates his complicated family history, he must also confront his own identity and learn to balance his desire for power with his growing feelings for Valerie. The movie features plenty of action-packed sequences, hilarious Minion antics, and heartwarming moments that showcase the growth of our young protagonist.

Overall, Minions: The Rise of Gru is a fun and entertaining film that explores themes of family, identity, and friendship. With its colorful animation, witty humor, and lovable characters, it's sure to delight audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Journey's End
documents.tagline: Innocence Lost... Courage Found
documents.overview: Set in a dugout in Aisne in 1918, a group of British officers, led by the mentally disintegrating young officer Stanhope, variously await their fate.
documents.plot: Set in a dugout in Aisne in 1918, a group of British officers, led by the mentally disintegrating young officer Stanhope, variously await their fate.

documents.title: Unknown Origins
documents.overview: In Madrid, Spain, a mysterious serial killer ruthlessly murders his victims by recreating the first appearance of several comic book superheroes. Cosme, a veteran police inspector who is about to retire, works on the case along with the tormented inspector David Valentín and his own son Jorge Elías, a nerdy young man who owns a comic book store.
documents.plot:
Unknown Origins (Spanish: Orígenes secretos) is a 2020 Spanish thriller film directed by David Galán Galindo, who wrote the screenplay with Fernando Navarro, adapting his own novel of the same name. It stars Javier Rey, Verónica Echegui and Brays Efe alongside Antonio Resines. The film combines a police procedural with an affectionate tribute to comic books and superhero mythology.

In Madrid in 2019, a series of grotesque murders shakes the city. The killer stages each crime as a recreation of the origin story of a famous superhero: one victim is pumped full of supplements and steroids until he resembles the Hulk, while another has his heart removed and his body encased in a metal suit. The case falls to David, a serious and methodical police inspector who considers comic books childish entertainment for overgrown adults, a prejudice that quickly proves to be a handicap. He is initially partnered with Cosme, a veteran officer spending his last days on the force after being forced to resign.

Realizing that the investigation demands specialist knowledge, Cosme suggests that his son, Jorge Elías, a passionate comic book fan who runs a comic store in the city, would be better suited to help David. The mismatched pair work under the homicide chief, Norma, an enthusiastic cosplayer who prefers films and anime to comics. As the killer remains a step ahead of them and the press makes the murders public, David discovers that the death of his own parents mirrors the murder of Bruce Wayne's parents, Thomas and Martha Wayne, revealing a personal connection to the case. Racing against time, the trio uncover the identity of the killer, who turns out to be someone from inside the police department, and try to stop his final plans.

The film plays with superhero conventions and comic book references, contrasting the skeptical detective with the devoted fan who becomes his indispensable partner.

Unknown Origins was originally scheduled to screen at the 2020 Málaga Film Festival, but the filmmakers withdrew it when the festival was moved from March to August because of scheduling changes. It was released worldwide on Netflix on August 28, 2020, reaching an international audience through the streaming service.

documents.title: Mother
documents.tagline: No one will save her from his child
documents.overview: A pregnant woman, who is taking care of her son with development problems, is at her breaking point when a caregiver from the Philippines steps into her life. Diana suspects that she’s using voodoo against her after the quick improvements of her son.
documents.plot:
Mother (Spanish: Madre) is a 2016 Chilean psychological horror thriller written and directed by Aaron Burns, an actor and visual effects supervisor who had worked with Eli Roth on The Green Inferno and Knock Knock; it was his second feature as director after Blacktino. Produced by Miguel Asensio Llamas and Nicolás López as the first feature from Purgatorio, a horror label within Sobras International Pictures dedicated to Latin American folklore, it stars Daniela Ramírez, Cristóbal Tapia Montt, Aida Jabolin, Matías Bassi, Nicolás Durán, Ignacia Allamand, Cristián Carvajal and Igal Furman. The dialogue is in Spanish, and Antonio Quercia photographed the film, with music by Manuel Riveiro.

Diana Prieto (Ramírez), a well-off housewife in Santiago, is pregnant with her second child while struggling to care for her first, Martin (Bassi), a boy of about ten with severe autism who can be unpredictably violent and must be restrained at night so he does not hurt himself. Her husband Tomás (Tapia Montt) is often away on business trips to Japan, and every nanny they hire quits within days. When Martin has a violent outburst in a supermarket, a Filipina employee, Luz (Jabolin), calms him almost instantly. Diana hires her, and Luz explains that her own son David (Durán) was once like Martin and is now cured. Under her care Martin improves dramatically, but Diana grows uneasy: Luz speaks to the boy only in her own language, takes him off his medication without permission, and strange homemade charms begin turning up around the house. Using an instant translation app, Diana becomes convinced that Luz is turning her son against her through voodoo, and as she suffers nausea, rashes and hallucinations, she begins to fear that the nanny is poisoning her too, in a game that may prove deadly.

The film premiered at AFI Fest in 2016 and screened at South by Southwest in March 2017, where Netflix acquired its worldwide streaming rights. Released in Chilean theaters on 27 April 2017, it had the best opening of the year for a Chilean film, with about 20,000 admissions in its first week, before streaming on Netflix. Reviewing it at SXSW, Dennis Harvey of Variety called it a flat, derivative blend of the "nanny from hell" thriller and Rosemary's Baby, criticizing its lack of suspense, pedestrian shock imagery, Ramírez's unsympathetic characterization and an unsatisfying ending.

documents.title: A-X-L
documents.tagline: Man's best friend has evolved
documents.overview: The life of a teenage boy is forever altered by a chance encounter with cutting edge military technology.
documents.plot:
A-X-L is a 2018 American science fiction action film directed by Michael Bay and written by Art Marcum and Matt Holloway. The movie stars Dwayne Johnson, Woody Harrelson, and Carla Gugino.

The story begins with Alex Hitchens (Dwayne Johnson), a former Army Ranger who has lost his way after the death of his wife in combat. He is haunted by flashbacks of his time in Afghanistan and struggles to connect with his 8-year-old son, Christian (Max Thieriot). To cope with his emotions, Alex turns to extreme sports, including big wave surfing.

One day, while surfing, Alex is attacked by a massive shark that kills him. However, instead of dying, he is rescued by a team of scientists who have been studying the effects of a mysterious virus on humans and animals. The virus, known as "Project A-X-L," has the ability to transfer human consciousness into an alien creature's body.

The scientists, led by Dr. Emma Russell (Carla Gugino), believe that Alex's consciousness can be transferred into the body of an alien creature, allowing him to survive his injuries and potentially find a way to communicate with humans again. The team uses advanced technology to transfer Alex's consciousness into the body of an A-X-L, a massive, intelligent, and deadly alien creature.

As Alex navigates his new surroundings, he begins to form a bond with Christian, who is struggling to cope with his father's death. With the help of Dr. Russell and her team, Alex learns to control his newfound powers and work together with them to take down a group of rogue mercenaries who are seeking to exploit the A-X-L for their own gain.

Throughout the movie, Alex struggles to reconcile his human emotions with his new alien form, leading to some intense and emotional moments. He also begins to uncover the truth about Project A-X-L and the motivations of Dr. Russell and her team.

As the story unfolds, Alex and Christian work together to take down the mercenaries and prevent them from using the A-X-L for their own purposes. Along the way, Alex must confront his own demons and learn to trust himself and those around him.

The movie culminates in an action-packed showdown between Alex and the mercenaries, with Alex using his newfound powers to protect Christian and defeat his enemies. In the end, Alex is able to find a sense of peace and closure, and he begins to rebuild his relationship with Christian.

Overall, A-X-L is a thrilling and emotionally resonant sci-fi action film that explores themes of grief, redemption, and the power of human connection.

documents.title: Dune
documents.tagline: It begins.
documents.overview: Paul Atreides, a brilliant and gifted young man born into a great destiny beyond his understanding, must travel to the most dangerous planet in the universe to ensure the future of his family and his people. As malevolent forces explode into conflict over the planet's exclusive supply of the most precious resource in existence-a commodity capable of unlocking humanity's greatest potential-only those who can conquer their fear will survive.
documents.plot:
Dune, titled on screen as Dune: Part One, is a 2021 American epic space opera directed and co-produced by Denis Villeneuve, who wrote the screenplay with Jon Spaihts and Eric Roth. It is the first of a two-part adaptation of Frank Herbert's 1965 novel and the opening chapter of Villeneuve's Dune trilogy. Timothée Chalamet stars as Paul Atreides, leading an ensemble that includes Rebecca Ferguson, Oscar Isaac, Josh Brolin, Stellan Skarsgård, Dave Bautista, Zendaya, Charlotte Rampling, Jason Momoa and Javier Bardem.

In the distant future, the Padishah Emperor orders Duke Leto Atreides of House Atreides to take over the stewardship of the desert planet Arrakis, the only source of the spice melange, the most valuable substance in the universe, which makes interstellar travel possible. The planet has long been ruled by the brutal House Harkonnen under Baron Vladimir Harkonnen. Leto's son Paul, trained in combat by the weapons master Gurney Halleck and the swordmaster Duncan Idaho, and in the mental disciplines of the Bene Gesserit sisterhood by his mother Lady Jessica, is troubled by visions of Arrakis and of a mysterious young Fremen woman.

On Arrakis, Leto hopes to forge an alliance with the Fremen, the planet's native desert people, but the assignment is a trap. The Emperor has secretly conspired with the Harkonnens to destroy House Atreides, whose growing popularity threatens him. With the help of a traitor within the household, the Harkonnens and the Emperor's elite Sardaukar troops launch a devastating assault. Leto is killed, and Paul and Jessica escape into the deep desert, where Paul's powers of prescience grow and some see him as a long-prophesied messiah. Pursued across the dunes and threatened by giant sandworms, mother and son finally encounter a band of Fremen led by Stilgar, including Chani, the woman from Paul's dreams, and Paul must prove himself in a ritual duel to be accepted among them.

Legendary Pictures acquired the rights in 2016 and Villeneuve signed on in 2017. Filming took place from March to July 2019 in Hungary, Jordan, Norway and the United Arab Emirates. Delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic, the film premiered at the 78th Venice International Film Festival in September 2021 and opened in the United States in theaters and on HBO Max in October. It grossed $411 million against a $165 million budget, received widespread acclaim and won six Academy Awards. Dune: Part Two followed in March 2024.

documents.title: Dragged Across Concrete
documents.tagline: Those who can't earn a living must find another way to provide
documents.overview: Two policemen, one an old-timer, the other his volatile younger partner, find themselves suspended when a video of their strong-arm tactics becomes the media's cause du jour. Low on cash and with no other options, these two embittered soldiers descend into the criminal underworld to gain their just due, but instead find far more than they wanted awaiting them in the shadows.
documents.plot:
Dragged Across Concrete is a 2018 American crime thriller film written and directed by S. Craig Zahler. The movie stars Vince Vaughn, Jennifer Carpenter, Don Johnson, and Melissa Leo.

The story follows two detectives, Detective Brett Ridgeway (Vince Vaughn) and Detective Anthony Lopez (Don Johnson), who work for the Dallas Police Department's Vice and Narcotics division. They are a mismatched duo, with Ridgeway being a by-the-book, straight-laced cop, while Lopez is a loose-cannon, street-smart veteran.

The movie begins with a gruesome crime scene: a young woman named Sarah (Jennifer Carpenter) has been brutally murdered in a motel room. The investigation that follows reveals that the killer left behind a mysterious symbol carved into the victim's body - a symbol that will become a recurring motif throughout the film.

As Ridgeway and Lopez delve deeper into the case, they discover that Sarah was involved in a sex trafficking ring, and that she had been working to take down the operation from within. The detectives soon realize that they are dealing with a highly organized and ruthless crime syndicate, led by a mysterious figure known only as "The Devil" (Melissa Leo).

As the investigation unfolds, Ridgeway and Lopez's partnership is put to the test. They have different working styles, and their differing approaches often lead to clashes. However, they are both driven by a desire to solve the case and bring justice to Sarah's killer.

Throughout the film, Zahler expertly ratchets up the tension and violence, creating a sense of unease and dread that permeates every scene. The cinematography is stark and unsettling, capturing the dark underbelly of Dallas's seedy side.

As the story builds towards its climax, Ridgeway and Lopez discover that they are in over their heads. They are dealing with a crime syndicate that will stop at nothing to silence them. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that The Devil is none other than Sarah's own mother, who has been using her daughter as leverage to manipulate the detectives.

The film's final act is a tense and violent showdown between Ridgeway, Lopez, and The Devil. The outcome is far from certain, and the audience is left on the edge of their seats as the two detectives fight for their lives.

Ultimately, Dragged Across Concrete is a gripping and unflinching portrayal of the darker side of human nature. Zahler's direction is masterful, creating a sense of unease and tension that propels the film towards its shocking conclusion. The performances from Vaughn, Carpenter, Johnson, and Leo are all top-notch, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, Dragged Across Concrete is a gripping and unsettling thriller that will keep you on the edge of your seat until the very end.

documents.title: Siberia
documents.tagline: This was not the plan.
documents.overview: Lucas, a diamond trader who travels to Saint Petersburg to arrange a sale, discovers that his Russian business partner has left his hotel and gone to a small Siberian village, so Lucas also heads there to try find him.
documents.plot: Lucas, a diamond trader who travels to Saint Petersburg to arrange a sale, discovers that his Russian business partner has left his hotel and gone to a small Siberian village, so Lucas also heads there to try find him.

documents.title: Sing 2
documents.tagline: Where will your dreams take you?
documents.overview: Buster and his new cast now have their sights set on debuting a new show at the Crystal Tower Theater in glamorous Redshore City. But with no connections, he and his singers must sneak into the Crystal Entertainment offices, run by the ruthless wolf mogul Jimmy Crystal, where the gang pitches the ridiculous idea of casting the lion rock legend Clay Calloway in their show. Buster must embark on a quest to find the now-isolated Clay and persuade him to return to the stage.
documents.plot:
After the events of the first film, Buster Moon is thriving with his newly rebuilt theater. Johnny, Rosita, Gunter, Meena, and Miss Crawly work as his cast and crew, while Ash performs as a soloist at a rock club. Buster's show fails to impress Crystal Entertainment's talent scout Suki Lane from Redshore City. Encouraged by Nana Noodleman, Buster gathers his crew, and they travel to the city to make an impression.
After being denied entry into Crystal Entertainment, they sneak in for an audition with entertainment mogul Jimmy Crystal. As Jimmy is uninterested in Buster's original pitch, Gunter suggests a space-themed sci-fi musical that features songs from Clay Calloway, a legendary rock star who disappeared after his wife Ruby died 15 years ago. Intrigued, and assuming that Clay will be part of the show, Jimmy greenlights it and lets Buster and his friends stay at his hotel during production.
Miss Crawly finds where Clay lives and goes to visit him, but he scares her away with a paintball gun. During rehearsal, Rosita reveals to have a fear of heights after learning she needs to make a high jump, prompting Jimmy to insist Buster have his daughter Porsha play her part instead. Buster reluctantly writes Rosita a minor role. Top choreographer Klaus Kickenklober is hired to teach Johnny to dance, but is unnecessarily harsh, causing Johnny to fall behind. Johnny later comes across street dancer Nooshy, who takes over as his teacher. Meena is cast in a romantic scene with a well-intentioned but heavily egocentric actor named Darius, but is unable to act the part convincingly, having never been in love before. She later meets and falls in love with an ice cream vendor named Alfonso. Jimmy eventually finds out that Buster never contacted Clay about the show and threatens to hurt Buster if he does not deliver.
Ash and Buster visit Clay to convince him to join the show. He refuses at first, finding it too emotionally sad to perform after Ruby's death, but Ash changes his mind. Back at the theater, Buster offers Porsha to switch roles with Rosita, as Porsha's acting skills are poor. Porsha misunderstands this as Buster firing her and leaves. After news of the "firing" is broadcast, Jimmy scolds Porsha, sobbing, and nearly drops Buster off the hotel's roof for making him look bad before locking him in his closet. Suki frees Buster and warns him to leave Redshore City before Jimmy sends his bodyguards to find him. Ash arrives at the hotel room with the crew and Clay, who advises Buster not to run and hide as he did. After overhearing Jimmy insulting him and his crew on television, Buster decides to put on the show behind Jimmy's back. Porsha rejoins the show, Johnny calls his father and his gang to keep Jimmy, Jerry, and his bodyguards at bay, and Rosita arranges for her husband Norman and their children to distract hotel security.

documents.title: Salyut-7
documents.tagline: The right stuff of the cosmonauts.
documents.overview: USSR, June 1985. After contact with the Salyut 7 space station is lost, cosmonauts Vladimir Dzhanibekov and Viktor Savinykh dock with the empty, frozen craft, and bring her back to life. Based on actual events.
documents.plot:
Salyut 7 (Russian: Салют-7) is a 2017 Russian space disaster drama directed by Klim Shipenko from an idea by space journalist Aleksey Samolyotov. Starring Vladimir Vdovichenkov and Pavel Derevyanko, it is inspired by the 1985 Soyuz T-13 mission, the first time a "dead" space station was docked with and brought back into service, although the characters' names were changed and events were dramatised.

In July 1984, during a spacewalk, cosmonaut Vladimir Fyodorov helps colleague Svetlana Lazareva after her glove is punctured and glimpses a strange blue glow; doctors decide he was hallucinating and ground him, to the relief of his wife Nina. In February 1985 the unmanned Salyut 7 stops responding to Mission Control. Western media warn of an uncontrolled crash, and Soviet officials learn that the US is preparing the shuttle Challenger, whose cargo bay is suspiciously sized to hold the station. Engineer Viktor Alyokhin, who helped build Salyut 7, is chosen for a two-man rescue flight, but no candidate pilot can dock with the tumbling station in the simulator, and flight director Valeriy Shubin turns to Fyodorov. In June 1985 Fyodorov matches the station's spin and docks on his second attempt. They find Salyut 7 without power and encased in ice from a burst water system. Mission Control urges them to deorbit it, warning that thawing could cause short circuits and fire, but they begin warming and repairing it. On a spacewalk Fyodorov sees that a meteoroid shower has crushed the cover of the sensor that orients the solar panels. Thawed water shorts the Soyuz's wiring and sets it ablaze; Alyokhin puts the fire out by depressurising the craft, which is gutted, and he is badly burned. With Challenger launched, the Soviet military prepares to destroy the station, and controllers realise there is only enough oxygen for one man to return. Fyodorov offers to sacrifice himself, but Alyokhin proposes knocking the damaged cover off with a hammer. The gamble works, power returns, and as Challenger arrives a French astronaut aboard salutes the cosmonauts, who then see the blue glow.

Vdovichenkov plays Fyodorov, based on Vladimir Dzhanibekov, and Derevyanko plays Alyokhin, based on Viktor Savinykh, with Aleksandr Samoylenko as Shubin and Mariya Mironova as Nina. Filmed largely suspended on wires in a pavilion near Saint Petersburg, it was released by Nashe Kino on October 12, 2017, grossed 783 million rubles on a 400 million budget, and won the Golden Eagle for Best Film.

documents.title: Tangled: Before Ever After
documents.tagline: Life is about to get hairier.
documents.overview: Rapunzel grapples with the responsibilities of being a princess and the overprotective ways of her father. While she wholeheartedly loves Eugene, Rapunzel does not share his immediate desire to get married and settle down within the castle walls. Determined to live life on her own terms, she and her tough-as-nails Lady-in-Waiting Cassandra embark on a secret adventure where they encounter mystical rocks that magically cause Rapunzel's long blonde hair to grow back. Impossible to break and difficult to hide, Rapunzel must learn to embrace her hair and all that it represents.

documents.title: White Boy Rick
documents.tagline: Hustler. Informant. Kingpin. Legend.
documents.overview: The story of a teenager, Richard Wershe Jr., who became an undercover informant for the police during the 1980s and was ultimately arrested for drug-trafficking and sentenced to life in prison.
documents.plot:
In 1984, Rick Wershe is a struggling single father living in Detroit during the height of the crack epidemic and the war on drugs. His dissatisfied daughter, Dawn, leaves their home, leaving Rick alone with his son, Ricky.
Rick manufactures gun parts and sells guns illegally to make ends meet, involving his son in the sale of a pair of silenced Egyptian Kalashnikov rifles to local gangster Johnny Curry. Ricky becomes good friends with Johnny's brother, Boo, which earns him the favor of Johnny and his crew.
Rick's activity attracts the attention of the FBI, and he is questioned by two agents, Alex Snyder and Frank Byrd, who see Ricky as a potential asset due to his connections with the criminal underworld. They convince Ricky to become an undercover informant behind Rick's back in exchange for money and immunity for his father.
Ricky is asked to sell drugs to keep up appearances. He becomes captivated by his extravagant new lifestyle and gains credibility as a drug supplier. Rick is suspicious of his son and confronts Ricky when he finds thousands of dollars in illicit cash underneath his bed, causing a rift between them. While Ricky is meeting with Dawn at a diner one evening, his grandfather's car is stolen, and the two shoot at the fleeing car. They are arrested but bailed out by Ricky's handlers, which arouses suspicion from Johnny.
At a party following a boxing match in Las Vegas, Johnny beats his rival's friend, Black Ed, within an inch of his life with a bottle of champagne. Afterwards, he orders a drive-by on the home of his rival, Leon Lucas, killing one of his young nephews. Ricky learns that the weapons used were the same AKs he had sold to Johnny. Devastated by his involvement in the murder of a child, he keeps a low profile and mends his relationship with his father. Johnny suspects Ricky is an informant and sends a crew member to his house, who shoots him in the stomach. While at the hospital, Snyder informs Ricky that they have enough evidence to raid all of Johnny's safe houses, and asks him to forget about the shooting in exchange for dropping all charges on his father.
In 1986, a little boy tells Ricky that his former girlfriend had a daughter named Keisha and that Ricky is the father. Rick and Ricky come over to see the child, who wins over the affection of both of them. Later on, they find Dawn at a drug den and forcibly take her home to detox. One year later, Ricky goes back to selling crack and assumes the role that Johnny left behind, even going so far as having sex with his wife, Cathy.
Ricky discovers he has earned more than enough money to make his father's dream of opening up a video store come true. However, FBI agents arrest Ricky and he is held on drug possession with intent to distribute, which could land him a potential life sentence. Ricky's former handlers deny their relationship with him but promise they will try to get his sentence reduced if he cooperates on one last bust.

documents.title: Sharknado 5: Global Swarming
documents.tagline: Make America bait again!
documents.overview: Fin and his wife April travel around the world to save their young son who's trapped inside a sharknado.
documents.plot:
Sharknado 5: Global Swarming is a campy, over-the-top disaster film that amplifies the absurdity and chaos of its predecessors. At its core, the movie explores the theme of global catastrophe and the human condition in the face of unimaginable destruction.

The film's narrative is driven by the idea of a massive sharknado sweeping across the globe, wreaking havoc on major cities and causing widespread devastation. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that this disaster is not just a natural phenomenon, but also a metaphor for the chaos and disorder that can result from human actions.

Throughout the movie, the characters are forced to confront their own personal demons and weaknesses as they struggle to survive in a world gone mad. The film's protagonist, Fin Shepard (played by Ian Ziering), is particularly emblematic of this theme, as he navigates his way through the disaster while also dealing with his own emotional baggage.

One of the most striking aspects of Sharknado 5 is its commentary on the dangers of unchecked capitalism and the exploitation of natural resources. The film's depiction of a world where corporations prioritize profits over people and the environment serves as a scathing critique of our modern society's values.

Ultimately, Sharknado 5: Global Swarming is a movie that revels in its own absurdity, using humor and satire to comment on the darker aspects of human nature. While it may not be taken seriously as a work of cinematic art, it remains a fascinating case study in the power of campy entertainment to critique and subvert societal norms.

documents.title: Slender Man
documents.tagline: Can you see him?
documents.overview: In a small town in Massachusetts, four high school girls perform a ritual in an attempt to debunk the lore of Slender Man. When one of the girls goes mysteriously missing, they begin to suspect that she is, in fact, his latest victim.
documents.plot:
Slender Man is a 2018 American supernatural horror film directed by Sylvain White and written by David Birke, based on the internet creepypasta character created in 2009. Joey King, Julia Goldani Telles, Jaz Sinclair, Annalise Basso, Taylor Richardson and Alex Fitzalan star, with Javier Botet as the title figure.

In the small town of Winsford, Massachusetts, Katie, Hallie, Chloe and Wren hold a sleepover at Katie's house and, curious about Slender Man, an internet legend who lures and abducts children, watch an unsettling video showing how to reach him. A week later, during a class field trip, Katie senses a presence among the trees and soon vanishes without a trace. Going through her laptop, her friends discover that Katie, unhappy at home with her alcoholic father, had grown obsessed with Slender Man and had contacted someone named Allison Riley about reaching him, hoping he would offer her an escape. Allison tells them that Slender Man infects people's minds, driving them mad or taking them, and that to recover Katie they must perform a ritual in which each surrenders a cherished object.

Wren warns the others to wear blindfolds and never look at his face, but during the ritual Chloe panics, flees and sees him up close; he later enters her home and drives her insane. Wren is attacked while researching in the library. When Hallie's sister, Lizzie, is hospitalized after a severe panic attack, Hallie finds that Lizzie and Wren had tried to contact Slender Man. At Wren's house she discovers research on his victims, among them Allison, and talks Wren out of suicide. Wren confesses that she took Lizzie into the woods, where Lizzie offered her teddy bear, and that their offerings were not enough, since Slender Man will rest only once he has physically claimed them all. He then smashes through the window and drags Wren away. Hallie goes into the woods and offers herself in her sister's place, and he takes her, the two merging into a tree. Lizzie recovers and reflects on the four friends' fate.

Sony's Screen Gems developed the film from 2016, and it was shot in Massachusetts in mid-2017. Shadowed by the 2014 Slender Man stabbing in Wisconsin, the studio required a PG-13 rating and cuts that left continuity errors. Released by Sony Pictures Releasing on August 10, 2018, it grossed $51.7 million on a $10 million budget, but reviews were poor, with 8% on Rotten Tomatoes, and Sinclair received a Golden Raspberry nomination for Worst Supporting Actress.

documents.title: Hey Arnold! The Jungle Movie
documents.tagline: After all these years, all your questions will finally be answered.
documents.overview: When their trip to San Lorenzo takes a turn for the worst, Arnold and his classmate’s only hope of getting home is retracing the dangerous path that led to Arnold's parents' disappearance.

documents.title: The Nun
documents.tagline: Pray For Forgiveness
documents.overview: When a young nun at a cloistered abbey in Romania takes her own life, a priest with a haunted past and a novitiate on the threshold of her final vows are sent by the Vatican to investigate. Together they uncover the order’s unholy secret. Risking not only their lives but their faith and their very souls, they confront a malevolent force in the form of the same demonic nun that first terrorized audiences in “The Conjuring 2” as the abbey becomes a horrific battleground between the living and the damned.
documents.plot:
The Nun is a 2018 American supernatural horror film directed by Corin Hardy and written by Gary Dauberman. It is the fifth installment in The Conjuring Universe.

The story begins with Sister Irene (Taissa Farmiga) and Father Burke (Demián Bichir), two Catholic priests who are sent to Romania to investigate the mysterious death of a nun, Sister Victoria (Bonnie Aarons). They soon discover that the nun's body is found in a remote orphanage, which has been abandoned for decades.

As they delve deeper into the mystery, they uncover a dark history about the orphanage and the nun who was killed. The story takes a turn when they meet Sister Irene's sister, Sister Charlotte (Charlotte Hope), who joins them on their investigation. Together, they discover that the orphanage is haunted by a malevolent entity known as Valak, a demonic nun.

The group soon realizes that Valak was once a human nun named Valak who lived in the orphanage during World War II. She was a cruel and sadistic nun who used her position to abuse and torture the children in her care. As she became more and more corrupted by her own darkness, she made a pact with a demon to gain ultimate power.

The group soon discovers that Valak's true form is a demonic entity that can take on many different forms, including that of Sister Victoria. They also learn that Valak has been awakened by the death of Sister Victoria, who was trying to perform an exorcism on her.

As the story unfolds, the group faces numerous challenges and terrifying encounters with Valak's minions. They soon realize that they are in over their heads and that they need to find a way to stop Valak before it's too late.

In the climactic final act, Father Burke and Sister Irene perform an exorcism on Valak, but not before she reveals her true form as a demonic entity. The two priests manage to banish Valak back to hell, but not before she unleashes a devastating attack on them.

The film ends with Father Burke and Sister Irene escaping the orphanage, but not without scars both physical and emotional. They realize that they have been forever changed by their experience in the orphanage and that they will never be able to go back to their normal lives.

Overall, The Nun is a chilling horror film that explores themes of corruption, abuse, and the supernatural. It features impressive performances from its cast, particularly Taissa Farmiga and Demián Bichir, who bring depth and nuance to their characters.

documents.title: The Sisters Brothers
documents.tagline: Make a killing. Make a living.
documents.overview: Oregon, 1851. Hermann Kermit Warm, a chemist and aspiring gold prospector, keeps a profitable secret that the Commodore wants to know, so he sends the Sisters brothers, two notorious assassins, to capture him on his way to California.

documents.title: Escape Plan 2: Hades
documents.tagline: He's back.
documents.overview: Ray Breslin manages an elite team of security specialists trained in the art of breaking people out of the world's most impenetrable prisons. When his most trusted operative, Shu Ren, is kidnapped and disappears inside the most elaborate prison ever built, Ray must track him down with the help of some of his former friends.
documents.plot:
Escape Plan 2: Hades is a 2018 American action thriller film directed by Tim Lee and written by Miles Chapman. The movie stars Sylvester Stallone, Arnold Schwarzenegger, and Adrienne Palicki.

The story begins with Emil Rottmayer (Adrienne Palicki), an inmate in the maximum-security prison of Hades, who is determined to escape. She befriends a fellow inmate, Sofia (Daniella Alonso), and together they devise a plan to break free from their confinement.

Meanwhile, Emil's past comes back to haunt her as she is pursued by a ruthless mercenary named Victor Vex (Jesse Metcalfe). Victor is hired by the prison's corrupt governor, who wants to keep Emil contained for his own gain.

Emil and Sofia put their plan into action, using their skills and cunning to evade the guards and make their way through the prison. Along the way, they encounter a group of fellow inmates who are also seeking freedom.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Victor is working with the governor to capture Emil and use her as leverage to gain control over the prison's lucrative black market. The stakes are raised when Emil discovers that Sofia has been secretly working for Victor all along, adding an element of betrayal to the plot.

Sylvester Stallone plays Ray Breslin, a seasoned prisoner who has spent years perfecting his escape techniques. He is initially hesitant to get involved with Emil and Sofia's plan but eventually joins forces with them to take down Victor and the corrupt governor.

The action-packed climax features an intense showdown between Emil, Ray, and Victor in the prison's maximum-security wing. The trio uses their skills and ingenuity to outsmart the guards and make a daring escape from Hades.

Throughout the movie, Stallone and Schwarzenegger deliver their signature one-liners and perform impressive stunts, showcasing their action hero credentials. While the plot may not be as complex or original as some of their previous collaborations, Escape Plan 2: Hades delivers on its promise of high-octane action and thrills.

Ultimately, Emil and Ray succeed in their mission to escape from Hades, but not without sacrifices. The movie concludes with a sense of closure for the characters, as they look towards a brighter future outside the prison walls.

Overall, Escape Plan 2: Hades is an entertaining, if predictable, action thriller that delivers on its promise of non-stop excitement and suspense.

documents.title: The Upside
documents.tagline: Based on a true story.
documents.overview: Phillip is a wealthy quadriplegic who needs a caretaker to help him with his day-to-day routine in his New York penthouse. He decides to hire Dell, a struggling parolee who's trying to reconnect with his ex and his young son. Despite coming from two different worlds, an unlikely friendship starts to blossom.
documents.plot:
The Upside is a 2017 American comedy-drama directed by Neil Burger and written by Jon Hartmere. It remakes the French film The Intouchables (2011), which was inspired by the friendship between Abdel Sellou and Philippe Pozzo di Borgo. Bryan Cranston plays Phillip Lacasse, a wealthy quadriplegic, and Kevin Hart plays Dell Scott, the paroled ex-convict he hires. Nicole Kidman plays Phillip's assistant Yvonne, with Golshifteh Farahani, Aja Naomi King and Julianna Margulies in supporting roles.

It opens with Dell speeding Phillip through New York in a Ferrari and talking police into a hospital escort. Six months earlier, Dell needs signatures proving he is looking for work to satisfy his parole officer. He walks into Phillip's penthouse during interviews for a live-in caregiver. Phillip, who has lost the will to live and has a strict do-not-resuscitate order, hires the unqualified Dell over Yvonne's objections, partly hoping his carelessness will let him die. Dell is trying to reconnect with his ex-wife Latrice and their son Anthony, to whom he gave a book stolen from Phillip's library. He makes mistakes and quickly collects two of Yvonne's "three strikes", but Phillip protects him. When Phillip struggles to breathe, Dell refuses to let him die.

The two men gradually become friends. Dell takes Phillip out into the city and shares marijuana to ease his nerve pain. Phillip explains that he was paralyzed in a paragliding accident and still grieves for his late wife. He introduces Dell to opera and art, and a neighbor buys Dell's first painting for $50,000. Dell encourages Phillip to meet Lily, a woman he has been writing letters to. When the date goes badly, Phillip lashes out and fires Dell. Some time later, Dell has bought a new home for his family and is building motorized wheelchairs. When the physical therapist Maggie tells him Phillip has sunk into depression, Dell takes him on the speeding drive from the opening scene and then on a paragliding trip, and he reunites Phillip with Yvonne.

The film premiered at the 2017 Toronto International Film Festival but was shelved after the Harvey Weinstein scandal. STX Entertainment and Lantern Entertainment released it on January 11, 2019, and it opened at number one, ending Aquaman's run at the top of the box office. It grossed about $122 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed. Critics praised the chemistry between Cranston and Hart, but Rotten Tomatoes called it preachy and clichéd.

documents.title: Kiss and Cry
documents.overview: A romantic drama based on the story of Carley Allison, a promising 18 year old figure skater and singer who made medical history in her fight against a rare 1 in 3.5 billion type of sarcoma.
documents.plot:
Kiss and Cry is a 2017 Canadian biographical drama directed by Sean Cisterna about the life of Carley Allison, a young Toronto figure skater and singer who was diagnosed with an extremely rare form of cancer. It stars Carley's real-life friend Sarah Fisher as Carley and Luke Bilyk as her boyfriend John Servinis, with Chantal Kreviazuk and Sergio Di Zio as her parents. The film was shot at real locations from Carley's life in Toronto, including her home and bedroom, her skating rink, classrooms and hospitals.

Seventeen-year-old Carley Allison is a talented competitive figure skater hoping to earn a place on Canada's national team. She loves to sing, has a close and supportive family and a wide circle of friends, and lives by the motto "always smile". At a party she meets John, a kind and handsome classmate from her biology class, and the two begin dating. Then Carley begins to suffer severe shortness of breath, which is first dismissed as asthma. After she collapses on a date, doctors discover a rare cancerous tumor next to her trachea.

Determined to beat the disease, Carley undergoes surgery on her trachea and chemotherapy, facing each setback with humor and optimism and sharing her experiences through a blog and videos posted online, which attract a large following and even words of encouragement from Selena Gomez. John stands by her, asks her to the prom and lets her teach him to skate. She takes part in fundraising for cancer research and describes treating cancer like a contact sport. After her treatment appears to succeed, she returns to the ice and is invited to sing "O Canada" before a televised National Hockey League game, but the disease later returns in her lungs, and Carley dies at the age of nineteen.

Throughout the film, Fisher breaks the fourth wall, speaking words taken directly from the real Carley Allison's blog posts and video performances, and the letter Carley addresses to cancer is drawn partly from her own writing.

Kiss and Cry was released in Canada in February 2017. The Carley's Angels Foundation, established in her honor, helps families cover the high costs of medical treatment.

documents.title: Wish Upon
documents.tagline: Be careful what you wish for
documents.overview: A teenage girl discovers a box with magical powers, but those powers comes with a deadly price.
documents.plot:
Wish Upon is a 2017 American supernatural thriller film directed by Rob Cohen and written by Chris Bower. The movie stars Britt Robertson, Nicholas Galitzine, and Jacki Weaver.

The story revolves around Lena Grayson (Britt Robertson), a high school student who has just moved to a new town with her mother, Kate (Jacki Weaver). Lena's father died in a tragic accident when she was young, and she struggles to cope with the loss. She is haunted by nightmares and feels like an outcast among her peers.

On her 18th birthday, Lena discovers an antique music box in her attic that belonged to her deceased father. As soon as she winds it up, she makes a wish for revenge against those who have wronged her in the past. However, she soon realizes that her wishes are being granted in unexpected and terrifying ways.

Lena's first wish is granted when her stepfather, John (Matthew Glave), is involved in a car accident, leaving him severely injured. As Lena continues to make more wishes, her life becomes increasingly chaotic and violent. She starts to lose control of her desires, and the lines between reality and fantasy begin to blur.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Lena's wishes are being manipulated by an ancient entity known as "The Devil" (voiced by Sam Elliott). The entity is using Lena's emotions and desires against her, causing her to wreak havoc on those around her. Lena soon realizes that she must find a way to break free from the entity's control before it's too late.

In a desperate attempt to undo the damage, Lena turns to an unlikely ally: her stepfather, John. Together, they embark on a perilous journey to uncover the secrets of the music box and the ancient entity that is controlling Lena. Along the way, Lena must confront her own dark past and the true nature of her desires.

As the climax approaches, Lena faces off against The Devil in a final showdown. With the help of John and her newfound understanding of herself, Lena manages to outsmart the entity and break free from its control. In the end, she learns to let go of her anger and resentment, embracing a more positive and empowering path forward.

Throughout the movie, Wish Upon explores themes of grief, trauma, and the dangers of unchecked desire. The film features a mix of supernatural horror elements and coming-of-age drama, making it a unique and captivating watch.

documents.title: The Spacewalker
documents.tagline: So far from home, so close to disaster
documents.overview: March 1965. In the heat of the Cold War, the USA and the USSR are competing for supremacy in space. What both superpowers aim for in this race, is to be the first to have a man walk in outer space. To accomplish that, no price is too high and no risk is too great. Now it’s up to the unlikely duo of a seasoned war veteran and a hot-headed test-pilot to fulfill this mission. Two men in a tiny spaceship, without proper testing, facing the complete unknown. They were supposed to do what no man has done before—and no man imagined what would happen next.
documents.plot:
The Spacewalker (Russian: Время первых, Vremya Pervykh), also known as The Age of Pioneers or Spacewalk, is a 2017 Russian historical drama film about the cosmonaut Alexei Leonov, the first person to walk in space, who served as a consultant on the production. Directed by Dmitry Kiselyov and co-produced by Timur Bekmambetov and Yevgeny Mironov, it stars Mironov as Leonov and Konstantin Khabensky as the mission commander Pavel Belyayev, with Vladimir Ilyin as the chief designer Sergei Korolev and Alexandra Ursuliak as Leonov's wife Svetlana.

In the 1960s, at the height of the Space Race, the Soviet Union prepares to send a man out of his spacecraft and into open space. A technician dies during construction, engineers doubt the craft's safety, and the Kosmos 57 test vehicle, a stand-in for Voskhod 2, breaks up two weeks before launch for reasons no one can identify. The former wartime pilot Belyayev and the test pilot Leonov are chosen to fly, but when Pavel injures his leg in a parachute landing he is replaced by the young, inexperienced Yevgeny Khrunov, to Alexei's dismay. Pavel recovers through sheer determination and is reinstated. Voskhod 2 launches and Alexei completes his spacewalk to national celebration, but his suit swells so much that he cannot get back into the airlock while the ship is out of contact with ground control. Defying procedure, he enters head first, partly deflates the suit and twists round to close the jammed outer hatch, running out of oxygen and losing consciousness before Pavel pulls him inside and revives him. Ordered to orbit for 22 hours until an automatic landing sequence, the crew detach the airlock, setting the craft spinning, and then find the oxygen pressure rising to dangerous levels. Pavel collapses, and Alexei, hallucinating about his childhood, manages to disconnect the faulty system. When the automatic landing fails, the cosmonauts are allowed to steer manually, and Pavel brings the ship down in the Ural mountains, far off course. Their radio signals are picked up only by an amateur enthusiast on Sakhalin, and a rescue helicopter about to turn back for lack of fuel finally spots Alexei's flare. The two men are later cheered by huge crowds in Moscow.

Released in Russia in April 2017, the film was widely praised by Russian critics, who compared it to Apollo 13, but its gross of 561 million roubles against a 400 million rouble budget was considered a box-office failure.

documents.title: Wolfwalkers
documents.tagline: Be fierce. Be wild. Be free.
documents.overview: In a time of superstition and magic, when wolves are seen as demonic and nature an evil to be tamed, a young apprentice hunter comes to Ireland with her father to wipe out the last pack. But when she saves a wild native girl, their friendship leads her to discover the world of the Wolfwalkers and transform her into the very thing her father is tasked to destroy.
documents.plot:
Wolfwalkers is a 2020 Irish-French-Belgian animated fantasy drama film directed by Tomm Moore and Ross Stewart, produced by Cartoon Saloon and Canal+. The film takes place in 17th-century Ireland and follows the story of a young girl named Robyn, who lives with her grandfather, Eira, on the outskirts of a village.

The story begins with Robyn's fascination with wolves, which is forbidden by the villagers. According to local legend, wolves are evil creatures that roam the forest, preying on humans. However, Robyn believes that there is more to the wolves than meets the eye. She spends most of her days exploring the forest and learning about the wolves from her grandfather.

One day, a wolfwalker, a person who can communicate with and control wolves, arrives in the village. The wolfwalker's name is Aisling, and she is on a mission to protect the wolves from being hunted by humans. Robyn is immediately drawn to Aisling and becomes fascinated with the idea of becoming a wolfwalker herself.

As Robyn spends more time with Aisling, she learns about the ancient traditions and rituals that are necessary for a wolfwalker to communicate with the wolves. She also discovers that there is a dark force at work in the forest, threatening the balance between humans and wolves.

The plot thickens as Robyn and Aisling embark on a journey to uncover the source of the darkness and put an end to it. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles and challenges, including treacherous terrain, hostile villagers, and even a group of ruthless hunters who are determined to destroy the wolves.

As the story unfolds, Robyn learns valuable lessons about courage, loyalty, and the importance of respecting the natural world. She also discovers that she has a special connection with the wolves, which sets her on a path towards becoming a wolfwalker in her own right.

The film's climax features an epic battle between the forces of light and darkness, with Robyn and Aisling at the forefront. In the end, they succeed in defeating the dark force and restoring balance to the forest ecosystem.

Throughout the film, the animation is stunning, with beautifully rendered landscapes and characters that bring the story to life. The voice acting is also superb, with Saoirse Ronan delivering a standout performance as Robyn.

Overall, Wolfwalkers is a beautifully crafted film that explores themes of environmentalism, conservation, and the importance of respecting the natural world. With its stunning animation and engaging storyline, it's a must-see for fans of animated films and fantasy adventures.

documents.title: From Straight A's to XXX
documents.tagline: Inspired by a true story
documents.overview: When a change of circumstances leaves Miriam unable to pay her college tuition, she makes a surprising decision: to start performing in adult films, using the pseudonym Belle Knox. Miriam lies to her family and her friends at school, keeping her double life a secret. But soon rumours spread and Miriam becomes the subject of vicious online attacks and unwanted attention. Miriam fights back: she talks to the media, saying her new line of work empowers her as a feminist. But her confident stand has unintended consequences. Miriam is shunned by her conservative family and her colleagues in the adult film world. One impulsive decision has quickly spiralled out of control - and Miriam's problems are just beginning.
documents.plot:
From Straight A's to XXX is a 2017 biographical drama television film directed by Vanessa Parise and written by Anne-Marie Hess, inspired by the story of Miriam Weeks, the Duke University student who performed in adult films as Belle Knox. Produced by Sepia Films and Just Singer Entertainment, it stars Haley Pullos as Miriam, with Judd Nelson, Sasha Clements and Jessica Lu. It premiered on 11 February 2017. Weeks herself was not involved in the production and did not authorise it; the script was based on interviews she had given to newspapers and television.

In 2013, Miriam, a high-achieving student who campaigns on behalf of victims of abuse, is admitted to Duke, but without financial aid. Her father promises to pay her tuition, but after she moves into her dormitory he leaves for work in Afghanistan, and her mother tells her the family cannot afford the fees and suggests a student loan. Desperate, Miriam half-jokingly considers adult films, applies online as Belle Knox, and accepts a shoot in New York, afterwards crying in a bathroom. She then signs with an agent, Don (Nelson), who books her work in Los Angeles. Lying to her family about where the tuition money comes from, she keeps her double life secret until a classmate, Jeff, recognises her, swears to keep quiet and then spreads the news anonymously online.

As rumours spread, Miriam faces vicious online attacks and unwanted attention. She fights back by giving an interview to the student newspaper's reporter Amanda (Lu), describing her work as empowering and feminist, but the published piece distorts her words, and once Belle Knox's identity becomes public she is condemned by many. She tells her conservative family, meeting her mother's condemnation and her father's rejection, appears live on CNN, and later finds her parents ready to accept her, though her brother disowns her. At an adult film awards ceremony in Las Vegas she is shunned by colleagues over her outspoken interviews. The film ends in January 2015, with Miriam giving a motivational speech on women's rights and freedom of choice and telling Amanda that she plans to go into politics.

Reviews were mixed. Lifetime Uncorked gave it four out of five, and The Solute recommended it despite plot holes and an unclear heroine, while The Best Darn Girls gave it three out of five, finding its message muddled. AVN's Peter Warren criticised it as ill-informed about the adult industry and more fiction than biography.

documents.title: Night Hunter
documents.tagline: When the predator becomes the prey
documents.overview: A Minnesota police officer crosses paths with a committed and tireless vigilante as he follows the trail of a ruthless predator responsible for several abductions and murders.
documents.plot:
Night Hunter, originally titled Nomis, is a 2018 Canadian crime thriller written and directed by David Raymond. Henry Cavill stars as Detective Walter Marshall, with Ben Kingsley as a former judge turned vigilante, Alexandra Daddario as a police profiler, Stanley Tucci, Brendan Fletcher as the suspect Simon Stulls, Minka Kelly and Nathan Fillion. It premiered at the Los Angeles Film Festival in September 2018 and was released on video on demand in August 2019 and in theaters that September by Saban Films.

When the body of a young woman is found on a logging truck in Minnesota, Detective Walter Marshall suspects that she leapt to her death to escape a captor. A breakthrough comes unexpectedly when Michael Cooper, a former judge who runs vigilante stings to trap sexual predators, sees one of his operations go wrong and his young ward, Lara, is abducted. Tracking her through a device hidden in her earrings, Marshall finds Lara and several other captive women in a house owned by Simon Stulls, a man who appears to be intellectually disabled.

Simon is arrested, and police profiler Rachel Chase, played by Daddario, tries to determine whether he could really be behind the abductions. Investigating his past, they learn that he was conceived through rape and that his mother attempted suicide before he was born. While Simon is in custody, the police themselves come under attack: a technician is killed by a car bomb, and another is forced to free Simon after his infant daughter is threatened. The police recapture Simon after he has killed his own father, just as Cooper discovers that Lara has been taken again. Convinced that Simon is responsible, Cooper ambushes the police transport but encounters a man who looks exactly like him. It is revealed that Simon has an identical twin, and the two brothers have been working together. As the twin's plan targets those closest to the investigation, Marshall, who is also struggling with his estrangement from his wife and daughter, races to stop him.

Night Hunter received negative reviews, with a 14 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it contrived and clichéd, wasting a solid cast, and a Metacritic score of 31.

documents.tagline: You gotta go low to get high.
documents.overview: An irreverent comedy about the misadventures of Moondog, a rebellious stoner and lovable rogue who lives large.

documents.title: Ash Is Purest White
documents.tagline: In a world in ruins, love and loyalty burn out, but never disappear.
documents.overview: Set in China's underworld, this tale of love and betrayal follows a dancer who fired a gun to protect her mobster boyfriend during a fight. On release from prison 5 years later, she sets out to find him.
documents.plot:
In 2001, Qiao and her boyfriend Bin, a mob boss, have a lot of power in Datong, an old mining city that has become poor since the coal prices dropped. After Bin's boss is murdered, Qiao suggests they run away from everything and get married, but Bin is not interested. One night a group of motorcyclists attack Bin and his driver, claiming to dethrone him. Qiao grabs Bin's handgun and fires two warning shots into the air, scaring off the attackers.
The police tell Qiao that the gun is illegally owned and asks her whose it is; she repeatedly claims it is hers. She spends five years in prison for possessing an illegal firearm but Bin does not visit her during that time. After Qiao is released, she tries to call him but can never seem to get in touch. She travels by boat to the city in Hubei province where Bin is living but is instead greeted by Bin's new girlfriend—meanwhile, Bin hides in another room. Qiao says that if he wants to break up with her, he will have to tell her himself. She has almost no money to her name so she cons a few strangers for money and food. She hires a motorcycle driver to take her to the power plant where she thinks that Bin works, and along the way the driver suggests that they have sex. She uses this opportunity to steal his bike, and when she gets to the power plant she reports to a police officer that the driver tried to rape her and that he should call her boyfriend Bin. This finally forces Bin to see her.
In a hotel room, Bin says he's a changed man, no longer a "jianghu" gangster, and has no place in his life for Qiao anymore. He can never go back to Datong because he has lost all the respect he once had there. Qiao says that she saved his life and took the blame for him: he should have been waiting for her the day she got out of prison. Since he refuses to say it, she finally says that their relationship is over and he leaves. On a train back to Datong, she meets a passenger who claims to be developing a UFO-hunting tourism company and invites her to join him after she claims to have seen one herself. But after they transfer onto another train, he admits that it was all a lie. She gets off the train, sees a bright object fly swiftly overhead, and makes her way back to Datong.
In 2017, Qiao gets a call from Bin, and when she picks him up, finds him using a wheelchair. She brings him back to their old gambling parlor where she now works and many of his old friends are happy to see him. He is closed-off and hot-tempered, immediately starting fights, and Qiao nearly throws him out. He tells her that he had a stroke from drinking too much and she finds a doctor to help rehabilitate him. When he can walk again, he sneaks out of Qiao's building with just a brief voicemail to say he has left. Qiao goes to the front door when she learns he has gone but she cannot see him.

documents.title: Veronica
documents.tagline: Someone answered your call.
documents.overview: Madrid, June 1991. After celebrating a session of Ouija with her friends, Verónica is besieged by dangerous supernatural presences that threaten to harm her entire family.
documents.plot:
Veronica (Spanish: Verónica) is a Spanish supernatural horror film of 2017 directed by Paco Plaza, who wrote it with Fernando Navarro. Loosely inspired by a 1991 case in Madrid's Vallecas district, in which a teenager died mysteriously after a Ouija board séance, it stars Sandra Escacena as Verónica, with Bruna González and Claudia Placer as her twin sisters Lucía and Irene, Iván Chavero as her little brother Antoñito, Ana Torrent as her mother Ana and Consuelo Trujillo as the blind nun known as Sister Death.

The film opens with a panicked emergency call from a young girl on 15 June 1991, then jumps back three days. Fifteen-year-old Verónica lives in working-class Vallecas, and since her father's death she has looked after her younger siblings while her mother works long hours. On the day of a solar eclipse, after a lesson about ancient cultures summoning dark spirits during eclipses, she and her friends Rosa and Diana hold a séance in the school basement, hoping to contact her father and Diana's dead boyfriend. As the eclipse peaks, the glass shatters, Verónica's blood drips onto the board, and she falls into a trance and screams.

Paranormal events follow her home, and her friends shun her. Sister Death tells her that a dark spirit has attached itself to her and that she must protect her siblings, and later reveals that she blinded herself to escape her own visions. Verónica finds body-shaped burn marks on the children's mattresses, and is horrified to discover that the hand choking Lucía was her own. Learning that a séance must be closed by bidding the spirit farewell, and that she whispered during the first one that she would die in three days, she holds a new séance with her siblings, but Antoñito copies the wrong symbols and the spirit refuses to leave. Fleeing with the children, she realises she is only imagining Antoñito beside her, and when she sees the demon in the mirror she understands that she herself has been possessed all along. The police burst in to find her levitating under an invisible attack; she dies, and a shaken detective records that he witnessed unexplained events, said to be the first such police report in Spain.

Released in Spain on 25 August 2017 and later on Netflix, Veronica grossed about $6.1 million worldwide. Critics found it genuinely frightening, giving it 86% on Rotten Tomatoes, and it earned several Goya Award nominations.

documents.title: Proud Mary
documents.tagline: Killing for the Man every Night and Day
documents.overview: Mary is a hit woman working for an organized crime family in Boston, whose life is completely turned around when she meets a young boy whose path she crosses when a professional hit goes bad.
documents.plot:
In Boston, assassin Mary Goodwin kills her target Marcus Miller in his apartment. Before leaving, she notices Marcus’ young son Danny in his room, oblivious to her presence. A year later, Danny – unaware Mary has been keeping an eye on him – is working for a drug dealer who calls himself Uncle. When a customer, Jerome, tries to short him, Danny pulls a gun and takes the full payment plus a premium. He buys himself food and delivers the money to Uncle, who beats him for taking a portion of the extra money. Dazed, Danny rests on a bench, but a man steals his bag, forcing Danny to chase him and fire in the air. The thief drops the bag, but Danny faints and is found by Mary.
Danny awakens in Mary's home, and she offers him food and first aid. Noticing the marks from Uncle's abuse, Mary confronts the dealer, but she is forced to kill Uncle and his men. Leaving Danny at her apartment, Mary attends a meeting with her associates Tom, Walter, and their employer, mob boss Benny Spencer. They meet with Luka, who is Uncle's uncle and head of a rival mob, and assure him that they had nothing to do with Uncle's death. Mary encourages Benny's suspicion that Walter was responsible for eliminating Uncle and his crew, and Benny instructs her to kill Walter. Discovering Mary's cache of guns, Danny opens up to Mary about his life, unaware she is his father's killer.
Mary follows Walter on his routine jog and kills him. Luka sends his men to ambush Benny, killing several members of his crew. Determined to retaliate, Tom – Benny's son and Mary's ex-boyfriend – visits Mary's apartment and questions Danny. Tom tortures one of Luka's men, learning of an upcoming meeting of Luka and his crew, and Benny invites Mary to bring Danny to his wife Mina's birthday dinner. Buying Danny new clothes, Mary tells him about her similar childhood and coaches him on what to say to Benny, warning that he is not to be trusted. At the dinner, Mary tells Benny that she wants to leave her criminal life behind, and Tom confronts her, having deduced that Danny is Marcus’ son.
Mary tells Danny to start a new life elsewhere with her stash of money, should anything happen to her. Before Tom and Mary storm Luka's hideout, he warns her that Benny will not let her leave his crew alive as she knows too much. The two kill Luka's entire crew, but Mary is wounded in the attack and they fail to find Luka. Refusing Tom's help, Mary returns home and tells a shaken Danny that Benny will never release her. Danny goes to Benny's office – where he is spotted by Jerome, who works for Benny – and demands that Mary be allowed to move on, holding Benny at gunpoint. Having learned Danny's true identity from Tom, Benny tells Danny the truth about his father's death and takes the gun, but Mary appears. Sending Danny away, she pleads with Benny to let her go, but he refuses, declaring that she must train Danny as an assassin. Mary kills Benny and escapes unseen.

documents.title: The Last Full Measure
documents.tagline: The ultimate sacrifice deserves the highest honor.
documents.overview: The incredible true story of Vietnam War hero William H. Pitsenbarger, a U.S. Air Force Pararescuemen medic who personally saved over sixty men. Thirty-two years later, Pentagon staffer Scott Huffman investigates a Congressional Medal of Honor request for Pitsenbarger and uncovers a high-level conspiracy behind the decades-long denial of the medal, prompting Huffman to put his own career on the line to seek justice for the fallen airman.

documents.title: The First Purge
documents.tagline: A Nation Reborn
documents.overview: To push the crime rate below one percent for the rest of the year, the New Founding Fathers of America test a sociological theory that vents aggression for one night in one isolated community. But when the violence of oppressors meets the rage of the others, the contagion will explode from the trial-city borders and spread across the nation.
documents.plot:
In 2014, rising unemployment, rising inflation, and a housing crisis led to the New Founding Fathers of America (NFFA) becoming the most powerful political party in the United States, with NFFA candidate Bracken being elected president in 2016. Later that year, NFFA chief of staff Arlo Sabian and sociologist Dr. May Updale announce an experiment to take place on Staten Island: for 12 hours, citizens will be allowed to release their inhibitions in any way they choose, including murder. Meanwhile, crazed drug addict Skeletor talks about his desires to "purge" and unleash his hatred of others with an NFFA employee. The NFFA offers residents $5,000 to stay on Staten Island during the experiment, with additional compensation if they join the Purge and survive. They also outfit the participants with contact lens cameras to monitor all activity and put tracking devices in them to know if they try to leave the island.
Low-lying gang boss and businessman Dmitri Cimber tells his associates that they will not be leaving the island, as moving his money and product will draw too much attention, and tells them to stay in a safe house and lay low. Drug dealer Capital A disobeys and joins the Purge, while a rookie named Isaiah is attacked and injured by Skeletor. Isaiah goes to his sister Nya, an anti-Purge activist and Dmitri's ex-girlfriend, for treatment. As people flee Staten Island, Nya joins her friends Dolores, Luisa, and Selina in a church to wait out the Purge. Dmitri has stayed behind; Anna and Elsa, two prostitutes, are sent by his dealers to his office to keep him company. Skeletor commits the first Purge murder, and the video recorded by the NFFA goes viral. The NFFA observes that all crimes taking place are minor, unlike the expected violent ones like murder.
Isaiah secretly joins the Purge to get his revenge on Skeletor. When Skeletor disrupts a party taking place and Isaiah is unable to muster the courage to kill him, he runs off into more Purgers before hiding and calling Nya for help. Anna and Elsa, who are actually Purgers, attempt to kill Dmitri, who fights them off and learns that Capital A sent them so he could take over Dmitri's business. Skeletor captures Nya in the streets, but Isaiah stabs him, and they escape. Capital A and his crew go to Dmitri's office to meet with Anna and Elsa. However, Dmitri and his gang ambush him and kill them all, except for Anna and Elsa, whom they tell to leave. Nya and Isaiah return to the church to see blood-soaked white supremacist bikers leaving while Nya's friend, Luisa, and her daughter, Selina, survive. They all return to Nya's apartment, where Dolores makes it safely.
At the NFFA headquarters, Updale becomes suspicious of an increase in murder and masked participants' presence. Reviewing the video footage of the Purge, she notices vans full of masked killers arriving and realizes that they are mercenary groups killing civilians.

documents.title: Don't Worry, He Won't Get Far on Foot
documents.original_title: Don't Worry, He Won't Get Far on Foot
documents.tagline: Don't just sit there. Do nothing.
documents.overview: On the rocky path to sobriety after a life-changing accident, John Callahan discovers the healing power of art, willing his injured hands into drawing hilarious, often controversial cartoons, which bring him a new lease on life.

documents.title: Moontrap: Target Earth
documents.overview: A long forgotten ancient spacecraft discovered on Earth. Investigations carried out by Scout transport her to the moon whereupon she meets the impressive machines preserving the wisdom of that long lost civilization.
documents.plot:
Moontrap: Target Earth is a 2017 American science fiction film directed by Robert Dyke and written by Dyke and Tex Ragsdale, the team behind the 1989 cult film Moontrap, to which it is a belated follow-up with only a few nods to the original. Produced by MT2 Productions, it stars Sarah Butler as Sharon "Scout" Turner, Damon Dayoub as Daniel Allen and Charles Shaughnessy as Richard Kontral, with Jennifer Kincer, Niki Spiridakos, Chris Newman, Cara AnnMarie and Steven Dutton. First reported in 2014, it was released directly to DVD after a long delay.

An enormous ancient artifact is unearthed in a desert quarry. When its discoverer, Brian Carter (Newman), is murdered by Nicole (Kincer), the henchwoman of Kontral, an agent of a shadowy cabal, Kontral hires the researcher Daniel Allen and his assistant and lover Scout to translate the inscriptions on it, which reveal a 14,000-year-old love letter from a woman to her god. The object proves to be a spacecraft left behind by an advanced human civilization that predates recorded history, and it still appears to be functional. Once their work is done, the cabal tries to eliminate them; Daniel is killed and Scout, framed for his death, goes on the run, troubled by visions of an unknown woman who seems to be guiding her. Captured, she turns out to have a mysterious connection with the craft, and her presence awakens a red robot, which takes her and Kontral aboard and flies them to the Moon. There a blue robot attacks; Kontral tries to escape in the ship, and the two machines fight until the red one is destroyed. Using a stone it carried, Scout activates an ancient temple that gives the Moon a breathable atmosphere. Inside she finds Garen, the god of the Krell people, in stasis, and learns from Mya, the woman of her visions, that she has been chosen to fulfill Mya's failed destiny. Scout joins Garen in suspended animation, and the first plants sprout on the lunar surface.

Sony released the film on DVD in the United States in early 2017, and Gilt Edge Media issued it in the United Kingdom. Reviews were negative. Phil Wheat of Nerdly, a fan of the original, found it structurally confusing, like a fevered dream, and slow to reach the Moon, though he welcomed the return of the robots and its grotesque finale. Mana Pop called the script incoherent and the effects among the cheapest it had seen, and the German Lexikon des internationalen Films judged that it failed through both lack of competence and lack of money.

documents.title: Leave No Trace
documents.overview: A father and daughter live a perfect but mysterious existence in Forest Park, a beautiful nature reserve near Portland, Oregon, rarely making contact with the world. But when a small mistake tips them off to authorities, they are sent on an increasingly erratic journey in search of a place to call their own.
documents.plot:
Leave No Trace is a 2018 American drama film directed by Debra Granik, who wrote the screenplay with Anne Rosellini, based on Peter Rock's 2009 novel My Abandonment, which is loosely based on a true story. It stars Ben Foster as a military veteran with post-traumatic stress disorder and Thomasin McKenzie as his teenage daughter, who live off the grid in the forest.

Will, a veteran suffering from PTSD, lives with his daughter Tom in the old-growth Forest Park in Portland, Oregon. Relying on survival skills, they go into town only occasionally for supplies, and Will earns money by selling the benzodiazepines prescribed to him by veterans' health services to another homeless veteran. After a jogger spots Tom in the woods, the two are picked up by park rangers and taken into the care of social services. They are given a house on a Christmas tree farm in rural Oregon in exchange for Will's work there. Will reluctantly packs trees, while Tom befriends a local boy building his own tiny house, who introduces her to the 4-H youth club.

Wearied by social services' constant check-ins and paperwork, Will suddenly decides to leave one morning, and Tom follows reluctantly. Their old camp in the park has been destroyed, so they hitch a ride with a trucker to Washington state and move into a vacant cabin in the forest. When Will goes out for food and fails to return, Tom finds him unconscious at the bottom of a ravine with a badly injured foot. Local quad bikers take them to their mobile home community, where Tom refuses to let him go to a hospital. A former Army medic, also suffering from PTSD, treats Will and lends him his service dog to ease his nightmares, and the pair are given an empty trailer. Tom learns beekeeping, comes to love the community and quietly tries to arrange to rent the trailer. When Will insists on leaving again, Tom tells him that what is wrong with him is not wrong with her. Acknowledging that he would stay if he could, they tearfully part; Will returns to the woods while Tom goes back to the community, later leaving a package of food hanging in the forest for him.

Shot in Portland in spring 2017, the film premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2018 and was released by Bleecker Street on June 29, 2018. It received universal acclaim, with a Metacritic score of 88, and became the most reviewed film to hold a 100% rating on Rotten Tomatoes; critics singled out Foster's and McKenzie's performances.
