documents.title: The Kid Who Would Be King
documents.original_title: The Kid Who Would Be King
documents.tagline: An army to fight. A demon to slay. A world to save. No pressure.
documents.overview: Old-school magic meets the modern world when young Alex stumbles upon the mythical sword Excalibur. He soon unites his friends and enemies, and they become knights who join forces with the legendary wizard Merlin. Together, they must save mankind from the wicked enchantress Morgana and her army of supernatural warriors.
documents.plot:
Alex is a thirteenen-year-old boy, who is a Year 7 student in a London suburb. When his best friend Bedders is bullied by older students, Lance and Kaye, Alex comes to his aid. Alex, Lance, and Kaye are given detention by the headmistress.
Lance and Kaye plot to harm Alex. That night, the duo chase Alex as he heads home, but Alex hides in a nearby construction site, where he finds and extracts a mysterious sword embedded in concrete. Later showing it to Bedders, they discover that its markings identify it as Excalibur, the sword of King Arthur. Alex then playfully "knights" Bedders.
The wicked sorceress Morgana awakens underground and sends her Mortes Milles demons after Excalibur. The next day, a teenager appears from inside Stonehenge and presents himself at Alex's school as a new student. The boy reveals himself to Alex as the wizard Merlin, capable of aging backward, but will occasionally shift into his elder Arthurian form. Alex plans to return the sword, wanting nothing to do with ancient myths. That night, Merlin saves Alex from a demon and explains that he has four days to destroy Morgana, or she will enslave all of Britain.
The Mortes Milles only appear at night and can only be seen by Alex and those he has knighted, but an upcoming total solar eclipse will enable Morgana to emerge fully into the world. Alex realizes that these events parallel an inscribed storybook his estranged father once gave him. Alex concludes he descends from Arthur through his father and later recruits and knights Lance and Kaye, who fight beside Alex and Bedders, defeating three demons with a car. Alex declares them a new Round Table. Merlin soon tasks Alex to find the entrance of Morgana's Underworld prison.
Alex leads the group to Tintagel, where he last saw his father. En route, Merlin trains them in swordsmanship. But when Morgana infiltrates the lesson, Lance betrays Alex and takes the sword for himself. Merlin barely saves them, and Excalibur is destroyed when Alex and Lance come to blows in a marsh. As Lance and Kaye start to leave, Alex calls upon the Lady of the Lake, whose arm emerges from the water and restores the sword.
Resolving their differences and rededicating themselves to the quest, the four overcome a horde of demons by luring them over a cliff. Arriving at Tintagel, Alex meets his aunt Sophie who tells him that his father was an alcoholic who abandoned Alex and his mother, Mary. Sophie reveals that it was Mary who inscribed the book, which enrages Alex, feeling his mother is a liar, and he has come a long way for nothing. Merlin stops him, telling Alex that Excalibur is not handed down by birthright, but by individual merit.
Alex and his friends arm themselves, and Alex uses the storybook to locate the entrance to the Underworld. Alex challenges Morgana, who takes on a monstrous form and breathes fire, but Alex strikes her down, and the children escape.

documents.title: Magic Camp
documents.tagline: Escape to Magic Camp!
documents.overview: Andy, at the urging of his former mentor and Magic Camp owner Roy Preston, returns to the camp of his youth hoping to reignite his career. Instead, he finds inspiration in his ragtag bunch of rookie magicians.
documents.plot:
Theo Moses is an aspiring young magician coping with the death of his father. His mother reveals his acceptance video from the Institute of Magic, a summer camp run by the eccentric Roy Preston; assuming his father applied for him, Theo agrees to attend. Andy Duckerman is a down-on-his-luck former magician with a grudge against the famous Kristina Darkwood, who has a successful solo act on the Las Vegas strip. Preston persuades Andy, his former student, to return to camp as a counselor alongside Darkwood.
At camp, the students are split into four different cabins to face each other in the end-of-year Top Hat competition, where one student will win the coveted Golden Wand. Andy is assigned to lead the Hearts cabin, including Theo; allergy-prone Nathan Jenkins; rabbit-obsessed Ruth Brusselbach; Judd Kessler, the less talented son of a famous magician; and antisocial Vera Costa. Darkwood leads the Diamonds, including previous Golden Wand winner and bully Vic d'Antonio, and Janelle Santos, who takes a liking to Theo.
The inexperienced Hearts struggle to learn magic, and a frustrated Andy almost quits, but discovers that Theo has a gift for card tricks. Determined to beat Darkwood, Andy helps the Hearts realize their hidden talents: Judd embraces costume design, Ruth has an affinity for birds over bunnies, Nathan can perform impressive mental calculations, and Vera begins to make friends. Helping Theo overcome his stage fright, Andy reveals that he and Darkwood met as campers, and became a couple as well as magic partners; she accepted a television deal behind his back, and her career took off while he fell into obscurity.
Darkwood convinces Janelle, whose wealthy parents send her to various camps instead of spending time with her, to give magic a chance. Attempting to humiliate Nathan, Vic is outdone by Theo and seemingly burns Theo's cards – a gift from his father, who introduced him to magic. Distraught, Theo bonds with Andy and his fellow Hearts, as well as Janelle. After the Diamonds check out all the camp's props for themselves, Andy takes the Hearts into town to train with whatever they can find, and the young magicians perform their acts in public.
Andy confronts Darkwood, who already reprimanded her team, and she reveals the truth behind their falling out: she tried to negotiate a deal for both of them, which he never gave her a chance to explain. She has booked him a matinee in Vegas for the next day; with Preston's encouragement, Andy accepts, knowing he will miss the Hearts' training but be back in time for the Top Hat competition that night. Preston informs the Hearts that Andy has gone to Vegas, but after his successful matinee, Andy is invited to perform the evening show – at the same time as the competition.
The students' families, including Janelle's parents, arrive for the competition. Without Andy there, a nervous Theo is encouraged by Preston, who shows him the supportive video Theo's mother submitted as his application.

documents.title: Benedetta
documents.tagline: I don't know God's ways, but he works his will through me.
documents.overview: A 17th-century nun becomes entangled in a forbidden lesbian affair with a novice. But it is Benedetta's shocking religious visions that threaten to shake the Church to its core.
documents.plot:
In 17th-century Pescia, Italy, young Benedetta Carlini is enrolled by her parents in a Theatine convent run by Abbess Felicita, to become a nun. Eighteen years later, while playing the Virgin Mary in a play, Benedetta has a vision of Jesus calling to her. One day, a young peasant woman named Bartolomea seeks shelter in the convent from her abusive father. Benedetta is assigned to oversee Bartolomea's integration into convent life. That night, Bartolomea kisses Benedetta.
Benedetta begins to have recurring visions of Jesus. After a particularly fraught vision, where a man whom she mistakes for Jesus saves her from being gang-raped, Benedetta falls into a deep illness. Felicita assigns Bartolomea to look after her. Benedetta has another vision of Christ, asking her to undress and touch his hands. The next morning, she wakes up with stigmata on her palms and feet.
An investigation ensues. Felicita is skeptical because Benedetta's stigmata manifested while she was asleep, not during prayer, and her forehead lacks the marks of a crown of thorns. Outside Felicita's chambers, Benedetta collapses. She then begins speaking in an angry male voice, castigating those who doubt her, as bleeding wounds appear on her forehead. Sister Christina, Felicita's daughter, suspects that Benedetta's wounds are self-inflicted, after spotting a nearby shard of glass.
Following a dispute between Felicita and local church leaders about the way popular interest in Benedetta's visions should be handled, Benedetta is elevated to the position of abbess in place of Felicita. Benedetta and Bartolomea move into Felicita's old quarters and begin a sexual relationship, later using a dildo carved by Bartolomea out of Benedetta's wooden Virgin Mary statuette.
In confession, Christina lies to the priest that she witnessed Benedetta inflicting her forehead wounds. The next day, the priest compels Christina to say her accusations publicly. When questioned by the priest, Felicita refutes Christina's claims because Christina has previously admitted to her that she did not actually see the wounds being self-inflicted. Benedetta, apparently possessed by the spirit of Jesus, orders Christina to flagellate herself. Felicita later observes Benedetta and Bartolomea having sex in their chambers through a peephole.
Humiliated, Christina jumps to her death from the roof of the convent. As a plague begins to ravage the countryside, Benedetta has a vision that Pescia will be spared and orders the abbey closed to prevent infection. Felicita secretly travels to Florence to report Benedetta's sexual indiscretions to the local papal nuncio. Meanwhile, Benedetta suddenly dies of unknown causes.
Shortly after Felicita returns to the abbey with the nuncio, Benedetta revives, saying that she was in heaven and has seen the fates of all those present. The nuncio, as representative of the pope, opens a court of inquiry into Benedetta's conduct.

documents.title: Black Water
documents.tagline: Some secrets never surface
documents.overview: A deep cover operative awakens to find himself imprisoned on a submarine. With the help of a fellow prisoner and an amateur agent, he must race against the clock to escape the vessel and expose who set him up.
documents.plot:
Black Water is a 2018 American action thriller directed by Pasha Patriki, starring Jean-Claude Van Damme and Dolph Lundgren in their fifth collaboration and only their second as on-screen allies. Patrick Kilpatrick, Al Sapienza, Jasmine Waltz, Aaron O'Connell, Courtney B. Turk and John Posey round out the cast. The film was released direct to video in the United States on May 25, 2018.

Scott Wheeler, a deep-cover CIA operative, wakes up as a prisoner in a secret CIA black site housed aboard a retrofitted nuclear submarine, alongside another captive named Marco. Through a series of memories he pieces together how he got there. Wheeler and his partner Melissa Ballard had been hunting for a leak within the agency using a USB drive that requires two components to operate: she carried the drive, while he kept the activation key. When armed men attacked their safe house, Ballard was apparently killed. Wheeler escaped, only to find his handler murdered, and was then captured by Agent Ferris, who believes Wheeler is responsible for the deaths of fellow agents.

Aboard the submarine, Wheeler realizes that Agent Rhodes, who claims to believe in his innocence, is in fact the traitor. Rhodes and his henchman kill the other CIA personnel and take control of the vessel's security team. Wheeler escapes and teams up with the rookie agent Cassie Taylor, while her partner Ellis Ryan is killed in an ambush. Together they force the submarine toward the surface and free Marco, a German special forces operative who knows too much to be released or killed. Rhodes plans to sell the drive, which holds information that would endanger agents around the world, and arranges an extraction in Cuba. As Wheeler and his allies fight through the narrow corridors, it is revealed that Ballard faked her death and has been working with Rhodes all along.

Writer Chad Law developed the project after producer Richard Switzer proposed an action film set on a submarine; Law and Switzer had previously worked with Lundgren on Altitude. Filming took place in early 2017, partly in Mobile, Alabama, and wrapped by the end of March. The film was poorly received, holding a 0% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on nine reviews, with an average score of 3.3 out of 10.

documents.title: Overboard
documents.tagline: A riches to rags story. If only he could remember it.
documents.overview: A spoiled, wealthy yacht owner is thrown overboard and becomes the target of revenge from his mistreated employee.
documents.plot:
Overboard is a 2018 American romantic comedy film directed by Tom Wheeler and written by Peter Chicago and Rich Wilkes. The movie stars Eugenio Derbez, Anna Faris, Eva Longoria, and John Lithgow.

The story begins with Captain Casey (Eugenio Derbez), a wealthy playboy who has made his fortune through various business ventures. He is known for his womanizing ways and has no qualms about taking advantage of those around him. One day, while on vacation in Mexico, Casey gets drunk and wakes up the next morning to find himself handcuffed to a bed with no memory of what happened.

As it turns out, Casey's wealthy fiancée, Delilah (Anna Faris), has been planning her wedding for months, but she is not ready to give up on their relationship. She decides to take drastic measures and hires two men to pretend to be Casey's friends, who will help her convince him that he needs to change his ways.

The plan works, and Casey starts to see Delilah in a new light. He begins to realize the mistakes he has made in his life and starts to make amends with those around him, including his business partner, Leon (Richard Portnow), who is being taken advantage of by Casey's antics.

As Casey gets to know Delilah again, they start to rekindle their romance. However, things get complicated when Casey discovers that he has been living a lie and that Delilah has been pretending to be his fiancée all along.

In the end, Casey must decide whether to continue with his newfound sense of responsibility or return to his old ways. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Casey and Delilah working together to build a better life for themselves and those around them.

Throughout the movie, Derbez delivers a charming performance as the lovable but flawed Casey, while Faris shines as the determined and independent Delilah. The chemistry between the leads is undeniable, making their romance feel genuine and heartfelt.

Overall, Overboard is a fun and lighthearted romantic comedy that explores themes of love, redemption, and personal growth. With its witty dialogue and engaging storyline, it's a great watch for fans of the genre.

documents.title: Sonic the Hedgehog
documents.tagline: A whole new speed of hero.
documents.overview: Powered with incredible speed, Sonic The Hedgehog embraces his new home on Earth. That is, until Sonic sparks the attention of super-uncool evil genius Dr. Robotnik. Now it’s super-villain vs. super-sonic in an all-out race across the globe to stop Robotnik from using Sonic’s unique power for world domination.
documents.plot:
Sonic the Hedgehog is a 2020 American live-action/animated comedy-adventure film directed by Jeff Fowler, produced by Neal H. Moritz and Terence Nance, and written by Pat Casey, Josh Miller, and John Whittington.

The movie follows the story of Sonic (voiced by Ben Schwartz), a blue anthropomorphic hedgehog with superhuman speed, who is on the run from Dr. Eggman (Jim Carrey), his arch-nemesis. Sonic lives in the Green Hill Zone, where he spends his days racing and having fun. However, when Dr. Eggman threatens to destroy the world using an army of robotic robots, Sonic decides to leave his home and find a new place to live.

Sonic arrives in the city of Greenhaven, where he meets Tom Wachowski (James Marsden), a single father who is struggling to connect with his 6-year-old son, Ben (Griffin Gluck). Despite initial reservations, Tom takes Sonic under his wing, and the two form an unlikely bond. As Sonic tries to adjust to life in the city, he must also evade Dr. Eggman's robots and stop him from carrying out his evil plans.

Throughout the movie, Sonic's character is portrayed as a lovable and mischievous troublemaker who often gets into humorous situations. The film features plenty of action-packed sequences, including high-speed chases and showdowns with Dr. Eggman's robots.

One of the standout aspects of the movie is its blend of live-action and animation. The CGI work is impressive, bringing Sonic to life in a way that feels both authentic and endearing. Jim Carrey's performance as Dr. Eggman is also noteworthy, capturing the character's manic energy and over-the-top personality.

Overall, Sonic the Hedgehog is a fun and entertaining film that brings the beloved video game character to the big screen. While it may not be a perfect adaptation, the movie's lighthearted tone and comedic moments make it a enjoyable watch for fans of the franchise and newcomers alike.

documents.title: The Angry Birds Movie 2
documents.tagline: Frenemies Unite
documents.overview: Red, Chuck, Bomb and the rest of their feathered friends are surprised when a green pig suggests that they put aside their differences and unite to fight a common threat. Aggressive birds from an island covered in ice are planning to use an elaborate weapon to destroy the fowl and swine.
documents.plot:
The Angry Birds Movie 2 is a 2019 animated comedy-adventure film directed by Fergal Reilly and Peter Burnham, produced by Columbia Pictures. The movie takes place after the events of the first film and follows the main characters as they face new challenges.

The story begins with the birds returning to their island home, where they are greeted as heroes for saving the world from the evil pigs. However, the peace is short-lived, as a new threat emerges in the form of a group of birds known as the "Guardians," who possess magical powers and claim that the birds' actions have disrupted the balance of nature.

The main character, Red (voiced by Jason Sudeikis), sets out on a journey to find the Guardians and learn more about their abilities. Along the way, he meets a new bird named Guy Diamond (voiced by Danny McBride), who becomes his ally in this quest.

As Red delves deeper into the world of magic, he discovers that the Guardians are being hunted by a group of ruthless birds known as the "Nerds," who seek to exploit their powers for their own gain. The Nerds are led by a character named King Sleazy (voiced by Bill Hader), a power-hungry bird with a penchant for manipulation.

Red and Guy Diamond soon find themselves in a battle against the Nerds, with the fate of the world hanging in the balance. Along the way, they meet new characters, including a wise old owl named Professor Oakley (voiced by Josh Gad) and a group of birds known as the "Guardians," who possess magical powers.

As the story unfolds, Red learns more about his own destiny and the true nature of the Guardians' powers. He also discovers that the Nerds are not the only threat to the world, but rather a symptom of a larger problem.

In the end, Red and his friends must band together to defeat the Nerds and restore balance to the natural world. The movie features plenty of action, humor, and heart, as the characters navigate their relationships and confront their fears.

Throughout the film, the animation is vibrant and colorful, with stunning visuals that bring the world of Angry Birds to life. The voice cast delivers strong performances, bringing depth and nuance to the characters.

Overall, The Angry Birds Movie 2 is a fun and entertaining film that explores themes of friendship, teamwork, and self-discovery. With its engaging storyline, lovable characters, and stunning animation, it's a must-see for fans of the franchise and animation enthusiasts alike.

documents.title: Monster Family
documents.overview: The Wishbone family are far from happy. In an attempt to reconnect as a family, they plan a fun night out. However, the plan backfires when they are cursed and all turned into Monsters.
documents.plot: The Wishbone family are far from happy. In an attempt to reconnect as a family, they plan a fun night out. However, the plan backfires when they are cursed and all turned into Monsters.

documents.title: The Kissing Booth
documents.tagline: She can tell her best friend anything, except this one thing
documents.overview: When teenager Elle's first kiss leads to a forbidden romance with the hottest boy in high school, she risks her relationship with her best friend.
documents.plot:
The Kissing Booth is a 2018 American teen romantic comedy film written and directed by Vince Marcello, based on Beth Reekles's 2012 novel of the same name. It stars Joey King as Elle Evans, a quirky late bloomer, Jacob Elordi as Noah Flynn and Joel Courtney as Noah's younger brother Lee, with Molly Ringwald in a supporting role.

Elle and Lee have been best friends since birth in Los Angeles, and they live by a set of friendship rules. After losing her mother to illness, Elle quietly nurses a crush on Lee's popular, bad-boy older brother Noah. On the first day of junior year, Noah gets into a fight with a classmate who touches Elle inappropriately, and later warns every boy at school to stay away from her. Elle and Lee organize a kissing booth for a school fundraiser, and Elle rashly promises that Noah will take part. When he does not show up, Lee takes his place and leaves with a classmate, Rachel, and a group of popular girls set Elle up to kiss an unwanted partner, but at the last moment Noah steps in and kisses the blindfolded Elle, and they kiss again in front of everyone.

Sheltering from the rain in a gazebo, Elle tells Noah she will not be just another conquest, and he admits his feelings for her. After he defends her at a beach party, they detour to the Hollywood Sign and spend their first night together, agreeing to keep the relationship secret from Lee until Elle can tell him. Elle also learns that Noah has been accepted to Harvard University. When Lee discovers them kissing, he storms off, feeling betrayed, and Elle blames Noah, who disappears from school for weeks. Elle and Lee eventually reconcile at an arcade, and she attends prom with Lee and his new girlfriend, Rachel. When Noah declares his love for her publicly at the prom, Elle runs away. At Elle and Lee's birthday costume party the next day, she confesses her love for Noah to Lee, who gives his blessing; driving off to find Noah, she discovers that the "Lee" in a Batman costume beside her is Noah himself. They spend the following weeks together before he leaves for college.

Released on Netflix on May 11, 2018, the film was panned by critics as clichéd and regressive, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 15% approval, but Netflix deemed it a major success because of its viewership and re-watch rate. It was followed by The Kissing Booth 2 in 2020 and The Kissing Booth 3 in 2021.

documents.title: God of War
documents.overview: During the 16th century, pirates rule the Chinese coastline, pillaging the small villages and terrorizing the citizens. When maverick leader Commander Yu enlists the help of a sharp young general, they devise a plan to defeat the pirates. A violent clash of wit and weapons will decide who will rule the land.
documents.plot:
God of War (Chinese: Dàng Kòu Fēng Yún) is a 2017 Chinese-Hong Kong historical war film directed by Gordon Chan, based on General Qi Jiguang's campaigns against the wokou pirates who raided China's coast during the Ming dynasty. Vincent Zhao stars as Qi Jiguang, with Sammo Hung as General Yu Dayou and the Japanese actor Yasuaki Kurata as the samurai commander Kumasawa, alongside Wan Qian and Wu Yue.

In the 16th century, Ming forces under General Yu Dayou launch an assault on a coastal fortress held by Japanese pirates, but the attack is repulsed with heavy losses. The so-called wokou turn out to be a mixed force of masterless ronin, disaffected Chinese and a disciplined contingent of samurai led by the veteran commander Kumasawa, who has been sent by his feudal lord on a mission of his own. After the defeat, command passes to General Qi Jiguang, who recruits a new army from tough local villagers. Qi's surprise attack drives the Japanese from their fortress, but because they escape, he is accused by court officials of failing his duty and even of colluding with the enemy, and narrowly escapes arrest.

The Japanese then split into three groups to strike simultaneously at the provincial capital of Taizhou, the town of Ninghai and the town of Xinhe, where the families of Qi's soldiers, including his wife, are living. Kumasawa hopes to overstretch the Ming defenses, while his young ward, Lord Imagawa, argues for a single massive assault. Learning of the plan, Qi first intercepts and destroys the ronin force, then marches to defend Taizhou, knowing that this leaves Xinhe almost unprotected. In his absence, his wife rallies the soldiers' wives and families into an improvised militia that holds off the samurai.

At Taizhou, Qi's army is nearly overwhelmed when Imagawa defies Kumasawa and attacks with the surviving ronin, but last-minute reinforcements turn the tide, and the Japanese retreat toward their ships. Qi relieves Xinhe and then strikes the invaders as they attempt to embark. Kumasawa sends Imagawa to safety and makes a last stand, dueling Qi personally before taking his own life in defeat. The film ends with Qi's wife awaiting her husband's homecoming.

God of War screened at the Seattle International Film Festival in May 2017 and was released in the United States by Well Go USA Entertainment on June 2, 2017, in Mandarin and Japanese with English subtitles.

documents.title: The Little Stranger
documents.tagline: These delusions are contagious
documents.overview: In a dusty post-war summer in rural Warwickshire, a doctor is called to a patient at lonely Hundreds Hall. Home to the Ayres family for over two centuries, the Georgian house is now in decline. But are the Ayreses haunted by something more sinister than a dying way of life?
documents.plot:
In 1940s Warwickshire, Dr. Faraday is called to visit a sick maid at the dilapidated Hundreds Hall. The maid confesses to faking and hopes the doctor will send her home. The Hall now belongs to Roderick Ayres, a scarred Royal Air Force veteran severely burned in the Second World War, who is being nursed by his sister, Caroline. Dr. Faraday recalls during his childhood in 1919 visiting the house, where his beloved mother had once been a maid to the grand Ayres family. He once broke an acorn from an elaborate plaster carving, to his mother's anger, in view of young Susan, the Ayres' first daughter, known as Suki.
There are intermittent noises occurring in the house, alarming Caroline, Mrs. Ayres and the maid. The servants' bells sound without anyone ringing them. A 19th century tube communication device linking the empty nursery to the kitchen also begins to sound inexplicably. When Mrs. Ayres goes upstairs to investigate, she is suddenly locked in the nursery. Experiencing shadowy figures and strange banging noises, Mrs. Ayres, in a frantic attempt to escape, breaks the windows, cutting both arms. After the others in the household rescue her from the room, she comes to believe that Suki's ghost is always nearby.
Not long afterwards, Mrs. Ayres kills herself by slashing her wrists with the glass from a broken picture frame. Roderick attends the funeral, admonishing Caroline to leave the house lest she might be the next to die. On the night of the funeral, Faraday and a reluctant Caroline make plans to marry in six weeks' time. Later, Faraday considers that the strange occurrences in the house may well be due to poltergeist activity. It is suggested that supernatural phenomena might be the product of random, unintended telekinesis, which may well be poltergeist-like activity caused by a living person (as opposed to a dead one).
Caroline eventually breaks off her engagement to Dr.
Faraday, insisting that she would not be happy married to him, and expressing her intention to sell Hundreds Hall. Faraday insists that she is merely exhausted and not thinking clearly.
One night, Faraday has a house call that keeps him off-premises. When he finally arrives home, he learns that Caroline has fallen from the second floor to her death.
At the inquest into Caroline's death, the maid reports that she awoke to hear Caroline going upstairs to investigate a strange noise in the hall. She also reports hearing Caroline cry out "You!," immediately before falling to her death. After Dr. Faraday testifies that Caroline's mind was undoubtedly "clouded," the coroner declares the death to be a suicide. The court concurs.
Months later, Faraday visits the Ayres home while it is up for sale, having kept the keys which Caroline gave him. As he leaves the premises, the lifelike spectre of a young Faraday standing at the top of the staircase (where Caroline fell) solemnly watches him before backing away into the darkness.

documents.title: Accident Man
documents.tagline: Accidents happen. He can guarantee it.
documents.overview: Mike Fallon, the Accident Man, is a stone cold killer.  When a loved one is murdered by his own crew, Fallon is forced to avenge the one person who actually meant something to him.
documents.plot: Mike Fallon, the Accident Man, is a stone cold killer.  When a loved one is murdered by his own crew, Fallon is forced to avenge the one person who actually meant something to him.

documents.title: The Recall
documents.tagline: They've come to claim what's theirs
documents.overview: When five friends vacation at a remote lake house, they expect nothing less then a good time, unaware that Earth is under attack by an alien invasion and mass-abductions.
documents.plot:
During a time when strange atmospheric disturbances are occurring at various locales around the globe, a group of teenagers go on a vacation trip to a secluded cottage in the woods. At a filling station along the way they have a bad encounter with a man (Wesley Snipes) who calls himself "The Hunter". At the cottage, the teenagers begin exploring and come across a seemingly abandoned cabin. Inside, they find pictures and realize it's the Hunter's house, and furthermore, that he was formerly an astronaut. When he returns unexpectedly they sneak out and run away.
That night, when the Hunter shows up in the woods outside their cottage, they believe he is there to attack them. One of them, Rob (Niko Pepaj), goes to the car to get his gun, but on the way back he sees an alien under the porch and panics but he doesn't tell his friends. Later, during the atmospheric disturbances, they see a glow of light. Only Kara seems to know what it is, and seems terrified of it. When an alien enters the house, Rob panics and accidentally shoots Kara. He breaks down and turns on his friends. Charlie stops him by rendering him unconscious. The remaining friends run for the car and drive away in panic. When Rob suddenly appears in the road, Charlie swerves to avoid him and crashes the car. They watch from the wreckage as a UFO appears and abducts Rob, allowing the others to make their escape.
Unbeknownst to the teenagers, the Aliens have come to Earth,
abducting thousands of humans. On the run from the aliens with the others, Brendan is injured by a bear trap placed by the Hunter. The Hunter appears and saves them from a pursuing alien, and takes them back to his cabin. The Hunter ambushes an alien in a pit and seems to take personal pleasure in killing it. The Hunter explains that he was abducted and experimented-on by the aliens years ago. He shows them scarifications left on his body by the aliens; furthermore, he demonstrates that he can move objects telekinetically. He explains that the aliens have visited Earth several times in the distant past, and through "enhancements" made to abductees, have controlled the evolution of life on Earth. Since his retirement as an astronaut he has been preparing for their return, dedicating himself to putting an end to their reign.
But the aliens besiege the cabin and the teenagers all end up being taken up to the spaceship, where they are among a few thousand humans who are abducted, experimented on, then returned to Earth. The teenagers all wake up back at their cottage, with no memory of having been abducted or experimented on. Kara, who had been killed, also appears to be alive and well. On the road, they are stopped by a military roadblock; although the alien ships have departed as mysteriously as they'd arrived, the government has responded to the mass abductions by putting a plan in place to quarantine anyone who shows the telltale scarifications from having been abducted.

documents.title: #realityhigh
documents.overview: When nerdy high schooler Dani finally attracts the interest of her longtime crush, she lands in the cross hairs of his ex, a social media celebrity.
documents.plot:
#RealityHigh (stylized #REALITYHIGH) is a 2017 American teen comedy directed by Fernando Lebrija and released on Netflix on September 8, 2017. Set in Southern California, it follows a studious high school senior who is swept into the world of a social media celebrity and briefly loses sight of what matters to her. Nesta Cooper stars as the heroine, Dani Barnes, alongside Keith Powers as Cameron Drake, Alicia Sanz as Alexa Medina, Jake Borelli as Freddie Myers and Kate Walsh as Dr. Fiona Shively.

Dani is a straight-A student who loves dogs, volunteers at a local dog clinic and is determined to win a scholarship to the University of California, Davis. Seen as an unfashionable nerd, she has one real friend, Freddie, who secretly has feelings for her that she fails to notice, because she has been infatuated since childhood with Cameron, one of the most popular boys at school. Cameron dates Alexa, Dani's childhood best friend turned tormentor, an admired influencer with a large following across social media. When Alexa drops Cameron for another online star, Fousey, Dani and Cameron grow closer.

Suddenly Alexa wants to be friends again. She apologizes for the past, offers Dani a fresh start and draws her into her circle of extravagant shopping trips and parties. Dani enjoys the attention and new status, starts dressing and styling herself like Alexa and gradually loses her grip on what is important. She lets Freddie down by skipping his first paid gig and losing the venue for their animal rescue event, and she fails Cameron by missing his meet and his big television appearance and by staying silent about his UCLA acceptance in front of his father. Cameron breaks up with her, and Alexa then turns on her, posting a viral video that uses supposed evidence to paint Dani as a drunk and a stalker, which spawns cruel memes.

Dani's younger sister shows her support by unfollowing Alexa, and Dani patches things up with Freddie. She persuades the Bob's Big Boy restaurant to host the animal rescue event, and its success earns her the college recommendation Fiona had promised. At the senior class bonfire on the beach, where everyone gathers except Alexa, who is mourning the loss of her YouTube channel, Dani and Cameron kiss and reconcile.

The film received mostly negative reviews, holding a 40% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, while Common Sense Media gave it one star.

documents.title: Bad Genius
documents.original_title: ฉลาดเกมส์โกง
documents.tagline: Genius students with one mission... Turning exam answers into millions.
documents.overview: Lynn, a brilliant student, after helping her friends to get the grades they need, develops the idea of starting a much bigger exam-cheating business.
documents.plot:
Lynn, a top secondary school student living with her father, is accepted into a prestigious school, earning a scholarship for her academic achievements. There, she is befriended by the good-natured but academically challenged Grace. Lynn begins to help Grace cheat in exams after finding out that their teacher has been leaking questions in private tutoring sessions. She is then approached by Grace's rich boyfriend Pat, who offers payment in exchange for also helping him and his friends. Although at first reluctant, Lynn agrees when she finds out that the school, despite her scholarship, collected extra fees from her father, who earns a modest income as a teacher. She devises a system of hand signals, based on certain piano pieces, and uses them to send answers during exams. Her base of clients eventually grows. However, her cheating is inadvertently revealed by Bank, another top student. She is reprimanded by her father, and also by the school, which suspends her scholarship and revokes her chance to apply for an international scholarship at university level.
Lynn returns to cheating when Pat and Grace ask her to help them with the STIC—an international standardised test for university admissions—a scheme which will earn them millions of baht. However, Lynn tells them that she can only do it with the help of Bank, who would never consider such dishonesty. Later, though, Bank, who is from a poor family and is staking his future on the same university scholarship, is attacked by thugs in the street and misses the scholarship exam. Lynn then approaches him with the offer and Bank reluctantly agrees. Together, they make preparations for the final operation. Lynn and Bank will fly to Australia in order to get a head start on the exams—which are held globally on the same day—and send back answers for Pat and Grace to distribute to their clients. However, on the eve of their flight, Pat lets slip that it was he who ordered the thugs to beat up Bank, in order to force him to join their scheme. Enraged, Bank attacks Pat and leaves. Lynn, shocked at the revelation, begins reconsidering her actions. However, Bank returns to confront Lynn and tells her to finish what she started.
In Sydney, Lynn and Bank complete the first sections of the test according to plan, but Bank is overcome by anxiety and gets caught. Lynn struggles to memorise the final section herself, but finally pulls through. She is pursued by the test administrator after feigning illness by forcing herself to be sick and leaving the test centre early, but is released when Bank denies knowing her. Returning home, Lynn finds that their scheme was a great success, but, broken by the experience, turns her back on her co-conspirators and rejects her share of the money. Some time later, she is approached by Bank, who has invested his share in revamping his mother's laundry business.

documents.title: Time Trap
documents.tagline: Escape to the future.
documents.overview: A group of students become trapped inside a mysterious cave where they discover time passes differently underground than on the surface.
documents.plot:
Time Trap is a 2017 science fiction action adventure film directed by Ben Foster and Mark Dennis. Brianne Howey, Cassidy Gifford, Olivia Draguicevich, Reiley McClendon and Andrew Wilson star as young people in remote Texas who search for their missing professor and enter a cave where time behaves impossibly.

Hopper, an archaeology professor, is searching for a group of hippies who vanished in the area in the 1970s while hunting for the Fountain of Youth. After spotting what looks like a cowboy frozen in place inside a cave tunnel, he dismisses his graduate students, Taylor and Jackie, and returns alone. When he fails to come back, Taylor and Jackie set out to find him, accompanied by their friend Cara, her younger sister Veeves and Veeves's friend Furby. At the cave entrance Furby stays above ground as a lookout while the others climb down a rope. Soon Furby stops answering the radio, and when Jackie tries to climb out, the rope frays and she falls, injuring herself and Taylor.

Searching for another way out, the group finds Furby dead near a second entrance. His camera footage reveals that he waited for days on the surface while barely an hour passed for those inside, and that the missing hippies were Hopper's parents and sister. Taylor realizes the cave lies inside a time distortion in which time below moves far more slowly than above. A brief trip to the barren surface leads them to conclude that thousands of years may have elapsed outside during their few hours underground.

The students encounter cavemen who have wandered into the distortion over the centuries, as well as a towering, futuristic humanoid who descends from the surface. Though he protects them and heals Taylor, he is poisoned by the cave's air, and before dying he shows them that humanity long ago abandoned a dying Earth for Mars and evolved there. Taylor finds Hopper near the heart of the phenomenon, a waterfall where his sister, Spanish conquistadors and a horde of cavemen are frozen mid-battle, and the survivors must find a way to escape the trap and return to a world that has moved on without them.

Time Trap premiered at the Seattle International Film Festival on May 19, 2017, and was released on video on demand in November 2018. Rotten Tomatoes reports that 67% of 12 critics' reviews are positive, and Metacritic assigned it 45 out of 100. The Los Angeles Times called it a handful of intriguing ideas in search of a more cohesive narrative.

documents.title: Elliot: The Littlest Reindeer
documents.tagline: Big Dreamers Dream Big
documents.overview: When Blitzen announces his retirement on December 21st, a miniature horse has 3 days to fulfill his lifelong dream of earning a spot on Santa's team at the North Pole try-outs.
documents.plot:
Elliot: The Littlest Reindeer is a 2018 Canadian animated Christmas comedy written and directed by Jennifer Wescott. The voice cast features Josh Hutcherson as Elliot, Samantha Bee as Hazel, and Martin Short, Morena Baccarin, Jeff Dunham and John Cleese. The film follows a miniature horse who dreams of joining Santa Claus's sleigh team and gets an unexpected chance when one of the famous reindeer retires.

Elliot lives on the struggling Witty Bitty Farm in North Dakota, which operates both as a petting zoo and as a training camp for aspiring sleigh reindeer, most of whom are arrogant and self-absorbed. Elliot trains alongside them, but the farm's owner, the former baseball player Walter Whittick, barely notices him, and his only real supporter is his best friend Hazel, a sharp-witted goat. When Blitzen announces his retirement, tryouts are held at the North Pole to find a replacement, and Walter hopes that his most athletic reindeer, DJ, will win the place and save the farm from financial ruin.

At the same time, a businesswoman named Ludzinka arrives and offers to buy the petting zoo animals. Walter agrees, unaware of her real intentions, but Elliot and Hazel discover that she plans to turn the animals into dehydrated food. Hoping to win the tryouts and rescue their friends, the pair stow away in Walter's flying vehicle as he travels north with DJ. At the North Pole, Hazel uses disguises to get Elliot registered for the competition, helped by an elf named Jolene, since Santa and his elves can talk with animals. Elliot faces a series of demanding trials against much bigger and stronger competitors, while Hazel uncovers signs that Christmas itself may be headed for disaster. Back at the farm, Ludzinka threatens the lives of the animals, and Elliot must choose between pursuing his lifelong dream and saving the friends he left behind.

The film was released in Canada in November 2018 and received negative reviews, with a 29 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes. The site's consensus called it a farcical Christmas romp only slightly more entertaining than a heap of coal, and Nell Minow of RogerEbert.com gave it one and a half stars out of four. Tara McNamara of Common Sense Media was also among the critics who reviewed the film for family audiences.

documents.title: Tag
documents.tagline: Based on a true story. We’re not kidding.
documents.overview: For one month every year, five highly competitive friends hit the ground running in a no-holds-barred game of tag they’ve been playing since the first grade. This year, the game coincides with the wedding of their only undefeated player, which should finally make him an easy target. But he knows they’re coming...and he’s ready.
documents.plot:
Hogan "Hoagie" Malloy, Bob Callahan, Randy "Chilli" Cilliano, Kevin Sable, and Jerry Pierce have been playing tag since 1983 during the month of May, with Jerry the only one who has never been tagged. Hoagie recruits Callahan, Chilli, and Sable for one last attempt to tag Jerry, telling them that Jerry plans to retire after this year's game because of his upcoming marriage. Rebecca Crosby, a Wall Street Journal reporter, decides to write an article on the friends. They are also accompanied by Hoagie's wife Anna.
Once in their hometown of Spokane, Washington, the group locate Jerry and attempt to tag him but are overwhelmed by his skill. He introduces his fiancée Susan. The others agree to not play the game at wedding-related events in exchange for invitations to the wedding.
Despite this, the group makes several attempts to tag Jerry, but come up short, with one of the attempts leaving Hoagie, Chilli, and Sable in traps set by Jerry. During the rehearsal dinner, Susan confides to the guys that she is pregnant.
Defeated, the group try to build a new plan. After finding out Jerry attends Alcoholics Anonymous meetings, they decide to strike his next meeting, which is on his wedding day. They make their move and almost tag Jerry, but he retreats to the communion wine storage. Jerry and the guys stay there for hours, until Susan comes by with the wedding just a few hours away. She berates him for risking their wedding for a childish game, then suddenly appears to have a miscarriage, so he comes out to help. Chilli is convinced that it is a ruse, but Jerry insists he is not playing around and the couple leaves.
The guys receive texts that the wedding is postponed due to the potential miscarriage. However, they see a post from a bridesmaid of Susan in her dress, showing that the wedding is still on schedule. Incensed by the trick, the gang decide to crash the wedding. Upon their arrival, Susan confirms the hoax, including the pregnancy. Angry at Jerry for lying, Hoagie decides to tag him at the end of the ceremony after he and Susan kiss. He charges at Jerry and ends up tackling the pastor to the ground and loses consciousness. Anna confirms that his condition is serious and calls for an ambulance.
Everyone meets up at the hospital, where Hoagie tells them he had lied about Jerry quitting after the season because he wanted to reunite with his friends after he himself recently discovered a tumor on his liver; he feared he might not be alive for the following year and was heartbroken at possibly dying without seeing Jerry get tagged.
Jerry lets Hoagie, lying on the hospital bed, tag him. The group starts the game again and changes the rules so Anna, Susan, and Rebecca can play as well.
Before the credits roll, video clips and a photograph are displayed of the real group of ten men that inspired the film, who continue to play.
During the credits Jerry finally gets tagged.

documents.title: The Humanity Bureau
documents.tagline: In the near future our government will decide who is expendable.
documents.overview: In 2030 the world is in a permanent state of economic recession and facing serious environmental problems as a result of global warming.
documents.plot:
In the future, war, climate and political agendas have robbed America of its resources. An agency called "the Humanity Bureau" ensures citizens are efficient. Inefficient citizens are deported to a city called New Eden. Noah Kross is an agent of the Humanity Bureau who manages the deportation of Chester Hills, a former governor of Colorado, who now lives in misery. When asked why he wishes to stay in squalor rather than be relocated to New Eden, he says he knows "the truth". He fires a shotgun at Kross and the hotel manager; Kross kills him in self-defense.
Kross evaluates a single mother, Rachel Weller, and her son, Lucas. Though apparently struggling, they wish to stay rather than go to New Eden. With the help of his friend Agent Porter, he delays sending in his report so the boy can perform at a musical recital the following day; Kross fondly remembers fishing in Canada as a boy and wants Lucas to have a positive memory of his recital. This act of minor insubordination upsets the Bureau and catches the attention of Kross’s supervisor Adam, who places him under investigation. Rachel's resistance to relocation and the "truth" purported by Chester motivate Kross to investigate New Eden. A defense contractor working for the bureau gives Kross a memory card.
The next day, Kross attends Lucas' recital and spends the night with them. When he wakes up the next morning, he sees the Bureau coming and rushes inside to get Rachel and Lucas. Rachel is being held hostage by Adam. Lucas shoots Adam in the eye with a BB gun and they escape. They drive to a gas station; Kross isn't able to purchase gas because his card has been canceled. Kross demands gas at gunpoint. When asked by the owner if Kross is a family man, he says he is "trying to be". The owner assists in their flight by crashing his truck into the Bureau vehicles pursuing Kross.
Back at the Bureau, Adam is admonished for failing to stop Kross. The Bureau's director opens a package of what looks like dust in front of him and shows Adam a child's tooth, warning him that if he fails again, he will end up in New Eden, revealed to be an extermination camp where unproductive citizens are incinerated. Kross has learned the truth and seeks to save Lucas and Rachel.
During their flight, Kross trades his Bureau vehicle for an unmarked station wagon and learns of a man who may know a way north. When they find the man, they learn that the way north to Canada is highly irradiated and that no one who ever goes returns. When he insists, the man gives Kross a geiger counter to measure radiation, and iodine tablets which provide some protection against radiation absorption. Kross gives Lucas a rabbit's foot for good luck during the trip.
Along the road, they spot a drone searching for Kross. After becoming tired and frustrated waiting for it to pass, Kross and Rachel get into an argument where Kross reveals that he knows the real Rachel Weller, and this woman is not her.

documents.title: White Fang
documents.tagline: Rediscover Jack London's Masterpiece
documents.overview: A loyal wolfdog’s curiosity leads him on the adventure of a lifetime while serving a series of three distinctly different masters.
documents.plot: A loyal wolfdog’s curiosity leads him on the adventure of a lifetime while serving a series of three distinctly different masters.

documents.title: Hellboy
documents.tagline: Demons Have Demons Too
documents.overview: Hellboy comes to England, where he must defeat Nimue, Merlin's consort and the Blood Queen. But their battle will bring about the end of the world, a fate he desperately tries to turn away.
documents.plot:
Hellboy is a 2019 American superhero film based on the Dark Horse Comics character created by Mike Mignola. A reboot of the Hellboy film series and the third live-action film in the franchise, it was directed by Neil Marshall and stars David Harbour in the title role, with Milla Jovovich as the Blood Queen Nimue, Ian McShane as Professor Trevor Bruttenholm, Sasha Lane as Alice Monaghan, Daniel Dae Kim as Ben Daimio and Thomas Haden Church as Lobster Johnson. Its story draws on the comic arcs Darkness Calls, The Wild Hunt and The Storm and the Fury.

In 517 AD, the Blood Queen Vivienne Nimue unleashes a plague on Britain until King Arthur defeats her with the help of a member of her own coven, dismembering her with Excalibur and hiding her remains across the country. In the present day, Hellboy, a demon raised by humans and working as an investigator for the Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense, travels to Tijuana to find a missing agent, only to discover that he has become a vampire. Back in Colorado, his adoptive father Bruttenholm sends him to Britain to help the Osiris Club hunt three giants.

During the hunt, Hellboy is betrayed by the club's hunters and nearly killed, but he defeats the giants and is rescued by Alice Monaghan, a young medium whom he once saved from fairies when she was a baby. Meanwhile, a vengeful pig-like changeling called Gruagach, aided by the witch Baba Yaga, is gathering the pieces of Nimue's body so that she can be resurrected. Joined by Alice and Major Ben Daimio of the British paranormal agency M11, who harbours a secret of his own, Hellboy learns that Nimue intends to use him to bring about the apocalypse by tempting him to embrace his destiny as the beast of the end times. Torn between the humans who fear him and the monsters who see him as their king, Hellboy must decide which side he belongs to.

Marshall's film is darker and considerably more violent than Guillermo del Toro's earlier Hellboy films, earning an R rating for its graphic gore and drawing more directly on Mignola's folklore-inspired stories.

Hellboy was panned by critics, with an approval rating of about 17 percent on Rotten Tomatoes, although Harbour's performance received some praise. It was a box-office bomb, grossing about 55.1 million dollars against a 50 million dollar budget, and the series was rebooted again in 2024 with Hellboy: The Crooked Man.

documents.title: Game Over, Man!
documents.overview: Three friends are on the verge of getting their video game financed when their benefactor is taken hostage by terrorists.
documents.plot:
Game Over, Man! is a 2018 comedy film that satirizes action movies and explores themes of masculinity, friendship, and the consequences of toxic masculinity. The movie follows three friends who must save their video game developer friend from an alien invasion.

At its core, Game Over, Man! is a commentary on traditional masculine norms and the expectations placed on men to be strong and stoic. The film's protagonist, Casey (played by Adam DeVine), embodies these traits, but as the story progresses, his character is revealed to be more vulnerable and emotionally expressive than initially thought.

The movie also explores the theme of male friendship and camaraderie, highlighting the importance of relationships in times of crisis. The three friends - Casey, Dylan (played by Blake Anderson), and Nick (played by Anders Holm) - work together to save their friend, showcasing the power of teamwork and loyalty.

Furthermore, Game Over, Man! pokes fun at the conventions of action movies, exaggerating the typical hero's journey for comedic effect. The film's over-the-top action sequences and absurd plot twists serve as a commentary on the genre's tendency to prioritize spectacle over substance.

Overall, Game Over, Man! is a lighthearted, humorous take on traditional masculine norms and the importance of male friendships, using satire and absurdity to make pointed commentary on modern society.

documents.title: Champions
documents.tagline: When winning isn't everything
documents.overview: A disgraced basketball coach is given the chance to coach Los Amigos, a team of players who are intellectually disabled, and soon realizes they just might have what it takes to make it to the national championships.
documents.plot:
Champions (Spanish: Campeones) is a 2018 Spanish sports comedy-drama directed by Javier Fesser, who co-wrote it with David Marqués. Javier Gutiérrez stars as the basketball coach Marco Montes, with Athenea Mata as his wife, Sonia, and Juan Margallo as Julio, alongside a team of players with intellectual disabilities. The story was inspired by Aderes, a team from Burjassot, near Valencia, made up of people with intellectual disabilities, which won twelve Spanish championships between 1999 and 2014.

Marco is the arrogant, short-tempered assistant coach of the professional basketball club CB Estudiantes. During a game he argues with the head coach over strategy and shoves him, and is promptly fired. That same night he drives drunk into the back of a police car. In court he is given a choice between two years in prison and ninety days of community service, which will consist of coaching Los Amigos, a team of players with intellectual disabilities.

At first Marco makes no secret of his contempt for the players and refers to them with a slur. As the weeks pass, though, he comes to know each of them, their individual histories and quirks, and he is struck by their persistence and their commitment to one another. His home life, meanwhile, is strained: Sonia wants a baby, and Marco insists he is not ready. A friend of Marco's, Iván, who is attracted to Sonia, tries to manoeuvre some time alone with her, but Marco turns up anyway, and the couple leave still at odds. Travelling to away games proves chaotic, as the team's blunt and boisterous behaviour constantly clashes with fellow passengers on public transport. When Marco confides in Sonia, she borrows a camper van from a colleague at the sporting-goods shop where she works and starts travelling with the team, and their marriage begins to heal. Los Amigos fight their way to second place in the national championship, Marco agrees to start a family with Sonia, and when he returns to professional coaching the players thank him for changing their lives.

Released in Spain by Universal on 6 April 2018, it was the country's highest-grossing Spanish-language film of the year, taking €19.1 million from 3.3 million admissions. It won three Goya Awards, including Best Film and Best New Actor for Jesús Vidal, and was Spain's submission for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film. It inspired a sequel and remakes in Arabic, German, English, directed by Bobby Farrelly, and Hindi.

documents.title: Elizabeth Harvest
documents.overview: The newly married Elizabeth arrives with her new husband, the scientist Henry, at a magnificent house. He tells her that she can do there anything she pleases, except to enter a certain closed room.
documents.plot:
Elizabeth, a new bride, is brought home on her wedding day by her husband Dr. Henry Kellenberg. Henry's house is palatial and only two other people live there; the housekeeper Claire, and Henry's adult son Oliver, who is blind. Henry shows Elizabeth around the house, telling her that she can enter any room except one, which is located in the basement.
After Henry leaves for work each day, Elizabeth is left to her own devices. Initially her new clothing and jewellery, and the various luxuries provided by her new home are sufficient to entertain her. But eventually her curiosity gets the better of her and she explores the forbidden room, where she discovers clones of herself. She runs out of the room in a panic, leaving the door open. When Henry returns, he quickly discovers her deceit and brutally murders Elizabeth. Claire and Oliver help him to dispose of her corpse in a shallow grave in the grounds.
Six weeks later, another "Elizabeth" is traveling home with Henry after their wedding, exactly as before. The new Elizabeth goes through the same experiences, also discovering the room with the clones, except she manages to kill Henry before he can kill her. When Oliver and Claire find out what has happened and that Henry is dead, Claire has a heart attack and is taken to the hospital.
Oliver imprisons Elizabeth and asks her to read Claire's journal to him; he tells her that he will not release her until she does. The journal reveals that the original Elizabeth was Henry's wife, but she died of a rare medical condition. Unable to bear her loss, Henry decided to create clones of her, and hired Claire (a biologist) to help perfect them. The initial attempts were abortive, but eventually they succeeded. From the journal, it is learned that Henry and Claire have awoken six clones in total, including the current "Elizabeth" who is actually the fifth. The journal also reveals Claire's suspicions that Oliver is actually a clone of Henry, and that when she confronted Henry with this revelation he did not deny it.
When Elizabeth tells Oliver this, he states that Henry blinded him out of jealousy when he was a child, not liking Oliver's growing friendship with one of the other child clones, and after he had confronted Henry about molesting one of them.
Elizabeth attacks Oliver and tries to escape, but suddenly a new (sixth and final) clone appears, holding a shotgun. Confused and disoriented, the new clone shoots and kills Oliver. Elizabeth is also fatally wounded by the new clone, but before she dies she tells the clone to read Claire's journal.
The new (and final) Elizabeth reads the journal which tells how Henry and Claire initially met, and details their work together on the cloning experiments. They had a brief intimate relationship at this time, but later Claire discovered that Henry simply wished to relive his wedding night with each new cloned Elizabeth, prior to murdering them, which horrified Claire.

documents.title: Mary Queen of Scots
documents.tagline: Bow to No One
documents.overview: In 1561, Mary Stuart, widow of the King of France, returns to Scotland, reclaims her rightful throne and menaces the future of Queen Elizabeth I as ruler of England, because she has a legitimate claim to the English throne. Betrayals, rebellions, conspiracies and their own life choices imperil both Queens. They experience the bitter cost of power, until their tragic fate is finally fulfilled.
documents.plot:
In 1561, after the death of her husband King Francis II, nineteen-year-old Mary Stuart returns to Scotland from France to take up her throne. She is received by her illegitimate half brother, James Stewart, Earl of Moray.
In neighboring England, Mary's twenty-eight-year-old, unmarried and childless cousin Elizabeth Tudor, the Protestant Queen of England, is threatened by Mary's claim to the English throne. Mary dismisses the cleric John Knox, a Protestant leader of the Scottish Reformation, from the Scottish court. He views the young Catholic queen as a danger to the Protestant religion in Scotland.
To weaken her cousin's threat, Elizabeth arranges for Mary, whom many English Catholics regard as England's rightful queen, to be married to an Englishman. Elizabeth chooses Lord Robert Dudley, her childhood friend whom she secretly loves; although he and Mary are unwilling, news of Elizabeth's case of smallpox convinces Mary to accept, provided she is named heiress apparent.
Reluctant to let go of Dudley, Elizabeth sends Henry Stuart, Lord Darnley to Scotland with the pretence of living under their religious freedom. Despite sensing the ulterior motive, Mary grows fond of Darnley so accepts his proposal.
Mary's marriage causes a constitutional crisis within both realms: Elizabeth is advised to oppose her cousin's marriage for fear that Darnley, a Stuart grandchild of Margaret Tudor, will elevate Mary's claim to her throne; Mary's council is suspicious of Darnley, fearing an English takeover.
Both kingdoms demand Darnley's return to England, but Mary refuses, leading Moray to mount a rebellion against her. Mary marries Darnley, only to discover him in bed with her private secretary, David Rizzio. She defeats the rebel forces but spares Rizzio and Moray and demands that Darnley give her a child. When their son, James, is conceived and born, Mary declares she brings "an heir to Scotland and to England" – offending the English.
Moray colludes with Darnley's father, Matthew Stewart, 4th Earl of Lennox, to undermine his sister. Spreading false rumors that her son was actually fathered by Rizzio, drives Knox to denounce Mary as an adulteress. Fearing these accusations and the possible discovery of his bisexuality, Darnley is pressured into murdering Rizzio.
Uncovering the plot, Mary convinces Darnley to escape with her, which is actually a ploy for her army to detain him. Mary agrees to pardon the conspirators if she is presented with evidence that Darnley took part. She ultimately forgives Moray and asks Elizabeth to be James's godmother. Both queens agree James is the heir presumptive despite the English court's hostility. Mary banishes Darnley but refuses to divorce him, despite her council's appeals. Her adviser and protector James Hepburn, Earl of Bothwell, then has him killed.
After Darnley's murder, Mary must flee, leaving behind her son.

documents.title: Lamborghini: The Man Behind the Legend
documents.original_title: Lamborghini: The Man Behind the Legend
documents.overview: Follow the launch of Lamborghini’s career as a manufacturer of tractors, a creator of military vehicles during World War II, and the designer of Lamborghini cars, which he launched in 1963 as the high-end sports car company Automobili Lamborghini.
documents.plot:
Lamborghini: The Man Behind the Legend is a 2022 American biographical drama written and directed by Robert Moresco, starring Frank Grillo as the Italian industrialist Ferruccio Lamborghini, with Romano Reggiani as the young Ferruccio, Gabriel Byrne as Enzo Ferrari, Mira Sorvino as Lamborghini's second wife Annita, Hannah van der Westhuysen as his first wife Clelia and Fortunato Cerlino as his father Antonio. The film traces Lamborghini's rise from farmer's son to creator of one of the world's most famous sports car brands.

After the Second World War, Ferruccio and his friend Matteo return from service in the Italian Army to their hometown of Cento. Ferruccio reunites with his girlfriend Clelia and tells his father that he wants to start a business building affordable tractors, despite his father's doubts. He marries Clelia, and when he cannot raise enough money, his father gives him the family land to secure a bank loan. Ferruccio founds Lamborghini Trattori and develops a new engine, but tragedy strikes when Clelia dies in childbirth, leaving him with a son, Tonino.

The tractor business eventually becomes a success, and Ferruccio falls in love with Annita, a woman Matteo had hoped to court, causing a rift between the two friends. By 1963, Ferruccio and Annita are married and running a new venture, Automobili Lamborghini, though his relationship with his son remains strained. After being insulted by Enzo Ferrari, Ferruccio resolves to build a grand touring car that will rival Ferrari's. He recruits the engineers Giotto Bizzarrini and Giampaolo Dallara and the New Zealand test driver Bob Wallace, and the company presents the Lamborghini 350 GT at the Geneva Motor Show, launching a fierce rivalry with Ferrari.

The film portrays the ambition, stubbornness and personal sacrifices behind the Lamborghini brand, framing its story around the rivalry between two Italian automotive legends.

Lamborghini: The Man Behind the Legend was released in select theaters in the United States by Lionsgate on November 18, 2022. It was panned by critics, receiving 6 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and Mira Sorvino was nominated for Worst Supporting Actress at the 43rd Golden Raspberry Awards.

documents.title: Rip Tide
documents.tagline: She's a fashionista out of water...but she's about to get back in the swim of things.
documents.overview: There comes a point in everyone’s life when you have to make a decision about the direction you’re going to take. For newly-18 American fashion model Cora, that time is now. She’s moved to an Australian coastal town to be with her favourite aunt, after a 'fashion faux pas’ back home.
documents.plot:
Rip Tide is a 2017 Australian teen drama film directed by Rhiannon Bannenberg, produced by Steve Jaggi and written by Georgia Harrison. Debby Ryan stars as Cora Hamilton, an American model, with Naomi Sequeira, Danielle Carter, Aaron Jeffery, Jeremy Lindsay Taylor and others in supporting roles. The coming-of-age story follows a young woman who escapes the pressures of the New York fashion world by traveling to a beach town in Australia to reconnect with her family and rediscover her own ambitions. The film was released on streaming platforms in October 2017 and later became available on Netflix.

Cora is a successful but unhappy model in New York, constrained by her demanding career and by her ambitious mother and manager, Sofia, who is working to secure her a lucrative contract with a prestigious agency. At a photo shoot, Cora tries to suggest her own design ideas for an outfit, but the director dismisses her, and she storms out in tears. As she leaves, she is filmed falling down a flight of stairs, and the embarrassing video goes viral, damaging both her career and her mother's.

Seeing a birthday card from her Aunt Margot, whom she has not seen since childhood, Cora decides to fly to Australia to stay with her. After an argument with Sofia at the airport, in which Cora insists she is not running away but following where her life is leading, she travels to the small coastal town where her family has roots. There she connects with her aunt and with a group of young locals, takes to the ocean and gradually uncovers parts of her family's history that her mother never shared. Away from the pressures of modeling, she rediscovers her passion for designing clothes and begins to imagine a different future for herself, but her mother's arrival and the lure of her old life force her to decide what she really wants.

The film was produced by Steve Jaggi, whose company made a number of youth-oriented features in Australia for the international market, and it gave Ryan, known for her work on Disney Channel series, a leading role in a coming-of-age drama set against the beaches and surf culture of the Australian coast.

documents.title: Project X-Traction
documents.tagline: There is a plan. They just don't know what it is.
documents.overview: When a China-run oil refinery is attacked in Mosul, Iraq, a Chinese private security contractor is called in to extract the oil workers. He learns, however, that the attackers’ real plan is to steal a fortune in oil, and teams up with an American former Marine to stop them.
documents.plot:
Project X-Traction, released in most markets as Hidden Strike, is an action-adventure film directed and edited by Scott Waugh from a screenplay by Arash Amel, starring Jackie Chan, John Cena, Ma Chunrui and Pilou Asbæk. The project began as a pairing of Chan with Sylvester Stallone, who withdrew and was replaced by Cena. It was shot in 2018, with Chinese locations standing in for the Middle East, and Cena spent months living in Yinchuan to work on it. Before its final title, it was known variously as Ex-Baghdad, Project X, Project X-Traction and SNAFU.

In Iraq, repeated attacks by mercenaries under former special forces soldier Owen Paddock force the closure of an oil refinery owned by the Chinese firm Unicorp. Security contractor "Dragon" Luo Feng leads a convoy of eleven buses carrying its civilian staff, among them chief engineer Professor Chang, her son and his own estranged daughter Mei, along the Highway of Death toward the Green Zone. Former US Marine Chris Van Horne, who needs money to repair a well in a rural village, reluctantly joins his mercenary brother Henry in the attack. Using a jet-engined truck to raise a sandstorm, the mercenaries seize two buses and take Professor Chang and her son hostage, as Owen plans to force her to restart the refinery and steal its oil.

Disgusted, Chris turns on Owen, who murders Henry. After fighting off French mercenaries together, Feng and Chris become allies, and Feng repairs his bond with Mei. Owen threatens the village to recover the notebook of restart codes that Chris had taken by accident, and Chris hands it over to protect the villagers. When Owen sends the oil away in a convoy of fuel trucks, the heroes storm the refinery, wreck the convoy with the jet truck and drive Owen's vehicle off a cliff. Later they fix the village well, and Chris accepts Feng's invitation to join him on a new mission.

Released in July 2023, theatrically in the United Arab Emirates and some other markets and on Netflix elsewhere, it grossed under $1 million in cinemas against an $80 million budget. On Netflix it became the most-watched film worldwide in its opening weekend, with 56.8 million views in 28 days. Critics were largely negative, with 24% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and complaints about weak chemistry between the leads, although some reviewers enjoyed it as light popcorn entertainment.

documents.title: Guns Akimbo
documents.tagline: Get loaded
documents.overview: An ordinary guy suddenly finds himself forced to fight a gladiator-like battle for a dark website that streams the violence for viewers. In order to survive and rescue his kidnapped ex-girlfriend, he must battle Nix, a heavily armed and much more experienced fighter.
