documents.title: Extremely Wicked, Shockingly Evil and Vile
documents.original_title: Extremely Wicked, Shockingly Evil and Vile
documents.tagline: The story behind America's most notorious serial killer.
documents.overview: A chronicle of the crimes of Ted Bundy, from the perspective of his longtime girlfriend, Elizabeth Kloepfer, who refused to believe the truth about him for years.
documents.plot:
In 1969 Seattle, law student Ted Bundy meets Liz Kendall, a young secretary and divorced mother. The two begin dating, and Ted helps Liz raise her young daughter, Molly.
By 1974, news reports announce the recent murders of multiple young women, including two who disappeared in broad daylight at Lake Sammamish; a man resembling Ted was seen by several people asking women to help him load a kayak onto a Volkswagen Beetle. A composite sketch of the attacker is released and, following hundreds of phone calls, Ted is arrested the following year.
A young woman named Carol DaRonch picks Ted out of a police lineup, claiming he had kidnapped and threatened to kill her before she managed to escape. Ted is released on bail, returning home to Liz who is upset after reading an article about him in the newspaper. Ted explains that Carol was shown his picture before the lineup took place, which is why he looked familiar to her, and says he believes he is being set up. After a four-day bench trial, Ted is found guilty of aggravated kidnapping and is sentenced to serve a minimum of one to a maximum of 15 years in the Utah State Prison.
A few weeks later, Colorado authorities charge Ted with the murder of Caryn Campbell, and he is transferred to Aspen, Colorado, in 1977. Liz refuses to believe Ted is guilty, but the events start to take a toll on her, and she begins drinking heavily as a result. While at Pitkin County Courthouse, Ted elects to serve as his own attorney and, as such, is excused from wearing handcuffs or leg shackles. During a court recess, Ted escapes from the courthouse by jumping out of a second-story window and running to the mountains through the town, but is recaptured after six days.
Liz visits Ted and ends their relationship. He later escapes again after sawing a square into his cell's ceiling. Two women at a sorority house are murdered at Florida State University, followed by vicious attacks on three more. After Ted is arrested, he tries to contact Liz, but she hangs up on him. He starts to receive a following of women who are fascinated by him, some even claiming they love him. Ted is also visited by an old friend, Carole Ann Boone, who believes he is innocent and moves to Florida to be closer to him during his upcoming murder trial.
A pre-trial plea bargain is negotiated in which Ted would plead guilty to killing the two sorority girls, Lisa Levy and Margaret Bowman, and twelve-year-old Kimberly Leach, in exchange for a 75-year prison sentence instead of a possible death sentence, but he refuses. Ted and Carole Ann grow closer as she visits him regularly; the two begin a relationship, but Ted continues to reach out to Liz who is following his trials via television. She carries the guilt of being the person who gave Ted's name to the Seattle authorities in 1975. Ted later proposes to Carole Ann mid-trial and they marry.

documents.title: Brotherhood of Blades II: The Infernal Battlefield
documents.overview: An imperial guard searches for the truth behind a conspiracy that framed him and his partners. The proof of his innocence lies with a wanted woman named Bei Zhai... but will she reveal what she knows? In this intense prequel to BROTHERHOOD OF BLADES, the only thing he can truly trust is his sword.
documents.plot: Shen Lian, a jinyiwei officer, killed his colleague Ling Yunkai in order to save the painter Beizhai during a mission to eliminate the rebels. After that, he had to get rid of the suspicion and investigation from Lu Wenzhao and Pei Lun on the one hand, and set fire to the jinyiwei's case library under the threat of a mysterious woman on the other hand. In the turbulent times, Shen Lian and Beizhai fell in love, but they fell deeper and deeper. Behind all this, a huge conspiracy was secretly laid out
production_companies: 东阳坏猴子影视文化传播有限公司

documents.title: Psych: The Movie
documents.overview: The ambitious friends come together during the holidays after a mystery assailant targets one of their own. A comedic thrill-ride follows, as the wild and unpredictable Psych team pursues the bad guys, justice … and, of course, food!
documents.plot:
As shown in the series finale, Shawn, Gus, and Juliet relocated to San Francisco, where they remain three years later. After Juliet's SFPD partner Sam Sloane is shot, Shawn and Gus attempt to find out who was responsible and why it happened. They soon learn that a mysterious organization is threatening the reputation, safety, and well-being of Juliet. At first, Juliet is reluctant to allow anyone to help her out with her problem, but an unpleasant development connected with her partner's shooting convinces her she needs Shawn's help.
Meanwhile, Shawn refuses to get married until he can locate his grandmother's engagement ring, which he had taken without permission from his dad's house, and which had been stolen from him while he was in the act of proposing to Juliet in San Francisco three years earlier. His efforts to retrieve the ring land him in hot water with a major fencer of stolen goods in the Bay Area.
Chief Vick, up for consideration for a position as police commissioner, is not aware that her daughter has started committing crimes. Gus, meanwhile, lands in trouble with his boss as a result of Shawn bringing his business to Gus's workplace. While working around all of these complications, the group encounters old friends, discover surprising pieces of information, and come to some major determinations about their futures.

documents.title: Slaughterhouse Rulez
documents.tagline: Bloodius. Hellius. Maximus.
documents.overview: An illustrious British boarding school becomes a bloody battleground when a mysterious sinkhole appears at a nearby fracking site unleashing unspeakable horror.
documents.plot:
Slaughterhouse Rulez is a 2018 British comedy horror film directed by Crispian Mills, who wrote it with Henry Fitzherbert. The first production from Simon Pegg and Nick Frost's company Stolen Picture, it stars Finn Cole as Don Wallace, Asa Butterfield as Willoughby Blake and Hermione Corfield as Clemsie Lawrence, with Michael Sheen as the headmaster, Pegg as housemaster Meredith Houseman and Frost as eco-campaigner Woody Chapman.

After his father's death, Don, a working-class teenager from the north of England, is sent by his widowed mother to Slaughterhouse, a venerable and exclusive boarding school, in keeping with his late father's wishes. He struggles to fit in amid the school's arcane rituals and sanctioned bullying, and the place harbors secrets: a pupil died by suicide the previous term, there have been mysterious disappearances, and an overzealous sixth-form prefect, Clegg, descends from a long line of war criminals. Don forms an uneasy alliance with his sardonic new roommate, Willoughby, an outsider bullied by the older boys, and falls for Clemsie, one of the sixth form's revered "goddesses". The ineffectual Houseman, meanwhile, pines for his former girlfriend, who is working in Africa and appears only in video calls.

To raise money, the scheming headmaster has made a deal allowing a company to frack for gas near the school, to the fury of Woody, who is camping in the woods. The drilling opens an enigmatic sinkhole, and from it emerge packs of ravenous subterranean creatures that begin attacking the faculty and devouring pupils. Don rallies a group of students to fight back against the monsters. In the end the creatures are defeated and the school is destroyed in an explosion, while the surviving pupils walk away and the headmaster's dog and Houseman, who have also survived, watch the destruction.

Shot at locations including Stowe School, Windsor Great Park and Chislehurst Caves, the film was released in the United Kingdom and Ireland on October 31, 2018, and in North America in May 2019, earning about £738,000 at the box office. Critics were mostly negative, giving it 38% on Rotten Tomatoes and 39 on Metacritic; Screen International found its story strands underdeveloped, while The Guardian credited Mills with directing "with zip" and found an amiable charm despite it being neither very scary nor very funny.

documents.title: The Night Eats the World
documents.original_title: La Nuit a dévoré le monde
documents.overview: After waking up to find himself all alone in an apartment where a massive party was being held the night before, Sam is immediately forced to face a terrifying reality: the living dead have invaded the streets of Paris.
documents.plot:
The Night Eats the World (French: La nuit a dévoré le monde) is a 2018 French English-language zombie film directed by Dominique Rocher, who wrote it with Jérémie Guez and Guillaume Lemans, based on Pit Agarman's novel of the same name. Anders Danielsen Lie stars as Sam, a man caught alone in a Paris overrun by zombies, with Golshifteh Farahani and Denis Lavant in supporting roles.

Sam, a musician, goes to his ex-girlfriend Fanny's apartment during a party to collect some tapes. After being bumped by a guest, he gets a nosebleed and passes out in the office, sleeping through sounds of chaos outside. The next morning the apartment is trashed and bloodied, and in the stairwell he finds Fanny and others transformed into zombies who charge at him. The zombies, fast and utterly silent, react in swarms to any sight or sound. A shotgun blast through the floor reveals that a man downstairs killed his infected wife and then himself, and Sam takes the gun, seals the building's doors and explores the apartments one by one, gathering supplies. He keeps a zombified elderly man, Alfred, trapped in the lift and talks to him, and plays music on equipment he finds.

As time passes, Sam grows lonely and unstable. After nearly dying trying to catch a stray cat, he fires at it in anger. Winter brings cold and cuts the water supply, and he survives on rainwater and a makeshift fireplace. Noticing the streets have emptied, he pounds a drum kit and screams, drawing a horde that almost climbs onto the balcony. One night he fires through his bedroom door and wounds a woman, Sarah, who has survived by crossing rooftops with a grappling hook. She later urges him to leave, warning that he will otherwise die or go mad, but he then finds her dead from the gunshot, revealing that their conversations were hallucinations. Among her belongings is a camera with photos of her family and of Sam on the roof. Deciding to leave, he burns his tapes and locks Alfred in an apartment, but the smoke sets off a fire alarm and zombies storm the building. Sam fights his way to the roof, swings across to the next building and gazes over the endless Paris skyline, where he briefly hears what may be another survivor.

The film premiered at the Angers Film Festival on 13 January 2018 and was released in France on 7 March. It holds 87% on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus praised its atmosphere and character focus, and a Metacritic score of 50.

documents.title: Spinning Man
documents.tagline: The only truth is knowing you know nothing.
documents.overview: Evan Birch, a family man and esteemed philosophy professor at a distinguished college, is the prime suspect when a female student goes missing.
documents.plot:
Spinning Man is a 2018 psychological thriller directed by Simon Kaijser from a screenplay by Matthew Aldrich, adapted from George Harrar's 2003 novel. Produced by Irish DreamTime and Chimney, with Ellen S. Wander and Keith Arnold as producers, cinematography by Polly Morgan and music by Jean-Paul Wall, it stars Guy Pearce, Pierce Brosnan and Minnie Driver, with Alexandra Shipp, Clark Gregg, Odeya Rush, Jamie Kennedy, Freya Tingley, Eliza Pryor and Noah Salsbury Lipson.

Evan Birch (Pearce) is a popular, respected philosophy professor at a distinguished college, married to Ellen (Driver) and the father of two children. Beneath his polished surface, however, he has a weakness for young women: he was once driven out of another university by scandal, has had affairs with students and constantly fantasizes about women he encounters. When Joyce Bonner (Rush), a high school cheerleader, disappears near a local lake, his past dalliances lead Ellen to doubt his alibi. The meticulous detective Robert Malloy (Brosnan) begins asking questions, and Evan's indignant refusal to let him search his car, invoking the Fourth Amendment, is only the first of many red flags. Evan insists he never met the girl, yet strands of her hair are found in his impounded car, and he turns out to have arrived forty minutes late to pick up his daughter from camp on the afternoon in question. His attraction to his admiring student Anna (Shipp) and the counsel of his cynical lawyer Paul (Gregg) complicate matters. Increasingly, Evan suffers memory lapses that are never fully explained, and he begins to justify his evasions with ideas from his lectures on the philosophy of language, arguing that truth is relative. The film deliberately keeps viewers uncertain whether he is a killer, a self-deceiving liar or simply a man who no longer trusts his own memory.

The project was first announced in 2016 with Peter Flinth directing and Nikolaj Coster-Waldau, Greg Kinnear and Emma Roberts attached, but in April 2017 a new cast and director were announced, and principal photography began in May 2017. Lionsgate Premiere released the film in limited theaters and on demand on 6 April 2018. Reviews were mixed, with a 50% Rotten Tomatoes rating and a Metacritic score of 44. Variety praised Pearce's performance and Brosnan's crisp detective but felt the film's game of toying with the audience left viewers guessing without caring, while The Hollywood Reporter credited the cast as its main reason for watching.

documents.title: John Wick: Chapter 3 - Parabellum
documents.tagline: Every action has consequences.
documents.overview: Super-assassin John Wick returns with a $14 million price tag on his head and an army of bounty-hunting killers on his trail. After killing a member of the shadowy international assassin’s guild, the High Table, John Wick is excommunicado, but the world’s most ruthless hit men and women await his every turn.
documents.plot:
John Wick: Chapter 3 – Parabellum is a 2019 action-thriller film directed by Chad Stahelski and written by Derek Kolstad. The movie takes place immediately after the events of John Wick: Chapter 2.

The story begins with John Wick (Keanu Reeves) on the run from the High Table, a council of powerful crime lords who have declared him "excommunicado" due to his killing of a member of the Adjudicator's guard. With a $14 million bounty on his head, John Wick must navigate a treacherous landscape of assassins and hitmen to survive.

As he tries to stay one step ahead of his pursuers, John Wick is aided by Sofia (Halle Berry), an old acquaintance who helps him evade capture. However, their partnership is short-lived, as they soon find themselves facing off against the Adjudicator's guard, led by The Bowery King (Asia Kate Dillon).

Meanwhile, a new player enters the scene: Zero (Mark Dacascos), a legendary assassin with ties to John Wick's past. As the body count rises and the stakes grow higher, John Wick must confront his own demons and face off against some of the deadliest assassins in the world.

Throughout the film, Stahelski employs innovative action sequences that showcase Reeves' impressive physicality and stunt work. The movie's climax features an epic showdown between John Wick and Zero, with the fate of the High Table hanging in the balance.

One of the standout aspects of John Wick: Chapter 3 – Parabellum is its exploration of the world-building and mythology that underpins the franchise. The film delves deeper into the rules and hierarchies of the High Table, revealing a complex web of alliances and rivalries between the various crime lords.

Ultimately, John Wick: Chapter 3 – Parabellum is a non-stop thrill ride that delivers on its promise of high-octane action and stylish visuals. With its breakneck pacing and intricate plot twists, it's a must-see for fans of the franchise and action enthusiasts alike.

documents.title: Palmer
documents.tagline: Family is who you make it.
documents.overview: After 12 years in prison, former high school football star Eddie Palmer returns home to put his life back together—and forms an unlikely bond with Sam, an outcast boy from a troubled home. But Eddie's past threatens to ruin his new life and family.
documents.plot: After 12 years in prison, former high school football star Eddie Palmer returns home to put his life back together—and forms an unlikely bond with Sam, an outcast boy from a troubled home. But Eddie's past threatens to ruin his new life and family.

documents.title: Missing Link
documents.tagline: Meet Mr. Link
documents.overview: The charismatic Sir Lionel Frost considers himself to be the world's foremost investigator of myths and monsters. Trouble is, none of his small-minded, high-society peers seems to recognize this. Hoping to finally gain acceptance from these fellow adventurers, Sir Lionel travels to the Pacific Northwest to prove the existence of a legendary creature known as the missing link.
documents.plot:
Missing Link is a stop-motion animated adventure comedy film directed by Chris Butler and produced by Laika Entertainment. The movie follows the story of Sir Lionel Frost, a wealthy and eccentric British aristocrat who sets out to find the legendary Sasquatch.

The film begins with Sir Lionel Frost (voiced by Hugh Jackman), a self-absorbed and somewhat dim-witted nobleman who is obsessed with finding the mythical creature known as the Sasquatch. He believes that if he can prove its existence, it will bring him fame and fortune. However, his obsession is not driven by any genuine interest in the creature, but rather by a desire to boost his own social status.

Frost's life takes an unexpected turn when he meets Sir Walter (voiced by Stephen Fry), a wise and witty explorer who has spent years searching for the Sasquatch. The two men form an unlikely partnership, with Frost agreeing to help Walter find the creature in exchange for a share of the fame and fortune that will come from its discovery.

As they embark on their journey, they are joined by Annie (voiced by Zoe Saldana), a fierce and independent Native American woman who is also searching for the Sasquatch. Annie's motivations are rooted in her desire to protect her people's cultural heritage and traditions, which she believes are being threatened by the encroachment of European settlers.

Throughout their journey, the trio faces numerous challenges and obstacles, including treacherous terrain, hostile creatures, and rival treasure hunters. Along the way, Frost learns valuable lessons about humility, friendship, and the importance of respecting other cultures.

As they near their destination, the group discovers that the Sasquatch is not just a mythical creature, but a real being who has been living in secret among humans for centuries. The Sasquatch, named Nikabrik (voiced by Ryan Reynolds), is a complex and multifaceted character who is both fierce and vulnerable.

In the end, Frost and his companions must confront their own biases and prejudices in order to help Nikabrik find its place in the world. Through a series of heartwarming and humorous moments, the group learns to appreciate each other's differences and work together towards a common goal.

The film features stunning stop-motion animation, witty dialogue, and a talented voice cast. While it may not be a perfect film, Missing Link is a charming and entertaining adventure that explores themes of identity, community, and acceptance.

documents.title: Remi, Nobody's Boy
documents.overview: At the age of 10 years, young Rémi is snatched from his adoptive mother and entrusted to the signor Vitalis, a mysterious itinerant musician. Has its hard sides - he will learn the harsh life of acrobat and sing to win his bread. Accompanied by the faithful dog capi and of the small monkey Joli-Coeur, his long trip through France, made for meetings, friendships and mutual assistance, leads him to the secret of its origins.
documents.plot:
Remi, Nobody's Boy (French: Rémi sans famille) is a 2018 French historical adventure drama directed by Antoine Blossier and based on Hector Malot's 1878 novel Sans Famille, a classic of French children's literature. Maleaume Paquin stars as the young Rémi, with Daniel Auteuil as the street musician Vitalis, Virginie Ledoyen, Ludivine Sagnier and Jonathan Zaccaï in supporting roles. The film was released in French cinemas in December 2018.

The film is framed by a stormy night at an orphanage, where frightened children gather around an old man who tells them the story of his childhood. His name is Rémi. Abandoned as a baby and found outside a church, Rémi grew up happily in a French village in the 19th century with the woman he believed to be his mother, who loved him dearly. Their life changes when her husband, a stonemason working in Paris, is badly injured in an accident and returns home embittered and in debt. Revealing that Rémi is not their son, he decides to take the boy to an orphanage to be rid of another mouth to feed.

On the way they meet Vitalis, a former violinist who now travels the countryside as a street performer with a mischievous monkey named Joli-Cœur and a loyal dog named Capi. Discovering that Rémi has a beautiful singing voice, Vitalis offers to rent the boy from his foster father, sparing him the orphanage. Rémi reluctantly sets out on the road with Vitalis and his animals, and the old musician teaches him to read, to sing and to perform. Their wanderings across France bring hardship, danger and moments of joy, including a friendship with a sickly girl and her wealthy mother. Along the way Rémi learns more about the mystery of his birth and about Vitalis's own hidden past, while the bond between the boy and his gruff mentor grows into something like that of father and son.

The film was a popular success in France and received generally positive reviews, with praise for Auteuil's performance, its photography and its faithful but accessible treatment of the classic novel, which had previously been adapted many times for film, television and animation.

documents.title: Vivarium
documents.tagline: You're home. Forever.
documents.overview: A young woman and her fiancé are in search of the perfect starter home. After following a mysterious real estate agent to a new housing development, the couple finds themselves trapped in a maze of identical houses and forced to raise an otherworldly child.
documents.plot:
Vivarium is a 2019 science fiction horror film directed by Lorcan Finnegan and written by Lev Grossman. The movie stars Imogen Poots, Jesse Eisenberg, and Rory Kinnear.

The story begins with Tom (Jesse Eisenberg), an artist who lives in a suburban neighborhood with his wife, Gemma (Imogen Poots). They are struggling to have children, as Gemma is unable to conceive. One day, while driving through the suburbs, they come across a peculiar house that seems to be calling out to them. The realtor, Mr. Howarth (Rory Kinnear), shows them the house and tells them it's perfect for their needs.

As Tom and Gemma move into the house, they start to experience strange occurrences. They soon discover that the house is a kind of "vivarium," a place where humans are bred like animals in a lab. The couple soon realizes that they have been chosen as the next pair of parents in this experiment.

The vivarium is inhabited by other human-animal hybrids, including a family with two children who seem to be the product of this breeding program. As Tom and Gemma try to understand what's happening, they are forced to participate in the breeding process, which involves a series of surreal and disturbing events.

Throughout the movie, Tom and Gemma's relationship is put to the test as they struggle to cope with their new reality. They begin to question their own humanity and the nature of their existence. The film builds up to a shocking climax as Tom and Gemma realize that they are trapped in this vivarium forever, forced to breed more hybrids until the experiment is complete.

The ending of Vivarium is intentionally ambiguous and open to interpretation. As the credits roll, we see Tom and Gemma's children growing up in the vivarium, while Tom and Gemma themselves seem to be stuck in a never-ending cycle of breeding and rebirth. The film raises questions about the ethics of scientific experimentation on human subjects and the consequences of playing God.

Overall, Vivarium is a thought-provoking and unsettling film that explores themes of identity, humanity, and the consequences of scientific hubris. With its unique blend of sci-fi horror and social commentary, it has become a cult classic among fans of the genre.

documents.title: Private Life
documents.overview: Richard and Rachel, a couple in the throes of infertility, try to maintain their marriage as they descend deeper and deeper into the insular world of assisted reproduction and domestic adoption.
documents.plot: Richard and Rachel, a couple in the throes of infertility, try to maintain their marriage as they descend deeper and deeper into the insular world of assisted reproduction and domestic adoption.

documents.title: Mamma Mia! Here We Go Again
documents.original_title: Mamma Mia! Here We Go Again
documents.tagline: Discover how it all began.
documents.overview: Five years after meeting her three fathers, Sophie Sheridan prepares to open her mother’s hotel. In 1979, young Donna Sheridan meets the men who each could be Sophie’s biological father.
documents.plot:
Mamma Mia! Here We Go Again is a musical romantic comedy film directed by Ol Parker, based on the songs of ABBA. The movie is a sequel to the 2008 film Mamma Mia!, and it features an all-star cast, including Lily James, Amanda Seyfried, Meryl Streep, Pierce Brosnan, Colin Firth, Stellan Skarsgård, Dominic Cooper, Cher, and Hugh Skinner.

The story begins with Sophie Sheridan (Amanda Seyfried), the daughter of Donna Sheridan (Meryl Streep), who is now a mother herself. The movie takes place on the same Greek island where the original film was set, and it follows Sophie's journey as she prepares to open her own hotel.

As Sophie is getting ready for her wedding, she discovers an old diary belonging to her mother, Donna, which reveals secrets about her past and the events that led up to the creation of ABBA. The story then flashes back to 20 years ago, when Sophie was a young girl living on the island with her mother.

The film features three main plotlines: Sophie's present-day journey as she prepares for her wedding, Donna's backstory as she navigates her relationships and career in the 1990s, and the origins of ABBA. The story is interwoven with flashbacks to Donna's time on the island, where she meets Sam Carmichael (Pierce Brosnan), Bill Anderson (Stellan Skarsgård), and Harry Bright (Colin Firth).

As Sophie delves deeper into her mother's past, she discovers that Donna had a complicated love life and was torn between three men: Sam, Bill, and Harry. The story takes the audience on a journey through time, exploring themes of love, heartbreak, and self-discovery.

Throughout the film, ABBA's iconic songs are featured prominently, with many of them being performed by the cast in elaborate musical numbers. The movie also features cameos from Cher, who plays Ruby Sheridan, Sophie's grandmother, and Hugh Skinner, who plays Young Sam.

The ending of the film is a heartwarming tribute to Donna's legacy and her impact on Sophie's life. As Sophie prepares to open her hotel, she reflects on the lessons she learned from her mother about love, forgiveness, and following one's dreams. The movie concludes with a grand musical number featuring the entire cast, celebrating the power of music and the enduring spirit of ABBA.

Overall, Mamma Mia! Here We Go Again is a delightful and entertaining film that celebrates the music of ABBA and the enduring legacy of its iconic songs. With its talented cast, stunning locations, and catchy musical numbers, it's a must-see for fans of musicals and romantic comedies alike.

documents.title: Monster Hunter
documents.tagline: Behind our world, there is another.
documents.overview: A portal transports Cpt. Artemis and an elite unit of soldiers to a strange world where powerful monsters rule with deadly ferocity. Faced with relentless danger, the team encounters a mysterious hunter who may be their only hope to find a way home.
documents.plot:
Monster Hunter is a 2020 action fantasy film written, directed and produced by Paul W. S. Anderson, based on Capcom's video game series. It stars Milla Jovovich, in her sixth film with her husband Anderson, as U.S. Army Ranger Captain Natalie Artemis, with Tony Jaa as the Hunter and Ron Perlman as the Admiral, alongside T.I., Meagan Good, Diego Boneta, Josh Helman and MC Jin as members of Artemis's squad. The film follows soldiers transported to a hostile world ruled by gigantic monsters.

In a parallel world, humans struggle to survive among huge, savage creatures. A warrior known as the Hunter is separated from the Admiral's crew when their ship is attacked by the Diablos, an enormous horned beast that tunnels beneath the dunes. On Earth, Artemis and her United Nations security team are searching the desert for a missing squad of soldiers when a sudden storm pulls them through a dimensional portal into the new world, where they find the charred remains of the soldiers they were looking for.

The team's bullets and grenades prove useless against the Diablos, and the survivors take refuge in a cave, only to be attacked by spider-like monsters called Nerscylla. Artemis escapes alone and encounters the Hunter. After fighting each other, the two grudgingly agree to cooperate. She learns that the portals are created by the Sky Tower, a structure across the desert, and that they must kill the Diablos to cross safely. Learning to use the Hunter's weapons, Artemis helps him lay a trap for the beast, and their journey eventually leads them to the Admiral and his crew, and into a deadly confrontation with the fire-breathing Rathalos, which threatens to break through the portal into our world.

The film emphasizes large-scale creature battles and visual effects, borrowing monsters and characters from the game Monster Hunter: World.

Monster Hunter opened in China on December 4, 2020, and in the United States on December 18 amid the COVID-19 pandemic. It was a box office bomb, grossing 47.9 million dollars against a 60 million dollar budget, and received mixed reviews, with 44 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 47; critics praised the action and effects but faulted the direction and editing.

documents.title: Peppermint
documents.tagline: The system failed. She won't.
documents.overview: A grieving mother transforms herself into a vigilante following the murders of her husband and daughter, eluding the authorities to deliver her own personal brand of justice.
documents.plot:
A woman is engaged in a brutal fight with a man in a car and finally kills him with a shot to the head. Five years earlier, the woman, Riley North, is working as a banker struggling to make ends meet. Her husband, Chris, owns a failing mechanic shop. They have a ten-year-old daughter, Carly. Chris's friend tries to talk him into robbing Diego Garcia, a powerful drug lord. Chris turns him down, but not before Garcia has already discovered his involvement and ordered his men to make an example of him. Riley and Chris take Carly out for pizza and to a carnival for her birthday. As the family walk to the car, Diego's men gun down Carly and Chris in a drive-by shooting. Riley is wounded but survives. Despite her injuries, Riley can positively identify the shooters. The detectives handling the case are hesitant to pursue charges against the three, as they are members of Garcia's drug cartel, which wields considerable influence. Detective Beltran explains to his partner, Carmichael, that the last detective who tried to bring Garcia to justice was murdered.
Before the preliminary hearing, Riley is visited by the perpetrators' lawyer, who tries to bribe her. She refuses the bribe, but the lawyer notices she has anti-psychotic medication at home and uses this information to paint her as an unreliable witness. Judge Stevens, who is secretly on the cartel's payroll, declares there is insufficient evidence to allow the perpetrators to stand trial and dismisses the case, while the prosecuting lawyers do nothing. Outraged, Riley tries to attack her family's killers, but is tasered and placed on a psychiatric hold in a mental institution. En route, she escapes and vanishes. Five years later, Detectives Beltran and Carmichael arrive at the site of the carnival and find the three shooters hanging from a ferris wheel, having been executed by Riley. The executions attract the attention of FBI agent Lisa Inman, who meets with Beltran and Carmichael. Inman explains that before vanishing, Riley robbed the bank she used to work at, and that she has now returned, having stolen various assault rifles and ammunition from a gun store.
Riley executes Judge Stevens by blowing up his house, having already killed the defense and prosecution lawyers involved, deaths which Inman, Carmichael, and Beltran learn of, after the explosion. They decide to inform the media about Riley, which sparks a debate on social media between those who view her as a hero and those who see her as a criminal. Riley heads to a business that is a front for Diego's money laundering, where she kills most of his men, saving only one for interrogation. Diego realises Riley is responsible for his recent shipments going missing and resolves to kill her. Meanwhile, Inman discovers Riley has been living on Skid Row, learning she is the reason for the recent changes to crime patterns in the area.

documents.title: Us
documents.tagline: Watch yourself
documents.overview: Husband and wife Gabe and Adelaide Wilson take their kids to their beach house expecting to unplug and unwind with friends. But as night descends, their serenity turns to tension and chaos when some shocking visitors arrive uninvited.
documents.plot:
Us is a 2019 American horror film written, produced, and directed by Jordan Peele. The movie follows the story of the Wilson family, who are forced to confront their doppelgangers, known as "the Tethered."

The film begins with Adelaide Wilson (Lupita Nyong'o), a young girl who, as a child, escapes from a haunted house at a carnival in Santa Cruz, California. The experience leaves her with a traumatic memory that she tries to suppress.

Years later, Adelaide is now an adult and living in the suburbs with her husband Gabe (Winston Duke) and their son Jason (Evan Alex). They are preparing for a family vacation to the same Santa Cruz beach where Adelaide had her terrifying childhood experience. Unbeknownst to them, this trip will bring about a series of events that will change their lives forever.

Upon arrival at the beach, Adelaide begins to feel an inexplicable sense of unease and disconnection from her surroundings. She starts to notice strange occurrences around her, which she initially dismisses as mere coincidence. However, it soon becomes clear that something is amiss.

As the night falls, a group of masked figures emerges from the shadows, revealing themselves to be Adelaide's doppelgangers, known as "the Tethered." The Tethered are identical in appearance to their human counterparts but have been living underground for years, feeding on the fear and suffering of those above ground.

The Tethered, led by Red (Lupita Nyong'o), begin to terrorize Adelaide's family, using their knowledge of the Wilsons' deepest fears against them. As the night wears on, it becomes clear that the Tethered are not just mindless monsters but rather a manifestation of the darker aspects of human nature.

As the situation spirals out of control, Adelaide is forced to confront her own dark past and the trauma she has been trying to suppress. She also begins to realize that the Tethered are not just random duplicates but rather a product of a sinister experiment designed by the government to create an army of mindless drones.

In the end, Adelaide must make a choice between saving herself or saving her family. In a shocking twist, she decides to sacrifice herself to save her loved ones, using her knowledge of the Tethered's weaknesses to defeat them.

The film ends with Adelaide and her family escaping from the beach, but not before Red reveals that there are more Tethered out there, waiting to be unleashed. The final shot is of a group of children playing in the park, unaware of the horrors that lie beneath their feet.

Throughout the movie, Peele explores themes of identity, class, and the duality of human nature. The film's use of horror elements serves as a metaphor for the darker aspects of society, highlighting the ways in which we often turn on each other when faced with fear and uncertainty.

Overall, Us is a thought-provoking and terrifying film that challenges audiences to confront their own fears and insecurities. With its clever plot twists and outstanding performances, it has become a modern horror classic.

documents.title: First Reformed
documents.tagline: The kingdom come undone.
documents.overview: A pastor of a small church in upstate New York starts to spiral out of control after a soul-shaking encounter with an unstable environmental activist and his pregnant wife.
documents.plot: A pastor of a small church in upstate New York starts to spiral out of control after a soul-shaking encounter with an unstable environmental activist and his pregnant wife.

documents.title: Charlie's Angels
documents.tagline: Unseen. Undivided. Unstoppable.
documents.overview: When a systems engineer blows the whistle on a dangerous technology, Charlie's Angels from across the globe are called into action, putting their lives on the line to protect society.
documents.plot:
Charlie's Angels is a 2019 action-comedy film directed by Elizabeth Banks, starring Kristen Stewart, Naomi Scott, and Ella Balinska as the main characters. The movie is a reboot of the classic 1970s television series of the same name.

The story begins with Charlie Townsend (Dustin Hoffman), a wealthy businessman who runs a private investigation agency called Townsend & Associates. However, Charlie has passed away, leaving his agency in disarray. His three daughters, Alex (Kristen Stewart), Sabrina (Naomi Scott), and Eleanor (Ella Balinska), are recruited by their father's business partner, Bosley (Patrick Wilson), to take over the agency.

The sisters, who were once part of a secret organization called Charlie's Angels, must now work together to solve cases and bring down villains. They soon discover that they have been replaced by a new team of agents, led by a ruthless and cunning adversary known as Madison Lee (Lily James).

As the story unfolds, Alex, Sabrina, and Eleanor embark on a series of missions, including infiltrating a high-stakes poker game and stopping a plot to steal a valuable artifact. Along the way, they must navigate their complicated relationships with each other and with Bosley, who is struggling to keep up with the modern world.

Throughout the film, the sisters showcase their unique skills and personalities, from Alex's tough-as-nails exterior to Sabrina's bubbly and charming demeanor. Eleanor, the youngest sister, brings a fresh perspective and a talent for hacking.

As the stakes grow higher, the Angels must confront Madison Lee and her team of henchmen in an epic showdown. The film culminates in a thrilling action sequence, with the sisters using their combined skills to take down the villains and save the day.

One of the standout aspects of Charlie's Angels is its strong female lead characters. The movie celebrates women's empowerment and sisterhood, showcasing the strength and camaraderie between Alex, Sabrina, and Eleanor as they work together to achieve their goals.

Overall, Charlie's Angels is a fun and action-packed film that pays homage to the original series while introducing new characters and themes. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and exciting plot twists, this movie is sure to delight fans of the franchise and newcomers alike.

documents.title: The Boss Baby: Family Business
documents.tagline: Playtime is over.
documents.overview: The Templeton brothers — Tim and his Boss Baby little bro Ted — have become adults and drifted away from each other. But a new boss baby with a cutting-edge approach and a can-do attitude is about to bring them together again … and inspire a new family business.
documents.plot:
The Boss Baby: Family Business is a 2021 American computer-animated comedy film directed by Tom McGrath, produced by Illumination Entertainment and Universal Pictures. 

The movie takes place five years after the events of the first film. The Boss Baby (voiced by Alec Baldwin) has been working with his brother Tim (voiced by Miles Bakshi) to help their father, Ted (voiced by Steve Buscemi), who is now retired from being a boss. However, when a new villain emerges in the form of Francis Francisca (voiced by Marisa Tomei), the Boss Baby must team up with his brother and their mother, Janine (voiced by Amy Sedaris), to stop her and save the family business.

Throughout the film, Tim struggles to find his place in the world as a "boss" and prove himself to his father. Meanwhile, Francisca is determined to take over the family business and eliminate the Boss Baby once and for all. The movie features plenty of action, humor, and heartwarming moments as the characters navigate their relationships with each other.

One of the standout aspects of the film is its exploration of themes such as identity, family dynamics, and the challenges of growing up. The movie also expands on the world of the Boss Baby universe, introducing new characters and plotlines that add depth to the story.

Overall, The Boss Baby: Family Business is a fun and entertaining film that is sure to delight both children and adults. With its colorful animation, witty humor, and engaging storyline, it's a great addition to the Boss Baby franchise.

documents.title: Hotel Transylvania: Puppy!
documents.tagline: A Hotel Transylvania Short
documents.overview: The residents of Hotel Transylvania find their world turned upside-down when youngster Dennis gets a surprise monster-sized pet.
documents.plot:
Hotel Transylvania: Puppy!, released simply as Puppy!, is a 2017 American computer-animated comedy short film written and directed by Genndy Tartakovsky and produced by Michelle Murdocca for Sony Pictures Animation, with distribution by Columbia Pictures. Set in the world of the Hotel Transylvania films, it was shown at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival in June 2017 and then released in cinemas that summer as the opening short before The Emoji Movie. Tartakovsky made the short while also working on Hotel Transylvania 3: Summer Vacation, and it takes place between the second and third features, serving as a teaser for the latter.

The short opens with little Dennis begging his parents, Mavis and Johnny, for a puppy. Mavis gently refuses, explaining that a pet is a big responsibility, and when Johnny suggests a goldfish instead, the heartbroken boy turns into a bat and flies off wailing that he wants a puppy. Dracula finds his grandson sulking on a window ledge and, unable to resist the boy's pleading face, agrees to get him one. Soon a knock at the door is followed by an enormous blue dog bursting into the family's living room, flattening Dracula against a wall. Dennis is overjoyed and names his new friend Tinkles, while Mavis glares at her father, who insists that every monster needs a good pet, and then discovers that the giant puppy has already had an accident on her floor.

The next night, Mavis asks a sleepy Dracula to look after Tinkles while she takes Dennis to school. The count barely gets back into his coffin before the dog wakes him needing to go outside, then demands to be fed. Dracula brings a wheelbarrow of meat and puts the animal through a series of tricks, which goes well until he commands Tinkles to speak and the dog replies, "Hi. How are you?" Back at the front desk, Dracula grows ever more exasperated by the huge pet looming behind him, and when a family of skeletons checks in, Tinkles lunges at them and starts chewing their bones, wrecking the lobby. Returning with Dennis, Mavis is horrified by the chaos and asks what happened; Dracula simply points to the dog, and the short ends with him sighing to the audience that he needs a vacation, a nod to the next film, also hinted at by the cruise brochure Mavis reads.

The voice cast reunites Adam Sandler as Dracula, Selena Gomez as Mavis, Andy Samberg as Johnny and Asher Blinkoff as Dennis, with Joe Whyte as the voice of Tinkles and Rose Abdoo as the hotel's witch maids.

documents.title: Boo 2! A Madea Halloween
documents.tagline: Peek-A-Boo.
documents.overview: Madea and the gang encounter monsters, goblins and boogeymen at a haunted campground.
documents.plot: Madea and the gang encounter monsters, goblins and boogeymen at a haunted campground.

documents.title: Braven
documents.tagline: They threatened his world. He will destroy theirs.
documents.overview: A logger defends his family from a group of dangerous drug runners.
documents.plot:
Braven is a 2018 American action thriller film directed by Michael Chaves and written by Bryan Woods and Chris McKenna. The movie stars Jason Momoa, Stephen Lang, and Garrett Hedlund.

The story begins with Jack Taylor (Jason Momoa), a former Special Forces operative who has retired to a remote cabin in the woods of Maine with his wife, Liz (Sandra Hüller). They live a peaceful life, away from the chaos of the world. However, their tranquility is disrupted when Liz is kidnapped by a group of Russian mercenaries led by Viktor Kuznetsov (Stephen Lang).

Viktor is a ruthless and cunning adversary who will stop at nothing to get what he wants. He demands that Jack's son, Josh (Garrett Hedlund), participate in a brutal fight tournament, where the winner gets to leave Russia unharmed. If Josh loses, his father will be killed.

Determined to save his family, Jack sets out on a perilous journey to rescue Josh and take down Viktor. He faces numerous challenges along the way, including treacherous terrain, hostile locals, and Viktor's henchmen. As he navigates through the wilderness, Jack must confront his own demons and use his combat skills to survive.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Jack has a personal vendetta against Viktor, who is responsible for the death of his brother in a previous mission. This motivation drives Jack's actions throughout the film, as he seeks revenge against those who have wronged him.

The action sequences in Braven are intense and well-choreographed, with Jason Momoa delivering impressive performances in hand-to-hand combat. The movie also features stunning cinematography, capturing the beauty of the Maine wilderness and the brutality of the fight scenes.

Ultimately, Jack faces off against Viktor in a thrilling showdown, where he must use all his skills and experience to emerge victorious. In the end, Jack rescues Josh and exacts his revenge on Viktor, bringing closure to the story.

Overall, Braven is a gripping action thriller that showcases Jason Momoa's physical prowess and acting abilities. While it may not be a complex or nuanced film, it delivers plenty of excitement and suspense, making it a great choice for fans of the genre.

documents.title: 12 Feet Deep
documents.tagline: 100,000 gallons of water. 50 meters wide. NO. WAY. OUT.
documents.overview: Two sisters are trapped under the fiberglass cover of an Olympic sized public pool and must brave the cold and each other to survive the harrowing night.
documents.plot:
12 Feet Deep, originally titled The Deep End, is a 2017 American psychological horror thriller written and directed by Matt Eskandari. Alexandra Park and Nora-Jane Noone star as sisters who become trapped beneath the fibreglass cover of an Olympic-sized public swimming pool, with Diane Farr and Tobin Bell in supporting roles. The film was released by Mar Vista Entertainment in June 2017 and received generally positive reviews.

Bree goes for a swim at a local aquatic centre just before it closes for the holidays and is joined by her sister Jonna, a recovering drug addict who has been clean for three months. Meanwhile, the pool manager, McGradey, catches the janitor Clara, an ex-convict on parole, stealing from the lost-and-found box and fires her, before announcing that the facility is closing. As the swimmers pack up, Bree realises that her engagement ring is missing, and the sisters spot it stuck in a grate at the bottom of the deep end. While they dive to retrieve it, McGradey, unaware that anyone is still in the water, activates the motorised pool cover and leaves the building for the holiday weekend.

Trapped in the dark between the water and the heavy cover, with only a small opening to breathe through, Bree and Jonna try desperately to break free. Their situation worsens as the water grows colder and Bree, who is diabetic, begins to need her insulin. In the confined space, old resentments surface: Jonna admits that she threw the ring into the pool out of envy of Bree's stable life and engagement, and the sisters revisit painful memories of their abusive, alcoholic father. Their hopes of rescue rise when Clara returns to the building, but the janitor sees the sisters' predicament as an opportunity, demanding the PIN numbers to their bank cards and leaving them at her mercy as the night drags on.

The film uses its single, claustrophobic setting to build tension, while its emotional core is the fractured relationship between two very different siblings who must rely on one another to survive.

12 Feet Deep was generally well received for a low-budget thriller. JoBlo.com called it a well-crafted, entertaining thriller and rated it eight out of ten, while That Moment In described it as well directed and engrossing, more of a tense character piece than a conventional shocker.

documents.title: Feed
documents.tagline: Control yourself
documents.overview: Olivia and Matthew Grey, 18-year-old twins born into a world of privilege and high expectations. There are almost no boundaries between them - even their dreams are connected.
documents.plot:
Feed is a 2017 American drama film directed by Tommy Bertelsen and written and produced by Troian Bellisario, who also stars. Inspired by Bellisario's own experience of anorexia, which she overcame, it follows a high school senior whose physical and mental health, grades and relationships collapse after the death of her twin brother. Bellisario plays Olivia "Liv" Grey, with Tom Felton as her twin, Matt, Ben Winchell as her crush Julian, James Remar and Paula Malcomson as their parents, Tom and Samantha, and David Warshofsky as Dr. Rothstein.

The twins Olivia and Matt are as close as they are different. Liv, a would-be valedictorian, strives for excellence, which her father seems to demand of her far more than of her fraternity-bound brother, yet easygoing Matt is also the one who looks out for her, sometimes overprotectively. After a Halloween party, Matt argues with Liv over her decision to get drunk and hook up with their friend Julian, and he crashes the car they are riding in and dies. Unable to bear her guilt alone, Liv begins to see Matt, or a hostile version of him, at the moments she most needs him. This phantom tells her what to do, what to say and what to think, and above all when not to eat; Liv imagines that she is saving her food for Matt, who can live on only if she makes the sacrifice. While she tries to keep up a facade of normality, her health deteriorates, and after a suicide attempt during a party hosted by her parents, she is sent to an inpatient treatment center for eating disorders. Even there Matt torments her, pushing her to lie to her therapists and to hide food for him against the center's rules. In a therapy session, Liv finally speaks honestly about how she has been feeling, sending Matt's ghost into a rage in which he screams that he hates her and never loved her. After confronting him, she lets go of this version of her brother and recognizes that the voice urging her to control her eating was never really his.

Bellisario began writing the script at 23, about four years after being hospitalized for anorexia, and developed it over roughly eight years, describing the film as inspired by her illness rather than autobiographical. It marked her debut as a writer and producer, and she worked closely with her former therapist while making it, an experience she called both therapeutic and inflammatory. The film was released on video on demand and digital platforms on 18 July 2017.

documents.title: Long Shot
documents.tagline: Unlikely but not impossible.
documents.overview: Journalist Fred Flarsky reunites with his childhood crush, Charlotte Field, now one of the most influential women in the world. As she prepares to make a run for the Presidency, Charlotte hires Fred as her speechwriter — much to the dismay of her trusted advisers.
documents.plot:
Long Shot is a 2019 American romantic comedy film directed by Jonathan Levine and written by Dan Sterling. The movie stars Seth Rogen, Charlize Theron, O'Shea Jackson Jr., Bob Odenkirk, and June Diane Raphael.

The story begins with Fred Flarsky (Seth Rogen), a charismatic but unemployed journalist who has been living in his parents' basement since the 1990s. He is still close to his childhood friend Charlotte Field (Charlize Theron), who is now a successful and ambitious Secretary of State under President Andrew Dixon (Bob Odenkirk).

Years later, Fred receives an invitation from Charlotte to attend her inauguration as the new Secretary of State. During the event, they reconnect, and it becomes clear that their friendship has evolved into something more. However, their social differences and past traumas make a romantic relationship complicated.

As they spend more time together, Fred is drawn back into his old life, including his job at a tabloid newspaper and his relationships with his eccentric family members. Meanwhile, Charlotte's team is working to pass the "Global Health Security Act," which aims to strengthen international cooperation on pandemics.

Despite their growing feelings for each other, Fred struggles to balance his desire for romance with his own sense of identity and purpose. He also faces challenges from his friends and family, who are skeptical about his relationship with Charlotte due to her high-profile position and his lack of ambition.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Charlotte's past is marked by trauma and a complicated relationship with her father, who was a politician. Her desire for power and control stems from a need to prove herself and overcome her insecurities.

Throughout the film, Fred and Charlotte navigate their feelings for each other while also confronting their personal demons. They must decide whether their love can overcome their differences and help them grow as individuals.

The movie culminates with a dramatic speech by Charlotte at the United Nations, where she advocates for global cooperation on pandemics. Meanwhile, Fred's past comes back to haunt him in unexpected ways, forcing him to confront his own insecurities and doubts.

Ultimately, Fred and Charlotte find a way to reconcile their differences and make their relationship work. The film ends with a heartwarming moment of intimacy between the two leads, as they finally find happiness together.

Overall, Long Shot is a charming and witty romantic comedy that explores themes of identity, power, and love. With strong performances from its leads, the movie delivers a satisfying and entertaining ride for audiences.

documents.title: Truth or Dare
documents.tagline: First you play the game, then the game plays you.
documents.overview: A harmless game of "Truth or Dare" among friends turns deadly when someone—or something—begins to punish those who tell a lie—or refuse the dare.
documents.plot:
Truth or Dare is a 2018 American supernatural horror film directed by Jeff Wadlow and written by Michael Renison and Wadlow. The movie follows a group of friends who embark on a trip to Mexico, where they participate in a traditional game called "Truth or Dare," which has a dark and sinister twist.

The story begins with a flashback of the main character, Olivia Barron (Lena Headey), as a teenager, playing Truth or Dare with her friends. The game is presented as a harmless tradition, but it ultimately leads to tragedy. The movie then jumps forward in time to show Olivia's daughter, Lucy (Bailee Madison), who is now a college student.

Lucy and her friends - Lucas (Tyler Posey), Ronnie (Violett Beane), Mark (Sam Lerner), and Tyson (Haley Lu Richardson) - are on a trip to Mexico for spring break. They decide to play Truth or Dare, which is presented as a fun and exciting game by their friend, Olivia's sister, Kate (Natalia Dyer). However, things take a dark turn when they realize that the game has a sinister force behind it.

As the night progresses, the group starts to experience strange and terrifying events. They are forced to participate in increasingly disturbing challenges, which seem to be connected to an ancient ritual. The group soon realizes that they are trapped in a supernatural cycle of horror, where they must play the game or face dire consequences.

The movie builds up to a thrilling climax as Lucy and her friends try to survive the night and uncover the truth behind the game. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including creepy creatures and supernatural entities. The group's dynamics are also put to the test as they struggle to work together and trust each other.

Throughout the movie, there are several twists and turns that keep the audience guessing. The film's climax features a shocking revelation about Lucy's connection to the game and the true nature of the sinister force behind it. In the end, only one member of the group survives, leaving the others to face their fate.

Overall, Truth or Dare is a tense and suspenseful horror movie that explores themes of friendship, loyalty, and the dangers of playing with forces beyond human control. The film's use of supernatural elements and creepy atmosphere creates a thrilling experience for viewers.

documents.title: Heavy Trip
documents.tagline: Better shit thighs than eternal constipation.
documents.overview: Turo is stuck in a small village and the best thing in his life is being the lead vocalist for the amateur metal band Impaled Rektum. He and his bandmates have practiced for 12 years without playing a single gig. The guys get a surprise visitor from Norway -- the promoter for a huge heavy metal music festival -- and decide it's now or never. They steal a van, a corpse, and even a new drummer to make their dreams a reality.
documents.plot: Turo is stuck in a small village and the best thing in his life is being the lead vocalist for the amateur metal band Impaled Rektum. He and his bandmates have practiced for 12 years without playing a single gig. The guys get a surprise visitor from Norway -- the promoter for a huge heavy metal music festival -- and decide it's now or never.
